My god this game was criminally underrated.
Let me make it clear from the start, I love this game. The writing is brilliant, thumbs up to Dan Houser, the guy can write; the dialogue  just crackles and drives home that noir feel perfectly. Bungie and Ubisoft should really give him a call and let him write their next game, god knows they could use a bit of originality (yeah I just went there).
The cut scenes, people ♥♥♥♥♥ about the cut scenes, and all I can say to that is shut up, this isn't for you then. The cut scenes are seamless right alongside the gameplay, they connect you with the character and the struggle for redemption, and damn do they have some production value. IF you sat through the 40 minute MGS cut scenes and want to complain about a 5 minute MP3 cut scene...you don't really have a leg to stand on.
So gameplay, how is it. Incredible. Some of the best third person shooting mechanics out there. The game is a bullet ballet of the highest order with enough heroic blood shed to please any action junkie. Shootouts have never looked prettier in gaming. This may sound odd but the hit animations really take this game to the next level. You see the physical damage your rounds cause, entry and exit wounds aboutnd, blood splashes, gore decorates the walls and floors. This is a mature shooter that puts your right in the middle of the action rather than censoring it and it manages to be beautiful at the same time; the first time you dive through a glass window dual wielding pistols in slow motion while tracer rounds dance around you will put a giant smile on your face.
Rockstar has always been known for upping the bar whenever they release a game and MP3 is no different. This does for action gaming what GTA 3 did for the sandbox genre. If you somehow missed this train there is no better time than now to jump aboard. MP3 is a masterpiece.
My highest reccomendation.

Portal 2 is the sequel to Portal and adds more puzzles and more fun.
At the beginning of Portal 2, Chell is awakened in a “long-term relaxation chamber” in Aperature Science by a little hilarious, British personality named Wheatley. Wheatley's goal is to help you escape, however you soon find out that GLaDOS is still alive. Chell is once again forced to use her portal gun to navigate the ruins of the facility and deal with the resurrected GLaDOS. The story takes some very interesting twists and turns along the way and the terrific dark humor of the first game remains intact.
The gameplay from the original game returns in all of its mind-bending glory. Players use the portal gun to shoot blue and orange colored portal holes onto walls to traverse over deadly pits, transport Weighted Storage Cubes to switches to open doors and lower elevators and redirect lasers. Additions to the gameplay include the propulsion and repulsion gels which do pretty much as they describe, either sliding the player off at great speed or sending them bouncing high into the air. In addition, players must redirect light bridges and conveyer beams with portals as well.
One of the most exciting new features in Portal 2 is the inclusion of co-op gameplay.
Co-op gameplay gets its own storyline and characters, Aperture Science robots ATLAS and P-Body, each armed with their own portal gun and even more challenging puzzles for the gamers to solve. You can either play with a friend (split-screen or online) or team up with a random player.
I highly recommend Portal 2 to anyone who is looking for a good fun game that will take up a few hours and even make you think instead of the average First Person Shooter.
Overall, Portal 2 is a masterpiece and definitely worth the money.

I've gotten the game to run perfectly and if you have an AMD card, you'll want to set your game to Fullscreen Window or Windowed mode.  Problems are solved.  I'm running the game at 60FPS with all settings maxed out except for PPF which is just at 16.  I'm not even using compressed textures.  An AMD 6350 and R9 270 DC II OC - running the game beautifully.
---------------------------------------------------------
If you're an AMD user, expect a bad time. I bought this for the Summer Sale and played 32 minutes before abruptly being thrown to the desktop. Then the game didn't start. Then I spent the next two hours (no joke) looking for fixes. After trying various fixes that didn't work, I managed to finish the game.  I rolled back all of my changes, fired up a new game for the giggles and found that it ran perfectly.  I'm absolutely baffled.  The only lingering issue is I'll have complete freezes and lock-ups that will last from 2-7 seconds during gameplay. No difference noticed when messing with the settings.
I highly suggest removing CCC and just installing the 14.4 drivers on your own if you've got an AMD card. With my specs, the game should run at 60FPS without issue.  This is what I've done to get it working for me.

Many of the wartime stories that have already been proven to be false and accusations that were falsified can be found here and expanded upon. All Germans are presented as the root of all evil with no souls. Certain myths of the war are used heavily in the story... and of course Jewish technology saves the world. It's a pile of crock, but the gameplay is fun at the very least.... if you can stomach the over-the-top stuff.
Not worth full price for all of the issues I've had with it, so I'm happy I grabbed it at 50% off on the sale. I can't recommend this at full price or if you're an AMD user because of the plethera of problems that still exist with no real fixes.  However, the game have proven to be quite fun.

I've been a May Payne fan ever since the first one came out so I was worried about the new direction Rockstar was taking about 'the new Max'. After completing the campaign I have to admit that it isn't bad at all. The presentation is great, Max's voice actor delivers and the whole atmosphere, though not New York, comes together. The graphics are great, the physics are nice and I didn't have any problem with the music or sounds. BUT and it is a big but: there are couple of things which simply killed the game for me. First. if either MSAA or FXAA is enabled, it screws up mouse movement BIG time. Seems like Rockstar still can't properly develop for the PC. Second: the enemies are so bullet-spongie that you can only advance with headshots which is not what I've wanted and also makes certain situations a nightmare. Third: usually I don't have a problem if games take over my character to advance to the next area/level but here it's just ridiculous. Also it constantly switches back to the default weapon which sometimes can screw you over. Fourth: weird gameplay issues like iniating a reload, enter bullet time then exiting the cover simply cancels the reload... WHAT?? Also other weird movement issues... So yeah, great ideas ruined by technical and gameplay problems. As for the multiplayer side of things: it would be a nice touch, however it's still full of cheaters... worthless. To be honest I partially regret my purchase since I didn't wait till the price was low enough. I wanted to write that ' I would only recommend this game if you want a nice singleplayer experience for couple of hours and you can get the game for 5€ or less', however after thinking it through: NO, don't get this game, watch the story on YouTube and get another one instead.

Alright, so I waited until completion of the game before making a review on it. While my initial reaction of the game was great, I wanted to play the whole way through before sharing my thoughts.
As my budget was thight, paying 60$ for a new game wasn't very appealing to me so I decided to wait. Recently, as part of the summer sale, the game dropped to a very appealing 30$ (which is insane) so I decided to bite the bullet and OH BOY! am I glad I did.
I don't judge a game based on the value it gives me. With that being said I don't mind paying full price for a single player only game that takes, in this case, around 15 hours to complete. If you only play games to get incredible amount of value (MMOs, online FPS, MOBAs, etc) then you will probaly be disapointed. Sure the game might get a second or even 3rd playthrough out of you but know that you won't be playing this game for more thand 45-50 hours and that's a stretch. If that bothers you then I suggest either avoiding the game or wait for it to drop in price.
For anyone else, Wolfenstein is a really fun and fast paced shooter with old school roots that doesn't take itself seriously while still giving you a good story focused around a handful of interesting characters. The weapons both look and sound amazing and are extremwly satisfaying to use. You have the choice to go either go fully commando and blast your way through a segment and feel like a complete badass with your dual shotguns (I know) or make your way trhough a level as silently possible picking off guards one by one with your knives and silent pistol using the pretty robust stealth system.
Like I said before, the game takes around 15 hours to beat and does warrant atleast a second playthrough in my opinion.
So if you are interested in anyway in this game and have the money to spend, I urge you to buy this game and support a good development team that took a risk in making a great singleplayer only FPS. You won't be disapointed.
Also, I think it's important to inform you that the download size is a gigantic 41gb, so if that's not achievable to you, I suggest looking into buying a physical copy of the game instead.

I played this game a while back, like around 2014, which was way different back then. I then uninstalled the game, until about a month ago, I started playing it again.
This game has a few plus and minus points.
Firstly, it is NOT P2W. It's just a common misconception among new players as they would be killed by a better player with a better loadout card like cobalt, which makes them think cobalt is the most op and have the most benefits. But they are incorrect - Cobalt and bronze are the same thing, with cobalt only looking better visually.
Secondly, the game is very fast-paced. I would not recommend for casual gamers with slower reflexes as this game constantly moves and cannot be played slowly. The game is very jerky and many players would like to jump around the walls like a crazy jackass rabbit, throwing your aim off.
Thirdly, the game is like a MOBA. Every character in this game is unique with its strengths and weaknesses, like a MOBA, they all have a set of skills which make it unique to them, with the exception of support skills like ammunition and defibrillators for medics. The game is roughly classified into 4 groups, Support/Assault/Recon/Engineers. Supports and basically the medics like Sawbonez and Phoenix. Assault people are like Thunder and Fragger, which focus alot on the frontline and be a fragging machine. Recons are like the people who sit behind, which mainly consist of the snipers like Aimee and Vassili. Finally, the engineers are people who are very focused on repairing or planting, which is very useful, like Fletcher and Proxy.
Fourthly, the map pool is relatively fine enough to sustain the current playerbase which is quite small IMO. Each map has a style to it, as well as different objectives to them. There are currently 3 modes, Objective, Stopwatch and Execution. Objective is the standard gamemode, featuring stuff like EV Escort, Item Delivery and C4 Destruction, with the maps being Bridge (EV and Delivery), Trainyard (C4 and Delivery), Dome (Delivery and C4), Chapel (EV and Delivery), Terminal (C4) and Underground (C4). Stopwatch is basically objective mode but with both sides competing to see who can do it faster. Execution is like CS:GO or any plant and defuse game. It's maps consist of Market, Gallery and Overground.
The negative points about this game would be its small playerbase, which is very inevitable as it is not a very well reviewed game by people, as well as its failure to publicise very effectively. I have not seen too much publicity with the exception of Alienware,Logitech and Humble Bundle.
Hackers are also a main reason for the crapiness of this game, as the anti-cheat system is not as good as it was last time. They are working on it, which I feel that it would be a good thing.
SD (the company) also loves to release things without stuff like testing, (ahem crafting) but apart from that, setting up a test mode for veterans to review would be a great thing and benefit the game alot, like maybe for level 20+ and such.
Content updates are somewhat frequent, releasing things like new maps or bug fixes or nerfs and balances. They also hear out to the community alot, as you can see from their youtube channel, they recently addressed the new crafting system which was a flunk, and they are taking suggestions to make the best out of it.
Graphics wise, the game can be quite intensive, as I have to run at 1080p with a GT630 with toned down settings, which still make it playable at 60fps. However, for even lower settings, there are configs to make the game the most playable at the lowest settings.
Overall, this game is ok, but I only recommend to people who can take the time to learn the game, as well as have decent reflexes, if not you would only be demolished very hard and quit the game very fast.

I have always been a massive fan of the Age of Empires series but when I saw this advertised on steam a few years ago I knew I had to get it.
Alot of people are dissapointed with this game and annoyed that it is barely any different or that they had to pay £15 for it. Firstly I managed to get it on sale so it was just under £4 (bargain) and I dont think the lack of change is a problem at all. In my opinion I think this is a perfect release for the AOE series. People LOVED this game when it came out and I know I played it alot when I was younger which is why this version is perfect for me and anyone else who fell in love with the originial game. The slightly retouched graphics are barely noticable but the introduction of steamworks and steamworkshop allow for ease of access for multiplayer games and the chat commands have become engrossed in normal conversation once again. Especially the famous WOLOLO. The contributions by other users on steamworkshop increase the quality of the graphics and allow for newer ways of playing the game and changing the textures etc for nearly any effect.
The only downside to this game is the single player is exactly the same. For me this is fantastic as I enjoy replaying games however it provides no new challenges and this might be a downside for other players. In this case I would suggest only buying this game if you know other people to play it with. But for players like myself it is perfect for reliving old memories and playing a game which is still plenty of fun.

Smooth fluid gameplay, gorgeous graphics, and engaging story.... Rockstar's Max Payne 3 delivers a pulse-pounding, rewarding experience that just doesn't let up. Many detractors of the game tout the "endless" unskippable cutscenes. The cutscenes are there for a reason: to tell a story. And they blend seamlessly with the interspersed gunplay so you're not drawn out of the game, and instead, you are taken on a wild ride of constant gunfights, gripping story, and awesome visuals. What's not to like about that?
The gameplay of shooting and dodging work very well. Max ducks into cover, and the added mechanic of having your character go into a sudden death mode when you run out of health, if you have one or more pill bottles in reserve, means you get a second chance if you "die". And the slow motion bullet cams and death cams when you take down the last of a group of enemies is just cool as hell. The music is good, the environment (Brazil) is well-done, and the settings are well-thought-out and levels are very detailed.

The perfect mix of old-school and new-school FPS. Wolfenstein The New Order has a great story, great German voice actors, good character development and solid visuals. The shooting aspects are strong and the game flows well. Semi-linear with areas to explore, and collect gear/ammo/collectibles/etc.
The game features an interesting way of gaining skills, having to complete certain challenges that vary in difficulty which grant permenant perks throughout your playthrough.
There is no multiplayer, which could be seen as a plus, as they put all their work into creating the best single-player campaign they could possibly do.
Overall I am mega impressed by this game. If you were a fan of the older Wolfenstein games, this is a some-what-continuation of Return to Castle Wolfenstein, and Wolfenstein(2009) and I highly suggest you play The New Order! For newer fans who never experienced Wolfenstein, The New Order is still a great standalone title. You may not understand some of the smaller intricacies and minor character reunions but the game does well enough on it's own to explain that so you won't be left in the dark.

(Single-player review): This game has great gunplay, solid cover mechanics, and a pretty interesting storyline. "Hard" difficulty is somewhat challenging but very fair in the sense that dying is a consequence of your actions rather than a broken gameplay mechanic or situation. The in-game graphics are some of the best I've seen, largely due to the amount of detail that the developers put into the characters and environments. There's also a wide range of colors that's really refreshing to see after playing through the dull environments of Max Payne 1 and, to a lesser extent, Max Payne 2.
Nitpicks: I found the "pop-in, pop-out" text and "frame-overlays" that happen throughout the in-game cinematics to be a bit distracting. I liked the comic book panel effects but, while I understand that the developers were going for a unique visual style, it would have been nice if there was an option to turn off (or minimize) the effects. Also, it was slightly disappointing to see how much the story of Max Payne 3 strayed away from the stories of MP1 and MP2. Then again, MP3 does a great job at further developing Max’s character and there are several scenes in it that wouldn’t have had the same impact to a player who has not played through the first two games.
TL;DR Buy this if you like to shoot things and like a good story. Or not.

This is the perfect sequel to a game that was already amazing. Portal 2 adds so much depth in every possible way. The levels are expansive and evolves as you play. It creates an immersion that you could never experience in the original game. You really forget that you're playing a puzzle game as you work your way through the ever changing sections. The loading screens are still here but they are less obtusive. This dynamic design is by far the most notciable change in the game.
The puzzles themselves are far more involved, theres many new ways to approach levels including propulsion gel, lazers and so many more. This game starts with a very short tutorial so It's recommended that you start with Portal 1 first as the learning curve could be difficult before you can wrap your head around the mechanics. In this game portals take a back seat to the various other mechanics at work. Every solution is clever but the tests themselves always seem fair and understandable. If there is to be a fault it is only that the game uses all of these elements so much that you can sometimes forget to use portals normally and overthink the design.
Story, Characters, Soundtrack, Pacing and so much more has all being improved. Every element of the game is compelling until the very end. To say more is to spoil the suprise. Play this game and its prequel now. Every PC owner should experience these games at least once.

This is easily one of the best, nostalgic throwbacks to recently grace us.  In the myriad of brown, dusty, twitch "checkpoint" grinds, this title streaks unabashedly across the screens with brazen stylization and an unapologetic formulas from yester-year.  The mechanics are simple.  In fact they’re stupidly simple.  That's perfectly fine given that the brain-dead controls are a wholly organic experience of the tried and true stripe.  Armor pickups, med-kits, hidden areas and an honest boss fight.  Let me reiterate, “boss fight” everybody!
The level designs are linear, but hosted over generously sized maps that ooze with atmosphere.  The game receives zero complaints from me regarding the art choices elected by the development team.  It is truly impressive how each environment really grinds in the feeling of oppressive and fascist idealism.  It gets the cylinders of the imagination firing in quick order when you first set eyes around this alternate Berlin.
The best aspect of the game is effectively the gun-play.  Every weapon has a tangible "punch" to it, giving a inordinate amount of pleasure in the audio alone.  This is apparent as by late game, with a slew of choices available, the assault rifle was still my go-to choice for savaging the lurid schemes of the enemies.  There is just something about the rapid-fire deep thundering of the gun as it sprayed liquid-nazi across the walls in brilliant gore.
Unfortunately I noticed poor detection at points with item pickups, resulting in several frustrating deaths as badly needed med-kits refused to come into hand.  Another mild complaint lies in the grainy surface textures.  However, the pace and flow generally kept me from lingering long enough to really dwell on the "non-issue."  Other than a few mild gripes, I'd say a nasty point lies in a few moments in the game where the difficulty ramped inordinately high.  After several teeth-grinding affairs, I discovered that the oldest mantra of “shoot everything a lot" still holds merit.
The most pressing complaint I have is more of a personal disappointment than a proper criticism.  It lies in the plot's overall scope.  Don’t get me wrong, I loved the whole messy experience and was fully enthusiastic from start to finish.  But in a standard play-through, you can't shake the feeling that you're not seeing enough of the world’s story in the supporting cast.  It’s a rising desire to drive home the immersion in this nightmarish alternate universe that this fractured timeline creates.  You’re left guessing at the shadows cast by their assumed and inferred histories.  You frequently find yourself teased with a cast of characters who are interesting on the surface levels, but are left relatively unexplored.  It creates a frenetic and hazy canon that goes unpolished in the end.  Though this may have been intentional in the designs, in its practice it is most unfortunate as the reality created gives grand desire for the imagination to linger in.  In the event of a sequel, it would serve the plot’s narrative if it owned more fully realized personalities participating.
Given a few dirty blemishes, the title holds amazingly well.  It clings to older conventions in fps games, but it chooses to own them to the letter with stark confidence.  A solid length of gameplay mixed with numerous difficulty settings and collectibles offering new replay modes grants the player a good return on their investment.

Dirty Bomb is a fast-paced FPS, where you get to choose among different mercenaries to complete the given mission. If you have played Brink before, which is also developed by Splash Damage. You will find a very similar concept to their gameplay system, and style. However there's no tweakings of your guns attachments nor parkouring around the map. THere's double jump though on some platforms. It's still the classical FPS shooter game.
There's three mission gameplays, Objective, Stopwatch and Elimination. Objectives as the name mentioned, to complete multiple objectives in stages. This game is similar to like TF2 Payload, but here as protecting the EV and delivering the data. Stopwatch mainly works the same as Objective, just that both teams are swapped to compete between who completes the mission faster. So teamwork is still the key here. For Elimination just clearing of the opposing players till the team is wiped. The matchmaking system here can sometimes seems leveled, but the number of level capped servers are too little. Most of the servers are uncapped, so you will be playing with high level players as well.
What's so overwhelmingly positive about this game is that, the reward system benefits the non-P2W users. Each mercenaries comes like a card, with different rarity. Lead being the lowest, and Obsidian being the highest grade. Almost every round you have won, will entitle you with a card crate. That you can unlock them anytime to get cards! Unlike Payday2 or CS:GO, where you need keys to unlock them. However the downside is that sometimes you get a card where the mercenary has yet to be unlocked. You will need to use your credits to unlock them. Each mercenaries requires 50,000 credits, which can be earned every round you play. Crafting of the cards is also available, however it's advisable to do them in later stages. Each week 2 mercenaries will also be rotated for new players to try them out, similar to how Evolve has done their class rotation. In Dirty Bomb mercenaries are broken down into 5 main classes, Recon, Engineers, Fire Support, Medics and Assault. This hasn't been cleared mentioned in the game. So new players may not know how to choose their class wisely, resulting in bad teamwork.
For networking, there are servers in Asia, Russia, Europe, US, Australia. For Singapore players, you get around 40ms-55ms in those Asia servers, and are capped at 150ms. So you wouldn't get high-ping players in your team. Overall Splash Damage has did a good job in maintaining the servers.

IF YOU ALREADY KNOW WHAT THE GAME IS LIKE, BUT WANT AN OPINION ON THE "FREEMIUM" ASPECT OF THE GAME, PLEASE SCROLL DOWN TO THE NEXT ALL-CAPS TITLE
What is it?
A fast-paced, objective-based FPS. You work as a team, one team attacking while the other defends, to destroy, escort, repair, and deliver objectives across maps which react to the objectives you successfuly attack or defend. In the main game mode, Stopwatch, you will play 15-minutes maximum of either attacking or defending. Afterwards, the teams switch sides and the new attackers attempt to do better than the old ones.
There are quite a few different Mercenaries (classes) to choose from. You start with 2 Mercenaries permanently unlocked (one AOE medic and one ammo-supplying airstrike-calling assault gunner) and can unlock the rest for 50,000 in-game credits. As of this review at 67 hours, I have unlocked 2 additional mercenaries and am well on my way to a third, so there doesn't seem to be much grinding required to unlock the game's full potential. In addition to the Mercenaries you are given and those you unlock, each week provides you with 3 more Mercs who are willing to fight for you temporarily. This lets you test out new classes before purchasing them, a big win in my opinion.
In total, there are 3 game modes: Stopwatch (described above), Objective (the first half of Stopwatch mode, where the game is decided entirely by whether the defenders can successfully hold off the onslaught from the attackers), and Execution. Execution mode is a very simplistic FPS game mode where each player has only 1 life. An attacking team attempts to plant C4 on 1 of 2 objectives while the defenders try to stop them until the time expires or until an entire team lies dead.
During normal gameplay, players have infinite lives, but are restricted by "spawn waves". When reduced to zero health, you enter a bleedout mode in which you can do nothing but call for a medic. During this phase, the enemy can execute you to prevent reviving. Every 30 seconds, the dead players from your team can respawn at your spawn point (the two teams have staggered spawn timers). This results in a natural-feeling "waves of enemies to fight" mechanic. If that's not your thing then there you go, but I definitely enjoyed it. It seems to reinforce the teamwork focus in the game, allowing you to re-enter the fight alongside your friends (very useful if you are normally a support player like myself).
Different classes have access to different weapons (one medic can only have different SMGs and assault rifles, while a different medic has access to shotguns). They also allow you to enter the fight with ammo packs or resupply stations, medical stations, med-packs, a fancy REVIVR gun, air support, orbital strikes, grenades, sticky bombs, proximity mines, concussion grenades, incendiary grenades, a minigun, faster interaction speed with objectives, a grenade launcher, a turret, etc.
FREE-TO-PLAY/FREEMIUM
PLEASE READ THIS SECTION
The game is free. 100% free. You can unlock literally everything in the game for absolutely no money if you enjoy the game enough to keep playing (with the exception of some founder-exclusive items I've heard about, but apparently they are either entirely cosmetic or are unique class loadouts that are inferior to their Free-To-Earn counterparts). I have currently earned enough credits in-game to permanently unlock 2 Mercenaries, buy all of the Bronze-level loadouts (any loadout above Bronze level is purely a cosmetic change from a Bronze level loadout) for both of those Mercenaries, and have 33k of the 50k required for a third permanent unlock. This game is NOT pay-to-win.
THE RANDOM LOOT DROP OPINION
You cannot purchase specific loadouts for a Mercenary. You can, however, view all of the potential loadouts for that Mercenary (usually about 12, depending on the Mercenary, not including cosmetics) and proceed to "craft" cards for that Mercenary at a specific level (Bronze is the highest level not including cosmetics, and you can earn enough credits for a Bronze card in a single match). When you want, for example, the <x> loadout for Skyhammer, you can "recycle" any loadout cards you don't want (each earns *slightly* less than is required to craft a new one) and use the recycled materials to ask for a random <Bronze-level> card for <Skyhammer>. With only 12 potential Bronze level cards for that Mercenary, you'll have the one you want in about 2 hours of gameplay, maximum.
tl;dr
I thought this game would be a grind. It is not.
I thought this game would be pay2win. It is not.
I was worried about the Randon Loot aspect of the game. I should not have been.
Play Dirty Bomb. It's awesome. Be a medic, be a sniper, be an engineer, I don't care. You'll love it.

A game that has immersive lore and settles around the fact that the war on the planet Auraxis will last forever between 3 factions with unique playstyles. First the Terran Republic, sporting weapons with accelent accuracy and a high fire rate and boasts the fastest Lightning Tanks and Mosquito fighters in the game, their color represented by Black and Red and their tactics are fast versatility and high maneuverability. The New Conglomerate showing their prowess in the form of heavy hitting weaponry and higher armor with their soldiers, their Vanguard Tanks and Reaver Fighters, their tactic is to overpower their foes with overwhelming force, represented by the colors Blue and Yellow. The final faction resembling humans who follow the ancient alien way of life and use their plasma weapons and MagRider hover tanks and Scythe fighters to outmaneuver and outclass their foes represented by their colors of Purple and Teal.
You will witness massive battles, massive clutch victories, massive airdrops, massive troop swarms, and massive armor engagements. A game where dying is only part of the fun. A game where you can aid your squad, platoon, or even outfit to victory.
What faction do I play as? Why of course the Terran Republic, I favor high mobility and quick strikes into enemy lines with the TR's signature Mosquito Swarms, Battle Columns, MAX crashes, and Galaxy Drops. I'm part of the 382nd Terran Air Wing of the Emerald Server, the supreme outfit when it comes to Galaxy Drops, Mosquito Swarms, and the pure advantage of numbers to throw against our enemies.
I recommend this game to anyone who wants to be involved in total controlled chaos, willing to die for the faction that they pick. Which faction will you choose to get involved in the endless war of attrition?

I don't think you could possibly put forward a more tired or less interesting basis for a game in 2014 than "what if you shot Nazis...in a first person shooter game?" That's why I wasn't exaclty in a rush to get this when it came out, but the constant refrain from people saying "really, it's good, I'm not kidding" combined with the Steam sale made me jump on this, and let me add to the refrain: the developers must have had similar thoughts about how interesting that sounds to them too, and set out to make something that really elevates above the premise.
Aside from a shrug worthy "that exactly what I was expecting" first half hour or so, the writing is really suprisingly self aware of the absurdity of a Wolfenstien game in 2014 and has a lot of thoughtful, even touching moments with well developed characters and a great idea to raise the stakes and make things interesting: what if, instead of just fighting the Nazis in fantasty world war II...the Nazis just...won already? Seeing the impact of Nazi Germany take the cultural place America has in the last few decades goes in some suprisingly interesting directions, particulary one in game news article I found describing the nuking of New York that ended the war, and the proud justification of it as a means to save thousands more lives that a protracted land battle would have won. I never cared for that excuse for Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and to see it turned on its head here gives me hope that a few more might take that as food for thought on the subject. Of course, don't get too carried away into my praise of the story here and think this belongs shoulder to shoulder with Gone Home or Telltale's Walking Dead; this is a Nazi shoot 'em game after all; just a far more thoughtful one that you'd think going in.
The shooting is great, and it sucessfully integrates a "perks" system into single player, which is something I don't I've seen yet. The visuals are generally good, though there is that Rage engine pop in, and don't expect the big generational leap we're all hoping for from PS4-Xbone ports--it looks like another nicely done 360 to PC port.
It won't dethrone Half Life 2 as the FPS campagin to beat, but it may be the best one I've played since. It's not a revelation, but it is really, shockingly, solid all the way through. If you're in the mood for a good shoot 'em up and have had enough CoD style multiplayer to last you for years to come, thank you very much, you couldn't do much better than this.

What I've played through thus far has been like a grittier and dirtier Inglorious Basterds game where the allies ended up losing WWII. This game has just about everything you could ever ask for for the kind of game it is. It's a call back to the earlier games of the genre whilst incorporating a lot of the better elements of modern game design. The guns all have fairly different dynamics and give you a wide variety of ways of dealing with the obstacles in your path. The levels are very tight and ambushes are frequent. The game does an overall great job of rewarding various styles of play based on what you prefer to do. I've so far taken a style that's best described as "sneak up until you screw up" and it's been a fairly great ride. The plot at times feels a little flimsy, but I think it's just because there's a ton of nazis to burn/stab/shoot/blow your way through between plot sequences. Also while this may seem obvious, this game does not in any way, shape, form, or fashion shy away from depicting nazi imagery and ideology which may be disturbing to some players.

I haven't played too far into this game yet, but so far I quite enjoy it. The storyline is very interesting and gripping enough to keep you interested in going further into the game. I have read several reviews complaining about the lack of online PVP play, but this does not bother me at all. Personally, I prefer these types of games that put little to no emphasis on their online play. I'm from the old school, where games had to be well made and well written having a good long story to them instead of relying on just running around aimlessly shooting your friends after a 5 hour single player romp. Pure online games like Titanfall have lost their allure to me, the premise of them has changed very little since Counter Strike 1.5. A well done single player FPS game is refreshing to see, and I hope to see more games follow this pattern in the future. So far this game feels very much like an old school shooter with shiny graphics, which is purely awesome!
All that being said, it does have some downfalls in the form of bugginess and technical prolems. At times, spent shell casings will float in mid air, as well as some broken debris from walls and crates that get shot up. Texture popping is an issue at times too. I have yet to experience any screen tearing, which is a good thing. Another problem is the loading times. I am using a Western Digital 1 TB Black HDD which is pretty quick, and when I die, or a new level has to load, I'm stuck for 30 seconds to a minute sometimes. And then, when it does and I go back into it it lags for a few seconds as if it still is not fully loaded. Cutscenes also lag and perform quite badly at times with random stoppages every few seconds while my hard drive LED is lit solid, telling me my extremely fast HDD is somehow a bottleneck, for a cutscene of all things! Another issue I have come across is a sudden complete lack of any Anti Aliasing, and a degradation of texture filtering. This happens in cutscenes and occasinally at random points in a level. This does not take away form the ability to play the game, but it makes it look like a high end PS3 game. The GPU RAM usage is also quite high. The game is also able to ustilize all 8 threads of my CPU quite heavily.
In conclusion, I got the game on sale for $40, which I am happy with. Even at full cost though, this would be a worthy game!

I hadn't played a Wolfenstein game since Spear of Destiny and was a little curious about the series.
I couldn't help but compare Wolfenstein to Rage and Dishonored. Wolfenstein doesn't have the same out of this world environments that Rage has and it doesn't have the sort of moral choices that make a real difference in the outcome of the game like with Dishonored. Also, the perk system in Wolfenstein seemed more like it was meant to distract the player from how easy most of the game is by giving them a treat each time they stabbed someone just so a certain number of times. The perks really don't translate to adding a new method of playing the game, they give you more ammo, a little bit of health regeneration, occasionally you can dismember enemies, or something else like that. Its not like how different skills can drastically change how you play the game like with Dishonored. Another comparison that came to mind is to the Metro Series whose story line (and the "moral" choices you must make) interested me more and also had better stealth versus run and gun gameplay styles than Wolfenstein (again imo). I guess overall I felt like Wolfenstein combined a lot of popular game elements I'd seen in other games I liked but didn't do any of them nearly as well.
However, Wolfenstein does have a gripping story that made me care about the characters. I got hit in the feels a few times when **** went down with a main character and the storytelling cutscenes are amazing. It also made me think I was playing a sort of messed up version of Uncharted. The game took me 18 hours to beat which I did in one sitting netting 65% completion. I played in on Uber difficulty for the entire game except the last boss which I had to reduce the difficulty to hurt me plenty for. So I guess despite all the things Wolfenstein wasn't, it's still a solid title that was worth purchasing at 50% off during the steam sale. It definitely passes the "movie test" (is it as much or more fun than a movie for as much or less than the cost of a movie per hour?). So I have no regrets except that I didn't unlock the explosives perk tree because I stealthed almost the entire god damned game even when I didn't have to.

Planetside 2 is maybe interesting and fun for a hour; then it goes down hill. The game was great upon launch when there was minimal microtransactions as well as less people wearing outlandish cosmetics that make the battlefield look like a circus. On top of this, SOE loves to engineer obsolescence, as soon as you purchase a nice gun with station cash a month later an update comes that reduces it in power, and adds a "better" gun on the market to funnel in buyers. This on top of a widely immature community leaves this something to be desired for the more serious gamers who come home from work looking for actual teamwork vs. the rubbish they have to put up with at their office.
That inference aside, the graphics are decent, but the game limits your FOV which makes you feel like you are playing a console game, thus making it hard to enjoy when you have to max out your mouse sensitivity so you can constantly look around you like some paranoid schitzophrenic. While I do admire the game's idea for encouraging teamwork, it just doesn't end up being that kind of encouragment. People stampede over one another to be the one who gets the objective bonus.
There are way too many guns on the market which most are completely impractical for a sci-fi battlefield style game. You would think in the future guns would be very limited in variety as a few guns could accomplish much more in the future, but instead it is treated like a flashy modern warfare game. I honestly wished this game was subscription-based or pay once; because then we wouldn't have a market with all this useless junk. The vehicles are fun to operate, such as the aircraft and tanks, but the tanks are weak because in the early days of the game, players cried all the time like whiney COD players that they kept getting killed easily when they bunny-hopped in front of a 20 ton armored vehicle with a giant cannon on it.
SOE, having the reasonable PR that they have, listened to all the whiners like they have done for so many years (RIP SWG); and now we have another game that started with good ambitions but failed with too much commercialization and unsuspecting players. Free-to-play attracts all sorts of people, including a bunch of people on a new generation that don't appreciate the team-oriented warfare in the same way that players did many years ago. Call me an old geezer, but you can't deny the faults at play here, it is a cookie cutter FPS.
Planetside 1 was better I argue, but of course that was molested by SOE as well back when they introduced the BFR and then nerfed the hell out of them to accompany the massive whining; thus making giant mecha-style war machines more vulnerable than a light APC.. Some developers just need to care less about the whiners and let the community sort itself out; but the thing is; when you have a microtransaction system with a wide emphasis on for-profit, you automatically erode the quality of the game as you betray many people to keep others who might be a temporary but larger demographic.
Overall:
Visuals: 7/10 (Decent lighting, textures, etc; poor FOV and too many cosmetics that looks cheesy like TF2.)
Audio: 6/10 (Some sound effects are too quiet, like certain rifles from 50 meters away.)
Controls: 9/10 (Boiler plate configuration for mouse, keyboard, etc. Lack of a reliable head-bob in flying aircraft.)
Gameplay: 4/10 (Team work isn't for the team, it is for the extra XP and rewards.)
Community: 3/10 (Too many immature gamers, too many whiners who just couldn't adapt to the game's style.)
Balance: 2/10 (The balance makes no sense, and is done on the account of some of the worst gamers you could play with.)
Maps: 9/10 (The geography was greatly executed, the terrain has a good variety of steep hills, canyons, flatlands and ravines. Facilities have interesting architecture.)
Artistic Style: 6/10 (I would have given this a high rating if it weren't for the completely obnoxious variety of vehicle ornaments, decals, camoflauges that have more colors then art seen in drug culture and the many cosmetics that accompany the players.)
Since the game is F2P, I say: Give it a try and see if you like it or not; not everyone will agree with my lengthy review but this is my opinion and I am sure I share this same view with many other players.

Max Payne 3 is a third person shooter by Rockstar Games, the same people who brought us the GTA series. I must say that they did a great job with this game and I feel that it was ported nicely on the PC. The gameplay felt smooth and never gave me many issues, though the cover system did screw me up sometimes, so I'm not a big fan of it. One of the main gameplay mechanics in this game is the bullet time effect. This is where you jump and move slowly while you shoot enemies. I didn't really use this in the game that much, except the times where it would automatically happen during the story. This game is pretty difficult, even on easy and normal modes, so if you like a challenge, you will like this game. I found it interesting how the game didn't use a life bar, but a damage meter that would fill up as you take damage. You had to take painkillers to reduce the meter, which is also interesting. The audio was great, and some of the music used was also great. The graphics were good and I only noticed a couple tiny graphic issues.
My main complaints with this game would be it's cover system and Rockstar making us have a Social Club account just to play. I had moments where I couldn't start the game because the Social Club login would screw up, making the game not start. I have looked in the forums and saw that this was a common issue, which is not a good thing. I feel that Rockstar should make Social Club an optional thing that people could sign up for. The game did cause Windows to completely crash, but that could have been a problem with Windows and not this game. Towards the end of my playthrough, I had issues where i couldn't exit the game properly. I had to keep using the task manager just to exit the game, which is tedious and annoying. Overall, I'd give this game an 7.5/10.

Okay after playing a lot and seeing how those "hardcore fan" people hated this game, I gotta say this game is wonderful. Setting asside the bugs and crashes which made the game a nightmare for me I decided to go with dx9 then enjoyed it to the fullest. As a "hardcore MP fan" I think this game was absolutely fantastic.
The story, although really irrelevant and felt forced after the first two since story has nothing to do with Max Payne and Max Payne 2 besides the Max himself being the protagonist, still felt like Max Payne but a different Max Payne. They have managed the keep Max as himself while abandoning the all noir atmosphere the first two have. Max is the same Max we know except just a bit more old and a little tired. Great one liners and scenes along with a different yet Max Payne like story telling was really well done.
Gameplay aspect is a little different because Max can only carry one big weapon along with two one-handed guns such as Uzi-type smgs or his signature pistols. When you go for the akimbo he drops the big gone completely too. The Max Payne we know carried the whole arsenal with him and you had to plan your strategy for every part of every level. Also gameplay felt MORE linear since most of the time you cannot go back and take that painkiller you left there when needed. Cutscenes are much more frequent. Also unique events such as going down a crane while shooting the bad guys in slow mo or a motor boat chase while shooting on the run type of events didn't exist in MP1 and MP2. They were fun tho.
Multiplayer was really good if you ask me. I bought the game from a sale so when I started there were few people left still playing so I don't think you will get a decent match after all this time. It was a great experience tho. However it would be better if they completely abandoned multiplayer and made the single player longer just like first two.
Also I want to add this: Max Payne in Max Payne 3 is one of the most ALIVE characters I've ever seen. His memories, his emotions, his monologues, his interactions with others, his behaviour, his lines and speeches EVERYTHING about him feels really alive and natural. Other characters are also like that in this game so I congratulate Rockstar for this. Most games today lack personalities.

Planetside 2 is absolute mayhem when it isn't an absolute snore-fest. I had never really played an MMO before, nor had I played PS1 ever. My group of friends were looking to find a new game we could all play socially and Tribes: Ascend never really satisfied the itch.
PS2 offers a ton of content, a lot of absolutely memorable experiences, and beautiful visuals provided you have a beefy enough rig to run half of it. PS2 is a tehcnical marvel in that 500+ player battles in a small area haven't really been done in the past, so the expectation for optimization would be nice, but unlikely.
There are other games that do infantry combat better, or tank versus tank combat better, or aircraft dogfighting better, but few games combine all three into the madness of a continent-sized king of the hill game. PS2 excels with a solid commanding unit that strategizes well, otherwise you could find yourself deployed into a random patch of desert with no one around for miles, or into a chaos pit of destruction where you can't move without being killed.
Some of the most exciting moments are when you are storming a stronghold with a few seconds left, pushing an enemy force out and running on foot over hills as aircraft fly overhead and tanks roll alongside your charging unit. There are few games where it really feels like you're in an epic future-war on alien worlds.
PS2 has its ups and downs, but I think the ups outweigh the downs. You really can't go wrong with the price of "free". The best way to play is to join a familiar group that you work well with. If you're just testing with friends, you can jump into the Public Test Server, which is almost always empty, and test things out there until you're ready for the real fight.

TL:DR AT THE BOTTOM!!!
In-Depth Version:
Although at first I did rate this game up, it is now a definite downsider to me. Not only are specific factions overpowered (Terran Republic's STARTING rifle takes 3 shots to kill someone, NC's starting AND SMG that I bought from their horribly grindish store were all 5-9 shot kills) but this game has every CoD-like aspect in it to make you want to throw the game away and move on to something more intense and punishing/rewarding like Red Orchestra 2.
Yes, this game IS an MMO shooter. A real MMO shooter. There are thousands of REAL players on your screen at once fighting, and though it does completely destroy your CPU (even with my up-to-date computer with more than decent specs) its still playable and fun in some ways. But having to shoot someone 6 times with a rifle to kill them while 20 people are firing at you (not to mention the guy you're shooting at is running away at lightning speed so you'll NEVER hit him) is not fun. Also getting randomly 1 hit killed by a Tank or AT Gun from hell knows where is not very fun. On top of that though, shooting someone with a massive bolt-action Sniper rifle that shoots a round the size of your foot and not killing him after hitting him 4 ♥♥♥♥ING TIMES is not fun. This game, though fun in its rare moments, is generally speaking not fun. It's frusturating and feels more like a chore than anything else.
It has a lot of potentional but is recieving criticism on people who shouldn't be giving it. People who play games such as CoD or Battlefield, but want some stupid overpowered game mechanics (like the MAX robots who have triple health) or ♥♥♥♥♥♥, borderline Pay-To-Win guns to make them feel like the couple extra bucks they made at work today was worth it. A game like this is good in theory but only should stick to certain formulas, such as CoD crack hype style where you can kill someone with at max 5 shots, or Red Orchestra realism style where if you're hit you're out cold. This in between ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t is and will ruin this game from now until its inevitable closing.
So to conclude, should you try Planetside 2? Sure. Will you have fun for most of the time you play it? Probably not. Is it cool to just kinda see? Yes. And is it fixable? That's if Daybreak stops their♥♥♥♥♥♥and stops listening to a bunch of idiots who know nothing of game designing.
TL:DR version: 4/10, not a complete dumpster but still trash in most areas.

i actually stopped playing the steam client and have used the fj client for quite awhile now. so i have many, many, many more hours than represented here. definitely would be considered a vet in-game.
just to be clear...rc is not p2w. players who pay money, do not get an advantage in battle over someone who plays for free. rc is a rare breed in many aspects, this is just one of them.
so simply put, this is an awesome game. in a voxel environment, you build robots from scratch then battle other robots in your choice of play modes. you can also sell the bots you build to other players, in the store known as the crf.
recently updates have been released that massively improved the game. rc is still in alpha, so it does have issues. however, i believe the devs are making great progress in overcoming these hurdles and soon this amazingly addictive game will be bug-free.  once stable and out of alpha, i predict rc to have profound impact on the gaming community. not only is it one of a kind...it's great fun too.
my advice to new players...
1 get premium (so worth it and really is one of the cheapest games out there)
2 using your robits (in-game currency) buy a fj bot from the crf
3 play some rounds in the bot
4 open the bot up in edit mode and look at how it was built (rc is all about connection points, damage is distributed through connecting cubes)
5 alter the bot to fix any weakness you've noticed or change the weapons up...play with it
6 lather
7 rinse
8 repeat
also now in the settings menu, there's options to display advanced info when building (center of mass, armor, shields, weight, etc) and this really helps when building. check out the info on your fj bot and use the cpu usage as a goal when you start building your own. one last thing....bloated goats float on boats :) clans are coming soon \o/

Yes, this game IS an MMO shooter. A real MMO shooter. There are thousands of REAL players on your screen at once fighting, and though it does completely destroy your CPU (even with my up-to-date computer with more than decent specs) its still playable and fun in some ways. But having to shoot someone 6 times with a rifle to kill them while 20 people are firing at you (not to mention the guy you're shooting at is running away at lightning speed so you'll NEVER hit him) is not fun. Also getting randomly 1 hit killed by a Tank or AT Gun from hell knows where is not very fun. On top of that though, shooting someone with a massive bolt-action Sniper rifle that shoots a round the size of your foot and not killing him after hitting him 4 ♥♥♥♥ING TIMES is not fun. This game, though fun in its rare moments, is generally speaking not fun. It's frusturating and feels more like a chore than anything else.
It has a lot of potentional but is recieving criticism on people who shouldn't be giving it. People who play games such as CoD or Battlefield, but want some stupid overpowered game mechanics (like the MAX robots who have triple health) or ♥♥♥♥♥♥, borderline Pay-To-Win guns to make them feel like the couple extra bucks they made at work today was worth it. A game like this is good in theory but only should stick to certain formulas, such as CoD crack hype style where you can kill someone with at max 5 shots, or Red Orchestra realism style where if you're hit you're out cold. This in between ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t is and will ruin this game from now until its inevitable closing.
So to conclude, should you try Planetside 2? Sure. Will you have fun for most of the time you play it? Probably not. Is it cool to just kinda see? Yes. And is it fixable? That's if Daybreak stops their♥♥♥♥♥♥and stops listening to a bunch of idiots who know nothing of game designing.

Is it a true Max Payne game? I suppose.
Is it the Max Payne game we wanted? Not exactly, but it's a different take on a franchise with refreshingly new locations.
I was a huge fan of Max Payne 1 and 2, and this game doesn't really feel like a sequel to these games, it's rather a spin off. The story, Max's voice over, and the gunplay are there, but put all together some things are pretty anooying. There are way too many cutscenes that interrupt the action that cannot be skipped for the most part. As for the cutscenes themselves, Rockstar really went to down with the visual effects and "noise" filters.
When you do get to shoot people, it's very enjoyable, but these action moments are so much shorter than previous Max Payne games. You get maybe 2-3 minutes of shooting before a cutscene is shoved in your face.
The graphics and the game engine itself are amazing. The way Max moves and the way rolls around different based on what guns he is carrying is not something I remember seeing in other games to such an extent.
Regardless, it's still a really great game that you should play if you're a fan or not of the series. If you like shooting people in slow motion while dodging bullets, then you'll probably like it. Get it and play it if you see it on a Steam sale.
Do not pick up the season pass though, as it's only multiplayer content which is barely played besides the maps from the stock game, so it's not really worth it in my experience.

Portal 2 is an amazing sequal to Portal. It has it all: Plenty of puzzles, a good story, good graphics, good dialog, good characters, and more. The puzzles really make you think, and the game is much longer than the previous. I enjoy building my own test chambers in the editor, and am learning how to use Hammer to make more advanced levels. Fantastic gunplay, gameplay, controls and mechanics. You could take away the entire storyline and level design and leave just the bare gameplay and this would still be worth a good few hours of your time. The UBER difficulty (the hardest one available for your first playthrough) starts off feeling easy, though I am confident this is just the game making the first level intentionally easy to get you started, as immidiately after it the game feels MUCH more difficult. It is definitely a fair difficulty though as the game provides you with all the tools you need to keep from getting annihilated by the very accurate and very damaging nazi gunfire. The lean system in this game is probably the best I've ever seen excluding the overly complex one in ArmA 3, with Wolfenstein's being loads more accessible.
Even with all that gameplay goodness the devs still saw fit to give you arguably one of the best stories any shooter has had in quite some time. This is said having played about halfway through ONE of the TWO alternate timelines that look to change a fair bit of the story as well, and you should be able to see above just how many hours that has run me (no padding there either apart from time spent solving collectable puzzles and tweaking graphical settings). I will of course update this review if they somehow ♥♥♥♥ the pooch in the third act or something.
Visually the game is lovely in terms of its aesthetic, with incredible looking characters and creatures for you to shoot, and environments for you to splatter with their blood. The only real complaint I have with the graphical fidelity is that a fair number of textures are low res, but really this only stood out to me at a glance in less than a handful of instances. Otherwise all the other times I noticed it I was actively looking close up at objects you would otherwise pass by in normal play of the game.
Overall this has been one of the most enjoyable shooters I have played in quite a long time. It really takes a lot for a single player experience to captivate me enough to want to play it all the way through in consecutive sessions, and I can honestly see myself doing so with this game.

This game has some serious problems. But let's start by saying something positive:
+ Gameplay is fine. Shooting works really well and bullet time is fun and very cool.
+ Max Payne's voice actor is still one of my all time favourites, and I actually like many parts of the dialog
+ Multiplayer was surprisingly fun, but I still didn't play it for long.
The bad, here we go:
- Mandatory Rockstar Social Club. Seriously, why!? I can understand it for the multiplayer, but why can't I even play the single player without making an account? Isn't Steam DRM enough?
- This game has WAY TOO MUCH cutscenes. Prepare to get interrupted all the time! It's really horrible. See a door? You can be sure there is a cutscene as you open it. Every freakin' time. Don't get me wrong, I like many story-heavy games, but the way this game does it simply does not work. And there are a lot of unskippable scenes as well, ruining the replay value. Please, you can have 1 hour long cutscene if you want but don't put those short cutscenes after every corner! In this regard, this game is an absolute mess and this is the worst part of the game. How sad, as like I said, the gameplay and shooting actually work well. Taking control away from the player constantly just doesn't make a good gameplay.
Even if you skip all the cutscenes you can, you will still be watching them a lot. Because so much of that is unskippable.
-The general feeling that the player is not in control of anything.. The game is also extremely linear. Which is usually acceptable for more story driven games, but all the time I just feel that the player has absolutely no freedom in doing anything. Usually you have 1-3 weapons you can find in an area and every player will solve the levels in exactly same way. Even if you THINK about making even small exploring and looking at the area you are in, Max will instantly start saying things like "I had no time to lose, I had to go forward" repeatedly until you go forward.
- Overly grim dark tone. All Max does in cutcenes is drink booze and etc. I could not care less about the story in this game.
- The screen is constantly flickering and distorting. No, it's not a glitch, it's this game's way of storytelling and simulating how Max is always drunk or hangover during gameplay. But it only gave me headache. I am not even joking.
- DLC for the multiplayer mode kinda ruins it for those who aren't going to buy everything.
Max Payne 3 is a great example of how a game can have a good gameplay, but everything else does its best to ruin the experience. This game represents some of the worst sides of a modern video gaming, this is a direction I don't like.
My bottom line is that it might still be worth one playtrough if you are a fan of the series, but I say that very carefully for the reasons listed above. It still gets a thumbs down for me.

Damn this game has changed over the last couple of months. Where do I even start? 2 new map, 2 new maps,new menu,casual matchmaking and ranked has arrived. The move away from Nexon is the best decision SD has ever done. They are bringing up so much content in so little time that I cant even keep up sometimes. Its just amazing. The core of this game is amazing, the graphics and style of the game still amazes me still and when you get good at the game and consistanly get headshots,aces,godlikes you feel so good. The maps are well designed with a clear objectives, the maps ususall flow quite well and overal just fun to play on. Im even having fun on Dome which is very interesting and different now.
Now I love this game to bits but this game can some times get annoying very fast. Weapon balance needs to come. Shotguns are OP,burt rifles are OP, Javelin is OP,Thunder is still OP even after sevaral 'balanced' changes. SD needs to realise what is OP and what isnt. Javelins rocket insta gibing is a bit ridiculous at times and with Javelins new ammo generater you hardly ever need to go to ammo stations or ammo packs because Jav produces so much ammo that the rest of the fire supports hardly ever need to use their ammo abilities anymore.

The amount of times that I have lost 25% or even 30% sometimes when we lost and a person from our team left is not fair.
This game has gone a long way since the break from Nexon and Im very happy with the result even though SD needs to realise what needs to change and instead of bringing out new content it needs to fix their current content to make sure that everything is fixed and good which tbh its not. Anticipating the brainless, blast-fest stereotype usually associated with first person shooters, I wasn't really expecting much from Wolfenstein TNO. How wrong I was!! WTNO is an excellent game which successfully grafts some sneaky, stealth elements onto the usual bullet chucking, grenade lobbing, machine-gun toting antics we've come to associate with the genre. It also came as a bit of a surprise to me, given the series' previous attempts at narrative, that the developers have really gone to town in seeking to create a story and characters that are worth following. As you gradually uncover their tragic backstories, you actually come to care what happens to B.J. Blaskowitz and his rag-tag gang of companions. That said, the world in which WTNO takes place is a bleak one, where tragic stories tend not to have warm, fuzzy endings, so don't get too attached. Also, WTNO plays out some sickeningly grim imagary at times - that 18 certificate is not just for show boys and girls - a strong stomach is advised.

Overall, I thought it was an excellent shooter in both mechanics and narrative, and a good romp all the way through. Killing nazis, it turns out, can be at turns somber and viscerally satisfying. I would note that I haven't played any of the other ones, so there is that.
Mechanically, the various guns display their specific roles quite well, from takedowns and stealth pistols to dual-wielding assault rfiles (that later can also turn into rocket launchers) and laserguns. The perk system is also well implemented, rewarding specific types of gameplay but never forcing you into one or the other, and doing so without forcing the player to 'farm' for achievements or unlocks. This ties into the level design, which does a fairly good job of allowing players to choose between stealth and assault (à la Deus Ex).
Storywise, there's some surprising emotional depth to what I, at least, thought would be a pretty straightforward FPS; they treat the characters well and take care to develop them enough that you genuinely do care about them. Your friends are good but battered, your enemies are evil but often multi-dimensionally so. The world is not just one of desert greys, which is also a nice change.
I'd recommend it - maybe not at $60, because it's a touch short, but it's a good entry into the library of modern FPSes.

Okee Dokee, time to write a review to a game I've quite recently been enjoying!
Dirty Bomb, the free shooter made by awesome company Splash Damage. Now before you go on about how I am going to be over favoring the Pros vs the Cons, I will try and be as biast as I can, and convince new players looking for reasons to play this game, and must I say here, it isn't easy getting into this game. At times you will find yourself annoyed by players, bugs, and many other problems. I remind you here, this game is still in beta, and making a game isn't as easy as spreading peanut butter on your bread (or chest you decide.)
Lets start with bad news first, THE CONS
RANKED MATCHMAKING - Ahhh ranked... a casual 5v5 stopwatch game. Now you must be wondering, why the hell are you including ranked in the cons? Well to put it, most new players will most likely quit playing ranked (or the game all together) as ranked balancing isn't the greatest in this game, and if a teamate leaves the game early, well, You're screwed. I've been in multiple games where players will leave early, hurting mine, and anyone who is left ranks. Even though ranked is a fun gamemode to play, it is not for new players. (and yes, I know ranked is in alpha stages and they're improving each day, I'm just expressing what I've experinced during ranked.)
PLAYER RETENTION - I'll just leave this here -
MERC COST - God damn, I didn't want to put this here. Well the only reason why I am putting this here is the cost of the mercs and the 30k credit bonus at level 3-5 (I forgot :D) Yes, some mercs cost 30000 but at the same time, people will just spend the 30k on cases and end up with nothing, *cough cough* player rentention *cough cough*
MAP SELECTION - Now, yes I know Dockyard is coming in a few weeks but I haven't seen a new map implemented into Dirty Bomb since I started playing, which was about May - June last year. Now the map selection isn't terrible, it just gets dry playing Chapel and Bridge (which are awesome maps) non-stop.
Alright, now you must be thinking why the hell did I still give this game a thumbs up? Well, here is the PROS
LOADOUT CARDS / MERCS - Splash Damage said themselfs, that cards over Bronze don't give any sort of advantage, so basically all that time you spent trying to get a cobalt card was all wasted. (he he he...) But I do like how every card has something different about them, from weapons to skins. (and you aren't using your Moms credit cards to buy cases and keys so you can get a knife)
GAMEMODES - Objective, the main gamemode you will be playing, where there is 1 round and a solid 7v7 or 8v8 team. You will most likely always have a full team playing this gamemode.
Stopwatch, 2 rounds, 7v7 and 8v8, basically ranked except more players and auto refilling team. (I may be inaccurate about the player count, I haven't played much stopwatch out of ranked.)
Execution - (UPDATE) Well I have now played the gamemode, and it is pretty good.
SPLASH DAMAGE THEMSELVES - Well I've only got to play with a couple of SD members, they have always been quite nice and polite, and never abused their powers. They also really care about the community, from the dev videos to implementing better anticheats for their community, shows some dedication!
COMMUNITY - Wow, I'd never thought I'd be saying this, the community would have to be part of the PROS list, but hey! Here they are! Coming from playing COD and CSGO to Dirty Bomb felt quite refreshing! No, well a few but not as many unhappy people and trolls as COD and CSGO.
ANTI CHEAT - Jesus, I haven't seen a cheater since EasyAntiCheat was implemented. It shows that Splash Damage has a care for their community, and doesn't want it ruled by moders and hackers.
Well I really do enjoy this game, and I would really recommend it. It is an underground shooter that is really well developed, really well cared about, and Stoker is ♥♥♥♥ing sexy.
If you are a numbers guy or gal, this game would be a 7.5/10, still many features and doo dads coming in the future, so this may change.
Thanks for reading!

Have you ever seen Dog Soldiers?  Let me tell you about Dog Soldiers.  It's a movie about these British soldiers who go on a field exercise somewhere in Scotland where it turns out they were sent there to be killed by werewolves. They hole up in a farmhouse and do their best to fend off monsters and find a way out of their predicament.  The thing is, it's a ridiculous movie that everybody involved in did their very best to do well.  It was a movie with a silly premise and a low budget where everybody gave 110% and the writing was way better than the premise deserved, but it ended up being really good for no apparent reason.  Wolfenstein is kind of like that.  Instead of half-assing a really silly story, they just double down and try to figure out "How do we make an alternate history story about super-science Nazis winning WW2 and a catatonic U.S. Ranger fighting them 15 years afterwords be worth doing?"  Hell if I know how, but they pulled it off.
This game is a lot more fun and engaging than its premise has any right to be.  Wolfenstein should not be as good as it is.

Wolfenstein: The New Order has to be thee best FPS I've played to date and that's saying a lot from me.  I've played them ever since the first FPS that ever came out under the same name and over the years I've gotten burned out from playing them.  They started to lose their appeal well over 5+ years ago and they all had the exact same thing going for them save a few titles.  I put down the genre for about 5 years now and I'm glad I looked into this one.  The trailers had me hooked and I usually don't pay full price for a game and usually wait until it's on sale, but I had to try this one out as it looked to have way more depth than any of them I've played so far.  Of course I'd be happy paying less than $60 for a game, but for me at least, this game was worth the money.  I've gone through the story once so far and I plan on going back trough it again to see what I've missed.  The game's timing felt well pacedand ended with enough play time in between.  I'm the kind of person that gets turned off if the game drags on for too long and this one felt long enough, not too short, not too long.  The AI is very well put together and at times it feels like a real challenge to get through.  I will caveat that I played this on the difficult mode, not Uber, which will be my next run through.  There were plenty of frustrating moments that felt like it was impossible, but once I finally made it past the almost hopeless challenge of getting bombarded with heavy armament, I felt victorius.  Wolfenstein never had much going for it when it came to story, and that's completely the truth for its first few iterations, however this time around I felt involved, intruigued and wanted to know all I could about the hero and his companions.  I would definitely recommend this title to anyone who even just likes FPS's as this one feels fresh, keeps you hooked with its story and definitely pays off in the end when you get to murder every last one of the Nazi scum.   I commend every developer, storywriter, artist, director and producer that provided such a fantastic piece of art.  Job well done to all!

Top tier gameplay, second to none.

Pros:
- great community
- teamplay on a big scale (48 player per platoon, divided in 4 squads)
- hundreds of players fighting at a time
- scifi things (lasers, energy shields, teleporting, flying tanks, ...)
- three more or less well balanced factions with specific adv./disadv.
- huge, beautiful maps (depending on settings of course)
- communication with developers
- a nice "culture" with fan art, YT-videos (check out Wrel or Moukass) and stuff
- free to play, with no pay to win (though some cool features if you pay)
Cons:
- no hard mode (you always have minimap, spotting, crosshair, lots of health)
- requires teamplay and some people who want to organize stuff to be fun (most people join an "outfit", i.e. a team)
- not such a good "shotter feeling" as in e.g. BF (often death feels not fair or the cause is not clear, hit detection sometimes feels buggy, but maybe it's just me)
- kinda buggy depending on what the update does (spawning below ground, server crash, people instant teleporting, game puts you where it wants you to be, immortal players, ...)
- incentive for random players to do teamplay / play objective is an ongoing topic, as people often just♥♥♥♥♥♥around being of no use. it's being worked on though
All in all a great game I had and still have a lot of fun with. You get to know cool people if you join an outfit, which makes the whole thing even better and let's you mostly forget the downsides completely.

Wolfenstein: The New Order has to be thee best FPS I've played to date and that's saying a lot from me.  I've played them ever since the first FPS that ever came out under the same name and over the years I've gotten burned out from playing them.  They started to lose their appeal well over 5+ years ago and they all had the exact same thing going for them save a few titles.  I put down the genre for about 5 years now and I'm glad I looked into this one.  The trailers had me hooked and I usually don't pay full price for a game and usually wait until it's on sale, but I had to try this one out as it looked to have way more depth than any of them I've played so far.  Of course I'd be happy paying less than $60 for a game, but for me at least, this game was worth the money.  I've gone through the story once so far and I plan on going back trough it again to see what I've missed.  The game's timing felt well pacedand ended with enough play time in between.  I'm the kind of person that gets turned off if the game drags on for too long and this one felt long enough, not too short, not too long.  The AI is very well put together and at times it feels like a real challenge to get through.  I will caveat that I played this on the difficult mode, not Uber, which will be my next run through.  There were plenty of frustrating moments that felt like it was impossible, but once I finally made it past the almost hopeless challenge of getting bombarded with heavy armament, I felt victorius.  Wolfenstein never had much going for it when it came to story, and that's completely the truth for its first few iterations, however this time around I felt involved, intruigued and wanted to know all I could about the hero and his companions.  I would definitely recommend this title to anyone who even just likes FPS's as this one feels fresh, keeps you hooked with its story and definitely pays off in the end when you get to murder every last one of the Nazi scum.   I commend every developer, storywriter, artist, director and producer that provided such a fantastic piece of art.  Job well done to all!
