I enjoyed Max Payne 3. It is a big departure from the first 2 games in the series. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but it's hard to give it an unconditional recommendation. It has a decent story (for a game), impressive visuals, and good cover-based gunfighting gameplay with the familiar bullet time mechanic. Some of the set piece battles are quite impressive and most of the gunfights are engaging. There are a couple of bad vehicle combat scenes which I just hate in general but they are few and far between. My biggest pet peeve though are the constant in-engine cutscenes that are constant throughout. I appreciate the attempt to inject story but it really distracts from the gameplay. Also, the constant post-effect-color-blur-flare thing gets annoying very quickly. I think it's supposed to show you how hung over Max always is but maybe actually giving the player a headache was the wrong way to go about it. Anyway in summary it's a relatively short but well put together action game with a few flaws but if you're a fan of the first 2 it's probably worth playing if you can get it on sale.

This is an old RTS-classic. Even after 15 years people still play it, and I know why.

Pro:
- Fun campaigns (FE campaigns are quite difficult though)
- Fluent gameplay
- 'Improved' visuals (even though it's not a big difference)
- Multiplayer lobbies (both HD and FE or joined together now)
- Mod workshop (after big update) is user friendly
Con:
- It's pretty much the same version, but with better visuals. 20 dollars isn't really worth it. I recommend buying it during Steam sales.
- Moonwalking soldiers when patrolling
- Lag on Steam platform (more often than on Voobly platform)

Oddly enough, this game is still fun to play to this day. However, as the RTS genre keeps growing and behemoths like Starcraft 2 exists soley for the purpose of destroying the competition of other RTSes out there, I don't know if I should acutally recommend this game. The only reason I am is because it's still a good game, but there are a few misleading features we need to talk about first.
Firstly this game is technically HD, but only because it supports 1080p resolution, the sprites, animations and environments haven't been updated at all and even the best workshop mods don't help out much, the variety of civilizations you can choose to play as gives the game a while lot of different play styles, but if you don't know exactly what each diffeence between the different civs means it will lead any newcomers to failure, also the game still stutters at times, even on my monster rig regardless of whether I play online or not... it's not very good.
The reason I wouldn't recommend this game is because it came out in 1999 and, despite the amount of work that could have gone into the game to make changes for the better and make it one of the hottest RPGs of today, all they did was update the resolution and compatability, a huge let down.
It's a good game for LAN parties for people who remember playing the game when they were twelve or so, not so much as of today.
You know what, I've changed my mind, I can't recommend this to anyone, except the nostalgic blind. There are much better RTSes out now and this one was more of a cash grab than it was the celebration of one of the best RTSes of all time by bringing it up to speed with what we've come to expect from an RTS of today.

Planetside 2 is an amazing game with the largest battles that I have ever seen in my history of gaming. There are 3 unique factions, each with different weapons and vehicles. The game has a huge map with four different continents. I love this game and it is a great free to play game.

These days there are not a lot of good FPS games, that get the singleplayer right. They tend to focus on multiplayer of which usually the player base dies within the first month as players are confused as to whether they are playing a part of a story or a deathmatch. By ignoring multiplayer altogether ID has produced a gem of epic proportions.
Within the first few minutes you are treated to an intro played out and not merely watched. With characters you relate to, the game gives you choices that affect those relationships. And if you allow it you feel as the protagonist does. Your hatred towards the Nazi's in this alternate timeline grows more and more. When a game can immerse you not just visually but mentally too then you have a winner.
Now how does it play. Well here we have a classic style gameplay method mixed with modern effects. Like old ID games tou must pick up health and armour. However we have moved on from the walk over you must manually pick up using hotkey to do so. Which is a little irritating but understandable as it allows medpacks and armour to be hidden at times thus adding a little bit of realism to the game. The days of giant mansized medpacks are over people.
Duel wield. Nice touch to the game I must confess to using this a little too much and it can at times make the game a little easy as accuracy is of such that you don't need to iron sight guns all too much and so you can use duel wield without actually sacrificing anything. So plus and a minus here.
Secrets. A homage to Wolfenstein 3D I imagine. Gold objects are hidden around the levels what used to give you a score now is a game of find the Nazi gold. Fun for completionists but I have never been so inclined.
I am glad that this game had the balls to use Swastikas. I have never been a fan of people changing the symbol of Nazi Germany to the iron cross. For 2 reasons one it is historically inaccurate and 2 it ironically associates the iron cross with Nazism, when it is a symbol of the German military pre, during and post Third Reich era. So way to go censorship is going to make the current German military seem like a bunch of Nazis.
AI the AI does seem decent enough to be a challenge. The game uses the classic ID 5 levels of difficulty scheme. I have about 1,000 hours off of Steam and a level 89 Vanu character on Emerald named Nopax.  This game used to be great and still is the best core game on the market.  That said the devs have botched everything since beta and as a result 99% of installs of this game do not currently play it.  It has 2 EU servers, 1 dead AU one, 1 dead west coast NA one and 1 alive east coast NA server.  DBG is just milking this now to fund other games, there have only been a very small handful of patches in 2015 and no content drops (they have added two or three weapons though).
Additionally the game is 2.5 years old and the playerbase is so used to hearing negative things about the game that they have become very toxic.  If you ask new player questions such as which gun is best to use for medics you will be greeted with "go play CS noob" or "please kill yourself do the world a favor".  This game actually makes me miss the friendliness of the League of Legends community.
The game offers camos for your soldier which are a very small edge that are purchased via real currency only.  It also has implants which add a small edge to your character but cost a fortune using in game currency and you must feed them.  As a result you need to use a weak one or pay real money.  It is not really P2W, but it definitely has a 5% or so edge for paying customers.
Back in the day I would have highly recommended this, but now do not even bother installing it.  Do yourself a favor and just play BF4 instead if you want combined arms.

Now that Robocraft is out of beta, I decided to take another look at the game that had fallen from grace with the infamous Epic Loot update. And you know what? It's fun again. It really is fun again, and I'm happy that the game has finally found its niche in the big ol' game industry. Everything in the game feels more or less balanced, and while matchmaking leaves something to be desired in places, things generally work out in the end. My problem lies with FreeJam, the folks running this show.
Gameplay involves having you use a Minecraft-style building system where you build a bot by putting together blocks, movement parts, weapons, and useful modules. Everything costs CPU, and generally, the more CPU you have (up to 2000), the more health you will have, but the less damage you will deal. The balancing on this is pretty good; smaller bots tend to be built more for speed or flanking to take advantage of high damage, while larger bots can be powerful pushing forces in capture-point gamemodes like Battle Arena. One thing I'll say about gameplay in particular is that it's very balanced--damage boost by CPU is balanced, individual weapons are more or less balanced, and all in all, it feels like a very solid package. Hell, the game will even give team buffs if a player disconnects, and these are so effective that you forget your team's even short one bot in the first place. I guess that's what the beta was for--making sure all these numbers and power curves were in order. It paid off, for sure. The game has a steep learning curve; you'll have to learn what kinds of weapons work in which situations, how to properly protect connection points for your various attachments, and hey, is triforcing putting together pieces of the Triforce? You probably will be tempted to just buy all your bots from the Community Robot Factory, but I recommend that you learn the tools of the trade yourself; it's far more satisfying to build from scratch and try new things to see if they're crazy enough to work then just buy "EZ TOPSCORE BOT #1572" off the CRF. Matchmaking is...mediocre. The game hardly considers your weapon choice in making sure teams are balanced, so it's not uncommon for you to be running super short-range Ion Distorter shotguns in a match where the entire enemy team is flying 50 feet above you. Just throw caution to the wind and hope you'll have a good match, I guess. It works out for me, at least.
Now then, my main issues pretty much all can be traced back to the statement "FreeJam isn't listening to the playerbase". No one asked for the complete flattening of the tiers, but FreeJam did it anyway (I think this was a good choice in the long term, however). No one asked for the currency-based system the game had been running on for two years to be replaced with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t RNG crate system,
No one asked for the ability to craft cosmetics, the entire selling point of Epic Loot, to be removed,
Do I sound like a broken record? Then you can see that Robocraft's had a very volatile development process through Early Access, as FreeJam took advantage of their Early Access state to get community feedback through its development...and then promptly ignored all of the feedback. This should be less of an issue now though, as since Robocraft has been fully released, FreeJam won't be making any of these groundbreaking changes anymore. Hopefully. Notably though, FreeJam does listen to feedback when it comes to weapon, module, and movement balancing, which is probably why the game feels so balanced. So all this shouldn't deter you at this point in time, but you should probably know this if you want to commit to this game--its landscape can change at random, sometimes for the better, and sometimes for the worse.
All in all, Robocraft is a great free-to-play game. Easy to pick up, but with a very steep learning curve that will keep the creative folk invested for hours. Have a penchant for block-based building games like Minecraft or Terraria? Come see what this game has to offer. Bored and need a good free-to-play game? Try this one on for size; it fits most. Left this game because you got♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off about Epic Loot? Come back and give Robocraft 1.0 a try. It's (mostly) better now, I swear.

While it's not the best game of the Max Payne trilogy, it's still an enjoyable game. Don't have too high expectations of the game and you'll have a fairly good time playing it. Max has turned a little chubby and extremely depressed, self-loathing and self-pitying since we last saw him and is drinking his miserable life away while being a bodyguard in Saõ Paulo.  The single player story is fairly short, it took me 9 hours to complete and it's not all that great of a story. It's decent.
Game play is much of the same. The bullet time is a lot of fun to use and you will need it. Mr. Drunkard Payne finds himself far too often overwhelmed by bad guys who wants him dead. This isn't very new for him, though. You will find yourself flowing through various of bad guys over and over again while getting Max high on painkillers - so it's not that very different from what we're used to with a Max Payne game. The game can however become rather repetitive so keep that in mind.
There are a few annoyances such as a shaky camera from time to time and random weird color schemes. But the game looks really good but the noir theme that was in the first two games is lacking and you're following Max Payne in a whole different kind of atmosphere (and story). The game has A LOT of cut scenes, too. I don't mind them but for some people constant cut scenes are a bore, so I thought it would be good to add.
If you're looking to buy this game then I'll suggest you'll get it on a sale, it's not worth the full price it had on release. It's however a rather action packed game and will give you a few entertaining hours if you look past some of its flaws. The DLC for the game is for multiplayer and I can't say how active that is since I never tried it once.

This game was recommended to me by my friends. I wasn't that impressed at first, because for one it was a bit confusing (especially the redeploy map) and it was hard to fight other people without a crowd of people around me; and even then, I would either get ONE hit on him/her with the Light Assault, or hit my other teammates. Driving and flying used to be a huge problem for me as well because I was still quite a noob and I would not realise that warpgates were at the edge of the map and I would fly or drive in a restricted area. However, I've improved and I use aircraft terminals and ground vehicle terminals when I can find them.
Another hard thing I still have trouble with today is that sometimes I find that just an arrow to signify a teammate is not enough. I always play Vanu Sovereignity and I hit my own team instead of a New Conglomerate; it probably sounds stupid to everyone else, but I think they look very similar. It's also hard to find an enemy that's shooting you, for when you turn around and find them you're already dead or you don't see the person as they have no indication that they are there. In another update I think the creators should add a bright outline of the person hitting you. This isn't much of a disadvantage for Infiltrators as well, since they already obliterate you in a couple shots (if not one) with their sniper rifle.
Since I like flying planes and driving vehicles, especially the Vanu Flash, I find it incredibly annoying as a plane when I crash into a branch and my plane just explodes. I have to spend time simply flying up high enough to be safe, when I could be using that time to help my faction in a battle. I know it'll be hard to actually make all the textures, sound and movement for the tree to break, so it'll be easier just to 'go through the tree' and NOT die instantly. And for all the people out there who are like 'Ugh, you suck. Just get better at the game', well, not everyone can get better in an instant. I'm not used to playing these kind of games.
On the other hand, I love the smoothness and the graphics of Planetside 2. The bases are all complex and built in a way that makes capturing and defending fair, and somehow, cold bloodedly, I think that everyone gets quite a satisfaction on killing people. The atmosphere of a battle is awesome, with tanks and Sunderers coming in with turrets and dropping off people, the shouts of 'I need medical aid!' and 'Throwing a grenade!', and the creative variety of aircrafts battling in the air above you, occasionally swooping down for an attack on land. I also like the tactics you can do, which are sometimes dumb but funny. When I was introduced to the game my friend showed me how he would plant a C4 on his own Flash and drive it into an enemy vehicle. Another friend of mine showed me what to focus on as certain classes.
I'd recommend this game to any player who wants to take a first-person-shooting game into the next level.

This game is a great game. With all honesty, I don't think I've ever played a shooter better than this one. It certainly beats the online gameplay from just about every mainstream (CoD, BF3) and non-mainstream (RushTeam, C&C: Renegade) game of it's kind ever. Instead of playing with say 16 other teammates, you can play with hundreds of other people. The game's servers constantly run in real time, so one day you may log on and capture the entire continent, and the next day you'll log on to find your team retreating while being slaughtered by the land's new owners. I must also give this game bonus points for being generally family friendly, ignoring online interactions. The online interactions are what make this game upsetting. You don't worry about hackers and such like other games, it's the young community. There are alot of younger players who take to the fields of this game, and as you can already guess, the majority of players are really immature.
Just about everyone forgets that those other players are actually people just like you behind the screen. Why do I say this? The annoying amount of friendly fire. It's one thing to accidentally launch a missile a little too early or a little too late or experience some lag and hit players from your own team. It's another thing when some kid thinks he's so funny to get Max class (a super overpowered expensive to buy class with rocket launchers and mini-guns galore), and walk into his own base killing every single player he can find. It gets really annoying. And if you try to fight back, the game will threaten to lock down your weapons and will assign you, "griefer points," to warn other players that you are a threat to your own team mates (likely because you are destroying a weapon vital to your own team). One moment you're repairing some guy in a mech suit, and the next moment he turns on his mic revealing he's a T-bagging fifth grader with the intent to cause a history-worthy massacre. Not cool man. Reading the book MASTERS OF DOOM at the moment, which chronicals the life of iD software, the  creators of the original Wolfenstein 3D. This lead me to check out Wolfenstein 3D again and it's amazing to see just how far gaming has come in such a short time.
The graphics on this are nothing short of amazing. Where to start...
I have a love-hate relationship with Dirty Bomb. The Gameplay mechanics and game itself is brilliant. The dev team.. not so brilliant.
The game:
Dirty Bomb is the best of both worlds in a single game; fast paced, action packed combat, good map design, good movement and physics, graphics are pretty. Gameplay is intense and gets me competitive. Overall the game is a gem, just being covered in dirt as I will later discuss.
The Devs:
For the most part, the devs of Dirty Bomb cherish the game and try to do what they think is best. The only problem is that seldom do they actually seek community feedback prior to applying changes to the game. Recently a new crafting system has been implemented without even notifying the community. Everyone was enraged. Many quit and boycott the game. The devs were trying to be more engaging with the community ironically enough, and I give them kudos for trying but... you can't ♥♥♥♥ the game and expect people to not bat an eye.
Crafting:
As a veteran, of course I hate it. We all do. Not that Splash Damage thought to even acknowledge us. The old trade up system worked a charm -- You collected different loudouts from cases, traded them up for a higher rarity, traded up several higher rarity to get Cobalt. The trade up system offered a great deal of progress, which gave incentive for players, veterans in particular, to continue playing and supporting the game that we dearly loved. The new crafting system could be good, but the overpriced, uneccessary, and illogical components get to me. Not only is crafting more expensive (you have to buy crafting kits in order to craft anything, or pay 50,000 credits which is the same as a single ♥♥♥♥ing merc.), It wil probably take 5000 hours of grinding to get enough weapon kits to craft a Colbalt. Not to mention all our cards that aren't Cobalt are ♥♥♥♥ing worthless now.
The Community:
Dirty Bomb has a good community, in that players want to support and enjoy competing with one another. Hackers are everywhere. There isn't a good anti-hack system, and for the most part hackers just create a new account. People in clans often dominate games, or due to the awful balancing system 80% of games are one sided and crap. Now and then you'll get a good one, or have to keep leaving games until you land a decent shuffle. The game has no balancing system for levels (yet).
Verdict:
I used to have such a fondness for this game. Now it is withering. I still like Dirty Bomb, this is no hate rant. I am just sad to see a game with so much potential to do so well being trashed by its devs. (Don't) keep it up. I haven't lost all faith, but if the next update is like the crafting one I am done. So are a lot of others. Please, Splash Damage - treat your game with some respect, and the community who keep it alive at that.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND this game to true fans of Max Payne 1 and 2. Game has lost its dark tone -- you no longer feel like you are alone against the world "thanks" to "helpfull" non-player characters literally bossing you through an excessively cinematic-driven story, linear play, no save ability, sparse checkpoints, and enemy AI which can sometimes make you swear even on Easy difficulty.
To top it off, you have to register for Rockstar Social Club, tie that registration to your Steam account, and log in every time -- even to play a single-player game.
As a long-time fan of Max Payne 1 and Max Payne 2 games, I am severely disappointed with this consolized, multi-playerized, half-arsed game.
Thanks to Valve and their amazing discounts at least I did not burn too much money, but if I knew how bad the game is beforehand (my bad, should have done my homework), I wouldn't have purchased it even at that price point because it is just not worth that much.
If you were a fan of noir and trippy atmosphere in the prequels, better save your money and your memory of Max instead of insulting yourself with this garbage.

If you are looking for a pure action shooter in the over the top style of Quentin Tarantino this is your game.
It carries all the hallmarks of the classic shooter that have gotten so overlooked in the current list of shooters. You can lean out from cover, there are multiple ways to move around a level, the enemies are aggreessive and will flank you if you stay still for too long, and the weapons are just plain fun. Each has their own unique secondary mode with most of them having the option for dual wielding no matter how ridiculous that may be for the weapon type.
The characters and story are fairly run of the mill though there are some disturbing exceptions and what you'd expect from this sort of game, just people trying to survive though there are plenty of quirky and memorable faces to be sure. For the most part those characters are well used and the voice acting is superb.
A word of caution however, this game can get grisly. There is a lot of blood and some very disturbing imagery involved that is not normally touched upon in games. To put it simply: you're fighting the Nazis, expect all that implies in gruesome detail, they didn't hold back much.
In short, go and kill some Nazis.

While I love the art direction and the setting of the game, old Starbreeze really dropped the ball here. Bad narrative with weak character interactions, empty hub level with fetch quests, gimmicky laser rifle that requires reloading via special recharging stations around the levels, completely breaking the pacing of combat, and sometimes forcing the player to cheese enemies - in one level the player encounters 4 heavily armored soldiers, and there's simply not enough ammo for other weapons to kill them off. Players are only allowed to talk to characters in the hub once (at best), usually resulting in a short conversation with forced drama for character backstories. Along with hilariously bad stealth mechanics, I still can't figure out how people who made Riddick and The Darkness could fail so hard at things they were really good at. Terrible pacing of the game doesn't help that much either, sometimes forcing the player to explore (follow the corridor, more like) sewers in a mini-sub and turn valves for 15 minutes, or levels that are all about walking around after NPCs and figuring out puzzles for grade schoolers, resulting in something that feels like HL2, but with developers having no clear idea what they were trying to do. Shooting does feel good, though, but there's just not enough of it in the game that tries to be a shooter, and the soundtrack is really great.
It's not as bad as most modern shooters, but it's not good either. Like Shadow Warrior last year, the game tries too hard to appeal to both fans and modern players, failing at it horribly, and ending up being a complete mess.

Pleasant surprise.  The new Wolfenstein is not only something much more than I expected, but an accomplishment in and of itself.  From gorgeous visuals, imaginative alternate reality, colorful characters, to a complete disregard for the modern formula of shooter, Wolfenstein:  The New Order steps up and beyond the plate of the standard FPS.
Being able to dual wield everything in the game is something I haven't seen in shooters since the world has come to accept realism as the best method for escapism.  The moment you pull out two shotguns and fire an endless barrage of buckshot death towards towering robot Nazi soliders is the moment Wolfenstein has wooed you with its outrageousness.  But absurdity alone cannot carry a game, which brings us to where the game truly shines.  Despite the complete over-the-top design and gameplay, the story plays itself out completely straight.  Despite many of the characters being nothing more than walking tropes, they're delivered in such a way that makes them endearing and engaging.  The hulking, barrel chested protagonist himself consistently delivers a sense of humanity and at times, vulnerability.  This combined with a complete overhaul of full throttle nonstop crazy shooting-fest delivers the motivation along with the killer gameplay.  All this, and it's a mere single player shooter.  Wolfenstein reminds us that the norm isn't necessarily the best and only approach to games, and reminds us of a time when outrageousness was championed genuinely.
I look forward the the future of gaming with MachineGames in it.  They have much to offer in a time of homogenized oversaturated game formula.

I expected this game to be an average shooter. When it was announced as being in development, I was only mildly curious, and as the release date approached, I wasn't excited. I probably made the decision to buy it because of the DOOM beta access.
Turns out, it is a very good game, with some of the best voice acting, mocap, and storytelling I have ever seen in a game. Some of the characters express ideas that you just never see in games, and rarely in cinema. Metaphysical naturalism, determinism, and nuanced religious musings are featured as optional character dialogue, and it fleshes out the characters and concepts on offer in an effective way. The ideas on offer in this game are thought-provoking and fresh, particularly when compared to other shooters.
I didn't understand the music at first, as the main motif didn't strike me as very Wolfenstein-ish, but as the game progressed, I discovered that the motif is intertwined with other themes, and the soundtrack as a whole made sense and was emotionally effective.
Sound effects are fantastic. Played with a decent pair of studio headphones. I'm sure it'd be amazing with a legit setup.
Gameplay and game systems are solid, but I wish I didn't have to farm for perks. There ought to be better ways to gain access to perks. They could also be more interesting. Perhaps you ought to be able to specialize, and be locked into a tree, but be rewarded accordingly, instead of having access to literally everything.
Overall, very good game. Nein/10.

A few things first, since a lot of people don't seem to get this.
-No this is not an Overwatch rip-off. They do have similar gameplay and class system. Dirty bomb is older anyway.
-There is absolutely NO P2W, it's to the points where you would feel bad for the developers not making any money. All loadout cards and characters are unlockable with ingame currency.
Dirty Bomb is a fast paced FPS where players are encouraged to run and jump through the map and its obstacles. It features multi stage objective gameplay where the attackers have to push back the defending team.
This game is player skill based. Learn to aim for the head and never stop moving will be your first lesson after joining the first game. All characters are well balanced including the two you start with. Loadout cards will have up to 3 slots, which will consist of really small perks, for example: Reloading whilst sprinting, and carrying 1 extra magazine. Although I myself are quite picky about my loadout cards you can't call higher tier cards an advantage over new players.
The grind is not that bad compared to other f2p fps's. You will recieve 3 small missions every 3 hours. This will be your main income ingame. These missions can be completed by decent players within 30 minutes.
Its a free game, there is no reason not to try it.

This game is great, don't get me wrong, but the game right now, is terrible. Now, that may contradict itself, but for any League of Legends players, you know what I mean. The game is amazing, beautiful graphics, amaxzing gameplay, and overall great ways to use the map to your advantage with the help of teammates. The problem arrises with the matchmaking system, loadout card system, merc unlock system, and community. The community isn't toxic, or vile by any means, it's just dwindling. Once you get a decent card, you're fine and dandy, no need to worry, when you want to earn one, welcome to hell, population, 66% lead. Cards you scrap are under valued, and cards you craft are undervalues, crafting a cobalt is impossible without massive grinding and not wanting your entire loadout inventory. Now the matchmaking system, is god awful. There is no party system, quick match continously will screw you over, execution mode is full of quick chat spammers and teabaggers, stopwatch takes forever, (I know, ironic), and ranked is full of people who will yell at you for picking an engineer over a medic, which they don't need.
The game is fun, and I would recommend it, but just not now. Wait until casual mode is released as well as a few extra fixes and then download the game. Though, there's no shame in downloading it now and getting an early start. See you out there mercs.

This Game is truly a history in the making. The Age of Empires Franchise is outstanding being the start of the Strategy Genre. AOE 2 really made its toll as a game as now it's been remastered, it really can't get any better. What makes this game so good is a number of things. To start of the gameplay is great. There is a key manging that you have to do to achieve a large army, a stable amount of resources and golden tunnel to victory. It does not match the Mangement of CIV 5 but there's a big difference with both of the games (but lets not go into that). The Graphics may not match most other strategy games like Company of Heores 2 and StarCraft but I think that's what makes it an AOE game in it's own sense. With the huge armies and big variations of units fighting this game really makes combat fun. When playing this game like most strategies you have to think carefully and plan your road ahead, you will come to do this alot with AOE2. Plan who to attack, plan what you are going to do with your first villagers so it requires alot of thinking but theres no harm in that.
You have the choice also to pick a huge variety of factions to play. Each faction is unique in its self for example: the Byzantines to having a STRONG♥♥♥♥♥Cavlary Unit, Heavy Armoured with a fast speed. But also having certain strengths and weaknesses and the Celts having Woad Radiers a strong brute type unit being swift and having high attack. Like the factions the units in the game have strengths and weaknesses. Enough about the units and Factions lets now talk about the music. The Music is catchy, you won't get bored of the music. The music is very fitting and is great to listen to.
What Makes AOE as a series is the Map Maker. There is a wide variety in making a may, from adding lots of different types of terrian to buildings and units. You can make your own campaign if you really wanted. The REAL Campaign Personally was alright, I enjoyed it but not enough to say it was AMAZING like the game itself. One of the things that really I enjoy about this game is the expression of custom battles and Skirmishes. You can have Skirmishes with Friends or Solo and the map will always be randomly generated. You can choose many different map types to choose from but also the premade maps from the Steam Workshop.
The Steam Workshop really increases the games overall score. The original AOE2 is outstanding but the Steam Workshop allows you to add maps, new units, OUTSTANDING new Textues and custom music as well, but also many other things.
Now Moving on to DLC "The Forgotten" the only ever DLC released for this game enchaces the game to a point. It adds new units, factions, campaign missions and other things. Personally I love AOE2, but the DLC is not worth the money. So I do not recommend buying this DLC.
Overall this game is truly amazing, I recommend buying it but not its DLC. You will never get bored of this game as a game is always different even if you play the same faction and use the same plan. I really want a AOE4, AOE 3 is amazing but thats a another review for another day.

As someone who has played every Wolfenstein game in existence (and yes, that includes the first two Apple ][ offerings), I wasn't sure how this new game would stack up with Raven's 2009 Wofenstein. That game was a wonderful shooter and still, to this day, I'll take any opportunity to say "Frightened, American?"
Well New Order stacks up very well, indeed. No lip service branding here: every bit of this game is evidence of the developers love for the Wolfenstein franchise. The game is a pure shooter for sure - but everything seemes to flow so well within it; the death animations, the gun balance, the play based skill trees, and the cut scenes actually feel to augment the experience. And the experience is nazi killin' fun.  The subject matter is
, though. The game makes you feel what the natural extension of a Nazi victory would mean, and some of that is very unsettling.
I'd recommend this game to fans of the franchise or to anyone looking for a story based thrill ride. It certainly delivers. Not pefect for sure (some of the skill trees "unlocks," can be a little silly and the AI isn't perfect), but very, very fun.
Oh, and, "Frightened, American?"

Josef Mengele; 16 March 1911 – 7 February 1979) was a German Schutzstaffel (SS) officer and physician in Auschwitz concentration camp during World War II. Mengele was a notorious member of the team of doctors responsible for the selection of victims to be killed in the gas chambers and for performing deadly human experiments on prisoners. Arrivals deemed able to work were admitted into the camp, and those deemed unfit for labor were immediately killed in the gas chambers. Mengele left Auschwitz on 17 January 1945, shortly before the arrival of the liberating Red Army troops. After the war, he fled to South America, where he evaded capture for the rest of his life.
Mengele received doctorates in anthropology and medicine from Munich University and began a career as a researcher. He joined the Nazi Party in 1937 and the SS in 1938. Initially assigned as a battalion medical officer at the start of World War II, he transferred to the concentration camp service in early 1943 and was assigned to Auschwitz. There he saw the opportunity to conduct genetic research on human subjects. His subsequent experiments, focusing primarily on twins, had no regard for the health or safety of the victims.
Assisted by a network of former SS members, Mengele sailed to Argentina in July 1949. He initially lived in and around Buenos Aires, then fled to Paraguay in 1959 and Brazil in 1960 while being sought by West Germany, Israel, and Nazi hunters such as Simon Wiesenthal so that he could be brought to trial. In spite of extradition requests by the West German government and clandestine operations by the Israeli intelligence agency, Mossad, Mengele eluded capture. He drowned while swimming off the Brazilian coast in 1979 and was buried under a false name. His remains were disinterred and positively identified by forensic examination in 1985.

Funny that everyone seems to be hating on the new updates. I'm loving them. I'm glad they got rid of the tech tree. It was overly convoluted and frustrating to try to level to a specific piece you want and required too much investment to get the pieces you want. Now you simply spend Robits (in-game money) on pieces that you want to forge which means you can have a much cooler robot sooner and you don't need to skip past pieces you have no interest in to get to the ones you do. Also, if you don't have enough Robits, you can recycle previous blocks and convert them into Robits.
The new loot crates means that after every match you're rewarded with new components (win or lose) and if you get ones you don't want, you can simply recycle them into money. They've also eliminated Pay to Win from what I can tell because even if you pay money, it only rewards you with the premium pieces (so you basically get twice the amount of loot per match and more money from the premium pieces if you recycle them) so it enables you to "level" faster, but you still have to play matches in order to win said loot. Way better than simply letting people buy robots outright. That was THE definition of Pay to Win. This way its much more balanced.
My only gripe is that its not very good at balancing teams anymore. I often join a match where one team is seriously OP and it sometimes feels like you're playing against players of a much higher tier. But since they reward you even when you lose, it balances out.
The game also looks way better and its more fun to play. No idea why people are claiming you don't have to aim... you sure as heck do!
Before I would have given the game a 6.5/10. Now I think its more like 8.5/10.

AOE2 has been in my top five PC games of all time forever and so I was super excited about the re-release in HD.  It's still the game I knew and loved, but prettier.  SO many memories came flooding back playing civilization after civilization and I was so very happy....
and then the expansion came....
The AI got ALL sorts of messed up.  The one thing, IMO, that always distinguished AOE2 from other RTS games is AI pathfinding.  Starcraft, Warcraft, C&C, all the biggies had computer AI that knew where you were from the second the game started and therefore made a fair fight impossible.  In AOE2, if you saw a scout, you knew you were gonna be attacked soon, which is the way it should be.  After the expansion, hordes of troops would be inside your camp with no scouting whatsoever.  Also, for lack of a better term, resource management of AI was wrecked.  I played 2vs2 with my step-dad for five hours and watched wave after wave of troops die, WITH NO RESOURCES LEFT ON THE MAP.  We saw AI troops walk right through walls, watched arrows decimate walls, and all tactics go right out the window.  It's pretty much an exercise in frustration playing with or against AI in it's current state.
I will give it a recommendation with one stipulation...
DON'T INSTALL ANY PATCHES OR BUY THE EXPANSION

it was a very dark night at The Crown, but there were few clouds to block the light of the moon. Even the stars had there role to play in illuminating the road below us. We are the Terran Republic, i was one of a number on night duty. We were tired, after a hard days fight...pinned down on both sides by our enemies. across the valley infront of us was the Vanu, and behind us over the lip of the cliff had been the New Conglomerate. And as we were about to be replaced by the next shift, the silence was shattered by a thunderous boom! it sounded as if an entire mountain had fallen..and night,lit up..
suddenly the dark sky was illuminated by tracer fire, small arms as well as plasma trails left by the Vanus Magriders there heavy tanks, wich had the farther range... in the sky above the the Vanus Magrider lines came a swath of darkness, like a great black cloud. Scythes,Liberator as well as a number of massive Galaxy Carriers, probably loaded to the gills with enemy infantry. the call went out to every availavle TR player active on the map,they started to arrive, a trickle at first but before long we had hundreds, still outnumbered. the base defenders manned the turrets, filled the air with flak. our Mech troops standing shoulder to shoulder in an attempt to blunt the threat of the incoming aircraft.Medics and Engeneers running bravely through the madness laying down ammo here and there, and as the Vanus forces in the air arrived.. so did there ground forces.brilliantly timed, Mechs, touph, well built leading the charge, Engeneers behind them repairing them, Medics repairing them, enemy snipers, cloaked in the fields watching them, all there ducks in a row. Enemy Lightnings..there light tanks, aptly named for there speed, forgo thicker armor for speed and manuverability.by this point  friendly squads had been formed, dishing out jobs for the defenders. great pillars of light, beacons placed by our forces allow air dropped reinforcements.  a wave of us ran into the base and formed a line at the terminal, changing our gear for the fight infront of us, a number bringing out there customized tanks, while The Crown was an easily defendable position, it lacks the size for us to man a large group of tanks, our double barreld Prowlers. our aircraft the Mosquitos, exrememly fast, able to tumble and flip behind the hands of a skilled player! i put thermal imaging on my rifle, just hoped the fight dont deterierate to the point where its needed, we need to keep them bottled on in the valley. i ran relay, bolstering our forces where needed. one moment an Engeneer dropping ammo, repairing our tanks or mechs..placeing mines and claymores at choke points, next a Sniper, picking off the occasional straggler with impunity. mostly a Heavy Weapons expert, firing homing rockets and missiles into the night. friendly Heavy Infantry with there massive heavy machine guns, litterally spit lead at our enemies. between them, our tanks and mechs, a barrage of grenades. we held our own, there forces falling before they could make much progress, but we new somehwere nearby, in the darkness was a Sunderer, a vehicle capable of acting as a mobile respawn beacon..it had to be destroyed, so those of us most proficient went out, a group a cloaked sniper. silently weaving through enemies and relaying its position to us, now its time to call in an air strike, a friendly squadron of Mosquitos, armed with hellfires, unguided, air to ground missile pods, most of them had the night vision purchased, or thermals. making locating and dispatching the Sunderer a simple task. the fight would drag for hours, one side having the advantage, then the next. by the time the sun started to rise our forces had been pushed back into The Crown, the very base we had been defending steadfast through the night.our forces were splintered, cut off from one another, desperatly fighting to protect the flag. the enemy would need to control 2 out of 3 flags to take our base.all around us you could hear weapons fire and explosions, proximity chat screaming for help, the wounded and dieing needed the medics, those still standing needed ammo from engeneers.
just when we thought it couldnt get worse, the New Conglomerate attacked, they had been watching through the night waiting for there moment. and with both the Vanu and our Terran Republic exhausted, there Reavers and Vangaurd tanks, lauphably slow but more armor and firepower then 10 Lightnings, found little resitance to be had and had us routed within the hour.
do you have the strength, the iron will to serve?

I was pleasantly surprised by this game.  Given the history of recent Wolfenstein games I was a bit skeptical about this game, but had heard good things.  I decided to make the purchase after finding a good deal for this game.

Well.... its a shame as this game used to be great, but now... pretty annoying, frustrating and generally entirely unbalanced.
sure, they ahve some great technical features but the problems they have are being resolved by fiddling with new stuff, rearranging deckchairs instead of fixing the fundamental problems.
If you're a new player looking to get into RC, I wouldn't bother. They have a new system of getting bits needed to build bots: crates that contain items you win after each battle, only i can imagine its one hell of a grind to get enough to build anythign decent. When you do get into battle in the higher tiers, you end up battling 'meta' builds that show up the poor design of the game - mainly bots built with thrusters for movement that simply move fast and cannot easily be shot down (so you can see why some players love them, the devs included).
RC used to be great, the creativity and enjoyment of a game where it didn't matter if you won or lost- you entered a new game and tried again. The fun was in the playing it, winning was good, but losing wasn't so bad either. Now, it seems that winnign ro losing is almostpre-determined depending on the bots you're up against. If you have been in a battle against 3 or 4 drones, you'll know what I mean. And that level of frustration means the game is simply dissatisfying.
FJ's response to this is to cater to the 'competitive players', ie the problem in the first place. They add new weapons that just end up being useless (eg flak, protoseeker) or annoying (LOML) as ways to counter the problem builds. Unimaginative solutions to what is essentially a fundamental problem - that the game is no longer fun.
Now they're adding clans, so expect even more combined forces of competitive players "seal clubbing" the opposition. I'm not sure I'll keep playing at this rate, I've already dropped to 1 or 2 quick games a day to see if its getting any better., that's 10 minutes a day after work, I just can't be enthused enough to play more.  I hope they'll rediscover a way to create balance, poossibly the one feature that the forum users suggested (of low/medium/high where you trade speed and strength - to have a slow but bulk tank or a fast but weak flyer) was rejected by FJ for undisclosed reasons, so I doubt they'll ever properly balance the game.

a really enjoyable, underrated title to end Max's trilogy. fun over-the-top gameplay antics with lots of setpieces that would - in real life - be the subject of international news every time Max gets to work.
the characters, writing, dialogue, voice acting, guns and level design are on par with R* standards and while the campaign is a bit short there are some replay incentives. the Brazilian environment is a contrast to the usual gritty, noir, concrete style of Hoboken which results in a more lush, green, bright, open, dilapidated, uneven landscape. a couple flashback levels are thrown in so you still get that original feel and offers a nice mixup.
my main gripes are the loading times, bullet time doesn't last long enough (if you dive and hit a wall, chair, etc bullet time will end) and half the cutscenes are unskippable or take a while to skip, which is immensely annoying when you have to retry the part or whole level (eg. New York Minute mode). also when Max recovers from a second wind, he will fully stand up instead of going to cover which meant more unnecessary damage, pill usage and facepalming.
all in all a worthy title to play and definitely worth it if you can find it for $15 or less.

James McAffery is brilliant as Payne and there are some AMAZING lines and one-liners in this game. Perhaps most integral is the absolutely perfect soundtrack by  the band Health. I was pleasantly surprised with this game. I was skeptical because they removed most of the noire from the previous games and skipped the comic book sequences. But all in all... the story was decent... not as good as the previous games, but Max Payne is just a really likable guy with his depressive and gloomy remarks and attitude which makes the dialogue so funny. The gameplay and action was dead on and really solid, but since they had a good combination between cutscenes and gameplay they prevented it from becoming too monotonous.

This is a great experience: Wolfenstein's dark and mature storyline is one of the better ones I've come across in the genre. Even if a little crazy at times.
It has likeable characters, and the world, in which the Reich won the war and came to power, is (beautifully) imagined by the devs. The concept art and locations are just stunning.
First of all it needs to be said. This is a heap better than the 2009 version. They've done a better job of the gunplay (dual wielding is amazing) and switching between weapons is easy. There is also a decent variety of weapons. Don't be fooled, a lot of them have secondary fire modes you can unlock later with an upgrade.
On this, the level design is well done. Though mostly linear, there are sometimes other (sneakier) ways of approaching the situation. Secrets such as upgrades, enigma pages and letters are placed to encourage a bit of exploration.
The audio is great. Epic soundtrack that fits well with the situation. Also, it has good boss battles with giant robots that make you think about how to make best use of the environment around you.
I will mention, that running on an AMD card performance was kind of crap at launch during the first 2 levels. I left the game for a bit and now it seems to have gotten better. Still could do with some optimisation though. In terms of bugs I only encountered one during my whole playthrough (falling through the level), but the well placed checkpoint system meant I didn't have to re-do too much.
I highly recommend this game.

Max Payne 3 is engrossing from the start, and just keeps getting better as the story and plot progresses. Although Max Payne himself comes off being a whiner in the begining, you get to understand his state of mind and his ways of thinking as you plod on through the game. With great visuals that portray the very gritty and seedy underbelly of São Paulo's criminal underground, to the great character portrayals that show of the characters personality traits well. Max Payne 3 is great game from start to finish. I have almost nothing bad to say about this game, except a few personal gripes that mainly relate to me and perhaps others. I found the game to be quite frankly... Hard to master. I landed up dying numerous times on the normal difficulty because some events in the game will place in situations where there is little to no cover availible to you, unless you run straight through a pack of enemies right smack dab in front of you. Make no doubt about it, in this game you NEED cover and bullet time PLENTY! I cannot stress this enough, or else you are going to be in for one Hell of a ride. Stil that's about all I can say that's bad about the game. There's also multiplayer for people that want more out the game once you've done everything you want with the single player portion.
All in all, Max Payne 3 is a highly enjoyable action game, with a good, if not bit predicatable story that manages to pull some high octane set peices to make for a fun ride, if it were not for the odd difficulty spikes in the game, I'd say it was about perefectly executed.

FreeJam has made multiple mistakes with RoboCraft; there's no one thing that I think "broke" the game.
Problem One: Crates
This, I would say, helped and hurt the game. By removing the money that you get at the end of a match and replacing it with a box with random stuff, you might get what you need just for playing. On the other hand, you may get items that you never will need, and selling it gets you next to nothing. And when you go to buy the things you need, that next-to-nothing money you got isn't enough. And then having Premium gives you Protonium Crates, which either gives you awesome stuff, or gives you a metric ton of blocks.
EDIT - I now understand that you will never get common blocks from protonium crates; however, useless blocks are still possible.
Problem Two: Balance
Holy crap, what to say? When I go into a match with 5 people on both sides, I would expect that we have generally the same number of weapons/type of weapons. But when I go in and I see the equivalent of an AC-130 Spectre bearing down on my team of minitanks, I start to question whether the removal of tiers was a good idea or not.

On its face, this game is quite similar to Max Payne 1 and 2, enough that I'd be confident recommending it to anyone who enjoyed the first two games. Now, there are a number of major differences. This is a modern shooter and so a large change is made- the addition of a cover system. You end up using a mix of cover and bullet time to defeat a large number of enemies, and I felt that enemy damage was cranked up a lot to compensate for the addition of cover. That said there is just not as much gameplay in this as there was in the first two, as instead of the in-game narration style of the first, MP3 is broken up frequently by long cutscenes, to which you are fed story. The story itself is standard revenge fare and most times it feels like it's being fed to you rather than you guiding it along in any meaningful way, though this is a corridor shooter at best. I felt that the characterization of Max was spot on and the tone of the dialogue was true, though not sure if I felt that the character fit the South American-styled story, and the justification for Max's inclusion in it was shaky at best. That said a thoroughly enjoyable, though short game, with less actual gameplay than even Max Payne 2's short running length.

I remember a very certain part of playing Age of Empires - I was only five, and was playing against my older brother. He played normally, apparently. I being naive as I was, didn't know how to advance ages, so I pretty much stayed in the Stone Age building everything tons of times and training nothing but villagers. He sent a scout along, saw what I was doing, got his scout swarmed and promptly quit.
This left a mark on me however, and I knew from the first day that I ♥♥♥♥ing loved playing Age of Empires. I'd make maps of nothing but giant armies clashing and blowing the PC up. I basically enjoyed it ever since I was a kid.
Naturally, when AoE II came out and pa brought it back, I was all over it. Played through everything and memorised all the cheats. It's been a staple in any of my games collections and I always had an Age of Empires near me, regardless of the series.
With that nostalgia out of the way, I'd like to review this game.
Age of Empires II came out in September 1999 - just two years after the original AoE - by Ensemble Studios, and to rave reviews, IGN giving it an 8.8/10. It featured civilizations across Europe, Africa and Asia (and with the Conquerors the Americas), alongside campaigns that told the story of Joan of Arc, Saladin and William Wallace to name just a few. It didn't stray far from the original isometric view of its predecessor, but it did keep a pleasant looking graphical update, alongside some pretty damn important updates of its own. It isn't much at the time but there were selectable formations, queuable units and basically improved on everything that AoE originally done. As with the original Age of Empires, AoE II comes with a scenario creator, allowing you to create maps for anything you can desire, with triggers, diplomacy settings and an ability to share these maps on the internet. I'll be talking about this in a moment, but Age of Empires II really set the bar for RTS's (RTSes?) and expanded perfectly on what was already an excellent game.
Now that this HD edition has been around for a good couple of years, it's really time to see just what it did to change things up.
For starters, the graphical updates. It's good that the resolution can be increased now, rather than being tethered to 1024 x 768, but there are some things that I felt weren't really necessary. For starters, the new "3D" water. It's pretty I guess. But it feels out of place with the rest of the scenery which almost conflicts with contrast. Smaller details like shadow rendering I pretty much just turned off after ten minutes, as it didn't add anything to the experience. The achievements are... nice. It's interesting to have but really, it doesn't feel right having them there anyway. It could be the age of the game, or it could be me. I'm iffy about acheivements.
There are things that really redeem AoE II: HD in my eyes however, apart from the "modernization" of the game. If you're apprehensive about gameplay, don't fret - the AI have been vastly improved. If you want to take it easy, you don't have to put up with bots resigning because they accidentally spawned with male villagers only (or something). They are a lot more aggressive now, and it can be commonplace to have your base attacked early if you're not careful. They give you a chance, and it can be often where you can advance to the Feudal Age a few minutes before everyone else. The gloves come off after that, though. The HD edition also brings in a new map size "LudiKRIS", which is as it sounds. I tried playing a map of that size and promptly had my laptop near freeze up.
The population cap has also been increased from 200 to 500, letting you have that bit of an extra edge with more villagers spread out, or to field an uber-large army that can curbstomp pretty much anyone who looks at you funny. Smaller additions but still notable include a mirror civilization - so two players who are facing Koreans and Spanish will be Spanish and Korean, a campaign system that has combined the originals with the Conquerors' campaigns, an updated multiplayer system, and the best bit...
The Workshop.
One of the best things that the HD edition brought to the table is Workshop support. Not only does this mean you can download maps that other players created, but there are a plethora of other delicious, delicious DLC that you can snatch away - from texture packs that completely overhaul vanilla (original) unit designs, to taunt packs, to campaigns done with love and kisses. With the workshop the amount of hours you can play with Age of Empires can go through the roof. Try out Gwyndlegard (sic?) while you're checking the workshop out. You will not be disappointed by how enjoyable the scenario is!
To summarize, while the HD edition has some flaws, they're really miniscule in that you're still left with an amazing game that doesn't feel aged at all, with some fantastic additions that makes this comfy-tier base building RTS feel up to date again. Buy this game, it will NOT disappoint you!

Wolfenstein: The New Order is not a very intelligent game.  Neither were any of the Wolfenstein games, matter of fact.  I remember back in 2004 when I was but a child, my Pops let me play Wolfenstein 3D on my old now-gone computer with that old, late '90s computer monitor...it was one of the greatest gaming experiences of my life and I will never forget it.  Hell, I even bought the damn game on Steam just for memories sake.  Fast-forward to now, and I got the entire collection of Wolfenstein games, (except for Wolfenstein 2009) I finally played Retrun to Castle Wolfenstein and loved it.
I actually didn't pay for this game.  While I was on vacation in America about a month ago, my Dad (being a fan of Wolfenstein 3D) bought The New Order for PC at a Gamestop, and after a few awkward moments relating to a drive-in ATM, we got back home and my Dad really wanted me to play The New Order too, so I could enjoy the game as much as he.  At first, we had no idea how to get the bloody thing on to my Steam account.  After a while, one little Google search got us to what we actually needed to do.  We had to link both of out Steam accounts just so I could play it, and it worked swimmingly!  And here I am, playing the newest entry to this series of Nazi killing, gun-toting adventures involving torture, the holocaust, evil....and of course, Nazis.
When I first booted the game up on my newly purchased Alien-Ware laptop, it worked surprisingly well on my high-end gaming laptop.  The game runs of the Id Engine 5, which happens to be the same engine that ran RAGE, and looks a hell of a lot better than that massive disapointment of a game, but that's a game to review at another time.  The textures look all right, with some minor pop-in issues, but they're not too distracting.  The lighting's great and adds to the atmosphere to the overall game-world and works incredibly well in the areas where you are situated in castle-like enviroments.  And the character models look really nice and well-detailes along with nice realistic facial animations that totally don't have the uncanny valley effect at all, and I'm not being sarcastic either.  So yeah, nice looking game.
As I was playing the first part of the game thats set in good 'ol 1946, when World War II was totally raging on by that point in time, and I was having a rollicking good time blowing the Nazi's heads off while going nuts with a mounted machine gun.  The gameplay is satisfying, ridiculous and friggin' fun.  This game is Bullet Storm and Shadow Warrior levels of fun and stupidity, and it has that classic Wolfenstein spirit that both Return and 3D had all those years ago, but with a modern twist and it is glorious!  I have never, in all of my gaming days ever thought I would hear a video game character say "damn Nazi spaceman" but now I have.  And what FPS lets you old two shotguns in both hands while blowing Nazi's heads off while guiding an angry scotsman out of a prison cell?  Not Call of Duty, that's for damn sure.  And the health system!  My God the health system!  It's like Quake all over again!  Not only can you only get health back from medpacks, but you don't have to do that stupid tactic that modern FPS games have been making you do for years; the stop & pop tactic that you seemingly have no choice but to use.  Here, in Wolfenstein: The New Order, we don't do that stop & pop crap here.  We actually respect the player's intelligence and expect the player to explore the map, find health packs to stay alive, and be hardcore.  Health only regenerates a small iota of your health and that's all.  No hand-holding and no arrows on the screen telling you where to go on this ride.
Seriosuly, I could go on and on about how happy I am about the old-school health mechanic, because I have been complaining like an old man saying "Back in my day, we didn't have these fancy-pants regeneration systems and cover...we used out bare-boned skill and wits to fight the enemy and take back Mother RussI-" and so on.  Another thing I absolutely love is how you have practically no limit to the amount of weapons you can carry.  You can carry as much weapons as you please except for the heavy mounted machine/lazer guns.  It's been years since I have played a game where you have no limit to your arsenal...no limit to the amount of killing machines that you would have in your inventory.
And then there's the story.  It's a very basic alternate history game where the main character of all the Wolfenstein games; B.J. Blazkowicz fights his way through a castle in 1946 to kill a man named Deathshead, who is a sadistic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that was the villain from Return to Castle Wolfenstein, and with Blazkowicz's not killing that evil dude, there are now evil Nazi robots that are totally helping the Nazis win World War II and now it's his duty to finish the job.  Blazkowicz finally bursts quite rudely into Deathshead's experimentation chamber after a lot of Nazi killin' where he slices guys' backs open and burns them for some reason.  Then, after a surprisingly short boss battle, Deathshead puts Blazkowicz in a situation where he has to choose between a Scottish dude and a young pansy to get sliced up.  Blazkowicz chooses one of those two and sees how evil that dude Deathshead really is.  Blazkowicz and whomever he let live then break free of their bindings and jump out the window with a big kaboom behind them.  Blazkowicz then takes a savage piece of shrapnel to the head and falls deep into the sea where some nice Polish people come to pick him up and take him into a mental institution so he can chill out for the next 14 years. That's the basic gyst of the story and the rest of the game is a bunch of dumb fun.
The New Order also features music.  Throughout the game you can collect songs that are German dubs of famous songs from the 1960s and they are really good.  I actually bought most of the songs on Google Play and you can look up the songs specifically made for the game if you're interested.
I love this game and is one of the most unique first person shooters that I have encountered in my gaming travels and is truly an amazing experience.  If you have the money and are planning on purchasing this game, I reccommend you buy thisgame right this second...or wait 'till it comes down in price, I don't care just....buy it!

Max Payne 3 is what happens when you take barely-competent devs, give them a classic, well-liked franchise, force them to play Uncharted 2 for hours on end, and set them free to make a game so bloated by bad decisions that it's hard to see the good through the bad.
I went in wanting to like Max Payne 3. I'd known most of the story, but I was still hoping maybe, just maybe, there'd be some redeeming quality about it.
Nope. The story was asinine, insulting to my intelligence, and essentially serves to completely take Max Payne away from his character, his motivations, and everything that he stood for. When it's not taking control away from you to force an ugly cutscene down your throat, it's told through internal monologues, the kind that made Max Payne and Max Payne 2 interesting to play through.
Here, however, they forget that Max Payne isn't an action here with a sailor's mouth and multiple personality disorder, leading you to wonder if maybe Max Payne had been replaced by Bruce Willis in a B-movie nobody watched.
I do give some nods to presentation, but they're reluctant. The graphics are top-notch, the environments look great and are varied nicely, but the screen effects, camera angles, and effects in Last Stand are distracting and ugly.
Some of the lighting effects and reflections were absolutely astounding though, and I do give Rockstar the most credit here: the game looks great. A shame.
If the game played as good as it looked, I'd be a little bit happier, but it just doesn't. Max Payne and Max Payne 2 worked because they were unrealistic and they knew it. Max Payne 3 is a weird mesh of realism and surrealism that doesn't work at all. You bullettime dodge and it all goes slow-mo while you shoot dudes in the head. That's not realistic.
Yet seconds later you hit a wall, bounce off, and take three seconds to get up. That is realistic, but it's not fun and it takes you completely out of your groove. It's a bad way for Rockstar to show off their admittedly decent physics engine, and it serves to both look dumb and play worse, which is a good feat.
The gunplay is top-tier. It hits hard, it feels good, and it sounds better. The enemy tiers are almost straight-ripped from Uncharted, though, and shooting helmets off guys, which forces you to headshot them multiple times, serves as an annoyance -- especially when they will one-hit you from across the room if even part of your body sticks out.
The sound design is a puzzling mix of beautiful effort put into sound effects and gun sounds and complete laziness with the soundtrack. The music is completely boring aside from the remixed MP1 theme and I struggle to recall any music I can remember that wasn't insidiously grating to my senses and intelligence. (Strip club, I am looking at you.)
There is one moment towards the end of the game where there's a good song playing and you're shooting dudes in the face and it all flows pretty nicely, but it doesn't make up for the lack of other memorable tracks.
Max Payne 3 feels like a betrayal to everything Remedy did with the prior Max Payne games. It turns Max from a sympathetic, hard-luck character into a mass murdering, suicidal drunk old man who somehow still pulls off Nathan Drake-like stunts. It pulls ideas and concepts from other games wholesale (Rockstar must really like Naughty Dog) and shoehorns them in with little regard for gameplay or story. The story tries to make you think, but it actually tells you what to think and then it repeats it a few times for good measure, then ends in a completely dumb way that contradicts the entire rest of the game.
Avoid at all costs if you've played MP1 and MP2 and liked them at all. If you're just starting the Max Payne series and you feel you must play this game, play it before the other two.

I'll be honest upfront.
Wolfenstein: The New Order is, in my opinion, a game so unobtrusive that... I can't really find fault beyond nitpicks. It's a very competent shooter with a surprisingly well acted story. I'll even say that this is one of the few games that actually sold me on the obligatory love subplot. This kinda surprised me, coming from a game that is, at it's core, 'there's a nazi, shoot him'.
I did mention a few Nitpicks, and in no real order:
The split timeline 'mechanic' is... Not really explored. There's only maybe one level that actually changes due to your choice. Minor changes thanks to a tiny minigame, but they're... Generally not used for anything but secret items. There's no change in enemies and no change in weaponry... So it feels tacked on.
Some enemies are grossly bullet spongey, even on 'normal' difficulty. The game has about 4 or so points where you will see that loading screen an asninine number of times because some INCREDIBLY heavily armored jerk murders you. They don't even have to reload! The normal guys do (Or at least they take breaks between bursts). Maybe a future patch will fix it and I'll be able to scrape this off the list of minor irks. Don't take me wrong, The game can be finished... But that final level is REAL annoying.
Finally... If you're the kind of person that goes 'Oooh, Alternate history!' (Like me) and go to look for all the changes, you'll be as disapointed as I was to find out the alternate history tracks from the trailers is basically your lot. I do understand that licensing and recording and junk... But it was a let down none the less not to hear something like an alternate Rolling Stones or The Kinks ('Sie haben mich wirklich' anyone? Just me?)
Oh. And some levels are quite linear. But hey, fish swim, birds fly, levels in 2014 are quite linear.
There. That's really all I got. It's not a back-to-basics shooter in the vein of the original... But it takes just enough from it in such a competent manner that it's worth getting.

The ability to build bases around the map with the harvested resources, which every map now features, works really well with the rest of the game. The main goal is to get a HIVE in your base to generate victory points for your faction to win the battle over a map.

The only downside I can think of, is the need to unlock a few expensive things, like the turrets, with certs (ingame experience currency) - but it's not a grindy game and if you played it for some time, you have enough certs anyway.

Remember how shooters used to be about, you know, shooting stuff? I know, it's a ridiculous notion in this day and age, but really, it used to be! Games like Quake, Doom and the orgiginal F.E.A.R., although they might have had some things at the side, were games like that: Focused on fast-paced, tense action where you were a totall badass and blew things up. Another series from that list is the grandfather of all shooters; Wolfenstein. Now Wolfenstein is back, and with it a shooter about shooting.
First off, let me start of with what it does besides shooting - it's better to get the worst out of the way. There is a story. One with lots of cutscenes. One that doesn't offer too much choice (though there is a little bit of choice involved). It's not a bad story - not at all, even - but sometimes it takes itself a little too seriously, even with the subject matter being treated here, and it's definitely not a great story either. It's solid, does its job, but it might be a bit out of place in a Wolfenstein game.
The best thing about the story is the world: An alternative 1960 where Germany won the second world war by using technology stolen from ancient civilizations. It's a bit far fetched, but the world created is extremely interesting: Massive concrete buildings, oppression... It's a dystopian sci-fi fan's dream, really. The enemy, the Nazi's Reich, is portrayed very efficiently: Brutal, inconsiderate, powerful.
Out of this world goodness streams the action. What kind of action? Action with alternate-reality guns. Assault rifles that blow heads off. Shotguns that blow heads off. Really, a bunch of weapons that blow heads (and other limbs) off. Each weapon is an absolute blast to use; they have just enough recoil and the sounds are utterly fantastic. Besides the fact that every weapon can be dual-wielded (even snipers, which is fun), they also have an alternate fire mode that can change the way the gun works entirely. From the rocket launcher on the assault rifle to the laser rifle on the sniper, there's plenty of variation when it concerns weapons.
One of the centerpiece weapons of the game (think Half-Life 2's gravity gun, if a lot less majestic and fun, but then again, who can top the gravity gun?) is the Laserkraftwerk. The first thing you might think is, if there would be a German laser gun, it would indeed bear that name. The second you might think is what it is, anyway? Well, it introduces some interesting mechanics when it comes to cutting through walls, fences and the like. It's a bit gimmicky, but stands out enough to be mentioned.
Oh, and its secondary fire is a railgun. Just saying.
So, all in all, what does Wolfenstein: The New Order offer? It offers a shooter. A damn fine shooter, even, that took me 12 hours to complete and had me giggling like a madman the whole way, at least when I got to shoot stuff. When I didn't, the story did keep me interested, but the action is where it's at, and because of that I can't recommend it enough.
Buy this. It's the finest shooter to release in years.
P.S.: Dual wielding snipers! Just think of the utter overkill! Doesn't it make your mouth water?!

If you liked the first two, this one's going to be a big change to what you are used to, it's a bright, colourful, bolted-down bullet dodging Gears of War, complete with ALL THE SLO-MO, but it held my attention long enough for me to get from start to finish, all problems withstanding.

UPDATE: I've divided the overly-lengthy review into sections to make it a bit easier to navigate.
A great story, fun gameplay and challenging A.I. make this title a brilliant game. The story is well-done and Rockstar put a lot of effort into it. The lifelike full body & facial animations, along with the top-notch voice acting compliment the story a lot and draw you into the game. The sounds and music of the game are also great and help base the entire plot and game world around you, with area-specific tunes and context-based sound effects.
The A.I. switches from "smart" to "standard" based on how many enemies you face, and the gameplay gets progressively harder. You WILL die many times on Normal. However, the game can tell when you're having an exceptionally hard time and help you with extra painkillers, slightly dumber A.I. and a little luck here and there.
----
The animations are breath-taking and had me grinning from ear-to-ear. It's essentially one big Hollywood action film. The levels were well-designed, and do not suffer from the same "cover-minded design" Mass Effect does, at least not as much.
Keep in mind, though, that this IS a linear game. The linearity is done magnificently and not in a restrictive form, though, and it's one of the good linear games. You have some freedom when it comes to tackling scenarios, but some things are "forced", like a sudden change of weapons due to the oncoming scene. The game is "cutscene-driven", in that most of the walking around will be done by the game, according to the plot.
This isn't necessarily a bad thing, though. These mini-cutscene animations are so well-done that you'll like the game's control, since it gives the entire plot and movie-like events more traction. Since this isn't some generic, repeated animation doing the walking, the progression from one point to another is far more believable and life-like. The plot isn't hurt like in most games, where the video-game-like movement throughout the level reminds you that this is just some video game.
----
Let me make this clear: This is not some console port. Rockstar put an amazing amount of effort into the PC version, packing insanely high-res textures, DX11 Tesselated models, high-resolution and low-compression videos, amazing lighting and shadows, true Ambient Occlusion (HDAO vs SSAO) and above all -- really great performance. There's some slight mouse lag issues, but that's solveable with NVIDIA/ATI-forced V-Sync and a Frame Rate Limiter.
Some of the cutscenes are pre-rendered, but only because they serve as loading screens to make sure the experience is never interrupted. Rockstar made sure to include very high-quality videos so the average PC gamer won't notice the sudden drop in quality thanks to video compression.
----
The game isn't terribly long, but it's just as long as it should be. You're looking at a 14-hour game, possibly more if you die a lot or if you stick around and look for collectibles. Multiplayer is also included, and it's pretty good. Not great, but enjoyable.
If you're the type of person to get all the collectibles and 100% the game, then you're going to have a blast. Collectibles in MP3 are story-contributing Clues and Golden Guns parts, each Golden Gun needing three parts with mostly two of those guns included in every level. Golden Guns give you 10% more damage and a bigger clip, and can be used as a reskin in multiplayer.
----
Finally, this game was amazing enough to get into my favourites and my 2012 GOTYs. It's a great experience that's worth the cost. 10/10.
