A pretty solid shooter with a good amount of variety, though I do I have a few gripes about it.
Excellent narrative; everything Max says throughout the game is spot on, and there's no shortage of it.
That said, the gameplay is pretty much entirely based around using your bullet-time to get headshots, so keep that in mind as you play it. Any shots that are not in the head feel like you're just wasting bullets.
I'm not a fan of the checkpoint system and really miss any sort of quicksave and quickload options. It makes it significantly harder to optimize your play.
The control also feels a lot "looser" than previous Max Payne games. I'm sure this is played up as Max being older and far less agile, but it can still feel a bit frustrating just the same.
Overall, it's certainly worth getting if only to hear Max's thoughts on this newest human cesspool of crime.

When I purchased this game, I expected a fun but otherwise unremarkable shooter. I was pleasantly surprised to find that it was far more than that. Not only was the gameplay top-notch, but the story and characters were surprisingly well developed for a shooter - I actually found myself interested in the characters and wanted to hear their stories and thoughts. The scenes at the resistance hideout provided a nice interlude where I could relax after a frantic mission and just learn about the world and characters through newspaper clippings and conversations.
The shooting is fast paced and intense, but also leaves room for some satisfying stealth play. Most levels had hidden routes where you could sneak around groups of enemies, pick off patrolling guards or stealthily take down the commanding officers. Alternatively, you could grab two assault rifles or shotguns and rush in guns blazing. Both options are equally fun and satisfying.
On the technical side of things, the game suffers from some optimization issues and engine limitations. I personally find the aesthetic of the game quite pleasing from a distance, but the fidelity of the textures is sub-par up close. Textures can look muddy or pixelated when close to the camera and experience some pop-in, especially on less-powerful computers. The game has no in-game option for anti-aliasing, leading to jaggy edges, but that can be forced through a driver control program easily enough for a vastly improved image. Additionally, the engine does not take advantage of more than one GPU so SLI or Crossfire setups don't provide improved performance.
I was able to run this maxed out at 1080p on a GTX 670 while getting a (mostly) solid 90fps. Attempting to run this in nvidia surround, however, tanked my framerate to about 16 or 17fps.
Technical issues asside, I highly recommend this to anyone looking for a fun, fast-paced shooter.

This is easily one of the best games I've played in a long time.
Sure, it's nothing but a mindless "shoot 'em up game" with filthy nazi's, but that's only if you play like that. There's four possible distinct playstyles: Stealth, cover based/tactical, bullet inferno, and boom boom. It's very likely that playing any one of those on their own would prove to be a dreadfully dull and boring game, but it's also very easy to mix and match play styles depending on the scenario.
This is a very creative game that clearly remembers the franchise's roots in old school 90's shooters and pays homage to that bygone era by incorperating dual weild on almost all the weapons, including the "sniper rifle", using vibrant and fun colors, and near-endless murder of hundreds, perhaps thousands, of unsympathetic baddies.
To be clear, this isn't just another "old school shooter", it takes pointers from the newer generations of games by having a real story, a story which happens to be extremely creative and refreshing, and featuring a small amount of health regeneration. Normally, I find health regeneration a negative in this kind of game, but the way it's executed makes it really good. Essentially, you regen health in chunks of 20 HP. If your HP is under the next increment of 20 but above the last one, you regen to the next increment (21 HP = Regen to 40, 20 HP = no regen).
This is a definite contender for Game of the Year and is easily one of the most fun and creative games I've played in far too long.

Dont get me wrong, Robocraft is a great game and is very fun to play due to its independent genre, however there are many issues and complaints that not only myself, but many others have. However, i know if i list too many problems, if the dev team sees this, they will probably not even consider it.(or consider it anyway) So, im just going to list two of my biggest complaints:
1. The game has become a very pay-to-win game, otherwise known as, if you payed to get premium, you can essentially beat anyone who has not payed for premium. If you do not buy it, it takes a very long time to grind for parts you want, even with the forge and recycler. If you do buy it, you get double the chance to get what you want from battles and also you can just buy protonium crates to get good items and build your dream robot.
2. Something is seriously off with scoring in games. I have played as and seen people who have scored top kills and damage with least deaths and still gotten lowest on their teams.(These were all in deathmatch so the score you get from capturing fusion towers wasnt a factor) A particular person I remember was AFK the entire game and got no damage, kills, assists, or heal. All he had was 2 deaths, and he got 2nd on his team. Scoring should be based more on damge and healing, not on kills. Many, many times people will score the highest damge and the lowest kills because of kill steals.
Again, Robocraft is a great game and is fun, but dev team... listen to your fanbase! make updates that people want, not updates that make them stop playing.

Despite being a Source game, it still manages to look good and run on pretty much any computer you throw at it. The music is well-timed and great to listen to, even outside of the game. Oh... and the game has 2 player cooperative play and an official map creator. Even if you beat the game, the player created content will keep you busy. (I recommend Mevious' maps if you want a challenge)

I can recommend this game, even at full price. I bought this game on release, when it was $40, and I still don't feel ripped out of my money.

It's one of the most enjoyable games I've played, but paying for membership is practically mandatory; it's wayy too grindy if you don't have the membership benefits. Joining a competent outfit is also a very good idea, as you receive certain multipliers and such, making it less grindy even for nonpaying players.
10/10 if you're willing to pay 8ish dollars a month
6/10 if you're not willing to spend a penny
Also, you need a decent computer. It's practically mandatory. Tweaking the graphics settings is also a very good idea for usable FPS.
(For reference, I have an i5-4590 and a GTX 1070, and I get 100+fps with tweaked settings, but only 50ish with all graphics maxed. Of course, FPS also dips below this when I'm a 100+v100+ fight.)
The combined arms aspect of the game is admittedly unbalanced in places. As a general rule, the game's overall meta seems to be drifting from a vehicle and air-support centric playstyle to a more noob-friendly "infantryside" meta, much to the disappointment of vets whomst'd've already sunk in hundreds of hours of playtime (or like $20) into attaining the perfect loadouts for their vehicles of choice. Air-to-Air (and the overall air meta), specifically, has taken one too many nerfs, and it's practically unplayable, now that everything on the ground is bristling with ground-to-air weapons and such. A large number of the game's "skyknights" (air-to-air only veterans) have downright quit because of the state of air play. Still, tank gameplay is rewarding at times, and I haven't even touched Harassers yet (dune buggy-like attack vehicles designed to flank and outrun enemies), so I may have more to look forward to from this game. (I haven't played since the ground vehicles were recently rebalanced, so it also may be garbage-trash).
The infantry aspect of the game is decent, but there's a large emphasis on numbers over skill. Hordes of noob platoons usually win against a handful of squads of skilled players. It's fairly unusual to find a truly balanced fight between factions.
The entire base-building aspect of the game makes me feel like I need chemo, but if you're willing to sink in hundreds of dollars (and I sincerely doubt you are) then you may enjoy this aspect of the game. It's a part of the game I steer clear of, but some players like it.
The general direction of the dev team is encouraging. Actual work is being done on the game, and genuine progress is being made at a very respectable rate (new vehicles are being considered and near-implemented, new weapons, rebalancing of things, etc., as seen on the test server). However, the emphasis on base building (which, to their credit, they're moving away from) is generally despised by the community. Still, the dev team generally does a decent job of communicating with the playerbase and taking our ideas into real change in the game.
Overall, I'd cautiously recommend this game to a friend. It's free, after all, and worth at least a try (though admittedly the start of the game left a bad taste in my mouth- Koltyr is AIDs incarnate; the start of the game isn't terribly noob-friendly). Still, I'd recommend trying it out.

Alright, i think the game has been out long enough and panned out enough to write a propper review of it.
Planetside 2 like the original is a First Person Shooter MMO. It is set on a world known as Axuraxis and battles are fought across 4 very very large continents. It has three factions, The Terran Republic which is the "Government" for say, loyalists and a professional army. Their guns and technology are all centered on speed over heavy damage and versitility. They possess the fastest Aircraft, Tanks, and guns in the game.
The Second faction, The New Conglomerate, are a band of Rebels or so called Freedom Fighters. Their theme is that of a rebel band who used to be miners and workers who have repurposed their tools for weapons to fight the power. Their technology is focesed on Defense and Damage. They possess the Hardest hitting weapons and vehicles in the game at the cost of a considerable slower Rate of fire for their weapons and Slow movement for their vehicles  compared to the other 2 factions.
The Third faction is The Vanu Soveirnty, Like the New conglomerate this faction is also a rebel faction that split off from the Terran republic. However, they do not fight for an idea of "freedom" like the NC does. These rebels have found left over alien technology on Auraxis and have converted them into their own use. They are much like a Cult, trying to spread "Truth and Enlightenment" to the other factions. Their faction is focused on Alien weaponry and Versitility. They do not do  quite as much damage as the NC nor are they as fast as the TR, but for that sacrifice they possess extremely versitile weapons and vehicles. Their Main Battle Tank the "Magrider" is a hover tank with the ability to strafe and scale mountains that the NC and TR's treaded counter parts simply can not do. The weapons they use are unique in how they fire, suffering from very little bullet drop like traditional firearms but as the cost of much more horizontal recoil or "Sway".
The game is a never ending Ground and Air war that is persistant. Unlike modern Shooters such as Battlefield or Call of Duty, there are no "Levels". It is fought on a gigantic map, the battlefield changing each time you take a base and move to the next. It also offers the feeling of a "real" war. It is commonplace to find battles involving 200 or more people, hordes of infantry advancing across the landscape with Tanks behind them and Aircraft battleing above them.
It is the only game of its kind to offer this unique experience of being part of a war and it is glorious.
As for the bad parts of the game, It does unfortunately have a Cash shop and it does allow those who pay real money to unlock new weapons and abilities without earning the XP (or certs as they are called) to get them. However on a game with the scope of battles being on such a massive scale, you do not tend to notice this. There are no weapons that are "overpowered" and ruin the game because you dont want to spend real money. They are all rather suprisingly well balanced, each having their ups and downs.
Luckily as well, unlike most Free to play games with a cash shop, it is very possible to progress and unlock items without spending a literal eternity to do it. Unlike other free to play games as well, it is by far one of the most beautiful and good looking shooters on the market. The Quality of its graphics and engine beg the question "why is this not a 60 dollar game like BF or CoD".
In all if you are looking to feel like you are part of a real war that actually matters and to experience what no other FPS to date has successfully captured, it is most certainly worth the download, if only to try it. Whether you like to be a shock trooper infantryman, a tanker, a dog fighter or even just a support role such as ferrying troops to the front line in a transport, this game has it for you.
As Unbiasedly as possible 10/10, may the war never end.

I was expecting Wolfenstein: The New Order to be just another generic shooter using a classic series to drive interest but I was pleasantly surprised to find the game to be a fun and engrossing FPS with a fantastic story and great gunplay mechanics.
The game takes place in 1946 onwards after the Nazi's won WWII and you play agent William 'BJ' Blazkowicz in a Allied force team taking on General Wilhelm "Deathshead" Strasse and his high-tech weapon and human experiment lab. The story goes much deeper as the game progresses with lots of detail and narrative development but I won't expand at the risk of spoiling such a captivating plot.
The presentation is slick and the locations are very nicely designed. It captures the classic feel of the Wolfenstein games and brings itself into the modern gaming era with a polished engine and atmospheric missions. The guns are huge fun to use and the combat is fast paced and fluid.
However the game is guilty in some respects of falling victim to the typical modern day shooters we see today. There are too many scripted sequences and forced gameplay scenarios which mimic that of the campaigns of Call of Duty and Battlefield. The cutscenes are plentiful too although these are intriguing rather than sometimes annoying like the frequent 'push-button to activate scripted events'.
The game isn't massive - I estimate perhaps 10+ hours although there is plenty of replay value here. There is no multiplayer either but Wolfenstein The New Order is a smart and brilliant game in its own right.
Unfamiliar fans of the series may want to hold back and wait until the price drops but if you are a fan of Wolfenstein and/or love FPS games; this is definitely worth a look today

So. Wolfenstein. Probably not the game you'd expect to hit the some of the highest heights of storytelling that you’ll see in a game. Also probably not the game you'd expect to deliver it all with a deep and frequently creative narrative. Creative manners of evisceration, is perhaps more in line with preconceptions, but certainly not in presentation, tone and story in which The New Order excels. All of the pieces of Wolfenstein may not be new, but the manner in which it is told is debilitating fresh, and effective. Within thirty minutes, you’re hooked, with one of the most effective openings you’ll see in any form of this genre. If you couldn’t already tell, The New Order does a great deal to subvert your expectations.
By appearances, the alternate history setting of Nazi domination, complete with quazi-supernatural weapons and
is utterly absurd, and with a lead character when initialised harks back to the Duke Nukem era, it often seems like Wolfenstein is doing all it can to undermine itself. Thankfully, elements from that setting are picked with care, highlighting and providing insightful, if not undiscovered (we've had a lot of texts about war guys) commentary on dystopia, power (or the distinct lack thereof) and universal causality. Thankfully, the game never takes itself too seriously, lest it sway too far from the somewhat pulpy  topic, managing to blend the more light-hearted elements of its roots with a sickly, cynical and all-round rather lovely tongue in it’s cheek.
Wolfenstein, and the folks over at Machine Games know how to craft a tale, and it's this presentation on which The New Order can hang its hat. It achieves levels of beauty, nuance, and depth frequently reached for by other studios, but almost as frequently lays unobtained. In contrast to practically every other game of this size, The New Order knows when to shut the hell up. Dialogue and timing is sharp and acerbic, animation is top-notch cinematography is often stunning, conveying a tremendous sense of confidence in its presentation, close to all of it earned. It’s super slick, and often a joy to expertise and partake in. Characters are strongly defined in a concise and engaging manner, setting them up to be utilized in a cacophony of intelligent and sincere personal relationships, but engage with the setting in a remarkably mature and often darkly comedic manner. While it can occasionally feel that the size of the cast being dealt with is a little too large for what is a 10 hour game, Wolfenstein is nothing if not constantly engaging, and the many twists, turns and heavy-hitting moments you encounter along the way lead up a remarkable conclusion that embodies all that this game does right.
All of this seems to forget the combat system within the game, which is, on most levels, serviceable, if not much else. The combat is pretty stock standard. You've got your iron sights, you've got your hypermobility, and you've got your moments of typical action-movie scale. A means of differentiation is the game’s dual wielding mechanic, which lets you forgo accurate aiming for, say, a couple of semi-automatic shotguns. While initially fun, it doesn’t have the legs as a core gameplay mechanic (perhaps exacerbated by the ammo shortages you’ll usually find yourself in) Stealth is usually a valid option, but you're not incentivised to go in any particular direction, as going in guns ablaze is usually equally effective, and will get you in and out in quicker time.  One criticism is the mini-bosses scattered throughout the game. These mechanised soldiers are boringly bullet-spongy, usually requiring spending a couple of minutes ducking in and out of cover, intersected with the unloading with a machine gun for a few seconds.
Thankfully, the combat is more than enjoyable enough to pull through what is one of the most effective examples of explicit storytelling within a video game. If you’re interested in what a linear experience can provide when taken in context with what is effective in other forms of media, or just want to hear what is a remarkably enjoyable and thoughtful story, The New Order is a game you shouldn't pass over.

A lot of times people have a difficult time telling where to start with a review, but I think the most important part of a game is whether or not it's functional, Wolfenstein: The New Order seems to be a decent PC Port, with my first generation i7 I have been able to get the game running at 50-60 fps throughout most of the game without many dips below 30 at all, at high-ish settings (V-sync disabled, haze flare post effects off, and shadow resolution set to to 4096).
There are moments where I have encountered some performance issues though, some times while playing the game, the frame rate will dip down to sub 30fps and be barely playable, sometimes there are graphical problems where pink will show up randomly in character models during animation, and sound will be completely off synch. However, I was able to fix it simply by just closing the game and reopening it.
Now on to the actual game. I will try to be as spoiler free with this as I possibly can.
Now here's the other important part, is the game actually good. Yes.
Gunplay, while not realistic at all, is really cool. Each weapon has two different firing methods that add some variety on how you can play through the game. For example, the pistol that regularly fires three burst shots has an attachable silencer which makes going through some of the levels more stealthy a lot simpler, and the sniper rifle's secondary firing mode turns it into a laser assault rifle which is incredibly handy for killing the mechanical unit.
There is a bit of a problem with this particular aspect, in that you can't access the secondary fire functions for each weapon until you unlock it on a particular chapter throughout your first playthrough, but once you get to the second playthrough, all firing modes are unlocked and you are a little more free in how you want to play the game, which makes it a lot easier.
One of the things that I do like about this game, is that there is definitely an incentive to play through the game at least twice. There's a choice you can make at the very beginning of the game which unlocks one of two different time lines. There isn't much difference in terms of the story that takes place between the two time lines, there's a very minor character that changes (would have been nice if this had more significance, but it's interesting enough), but the main difference is the types of unlockables you can get.
One time line has you collecting health upgrades, which add a permanent extra ten hit points to your maximum health for each one you collect, and the other lets you get armour upgrades (which increase how much armour you pick up by 10% for each you collect).  Armour only ever goes up to 100, but health can be overcharged, just like in classic first person shooters like Doom. If you go above your maximum health, you will gain extra hitpoints that go down until they hit your max hit point level (100 when you start, but more as you collect health upgrades).
There are also Call of Duty-like perks that you can get by killing Nazis with different weapons in different ways, playing through the game stealthily, and by (unfortunately) grinding at certain points of the game. These are fun to collect, and like your health upgrades, and secondary fire options, carry over to your next playthrough, all making playing through the hardest difficulty much easier.
Enemies are varied enough in that they never really seem to get old, AI can be a little bit stupid in some points, and it really shows during the stealth part of stages. Make no mistake, this game is an action FPS, with only some stealth elements. Certain sections of any given stage will have you trying to remain undetected while you try and kill commanders who will set an alarm off. It's still fun, but it's not nearly as in depth as games like Metal Gear Solid or Deus Ex, but it gets the job done. Using your throwing knives and taking out enemies using the knife with the take downs in the game is really satisfying, even if the animations aren't too varied.
The story is satisfying, if not a little bit anticlimactic.  There's some genuinely disturbing moments throughout the game with the different enemy characters you encounter, and the friendly ones aren't written too badly, especially considering that this is a video game.
It's a fun game, I'd recommend it anyways.

A fully rounded real-time strategy game that's simple to grasp with full, playable tutorial mission to get you started (as William Wallace of Scotland) and really hit that magic formula where town-growing and tactical defense are equally enjoyable.  Age Of Empires II: Age Of Kings (its full title) is set in mediaeval times covering a time period of some 1000 years and is a mixture of resource gathering, town building, research and development of technologies and Wonders, and stategic defence and town attack with multitudous unit types from knights to elephants!  There is a full story-rich campaign where you will play as various legendary leaders from the Middle Ages around the world such as Saladin and Joan Of Arc (with unique units to each character).  The campaign is immensely enjoyable and surprisingly informative, where you re-enact famous battles or battle through foreign towns (plundering them and making them your own) without being able to change the course of history.
There is also the option to play a sandbox game where you can choose to play one of several nations (again with unique units to each) and this never seems to get old.  Start with a new and small town with very basic resources, and try to build it to a much larger town and conquer other NPC towns on the map before they conquer you!  The game also offers full multiplayer support.
Age Of Empires II HD is still the same game it always was.  The single biggest changes are the much-improved resolution over the (now very old) original and full compatibility with today's Windows versions (no more needing to kill explorer.exe to play)!  The HD version also allows the player to carry more units than the original.  Finally, the equally excellent expansion The Conquerers is included at no extra charge.  The game doesn't look pixely or low-resolution, and it's held up surprisingly well for a game first released in 1999.  The HD remake ensures the game looks as good now (on high resolution wide-screen monitors) as it did back in the days of low res 4:3 monitors.  What the HD version is NOT is a complete remake, but a remake was never needed; the changes just restore the game back to its former glory.
Absolutely.  This title is often on sale so you don't have to pay full price if you're patient.  It's a delight not to need discs any longer, and to be able to run the game without killing explorer.exe processes in order to play.  It's also nice to have full wide-screen support and those all-important extra units.
It won't feel like a different game (it isn't), but it's been lovingly restored to the game it always was - for today's PCs.
An excellent and very addictive game from the age of traditional strategy that will sink many hours of your time without the steep learning curve often associated with today's strategy titles.  If you like games where you can build a town, defend it and conquer other towns, then this game is perfect.

B.J. Blaskowicz is back and he's killing more Nazis in this reboot to the Wolfenstein franchise. When I first heard about this game I figured Bethesda would screw it up and make it boring and add realism for no reason whatsoever. I'm happy to say I was completely wrong as Machinegames developed this game and they did a great job.
The goal of any Wolfenstein game should be to feel like your an one man army and the only thing standing between the Nazis and world domination is you. That feeling is definitely in this game as you make your way through 16 levels of shooting, and killing. The story is essentially that it's 1960 and the Nazis won World War II with there advanced technology thanks to the villain of the game General Deathshead. It's up to you to find the resistance and combat the Nazis and defeat Deathshead once and for all.
The game runs on the idEngine 5 which means it's not a technical marvel to look at and there are some fairly low res textures scattered throughout the game and there were lip-synching issues  but that's honestly not a big problem as graphics and one minor bug do not a game make. What makes a game is the gameplay and this game delivers in spades.
Wolfenstein: The New Order does a great job of bringing you back to the days when shooters were fun and more than just Call of Duty Modern Black OPS Battlefield 37: Now With Even More Shades of Gun Metal Gray. It's not realistic in the least and doesn't take itself very seriously at all and that's always a good thing to me because they're trying to throw everything they can and see how ridiculous they can get(laser guns on the Moon, need I say more). The game controls great and I never had a problem moving, shooting or stealthing around the levels trying to murder tons of Nazis.
If you're loooking to go back to the days of health meters, and feeling like a one man army this is game for you as it delivers the classic Wolfenstein experience with updated graphics.

Man, a couple years ago when I first started playing this game, it was so much fun! There was a balanced matchmaking system and every weapon was usable. Then they added things like nano-bot weapons (medics), and the Boss Battle mode, which allowed 1 Insanely powerful bot, or 4 pretty strong bots, to go up against a full team of low-level bots. Then they decided to remove the Tech-Tree, forcing you to unlock thing at a set rate, not allowing you to work to get the parts you were actually going to use. They also added a feature where after 10 seconds of not being damaged your bot would be completely healed, making nano-bots worthless and anyone who mained the medic role was basically screwed. Then they added the ability to have multiple weapon systems, which totally screwed up the balance. For example, the rail gun was insane at long ranges, and useless at short ranges, sometimes one shotting bots if you could land a shot, which was really hard to do. But with the removal of the pilot seat, just making you die when your bots health went below a certain threshold, this got rid of a bunch of the strategy in Robocraft, now you just spray and pray at bot instead of trying to figure out where their pilot seat was and targeting that section. But now if someone gets up and personal with you as a sniper, ou can just switch to a different weapon and take them down. This also allowed for people who either farmed for years, or spent a lot of money, to make insanely overpowered bots with no counter, and because they skewed up the matchmaking, these people get randomly put into low-level games. Then they decided it would be a good idea to remove the premium currency, which could be used to buy cosmetics, and if you had spent money on the game? Well looks like you will be getting some low-level crate in return. And with the expulsion of premium currency, they also got rid of the normal currency and replaced it with 'Cubits', so if you had coughed up some cash for the gold developer flag that cost something like $50, well now everyone can get it. In that same update, they also made so when you complete a battle you don't actually get any money, just a crate which can be opened to reveal some garbage items that are way below your current level. And also, if you try to sell these items yo buy what you really want, your only getting %25 of what it's worth, so you'll be farming for years before you build anything decent. Man, a couple years ago when I first started playing this game, it was so much fun! There was a balanced matchmaking system and every weapon was usable. Then they added things like nano-bot weapons (medics), and the Boss Battle mode, which allowed 1 Insanely powerful bot, or 4 pretty strong bots, to go up against a full team of low-level bots. Then they decided to remove the Tech-Tree, forcing you to unlock thing at a set rate, not allowing you to work to get the parts you were actually going to use. They also added a feature where after 10 seconds of not being damaged your bot would be completely healed, making nano-bots worthless and anyone who mained the medic role was basically screwed. Then they added the ability to have multiple weapon systems, which totally screwed up the balance. For example, the rail gun was insane at long ranges, and useless at short ranges, sometimes one shotting bots if you could land a shot, which was really hard to do. But with the removal of the pilot seat, just making you die when your bots health went below a certain threshold, this got rid of a bunch of the strategy in Robocraft, now you just spray and pray at bot instead of trying to figure out where their pilot seat was and targeting that section. But now if someone gets up and personal with you as a sniper, ou can just switch to a different weapon and take them down. This also allowed for people who either farmed for years, or spent a lot of money, to make insanely overpowered bots with no counter, and because they skewed up the matchmaking, these people get randomly put into low-level games. Then they decided it would be a good idea to remove the premium currency, which could be used to buy cosmetics, and if you had spent money on the game? Well looks like you will be getting some low-level crate in return. And with the expulsion of premium currency, they also got rid of the normal currency and replaced it with 'Cubits', so if you had coughed up some cash for the gold developer flag that cost something like $50, well now everyone can get it. In that same update, they also made so when you complete a battle you don't actually get any money, just a crate which can be opened to reveal some garbage items that are way below your current level. And also, if you try to sell these items yo buy what you really want, your only getting %25 of what it's worth, so you'll be farming for years before you build anything decent. They have also added some 'super-weapon' like a lock one missile launcher, aero flak, ion distorter and basically a chain gun. With the introduction of these weapons, the old ones are really lacking and gameplay isn't very balanced. They also completely got rid of the boss battle mode, which was my favorite game mode!

Those of us who played this game from very early on will remember how great a game this could have been, and how now it doesn't have a chance of lasting long term, even though easily could have if the devs had decided to play the long game instead of trying to make a quick buck. Well, I suppose I kind of ranted on about this, but this really could have been a great game. Fairwell Robocraft.

Being a big fan of RAGE and its engine, I was really looking forward to this game. But it left me uneasy having bought it full price when it was released.
GOOD
Story is excellent and it will make you emotionally invested. This is very welcome counter-balance to heavy FPS action. The story will never let you forget who you're fighting against. Sometimes it gets a bit overbearing, but there is plenty of jokes and funny references to go around.
BAD
I reloaded RAGE just to make sure I was remembering this engine correctly. Unfortunately I was. This game is technically one BIG mess. It doesn't support anti-aliasing or anisotropic filtering. If you enable it in the console, your FPS will go into crawl. It is worth noting that RAGE supported all these essential PC features fine back in 2011.
UGLY
Texture memory management is a joke and even with any of the latest graphics cards the game will look like it's from 2011 all over again. The ugly part is that even RAGE looked better back in 2011. Now in 2014, the same engine is used, but in far  worse way than in 2011. That is utterly inexcusable. For example, none of the shortcomings of the original RAGE implementation were addressed, such as texture pop-in. If you're a PC owner, you will be disappointed as this game's graphics appears to be dumbed down due to the current "next gen" consoles.
CONCLUSION
Despite brilliant story line, believable acting and satisfying gaming action, it's the technical execution which ultimately brings it down on PC. You may have heard an advice from other reviewers to wait in order to get this game from "bargain bin" and I concur.

On a planet with similar climate properties as earth, there are 3 factions fighting over multiple facilites in territories (regions) in which they can annex and capture and expand their grasp of the surface area in these 4 continents that are snow, desert, forest, and swamplike environments. The game spans to thousands of people per server, resulting in a massive battlefield atmosphere.. Classes, Fleets of gunships, convoys of tanks, platoons of troops etc.
The gameplay itself is solid, with bulletdrop on many weapons and movement being comparable yet sub-par. For example, you can scale sides of cliffs of infantry while standing on nothing but thin air. But that doesn't bother me at all, because doing that gives me an advantage for good sniping spots.
Moving onto the dynamics... this game is FREE-TO-PLAY! Which is great, having any one of my friends just hop in and play. There are 15$ month memberships and bundles where the per month price decreases the more you subscribe.. And there is also the daybreak cash premium currency, this is mostly useless unless you wish to buy decoratives or armor for your character, and new camos. But everything else that actually affects gameplay can be acquired by Certs (In-game credit points) for every 250 experience you earn.
For the graphics and optimization of the game... The game itself is poorly optimized but if you do run it at highest settings it does look pretty damn good. On my gtx 460 i ran it at straight up medium settings with about 35 fps, but now with a gtx 970, it is absolutely amazing at max.
Now to summarize this game up, it is a must download and try out for sure.. deff the best MMOFPS i've played, and when it was first released in 2012, i thought it was ahead of it's time, and in some aspects it still is. There may be a feel of repetition and grinding when you're playing by yourself, but once you get a great group of friends going you'll find yourself putting countless hours into the game.

WARNING:GAMEPLAY SPOILERS
In all seriousness, this is one of the best run and gun dumb shooters to date. Whilst it still sometimes take you away from the shooting action for too long, you definitely get way more action than in most modern shooters, and they keep cutscenes to a bare minimum.
It is also whacky game. Do not expect realism in the game whatsoever. You can duel wield automatic shotguns, fire laser sniper rifles, and control a Nazi mech suit. Sometimes I feel it takes itself a bit too seriously, but then something crazy happens and I forgive the game. The guns do have a good amount of kick and feel real good to shoot. It is up there with Killing Floor with how good the shooting feels.
Stealth is a viably choice. While very basic, it is essential in some levels. Not all though; if you like running and gunning and don't prefer stealth oriented play-throughs, you are still good, you just may have a slightly more difficult experience. Exploration is also key to survival. The levels aren't extremely open, but you still must explore to find health, armor, ammo, and golden collectibles.
TL;DR:Great run and gun shooter for any fan of the FPS genre, and IMO greatest FPS for a while.

So I forgot that I was gonna make a big review for this game since it was my most anticipated game of the year since I grew up playing the Wolfenstein series I never wanted it to stop but alas everything always comes to an end. (Just a quick heads up about Wolfenstein) Wolfenstein was basically the game that started the fps genre and thanks to it we wouldn't have Call of Duty, Battlefield, and much more. Wolfenstein is about a American soldier who has to go through many/crazy missions that always involve Nazis. Basically the Nazis have achieved in technology that we couldn't achieve including robots, mutant soldiers, and plus the atom bomb. Wolfenstein mainly focuses on single player only because the story to the series is too good. Now on to the game Wolfenstein: The New Order.
Wolfenstein: The New Order takes place in the year 1960 where the Nazis won the war now they rule the world with a iron fist. The character you play as is B.J. Blazkowicz the man who can save the world. The game starts out fabulous with stunning graphics including PC oh yeah one more thing this game is beautiful on PC especially on highest graphics. The prologue is probably the best mission because it shows that we are being hit hard by the Nazi war machine. It also shows how B.J. gets in a coma and wakes on the one faithful day in the year 1960. When you get to explore more later in the game you will get to see what most of Europe looks like under Nazi control including London, Great Britain, Poland, and Berlin, Germany. The developers decided to make nearly every weapon dual wield including marksman rifles, assault rifles, pistols, and shotguns you can also carry around a mini gun if that isn't enough. The game as well has many secrets all over the chapters and some are easy to find and some are not. You can literally walk right by a piece of gold, note, or a enigma code (Enigma codes are codes where you can unlock bonuses to the game).
The game has only one problem that I've seen a lot and that is the AI (Artificial Intelligence) the AI will sometimes not duck N cover from a grenade or even gun fire they are late sometimes but other than that the game is still fantastic. Wolfenstein: The New Order is a marvelous game that ends the franchise very well and I hope it will add some DLC to the game.
Other than that the game is fantastic and will always remain in my heart. 9.1/10

The setting is different, yes. So is Max - but James McCaffrey does an excellent job bringing him to life again with almost everything you remember.
The story is more chronological than before (with some flashbacks to the past, e.g. NYC) and not as great as in previous games - however, it is still well above the average. There are still some twists and interesting plot points.
Gameplay is flawless from both technical and fun point of view. Gameplay alone is worth the price. There are several very real things which I haven't seen anywhere else yet (e.g. sweat in heat or some character animations).
Graphics is top-notch with environments being incredibly detailed. Definitely worth those 35 GB.
Replay value is very high - many game modes to choose from, collectibles, "grinds". Oldschool mode and Max's original skin/character model being one part of it.
I've encountered 2 things I didn't like:
1.) Some visual effects related to alcohol, painkillers and some other things is too much. There are few short parts when it's difficult to watch the screen.
2.) The game crashed ~3 times during cut-scenes. Pausing the game before crash helped to solve the issue. 4 GB of RAM (+1 GB of VRAM) is probably not enough sometimes.
Other than that, the game is fantastic. I'm pleasantly surprised with its qualities.

So if you have a decent mid level tower, and you don't play Planetside 2, you need to kind of play. If you don't know anything about it, I will describe it in two ways. And please, wait till the end to make any judgments.
First, It's Free! Minor cash shop purchases and cosmetic changes, a subscription model, but nothing pay to win. This is the first ever WORKING free to play game I have ever seen.
Second, it's a Massively Multiplayer First Person Shooter. Say that five times fast. Ok, so, this game is HUGE! Each "map" is an entire planet, which you can seamlessly travel between, and take part in the conquest of each. They've also set the World Record for how many players were duking it out at once, which is 1158 people. That's on a single one of their maps, or planets. That means it could possibly happen on all four planets at once! CRAZY! Compare that to matches of Call of Duty or Battlefield where you have 32 and 64 players at once, respectively. That's a hell of a lot. On top of that, you have different classes, tanks, aircraft, weapons, etc. This is like Battlefield on CRACK!
So, check it out. It's on Steam, it's on their website. Watch some videos, but try it out for yourself. It costs you nothing but time. And for you console gamers out there, I believe it also recently came out on PS4 as well. Get out there and play it! GAME ON!

When Max Payne is around, any glass that’s half-empty is soon to be entirely empty, literally and figuratively. The guy can’t catch a break and has decided to drown his grief in alcohol. Having lost his family in the previous installments of the Payne franchise, he gets entangled in all sorts of nastiness again this time around, when a gig as a bodyguard in Sao Paolo goes south. In a gravelly voice and with a gloomy, sardonic demeanor, he narrates his woes to the player, who mostly gets to take control during the parts of the story where there’s shooting to be done. The monologue has a distinct hard-boiled/noir detective feel to it and Max’s world is one of double-crossing crooks, in which innocence is a rare commodity. Odd visual glitches occur and spoken words float across the screen from time to time, visualizing his feeling of being hung-over and off-balance.
Despite being a grade A boozehound, as well as addicted to painkillers which magically heal bullet wounds, Max’s reflexes are apparently still superhuman. As before, his speed and marksmanship are portrayed in the form of Bullet Time. This gameplay conceit was made popular by the first Max Payne game and has been incorporated in so many games since, that it has almost become cliché. It means that you have the ability to see things happen in slow-motion while you can aim and shoot in real-time. So you can take a leap sideways or forwards, sailing majestically through the air, while strategically pumping bullets into various parts of your enemies as their bullets whiz past you slow enough to see them travel. You will need to make use of this tactic a lot. A mechanic that allows you to take cover has been added this time around, giving you a few more strategic options, but because your foes tend to come running at you and silencers aren’t effective, stealth is short-lived and things tend to get hectic. Thankfully, you also have the option to blow up cars, gas tanks (and so on) near your enemies by shooting them, meaning you can cut down enemy numbers at a good pace.
Max has a low tolerance for bullets, by game standards (though he is still a fair bit more resistant than people are in real life), meaning you don’t last long at the normal firing rate. So you will find yourself suspended in midair quite a bit, possibly ending your journey sooner than planned by embarrassingly crashing into a wall or some other obstacle that you didn’t notice before taking flight. Though it looks silly, it does give the action movie acrobatics a charmingly realistic counterpoint.
Seeing how your survival often depends on taking out multiple targets on the go, before time resumes its normal speed, it’s annoying that the game doesn’t make it clear when an enemy is down for the count. When you hit someone, they will drop to the ground, but the amount of bullets it takes to keep them there is unpredictable. You are likely to find yourself getting shot in the back now and then, because one of the guys you thought was dead – a reasonable assumption after emptying a clip on him – was actually just mildly inconvenienced.
Max Payne 3 looks great. The beautifully detailed surroundings invite you to look around and there are rewards when you do so in the shape of ‘clues’ to be found and parts of guns that – if you collect them all – give a bonus on damage and ammo capacity. But the game is schizophrenic when it comes to pacing; often, if you take a moment to wander off the beaten path to find these goodies, either Max’s voice-over or a character you have with you, will remind you that time is of the essence and that you really should be hauling♥♥♥♥♥
Unfortunately the game is not without bugs and glitches. Some are hilarious one-offs, such as the time when Max, after landing on the floor on his back, started spinning around like a break-dancer on speed.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a breath of fresh air. It offers an alternate history of the mid-twentieth century where the Nazis won the second world war and ruled the world afterward. You play as William B.J. Blazkowicz and it's your job to fight back and restore the world to where it once was.
Level design and player freedom are excellent. Throughout the game, you'll find multiple ways to approach a situation which primarily allows you to choose between being stealthy or going in guns blazing. This goes hand-in-hand with the perk system as well; as you play, you unlock perks that are dependent on your playstyle. For example, if you choose a more stealthy approach, one of the first perks that you unlock is the ability to throw knives. While this is an excellent game mechanic, it is very easy for the player to forget about this perk system to the point that it becomes ancillary to the game as a whole.
The enemies in the game are also very good. During the game, you are progressively faced with enemies of ever increasing firepower and combat mechanics. First, you start out by fighting basic soldiers who will occasionally be accompanied by attack dogs. Then as you progress through the game, the enemies become stronger and more advanced. Now, on top of the soldiers that you were fighting, you're also fighting against biochemically engineered super soldiers who take a fair amount of lead to kill.
One of the more noticeable points of this game is how time progresses with respect to the enemies that you face and the weapons that you use. The hour-long prologue of the game takes place in 1946 during the second world war while the rest of the game takes place in 1960. This allowed the game developers to show the progression of technology through the scientific creations of the Nazis. Nazi robots that were present in 1946 have new and updated versions that are better at killing in 1960.
The story is incredibly rich and well written. Characters that were in Return to Castle Wolfenstein and the Wolfenstein that came out in 2009 are back to offer a new chapter to the story. These characters, as well as those that are new, have their own individual progression some of them being more defined than others. The playable character, B.J. Blazkowicz, also evolves as a character to some degree during the course of the game as the other characters change around him as well.
One great thing that Wolfenstein: The New Order does is that it caters to the people who played old school first person shooters in the 1990s. Many of the games back then featured run-and-gun playstyles that featured big guns and lots of ammunition. This game is no different and there is no shortage of Nazis to be killed either. There are also throwbacks to Wolfenstein 3D, such as the consumable dog food that provides health to the player.
While this game is incredibly satisfying and has a lot of good things going for it, there was one problem with it that stood out above everything else: the boss fights. The boss fights in this game offer no real challenge or originality in the way that they play out. Granted, that's how the boss fights were in Wolfenstein 3D and some of the later games in the Wolfenstein series, it would have been a welcome change if the boss fights were more than just a "run here and shoot this" fight.
In summary, this game was incredibly well executed and was absolutely enjoyable to play. I would highly recommend this to any fan of the series or someone that enjoys games with alternate timelines.
Final score: 9 out of 10.

Robocraft. ♥♥♥♥ing Robocraft. Freejam royally flushed this once brilliant game down the disgusting, uncleaned toilet that is the grindy p2w scene.
I have many hours on the standalone one, I used to play it religiously when it was good.
Lemme fill in some backstory before we begin ripping out this things filthy neck with the power of criticism. Robocraft was a game created by the lesser known freejam, a small gamedev company. At the beginning, freejam had built this fair and balanced game with a good amount of weapon and movement combos, along with its unoriginal but intuitive building mechanics. Said mechanics had realistic physics and required you to actually think logically when building your minion of death. The community wasn't toxic or cancerous at all back in these days. Robocraft also boasted about its leveling system, which rewarded players with new parts, better armour and weapons. However, ever since the homing missile update,♥♥♥♥♥♥started to hit the fan fast.
After said update, the community noticed the severe lack of communication that freejam had once used well. They seemed to not care, and the broken weapons only made it worse. Sure, they fixed the missiles, but they broke the 1-shot wonder that is the rail, they ripped the leveling system apart and replaced it with this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ 'buy scraps and then make that thing you wanted' system. They changed the UI around, which most of the community despised due to its complexity compared to the old one. The paint tool was also a money grabber. But the worst is the after match loot.
Freejam implemented a system which rewarded players, regardless on their premium status loot in the form of armour and weapons, the rarity of the loot depended on how well you did in the match. If a normal player got a blue crate, he/she'd get blue items, but if a premium opened it up, they got whatever the normal players got plus items from an extra rarity up. That's double loot and then some. It was very noticeable that premiums got extremely expensive weapons and powerful armour while normal players got the basic, white block, along with glass blocks and some basic weapons. This tore the community in half, with premiums and freejam on one side and us, the normal players on the other.
Most regulars, me included, dropped the game completely due to this. So my advice? Don't bother wasting time. You're just gonna get repeatedly punched in the gut by the p2w hand.

I just reinstalled and retried Planetside 2 for the first time since it came out, and I can say with unwavering certainty that it’s one of the very worst new player experiences I’ve ever had with a game.  It was mesmerizingly terrible at giving a positive first impression.
- Despite having just installed what one should reasonably assume was the latest version via Steam, the game still required a lengthy patching process from its own launcher upon startup, as well as a third party registration, without the ability to sync with my Steam account.
- The tutorial is stretched over a needlessly expansive area, and the narrator’s lines frequently bleed into and play over one another if one moves along ahead of the plodding pace it wants one to.  Needless to say, this renders any help such lines could lend incomprehensible and therefore useless, leaving one to flail about and learn through trial and error, rather than instruction, instead.
- The very first thing I experienced upon connecting to an Instant Action is getting spawn killed with an airstrike not one second after setting foot on the ground.  Fan-♥♥♥♥ing-tastic.
- The UI is one of the very worst I’ve ever encountered in terms of giving mechanical information to new players.  I know it shows information on controlled areas, flashpoints, how many friendlies and hostiles are detected in an area, etc, and that’s all nice; however, there are some much more practical questions it seems intent on not answering.  Where can I spawn?  How can I change respawn locations?  Why, when I attempt to decipher the help menu tooltips for the map, and find that I must use warp facilities to change spawn regions, am I greeted with an insta-death “restricted area” message upon attempting to reach one of those facilities?  Who knows!  I’m just constantly told to click the “Instant Action” tab, and let the game carry me off to wherever it thinks I’m needed, regardless of whether I want that region or not.
- When I attempted to ask other players in the game chat for clarification during the respawn interim of yet another spawn kill, I was greeted with the following automated message: “The dead can’t speak.”  I actually uttered an “are you ♥♥♥♥ing kidding me?” aloud in my office at this point.
I know Planetside 2 is a well-respected game, and I’m sure, once one is familiar with it, that there’s some reason for that.  This isn’t about that.  This isn’t a comprehensive review, nor is it a commentary upon the overall quality of the game. This is simply a commentary regarding the initial impression its current version gives to new, uninitiated players.  The short version is this: I felt unwelcome, not by the players, not by my squad, not by my faction, but by the game itself, as a newcomer to Planetside 2.  At every turn, it seemed as though I was getting punished for not knowing things that a proper tutorial should have taught me, for not realizing the answers to questions I didn’t realize I even needed to ask.  It felt as if it were deliberately obfuscating critical information that it just expected me to know without proper instruction.
I’ll make this as clear as I can: My initial impressions of Planetside 2 were so negative that I’ve no desire to learn the lessons necessary to further understand the game.  I’m sure the answers are there.  I’m just left with such a poor impression of my experience that I’ve no inclination to pursue them.  I’m leaving the game - again - and this time, I’m not returning.

Positive recommendation!
At its core, this is still the classic Age of Empires 2 gameplay experience. I have heard that the multiplayer had some bad bugs when the game launched, but I have also heard that they have (mostly) been fixed and ironed out by this point (I generally play singleplayer anyways, so I might be biased in this regard). All of the campaigns from both the original game and the expansion set are included here. You can discover hours upon hours of historical empire-building strategy and fun!
Basically, this is a classic real-time strategy (RTS) game that has truly stood the test of time. And, it is actually very educational too - this was the game that made me fall in love with world history when I was young; it is at least partly due to the Age of Empires series that I decided to study history at university. So, if you have a young one and want him or her to learn some history while also having fun on the computer, buy Age of Empires 2!
Also, if you have the extra funds, be sure to get the brand-new "Forgotten" DLC expansion, which adds brand-new civilizations, units, and campaigns not seen in the original game or its expansion.
All in all, this game comes highly recommended!

I have heard that the multiplayer had some bad bugs when the game launched, but I have also heard that they have (mostly) been fixed and ironed out by this point (I generally play singleplayer anyways, so I might be biased in this regard). All of the campaigns from both the original game and the expansion set are included here. You can discover hours upon hours of historical empire-building strategy and fun!
Basically, this is a classic real-time strategy (RTS) game that has truly stood the test of time. And, it is actually very educational too - this was the game that made me fall in love with world history when I was young; it is at least partly due to the Age of Empires series that I decided to study history at university. So, if you have a young one and want him or her to learn some history while also having fun on the computer, buy Age of Empires 2!
Also, if you have the extra funds, be sure to get the brand-new "Forgotten" DLC expansion, which adds brand-new civilizations, units, and campaigns not seen in the original game or its expansion.
All in all, this game comes highly recommended!

Max Payne 3 is one of the best games I have played in a while.  When the first Max Payne came out, it was the game that made "Bullet time" popular.  In the third iteration of the game, it is still fun.  It is impressive how much detail has gone into the world you play in.  Rockstar said in one of their developer diaries that they made thousands of different animations to increase immersion and quality, and I believe it. (The game is 30 Gb big)  While doing his trademark dive through the air, Max moves dynamicly and fluidly, the animation is almost never akward.  There are still quite a few issues with the game though, it crashed multiple times in my 9 hour playthrough and there was a strange issue where Max would get stuck behind cover and I could not move.  I would have to restart from the latest checkpoint which was extremely frustrating in hard gun fight.  Lastly, I can not connect to any online game, not that I would really want to play online that much.  After the campaign, you can unlock a few different modes to play with in singleplayer, go through and find collectibles or just have fun in the slo-mo.
8.5/10 would buy

This is going to be as short as possible without missing the important things.
Pros
Incredible gameplay and graphics that combines mmo, rpg,  fps and strategy elements all into one game. This game gives you a feeling like no other fps does when you are in a squad assaulting a base with tanks by your side, aircraft dogfighting overhead, engineers and medics providing support and snipers picking off enemies from afar. This game is super fun with a few of your friends.
Cons
HOWEVER: this game has a really steep learning curve (easily the hardest fps you will find), terrible pay model where 99% of weapons/upgrades can be bought with real money (not cheap either; most guns are $5-10 EACH!!). You can earn every weapon in the game by grinding HARD with it taking a few hours or more to get one weapon depending on your style of play sadly in this meta the fastest way to get stuff is by spawn trapping with a tank and farming infantry, which is not fun if you're the person on the receiving end. Also there is practically no story other than that you fight for a faction in an endless meatgrinder that churns 24/7 with no real events or reward for conquering a continent other than resources and points. While there is a playstyle for all, some playstyles are more imbalanced than others. Also as far as I know the developers have abandoned this game to work on the console version of it, so get it if you want some challenging fun but I definitely do NOT recommend you spend money on Planet$ide 2 as there is nothing promising for the future of this game.

I've played all the Wolfenstein games to date and TNO is my favorite, besides the original 3D back in the 90s.  This storyline is more believable than a zombie alternative universe.  It begs the question, "How would an alternate Nazi universe look like if they had won?"  The gameplay thrusts you into action immediately and doesn't let up, except for some cinematic storytelling, which I found really good.  If I'm going to play a SP game, I want a good story and an immersive atmosphere, along the the typical action and RPG elements I've come to expect.  The perk system is a nice bonus and allows you to play to a specific playstyle, i.e. stealth, tactical, explosives, etc., but you will find that you can master them all if you replay checkpoints and chapters.  While I found Uber not that hard, TNO allows you to replay on harder modes once you find and complete the enigma codes found in game, i.e. hardcore, ironman, etc.  It's a shame you cannot play hardcore plus ironman or any combination of the other two.  Graphically, the Id 5 engine is a great platform and I can run Ultra settings smoothly with an i7, 16GB RAM, and a 780 Ti without any problems.  I would rate Cryengine 3 and Frostbite 3 engine a bit higher, but this engine does an impressive job.  I'd highly recommend this game to any Wolfenstein fan or FPS/RPG shooter fan that doesn't mind the lack of MP, but enjoys a believable alternate future story, great soundtrack and cinematics, and lots of action.  You won't get tired of stabbing, shooting, or blowing up Nazi's, nor will you get tired of them calling you "Schweinehund!"

You're going to see a lot of reviews claiming that this game 'brings old-school shooters' back. That's silly. It's bringing an old-school title to the modern era.
There are excellent cover, leaning, alternate-firing mechanics, and dual wielding weapons to spice up the fps gameplay. Each weapon has a use in the game, a feature that often falls short in many shooters. Do you enjoy stealth killing enemies with silenced pistols and melee stealth kills? You can do that. In fact, you're going to be rewarded when you do that.
There's a nice little 'perk' system to add a little combat advantage to aid your style of play. You'll be able to increase ammo count in your assault rifle magazine for example.
The game isn't all about blasting (Well, it mostly is...) Nazi scum, though. The alternative timeline is fairly absorbing and the characterization is top notch. I didn't think I'd find myself getting invested in some of these characters by the end of the game, but I certainly did.
Worth two-playthroughs.

Polished. The engine is smooth as butter, graphics are vivid and detailed (if a little cartoonish), gameplay is very well-balanced.
One thing I have to mention is the truly excellent menu UI. Full marks to the developers for creating a UI that's snappy and responsive, with no pointless artsy frills. At some point in the recent past, game developers forgot that the point of the menu system is to let players get to the game with minimal fuss, and started making the UI as annoying as possible. I only have the highest praise for W:TNO's designers and programmers for a UI that's not just simple and responsive, but fully keyboard-accessible.
Just about every level starts out with a long unskippable sequence that requires you to do the same things in exactly the same way every time. Note to game designers: no matter how artistic or cinematic technically dazzling or well-executed your intro is, it gets old after the first time. This DESTROYS the replay value of the game. I've launched the game many times intending to replay a level, but scanning the list of chapters and remembering the intro to each one makes me close the game again. The train sequence with Frau Engel is especially long and gets really annoying, even on the first playthrough. These "interactive cutscenes" are ten times worse than the non-interactive ones, because with the latter I can go get a cup of coffee while it plays. With these, I have to sit at the computer and plod through the same actions again and again.
The decision to force the player to look at items and press 'E' to pick up anything, including ammo, seems like a ploy to increase playthrough time. Shooting enemies is fun. Collecting items isn't.
MachineGames need to take a leaf from Crytek and design weapons that actually look dangerous.
I like it when enemies try to flank me, but more often than not they can be looking directly at me and not spot me, just because I'm crouching.
I can headshot someone with dual-wielded pistols from a hundred metres away.
There are very few situations where you can play as a sniper. What's worse, you can't play as a stealthy sniper at all, because the marksman rifle isn't suppressed.
All too often in the game, there are points where you can only do one thing to proceed. This turns that part of the game into nothing but a glorified cutscene.
I'm playing B J Blazkowicz, ultimate badass war hero. Why do I have to find someone's missing toys, or fetch a welder? Don't tell me these are things even badasses do in real life. I'm sure B J also brushes his teeth, but I don't want to play that in a game.
Overall, all of the above add up to very little replay value. I'd have liked a game mode with sandbox-type levels where I can just play through wave after wave of enemies, as opposed to the finely-crafted but restrictive gameplay that the game currently has. Forget story, forget cutscenes, just give me an intense shooter that I can play over and over again, experiencing something different each time. Don't even bring up the "timelines", they're both practically the same.

In my experiences with Planetside 2 I've both loved and hated this game.
Planetside 2 is a Massively Multiplayer 'Battlefield-esq' FPS game with three factions fighting for control of territories. Each faction has its own unique selection of weapons and strengths and weaknesses. The game works like Battlefields conquest game mode where you have to hold and capture points with a variety of weapons/vehicles for your faction. Speaking of factions by the way, let’s break them down.
The rebel, separatist, 'freedom fighters' faction. Represented by the color blue. The NC tend to have the hardest hitting guns in the game but often have a slow rate of fire or are single shot weapons.
The militaristic, tyrannical, jingoistic empire faction. Represented by the color Red. The TC tend to have weapons with big magazines and fast rate of fires but don't do as much damage and have slightly longer reload times.
A cult made up of intellectuals, academics, and worshipers of the 'Vanu', an ancient alien race. Represented by the color Purple. The VS tend to have gimmicky plasma and alien based weapons.
Alright, is that out of the way now? Good.
After picking a faction I felt a little overwhelmed being thrown into the thick of Planetside 2. Being used to Battlefield and FPS games made me a little knowledgeable but my first few battles were hectic, chaotic, and usually ended up with me dying in a matter of seconds. However with all the frustrating battles I was in I also had plenty of satisfying ones.
. It took plenty of errors and deaths to finally figure out the unique 'playstyle' of Planetside 2. The game lacks the polish and shine of other FPS games. The VS purple outfits will look similar to the NC blue for some people, there's no really clear way to tell your teammates apart from the enemy(there is friendly fire in this game), and some factions have guns that seem OP at points. However, when I spent more time playing I came to gradually get used to Planetsides 'feel' and was able to start preforming well and ranking up kills. Assaulting and defending huge robot factories or bio-gardens became a blast. In one particularly epic battle while playing as the VS, we managed to defend a base for two hours from the combined assault of both the TR and NC. At the end of the entire thing it felt like we really accomplished something as a team.
Huge hectic battles
All factions are pretty well balanced
Free (there's an in-game shop where you can buy 'crets'(in game money) and a membership option but I found it's largely unnecessary)
For being a F2P game. There’s still a surprising amount of polish
Graphics are good, certainly not triple A tier, but nice to look at for a F2P game.
The instant action feature is really nice and along with the UI on the spawn screen you can usually find a battle to engage in the second you log on
Want to buy more guns? Lol I hope you like the grind m8
Depending on how many people are playing, certain factions can become completely OP or have much more people in them that can lead to huge imbalances. I've seen certain factions get up to making up 50% of the server and obliterating and capturing everything.
You earn certs at an incredibly slow pace. I'm talking about maybe 2-5 certs
you do well during a life. Maybe it's because I'm still a low level and I understand that they have to make money somehow, but the game is a grindfest.
Unless you join a squad, there's really no communication as a team.
The game is not noob friendly
Overall, I really like Planetside 2 and would recommend it to any friend who likes Battlefield or shooter games. It can get grindy at points and lacks the charm and polish other games have, but for a free game it's pretty good and I can see myself playing it regularly.

Campaign clocks in at around 8-10 hours and is about par for the length of most modern big-budget shooters in the market.
Game uses an optimised Euphoria engine - first debuted by the Grand Theft Auto 4 installments. Copious amounts of motion capture work has been put into this game and it helps to overcome the general floatiness/sluggishness of procedurally-generated movement that GTA4 was known for. A particularly striking moment would be a peripheral segment in the Brazilian slums with a trio of young aspiring footballers having a kickabout.  Being powered with an infrastructure meant for open-world games does come with a trade-off in the form of load times (masked by lengthy unskippable cutscenes). Replayability suffers as a result of the aforementioned loading.
Gunplay matches the best in franchise to date with extremely responsive controls and the return of the shoot-dodge/bullet-time maneuvres. Aiming returns to the era where projectiles travel dead centre without any deviation/spread. Weapon variety covers your usual fare of pistols, submachine guns and rifles - with an option to dual-wield with the lesser firearms. Levels provide cover generously by design and feature believable architecture that serves to mimick their real life counterparts as opposed to a seemingly random assortment of crates and walls. The game is also punctuated by a few rail shooter segments and chase sequences which are placed appropriately and definitely do not overstay their welcome.
Max Payne 3 is presented via a heavy use of cutscenes as opposed to the unique comic-book approach adopted by Max Payne 1 & 2. While the departure from its origins can be somewhat jarring to diehard fans, the cinematics ingame are well-directed and acted out by a competent cast of voice actors. Max himself still comes with a full arsenal of monologic quips and one-liners that he is most fondly remembered by.

Max Payne 3... is this a review? Who the hell knows. To understand my relationship with this game, we have to go back to where it all began, to how I reached this point.
It was a broody Autumn night, the rain beating down on my window like a sick symphony of drummers heralding the fall of summer and the arrival of darker times. Quite literally, a Winter was coming. Like many that fateful night I was drawn to the ever-present glow of the internet, the sick timesink poured over by millions of people just like myself. Grinding out the daily drudgeries by throwing myself head-first into a world without the coldness of reality, a world of code and graphics.
Bidden by some unseen force I found myself staring longily at the list of sales Steam had on their storefront, my eyes finding little to pique my interest at first. I was an ex-student, my finances were about as stable as a fat mouse trying to balance on a house of cards. In short, I was dirt poor.
I wondered what other lost souls were doing the same thing as me, drawn to the deals offered by Gabe Newell himself, that paragon of salesmanship and community relations all bundled into one. They were sheep, every one of them, willing to pump money into a faraway cause simply to lose themselves in a video game for a few precious hours.
Still, my interest slammed into one item in particular, my train of thought crashing to a halt like a twenty car pile-up on the motorway. The pile-up's name? Max Payne 3.
I had heard of the game, seen a few videos even. Back in the day I had even played the first two, gamer that I was. Without a second thought I threw it into my basket, becoming another anonymous customer of the great Valve machine. If only I knew what awaited me, maybe I'd have shaved my head bald, put on a hawaiian shirt and grown a beard.
For the next six hours I pumped minute after glorious minute into the pursuit of killing as many people as I possibly could. Wave after wave came at me, my finger pounding the mouse like a series of waves upon a once calm shore. The killing time had come.
It continued like this until I dived forth into sleep, eager to launch myself back into this sick adventure the very next day.
When daylight finally came, it's cruel beams cutting into my eyes like a knife through hot butter all I could think about was the game, the goal of finishing it top priority in my mind. With a sick smile I launched myself into it once more, the next few hours bringing my total up to ten and the game to it's completion.
And here I find myself, ranting deliriously about a thrown together collection of code and visuals that sucked away ten hours of my life. I ask myself only one question at this point, did I regret it?
No I did not.
