I have a love-hate relationship with this game.
The good parts of this game are absolutely amazing, but the bad parts of it nearly ruin the entire experience.
-Movement is outstanding. Everything in this game moves so smoothly, it's very satisfying to jump off of walls and leap around the map, all while keeping control of your weapons.
-The gunplay is some of the best I've ever seen in a game. Like I said above, everything is just so smooth. The animations are great, and it's very skill based for the most part. This game requires a lot of practice and target-tracking to obtain a lot of kills, you can't just run in and mow everyone down, unless you're playing against potatoes.
-While the mercs all have their own abilities, I wouldn't say that the game is soley based around pressing a key and winning a fight, like in Overwatch (with a few exceptions, I'm looking at you, Thunder!)
-FOR THE MOST PART, the game is very balanced in terms of the mercs & weapons. Obviously some will always be better than others, but in my opinion every merc and weapon is viable in at least some situations.
-As for the mercs, they are all wonderful characters each fit with their own unique looks and personalities. They all have their own goofy voicelines and always have something charming to say.
-The game IS NOT pay to win.
-The team balancing is horrendous. 85% of all games are just steamrolls, and that isn't an exaggeration.
-Some maps are just downright boring and not at all fun to play. If people would rather leave a match instead of playing a round just because of the map chosen, you know something's wrong.
-The loadout card crafting system is absolutely horrible.
-Development of the game has been painfully slow. The devs legitimately care about the game, but the playerbase is losing patience. It's been in beta forever it feels like.
-Other generic issues linked to F2P games, like noobs running around and being literally useless to a team.
The game is good, but has a lot of little issues that take away from the experience.
I say give it a try at the very least, you'll either love it or hate it.
Most of the bad parts of the game can be fixed, and I just sincerely hope that the devs listen to us and continue development. I am a big fan of this game and Splash Damage, I want this game to succeed just as much as they do.

Wolfenstein The New Order delivers everything it said it would... and much, much more. It's killin' Nazis, but it's doing it while having you explore, sneak, and loot all in a deeply immersive and fresh world and narrative. It's takes the old concept of a wolfenstein game of battling Nazi soldiers in World War II and brings it a breath of fresh air by dropping you in an alternate 1960s where the Reich rules the world not just in Mililtary, but also through it's ideology. It's not just a world where they have military bases everywhere but museums too: showing you the Nazis are firmly rooted in thier "new world." Concering the Gameplay, it feels great. All the guns have different uses and all feel extremely satisfying to shoot (aka no more peashooters!). The A.I. , suprisingly, feels fairly responsive despite their narrow cone of vision. If any negatives exist, It would be it's obsession with pressing the E button everytime you want to pick something up, as it gets annoying VERY quickly. One disclaimer I would say is that this game does give a very dark tone when describing the Nazis, specifically their war crimes: something that not too many games are willing to do, Which may be seen as a pro and/or a con. In my opinion, however, I think that this game has just a bit too much emphasis on it.

MP3 is no longer the dark detective noir story of MP1 and 2.  Instead, it takes Max Payne as a character and dumps him in a gritty and realistic world, set in Brazil.  Personally, I found this a good move; Max's character is given a lot of room to breath, and the dialogue and monologue help to characterize him in fantastic ways.
Gameplay-wise, MP3 is still incredibly difficult, but much more forgiving; multiple failures will restart you at a checkpoint with more painkillers and ammo.  Bullet-time is still a thrill to run around in.
And probably one of the more impressive aspects of MP3 is the animation.  Max twists his body around to maintain his aim, enemies fall down realistically, and Max won't magically slide down walls as he's jumping to the side; he'll smash into them.  Realistically!
If you're not tired of Max doling out "Max Paynisms" as well as bullet, MP3 is definitely worth the buy.

Fan since the beginning of the franchise, and I feel like Max Payne 3 is worthy of being the third. While the setting is different, it works well to drive the series forward, even if it may be somewhat of a cliche locale in modern gaming. While the comic-panel narratives are gone, MP3 reflects on the old style in Max's inner narrative having a generous layer of noir style dialogue and stylized cutscenes that hide level loads, providing a pretty fluid and cinematic experience. While the cutscenes can be a bother on a replay when you're trying to mash around killin dudes, you're definitely not wasting your money on this (at any price, really). The story is surprisingly long, there's eastereggs, clues, and gun parts to hunt for that benefit both your SP and MP experience.
Multiplayer is layed with unlocks and earnings as most modern shooters are now, and the possible combinations of kit provide a great nudge to keep duking it out against other Max fans online.

This game breaks new ground in terms of unflinching realism by being the first artistic work to really force the audience first to confront the futility, then the absurdity, and ultimately the idiocy, of trying to solve problems by voting.
By allowing players the option of calling their own votes, while faithfully simulating the workings of that political process, this brilliant game takes the player rapidly through the stages of hope, disbelief, frustration, dawning comprehension, and finally despair as they watch others begin struggling through the same lessons, while fruitlessly trying to warn rookies of the forgone failure of their activism. In only a few hundred hours of gaming, one achieves a level of understanding of the emptiness of the democratic process that normally takes decades to achieve.

Thinking about experimenting with new guns/movement? Better whip out that credit card, or be faced with a long run of crap rewards for top-rank in a battle.
Too bad, a game that was on track to be amazing, has become just another pay-to-kill-those-who-didn't.

DISCLAIMER:
First, Understand that I have played off and on since 2013. That doesn't mean I have done everything, nor does it mean I claim to be an 'expert'. So just hear me out. I'll go over the things that REALLY matter.
Back in 2013: Was dull, monotonous, and otherwise uneventful. Match after match was pretty similar... plasma cannons and speed. You could only add one type of weapon per bot. (All plasma or all laser)
2014: They added hoverblades, Helium, snipers, and eventually wings. THIS INTRODUCED SO MUCH LAG TO THE GAME. Developed a well rounded "tiered" system so players could find someone they are *evenly matched for. (A t10 gun would automatically make a bot t7 or higher. So no picking on the new guys) This made it easier for people to get into the game. Rewards were a mix of money and XP points for a level "web". So you had to choose how to progress carefully or risk stagnating in the lower tiers.
2016: I came back to this game as it is right now... Tiered system is gone, but that isnt that bad. I think they organized it by CPU levels instead. The lag has been mostly reduced, occasionally people will stop moving midair or "ghosts" murder you. (Ghosting is lagging out, dying, and killing people clientside. The damage is still calculated by the system) "Robits" are the new currency and are no longer distributed after a match. Depending on how well you do during a match rewards you with a "crate" at the end of the match. These range from Rusted to Protonium. They are entirely RNG based and you aren't likely to get a legendary item even from the protonium crates. They added chain guns, missile launchers, and shotgun cannons (all legendary). These items are exceptional, but just make you a higher priority target. Legendary weapons could almost be labelled as "Unique" instead. Epic weapons hold most of the fighting power at the moment and are overall better to have anyway. They changed it so that you can add multiple weapon types to the same bot and switch between them in the middle of a fight. Despite this, only the same weapons are able to be used at once. Levels are still important and are a decent way of seperating the playerbase. The higher you level, the more CPU you can use for each bot... This allows for much more powerful bots as you progress.
*Through Rose Colored Glasses* The game is great! It is easy to level and you alway have a chance for the most powerful weapons through this awesome RNG system!
*Glasses Removed* Through long hours of sweat, toil, and rage you too can eventually aquire a bot powerful enough to make the game enjoyable. Put a little money into getting "Premium" and that happens a little quicker. I recommend a week of premium. During which you play like a god almost non-stop and set yourself up for a long time.
Common Complaints:
Only premium users have full access to crates....
A: Yep. It sucks, play higher CPU gametypes to gain more possible loot results. (4 items vs 1 or 2) The better you play, the better the resulting crate.
Premium Color template...
A: I agree, it is pretty rediculous. However, I could care less about looks. It is a "creative" shooter, but don't let the 4 color availability take away from your butt kicking experience. I WOULD like to see a larger color pallate, considering the game has access to a hex color code system... Allowing the non-premium users access to a basic swatch of colors (black, gray, white, red, green, blue, yellow, etc) and letting the premium users have that 2 or 3 variations of each color. (Darker red for example)
Final Word of Warning: Play as hard as you can, but be forewarned. Even at higher levels, people still suck at this game.

Staring blankly into the backlit computer screen with a hollowed out zombie expression, I couldn't help but think that the Max Payne trilogy had left its searing brand in my soft, fleshy gray matter. The film noir writing style of this game was what managed to pry open my wallet and gut its contents. The third installment, while edgier and darker, had moments of circular story telling that dragged, but the moments were fewer than the rounds of a colt magnum. Cutscenes became a problem, however, as they were prolific but entertaining. Fans of the orginal MP games will cry into their empty bottles of painkillers when they find out that these cutscenes replaced the unique comicbook-style storytelling of the first two MP games. WOLFENSTEIN: THE NEW ORDER.
Note: My current completion rank is B+, this is early on the Über-Difficulty playthrough. This being the only setting that is actually HARD, all the others are rather easy. This coming from someone who was born in the early 90's just in time to catch the "classic-difficulty" thing that has been thrown around by older gamers.
Second note, is more of a complain really. The Enigma-codes, are rather annoying. I'm waiting for someone who has the time and brainpower to solve it and post the answers, mostly because its very hot outside (around 28-30c) so i really cant be bothered to boil my brain over code-breaking a notoriously high-math encryption system. With absolutely no pointers on how to do it. It would have been easier to have the codes decrypt automatically.
But those were not the only gripes that i had with Wolfenstein, oh no...
You remember that "20h Campaign" thing that they threw around in some interviews and press ? It only is that long if you play the game twice. The game has this different time-lines thing going, in the beginning you get to make a choice on who will be in a more major part in the game as part of the resistance. This splits the time-line into two, rather indistinguishable parts. Doing either one, opens different routes through certain levels and giving different bonuses (Health/Armour) to be found. Other than that, there really is no other reason to switch time-lines, other than completions sake.
What comes to the collectibles there are the classic gold-objects to be found, reasonably well hidden. I have tried to gather all that i can, this being rather easy since they are usually shown on the map. Some hidden objects are not shown on the map, this got really annoying in some areas where you though you already collected everything. Spending a great deal of time running around like a headless chicken trying to find that one golden egg... On the other hand. There is also ”Germanized” (if that qualifies as a word..) Vinyls of famous sixties music, unfortunately the one I can spot and make the connection to, is the Beatles one. And the records sound, mostly nice and if memory serves there is a want to listen the whole collection of this music. I unfortunately cant remember where.. I wish that they would have included more of them into the game.
But enough of my personal nags, lets get into the real reviewing.
Wolfenstein: The New Order. Is an Alt-History FPS, in which Nazis won WW2 and conquered the world with strange technologies and weapons. You take the role of B.J Blazkovich, The Guy, The Legend, The Original ”One Man Army”. And start in a very scripted section inside an airplane.. But don't go crying ”Bloody Murder!” just yet, the start section, although very scripted is actually rather well done and impressive. And after that you are washed up on the shore next to the main bad guys fortress and here the actual shooting sections begin. I will not spoil the plot any further than this, mostly because I feel that the story is well crafted so well that spoiling it, would be a right crime.
Lets just summarize the story into the simplest for, that I can steal from someone else. Its like Inglorious Basterds, but as a video-game.
Graphically the game looks pretty decent, but the color-pallet they went with was the all too familiar “Next-Gen shooter” assortment of bland grays and browns. With very little identifying colors popping out from the blandness. Not to get stuck on the excuse of “it was the desired effect, because its depressing”. The only game in my opinion that did that right was The Saboteur. (Personal bias showing like a motherf*cker.)
BUT, speaking of popping. Id-Tech 5, had the tendency for some extreme texture-popping and for unfortunately, its very apparent in Wolfenstein. The only way I got around it, was to lower the texture-detail. But this made everyone “look like a horrid burn-victim” and before someone else decides to show their opinions on why that is. I HAVE THE MACHINE POWER TO PUT THE TEXTURES ON ULTRA, its the games own optimization thats bollocked up. What else ?
I know that most of the games environments are.. Linear to say the least. Again falling into the “Next-Gen”-bin.. (Ignoring that.) And their way around it, with the two separate time-lines, really doesn't show enough difference to be mentioned. Only serving as a rather lazy way (in my opinion) to pad out the games length.
But in its core-mechanics, as an FPS with the “Classical”-twist. Wolfenstein does its job and does it extremely well. It is very satisfying to either sneak up on your enemies and stick your knife into various orifaces, or just say “f*ck this” and pull out your machineguns (notice the blural, referring to dual-wielding.) and just go nuts. One thing that was mildly dissappointing, was that the laser-weapon that is acquired rather early in the game, really serves no other purpose than to be the gimmick. Sure its usefull later against the Super-soldaten, but thats about it and no matter how frequently I looked for some piece of metal-cover to cut for a tactical advantage, I only managed to do it, again too few times to be mentioned. Not counting the vent-covers, but since that is mandatory, its immediately off the list.
Well I think I have whined enough, to start summarizing. Lets see...
Semi-decent Graphics. Solid fun old-school style shooter-action. Oh and I musn't forget the all so delightfull nod-back to the original Wolfenstein with the difficulty-selection icons. But getting distracted.. Very linear, but well crafted story. Padded out length and some other minor gripes...
Oh dear this is very hard for me, I cannot give it an A-Rank. And taking into account that I havent looked at all what the game has to offer (f*cking Enigma-Codes..).  AAARGh.
Well, until I have managed to take a look at the “new game-modes” that is SAID to hide under the Enigma-Codes.
I think, I must give Wolfenstein: The New Order.
B.
I'l settle for that rank, until I have determined whether or not, there is another ending hidden within the Enigmas. After that I will raise the rank with a +. AND THAT WILL BE IT. #DEALWITHIT
EDIT: Well, as some industrious fellow managed to crack the enigma-codes, i can safely say. It really isnt worth it. The only notable thing is an ironman-mode, so the rank stands. Simple as that..

So first off let me start by saying that I was able to play this thanks to steam's family sharing feature, so I do not know if my hour count will show up here, but as I write this I have played 10 hours of the game, now, on to the review. WARNING: Review contains minor early game spoilers but nothing major.
In Wolfenstein: The New Order you play as Captain Blazkowicz, a US soldier who is injured fighting against the nazi's, who then awakens years later to find they now rule the world. Now it is time to fight back, and lead the resistance against the Nazi's.
Pro's:
+Amazing Graphics - on Ultra it has some of the best graphics I've ever seen in any game, and on low it is still better than most games.
+Fun Gameplay - Dual weilding futuristic shotguns whilst blowing Nazi's to shreds has never been so fun!
+Good Story - The story for this game is pretty good, it is well explained as to why everything happens, leaving no unanswered questions.
+Lots to do - There are many collectables to collect and enigma codes to crack, doing which grants you more game modes!
Cons:
-It's quite short - The story took me just 10 hours to complete, however it was very enjoyable and there is much more for me to do in future playthroughs, so I will likely complete it multiple more times.
-In one of the first few missions you wind up getting injured and becoming a potato for 14 years. When you wake up you still have all your muscle, which isn't very realistic. Though it doesn't really affect anything so meh.
-No multiplayer - I'm not really bothered by this, but with the story being so short and it being such a fun game, it would certianly have been a great feature to include.
Overall I'd reccomend this game to essentially anyone who is considering getting it, it's one of the most fun games I've played in the last few years, and it's amazingly fun to take out rooms full of Nazi's whilst you dual weild gigantic machine guns. Overall I think I'd rate this game with a score of 87/100.

While the story itself isn’t groundbreaking, it is delivered masterfully by Rockstar’s sharp dialogue.  The gameplay is smooth and a lot of fun.  It's also quite challenging in spots.  If you are a fan of the first two games, you should know a lot has changed.  The noire aspect has been toned downed and there are no comic book style cutscenes.  On a technical level it is fantastic; the bullet damage on enemies alone is shocking.
It’s all high production level material; it just isn’t necessarily Max Payne.  Tonally, it is a little too self-absorbed.  As much as I admire tragic/fallen characters in fiction, the amount of self-deprecation that goes on in Max’s monologue is overwhelming. Also, be prepared for Metal Gear Solid level cutscenes in terms of length.  There are a lot of them.
Rockstar knows how to tell stories really well and Max Payne 3 is a shining example. If you can get past the lack of charm the first two games possessed and the absence of their self-referential humor, the story here is, for the most part, engaging.  I wouldn't put it anywhere near the level of the first two games, but as a gritty, standalone story it works.  Max Payne remains a compelling character.

A great old-fashioned shooter. 10/10
Beautiful environments and intelligent design make this game a breath of fresh air after a decade of shooters geared towards "realism" rather than "escapism".
Weapons are designed to fulfill a function rather than to give variety within a class of weapon. Enemies are not bullet sponges, but use cover intelligently and flank relentlessly. The game encourages stealth rather than imposing upon the player an entire stealth section. To this end, it becomes beautifully integrated into gameplay and becomes a real aid rather than a gimmick.
However, choosing from multiple weapons in combat is clunky and could stand to go the half-life route.
Level design is vicarious and not utilitarian. They make sense. The prison looks like a prison, feels like a prison, so-on and so-forth. Any onlooker can easily tell you where you are in the scheme of things., There are multiple avenues of approach that are not readily apparent. Caches of first-aid kits, armour and ammunition are placed nicely.
Also, no regenerate back to full-health nonsense. When you're in trouble, you're in trouble.
BJ encounters his arch-nemesis. A being capable of great cruelty that no one can ignore, even sub-consciously. He gets gravely inured and ends up in hospital. He awakens 14 years later from a vegatative state to defend his nurse from Nazis.
He then joins the resistance and aids them to great effect. The end-goal being revenge and justice for those lost.
While the plot is simple, the motivation has real substance. The antagonists are true totalitarian monsters and yet the supporting cast  makes the player question the protaganist's character. Is he prejudiced ? Is he truly just when he kills the enemy ? Does he do his work unthinkingly ? Is he a monster for killing so viscerally and with hate ?
It leaves the player with a lot of questions, allowing him to make his own decisions as to how he views BJ. It's suprisingly mature.
It is perhaps most apt, that whatever the player takes away from this experience will depend on how invested in the plot he really is. Just following and not thinking about the game will certainly lead one to conclude that this is just another shooter. There is a story with very strong characterisaction, but only to those who take it.
It is with sad irony that I note the many straight-faced comments where people admit they don't understand the extremely simple plot and yet say the story is bad. They then go on to make excuses saying they only noticed the killing of Nazis. It's as if no one even knows enough to give a brief overview.
I have one major criticism despite the praise I have for the unflinchingly simple plot and excellent characterisation. The game resorts to heavy-handed gesturing to motivate the player at times. It likes to impose upon the player a feeling of helplessness and then quickly alleviate the situation. This confuses me. If it intends to characterise oppression, it is excellent. But if it doesn't, it's simply a machine to move the plot along.
The game has a great soundtrack and various perfectly-timed music cues. Weapons sound appropiately meaty and certainly change with distance and environment. Accents I cannot judge, I do not live in Europe. But I find them lovingly protrayed. NPC barks and the little conversations they have are enlightening and not at all useless.

First off,
This game is beautiful. I had some frame rate issues at times, but the rest of the game is magnificent. The cutscenes are beuatifully rendered. The entire game is very pretty to look at. This game may have the Wolfenstein name on the front, but feels nothing like the old ones. This feels new. And new is good. It feels completely satisfying to kill every target you see because it responds dynamically. The game includes more that just another basic shooter. The alternative history background was definitely cool. It felt new. And new is good. The story holds up pretty well and the game makes it so you actually care for the characters, they feel more than just random NPC's a part of the story. There are dozens of other things that make this game great and I could go on for hours about it. But I wont.
However,
The game did have some frame rate issues as well as some audio syncing errors which I found amusing, especially during cutscenes. There were some parts of the game were the audio sync errors were a tad irritating. The stealth portions of the game I found glorifyingly easy and very immersion breaking. The game used the wave system at some parts which I found annoying at times, but easily ignored. There were some grainy areas of the game, but those went away after a few minutes
This game is phenomenal and I would recommend playing it. For every small negative aspects the game holds, there are 3 great positive aspects to counter it and definitely worth it. The game is not flawless, they are not making any revolutionizing decisions. This game is just fun as hell.

If Team Fortress 2 and Space Engineers had a child, it would be this game. Build unique creations and pilot them against other combatants. Over time, you will collect items at random, and you can sell the ones you don't want to buy something else you've been waiting for. In combat, enemy attacks can break off parts of your robot; When you lose too many important components (weapons, locomotion...), you are dead. If you want to stay alive, redundancy is the name of the game; The more parts you can lose and still function, the harder you will be to kill. Naturally, that puts minimalist bots at a disadvantage, but it leads to players building large and elaborate creations. I've seen giraffes, massive tanks, cars with 8+ wheels, planes with 8+ wings, walls of so many energy machine guns... The few successful minimalist bots I have seen rely on larger, more durable components like mech legs and high-level weapons. Level up through combat to unlock new gamemodes. I haven't tried it yet, but apparently there is some kind of in-game economy around selling robot designs and/or parts to other players.
My only complaint is that there is no PVE gamemode or story mode. The test mode used to spawn endless enemies, but it doesn't seem to do that anymore. There is combat versus players, and a similar team deathmatch mode versus AI, nothing else. Something along the lines of Mechassault's grinder or TF2's Mann Versus Machine mode would be nice.
Action? Check. Strategy? Check. Free to play? Check. Recommend? Check.

Well, for $60.00 and 40.7 gigs of hard drive space I'd say this game is all beauty and no play time. Okay, now seeing as this was Bethesda I probably was expecting to much from them with this game... like most who pre-ordered. Now, before the game came out I was in the middle of requirements that they had posted at the time. So when the pre-load came out I straight up downloaded it. On medium graphics the game doesn't disappoint the eyes, but my i5 quad core chugged in areas where driving and big open areas had gaint shoot outs. Outside of that, the game ran well.
Now the game's story started out very well, but when you got past the moon it just seem overly rushed and not the "We were short on time" kind of rush, it was the kind of rush job that even your highschool english teacher says you shouldn't do when telling a story.  Also the weapons at your desposal is somewhat limited, of course tho the big handheld laser thing is probably my favorite weapon after its 100% upgraded. Level design was so-so, I like it to a point, but there were some areas where I'd run into a game wall preventing me from going somewhere. Most of them were strickly because I didn't take the game path the dev's had planned out. Like in the early missions where a gaint robo hound (Not the small cybor german dogs)  chases you  until getting stuck. After getting it stuck (which I didn't really stop to see) I ran like hell down the hallway, turned killed the solo Nazi who was there and then hurried up the ladder, well tried to atleast, but there was a wall at the top of the ladder. Sort of dumbfounded I spent 5 minutes looking around and here I found a cut-able fence in the hallway I though had a robo mut waiting for me. So I cut it, went down the path and end up at the same damn ladder. Only this time the game wall was missing. That sort of game wall is really unexeptable. The character design was well, but you rarely got to know a load of them before they were killed off. This one really stuck out to me, the math girl. You rarely spoke to her or anything, yet at the end they give her a scene where it felt like they were trying to make you feel something for a character so her death ment something, which you really couldn't. Also another game mechanic that bugged me was the weapon upgrades. On the moon in the begining of the killing spree I found a scope for the laser rifle before getting the rifle. I thought to my self "Sweet now if I pick up this gun I can... wait... wheres the scope?" yeah, if you get a weapon part with out the weapon you don't keep the part, very irritating.
This game just feels like one of bethesda's side projects, tho this is certianly better then most of them (Fallout 3, Fallout New Vegas, and Elder Scrolls online) in the end it felt really half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ The story just felt like they got bored with it and left too many questions and just had a very unrealistic ending. Also, the u-boot....why do we not get to see the thing? Serriously, when your in the thing it feels too big to be even a large nuclear sub and after the mission where your on the sea floor you can see a little bit of it, but thats all.
Lastly the only issue I have with this game, is it's freaking file size. I live in the country were good internet is hard to get. So you can imagen my rage after waiting 2 days to download 40.7 gigs and get so little gameplay where I got Watchdogs in 1 day yet have more content in watch dogs while being able to only play low graphics quality compared to Wolfenstien on medium graphics. And also it's sorta ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t to post lower requirements before release on pre-order and then jack them up so high.
I can't stop playing this game. Buy it, well worth the money.

A few downsides towards the game of which I have found are; The AI is a bit derpy, they don't see you most of the time (though i only played on medium so could be an advantage), and other than that, the price. This is a game like no other. It has nothing to be compared to. The closest I can say is that Planetside 2  is battlefield 3 on gamma radiation. I.E. After you get past the (steep) learning curve, it hulks out. With aircraft, tanks, MAX units, (walking tanks) and three asymetrical factions, there's more here than you can imagine, if you can look past the occasional bug. See, the company running this game, Daybeak Games Company, is effectively and indie dev right now. They used to be affiliated with SONY.... uh...  No longer. Sony sold Sony Online Entertainment (SOE) to Daybreak Nova investments. SOE then became DGC.  However, they're still pumping out new content! To any of the newbs joining, if you see this, remember to join an outfit. And if you're not having fun, ask yourself, "What's going on that I can mess with? "   You can go infiltrator, and go invisible. You an go Light Assault, and fly. You can go medic, and revive and heal your teammates. You can go Heavy Assault, and go ham. Remember, there are tanks and aircraft waiting for you, not just infantry. You can pull your killstreaks from a vehicle terminal. Now get out there, soldier!
Update-- roughly 1000 hours later, this game is still engaging. TIP: Find an outfit of guys who actually want to play. There aren't many left, but they exist, and it's one of the most satisfying things in the game to watch you and your squad take a point from vastly superior numbers.

Ok, so first of all this is the greatest (strategy) game of all time. And you should buy this. You might say, however, that you already own the classic, non-hd edition, and you are wondering why in the world you should buy the HD edition. Because it's HD? Maybe, but that's not your main reason. Your main reasons are: 1- Because it works smooth on the newer operating systems and 2- Because multiplayer is pretty darned smooth. And what's better than AoE? AoE with friends.
And now for the Forgotten DLC. It is... a decent DLC, but it pretty heavily depends on your personal preference. It ads a few
nations, but it also adds quite a few campaigns. And these campaigns are quite unlike the original AoE campaigns. Matter of fact, the Forgotten campaigns focus on somewhat forgotten battles (as the name suggests) and the campaigns largely follow a narrative path. In other words, these campaigns revolve a lot more around the storyline.
In addition, the new campaigns look abolutely smashing; well designed from an aesthetic point of view.
I should note, however, that these campaigns are kind of dull. So in the end: the campaigns look nice, tell the story very well indeed, but unfortunately they are kinda dull. Great if you are interested in history or aesthetics, but if you are just here for the gameplay you might be disapointed.
Final verdict: 9/10

Max Payne doesn't pull any punches in delivering a hard boiled story, with it's share of 1 liners, metaphors and brutal visuals, the story can be quite gripping, although if you watch other forms of media in the same genre, most of what you see might feel a little unsurprising.
The gameplay is where MP3 shines, with a straightforward, but enjoyable cover mechanic, providing the player with the ability to blindfire, or pop out from safety for well aimed shots.
The classic bullet time comes back, feeling like it always did.
It can be activated in two ways, with the press of its button, or by performing a dive in combat, slowing down time as Max sideway shoots at his opponents, every bullet of every gun rendered in full 3D(like the previous games) allows you to soak in all this mayhem with some great visuals.
The enemies reactions, the bullet damage that is rendered, both on the npc's and objects in the game is probably one of the most detailed to date.
Watching opponents reactions to being shot in different places of their bodies lends a real drama to the in game-action in terms of all of this chaotic movement, as foes hittin in the leg with fall down, letting off shots accidentaly and screaming in pain - all while more enemies frantically screaming jump out of cover to let off shots at Max. It's something I found myself repeating, and repeating.. If I found a good section, I would just reload that checkpoint over and over to just experience the combat, in that set piece, in all it's different ways.
The level design is linear, drivin by the story in exact detail. Don't expect to be able to do much of anything besides go forward, which can kill the replayability of some parts of the game, will certainly be fun the first time through.
The cinematics of this game are what take place of the 'loading' screens, and can sometimes be frustrating to watch through, especially on portions where it feels unneccesarily long, but all at least look very nice and are well acted.
I personally found it refreshing that Max isn't a silent protaganist, hearing his thooughts on all parts of the level, during cinematics and gameplay portions lends some charm to the games moments.
There are a few modes given to the player, including a multiplayer game type, where you create a character based on the different in game factions. A time attack mode, and a minute mode, - a few modes to track score based gameplay.
All of which are nice, but I really wanted a more detailed mode that would allow the player to choose a level, and set up some battle conditions to fight enemies inside it. Like a bot match, but not so much.
I just wanted to shoot guys, and test environments and see what would happen in this games great combat engine. But for any replayability, you'll have to lean on the STORY mode, which can be difficult to do when you just want to explore the games combat at it's core.
All and all a great game, especially if you enjoy this type of gameplay.

What sets Dirty Bomb from other competitive shooters out there:
- Dynamic Class Based Gameplay
- Fun and (sorta) Dynamic Gameplay
The Good F2P Model:
- Rewards you for playing everyday
- Provides free mercenaries (classes) to try out each week
- Free rewards given almost every month (Upgraded crates and etc)
- The bronze card is the best card in every class and the higher tiers are simply skins
- Payment comes from purchase of cases, crates, merc unlocks and loadout card purchases
- Handsome payout of In-Game Credits every game (Not Real Currency)
My thoughts:
Dirty Bomb is a fantastic F2P Shooter that focuses on team-based and objective gameplay mechanics. Every mercenary (class) has a role to play except maybe the snipers (Vasilli and Aimee) whom in the wrong hands can sway a team's victory. The gameplay elements make it such that every game, there will be different experiences if your team chooses to do things differently. Objectives give each team a purpose and they will still focus on getting the objectives done. I would even go as far as to say this is a FREE version of overwatch. I often play dirty bomb just to improve my reaction times, quick reflexes and thinking.
Should you get it?
Yes, if you have experience playing FPS shooters. It is free and if you don't have games like R6S or Overwatch and have no money, this is probably a great game to play till you get money to spend on those games or end up splashing cash over here.

The game is very good. However, it is very short. I beat it in under ten hours at the highest difficulty without trying to speed run through it. I was looking through every room, trying to pick up supplies where possible and trying to find the gold trinkets/baubles and enigma codes.
However, there is some replay value as the maps are very varied and many paths are available to reach your goals. The game is not a massively open world and is linear, but variety in settings keeps it fresh. The moon, the legendary city of Germania, Atlantis, are among the places you can visit.
The story is largely ignorable because of its absurdity but the characters are very likeable.

Great shooting, excellent level design. Storyline is a decent continuation of the last two games despite having a different writer, but it's ruined by the unskippable cutscenes every minute or two.  If you're playing story mode, which encourages replaybility, get ready to watch a dozen of unskippable 6+ minute cutscenes at the begginning of each level. If you play Arcade which removes these, get ready to watch multiple unskippable 2-3 minute cutscenes during levels. Killed all enemies in a room? Cutscene. Opened a door? Cutscene.
Weapon balancing favors dual guns in both single player and multiplayer. Multiplayer is matchmaking based and takes ages to unlock new items and 60% of the time it will fail connecting to a game. There's no protection against cheating, so expect hackers with God Mode whenever you manage to connect to a match.
The basic singleplayer gameplay when it's not being interrupted by the constant cutscenes is extremely good, and so is the multiplayer when you manage to connect to a server despite being an unbalanced mess, though as of 2015 the online is mostly dead so if you buy the game then make sure it's because you want to play the campaign.

Ok, so first of all this is the greatest (strategy) game of all time. And you should buy this. You might say, however, that you already own the classic, non-hd edition, and you are wondering why in the world you should buy the HD edition. Because it's HD? Maybe, but that's not your main reason. Your main reasons are: 1- Because it works smooth on the newer operating systems and 2- Because multiplayer is pretty darned smooth. And what's better than AoE? AoE with friends.
And now for the Forgotten DLC. It is... a decent DLC, but it pretty heavily depends on your personal preference. It ads a few
nations, but it also adds quite a few campaigns. And these campaigns are quite unlike the original AoE campaigns. Matter of fact, the Forgotten campaigns focus on somewhat forgotten battles (as the name suggests) and the campaigns largely follow a narrative path. In other words, these campaigns revolve a lot more around the storyline.
In addition, the new campaigns look abolutely smashing; well designed from an aesthetic point of view.
I should note, however, that these campaigns are kind of dull. So in the end: the campaigns look nice, tell the story very well indeed, but unfortunately they are kinda dull. Great if you are interested in history or aesthetics, but if you are just here for the gameplay you might be disapointed.
Final verdict: 9/10

Great game! Think of your greatest moments playing Battlefield 2142, with classes and vehicules, but in a persistent world (with day/night cycles) and a map so huge there may be hundreds of battles fought simultaneously. Much of the purpose is to gain ground over any of the two other factions by capturing comm arrays. In some areas you may have to disable shield generators before capturing a base. No start or end of sessions; you just pop in when you want, play and get out when you want. You may spawn at held comm array/bases or go instant action and get dropped in the thick of chaos and start killing (or get killed...often). As for the free-to-play concept that is well known by now, yes there are in-games purchases but they don't feel pay2win rather than helpful assets. And some of them may be unlocked without money, like scopes or red dot sight for rifles. You may, if you want, subscribe to a premium account for about 10 bucks a month to receive Daybreak currency and discount on upgrades but, again, not necessary to enjoy the game on the free level. That did not ruin my experience with the game in any way and that should not stop you from playing this awesome game.

As a conclusion I think the game is worth a try if you are into strategy games,or maybe just want to revisit a timeless classic of the 90´s!

First things first, it's my first ever review on a game so take it with a grain of salt. That being said, at the period of writing this review, I haven't spent that many hours in game, however I can, with confidence might I add, point a thing or two about said game. Without further ado, let's cover the very basics of the Planetside 2.
Fun to play. Massive scale battles between 3 factions each having their own pros and cons. The battles take place in different contident with each map holding up to 2000 players a time. I’ll be honest, I didn’t expect much from Wolfenstein: The New Order. Since its announcement, there was a certain level of uncertainty surrounding the game; the public’s expectations were a little low, myself included, and there didn’t seem to be a lot of buzz behind it.
The FPS genre has its fair share of mediocre, uninspired, and vanilla shooters where the act of shooting bad guys becomes tiresome and uninteresting. Having little experience with the Wolfenstein series, I feared that any redeemable aspects of the game would go over my head as feelings of nostalgia from referential content would be lost on me. Admittedly, there were a lot of pessimistic feelings entering the game. But I’m happy to say I underestimated Wolfenstein: The New Order – what I expected to be just another shooter turned out to be a very solid one with a surprisingly emotional and intelligent story.
Quite frankly, it is one of the best shooters I’ve played in recent memory. With quality action, an emotional story, and likeable characters, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a smart shooter that pulls no punches.

This game is superb.  Make you own vehicle/robot with building blocks and then go and battle with them.  This game is still being developed.   You have different types of blocks, flying parts, modules, moving parts.  various jet engines, wheels, wings, rudders, hovers, weapons like long range shots with rail guns, close shots like shot guns,  and in medium shot weapons also.  You have plasma guns and laser guns.  You can mix and match these weapons.  You can mix and match the moving parts: mech legs, walker legs, wheels, etc.  YOu have various shields shapes.
Modules: currently there are modules you can equip on your robot/vehible.  Shield allows you to make a shield to block enemy fire.  Ghost modules make you invisible.  Blink module quickly teleports you several blocks away.  CPU module gives you extra energy.  Your weapons use energy.
This game also has different play modes.  Death match where two teams battle to get the most kills.  If you die you come back fully regenerated and keep playing until a team wins.  Battle Arena you play until you destroy the protnonium crystals at your enemy's base.  There are several other different play modes.
You win new parts at the end of each game and your chances for better parts (loot) increases depending on how well you play.
You can upload your robot/vehicle into a factory/market for other players to purchase.
Overall, the game is superb.  There are a few things in the game I personally do not like but that is simply personal preference -  for example I find the blink module sort of irritating when you get an enemy down to almost nothing and they blink away before dying.   Also the matching engine sometimes puts two teams together where one team has no chance.  One team may be all flyers and the other with few anit-aircraft weapons.
Mostly though, I love this game.  As you an see I have a lot of hours and thousands of games.  The game is free and the in game purchases are not necessary to enjoy the game.  To me, I like the game and so don't feel like im grinding to get new parts.  Ive been playing so much though that I have all the parts I need unless I want to build a whole lot of different bots.  Currently I have about 5 permanent bots i use.

As a fairly long-term on-off player, Robocraft is one of those games that I just keep coming back to. Despite one recent major change that I and many other players may not agree with, the core game itself still possesses its original charm in spades, and I can always have some fun with a quick match or a two-hour session building and battling.
To get it out of the way, the change that I mentioned comes in the form of the new, crate based loot system. It is worth noting, before I continue, that is pretty much my only complaint, and that I still would recommend Robocraft to anyone (if only, quite frankly, because it's free; and there's no real reason not to give it a try).
I understand Freejam’s need to make a profit, given that Robocraft is an indie game made by a new company, but the crate system means that the loot gained will likely not be in line with what the player needs; in a game which bases its appeal on creativity, this kind of limitation is a mistake which I find frankly staggering.
With that out of the way, do read on - I did say that I would recommend the game, after all.
The saving grace for Freejam on this front is that the game never forces you to spend money. In fact, curiously enough, the tutorial does not even mention that you can spend real money on the game. There is a prominent ‘Shop’ tab in the main menu, but Freejam apparently plan to live up to their name; for me, this remains a major point in their favour.
The building system is the best of any game I have ever played; the 'limitless creativity' that the developers are fond of boasting really is no joke.  The combat system is very competent; the older gamemodes such as 'Battle Arena' still play as well as ever and gamemodes like the recent 'Team Deathmatch' will appeal to nearly anyone who has played an FPS before.
The real charm of Robocraft (and the reason that the game still seems to have its hooks in me) is the way the two aspects mesh; the building system has as much, if not more impact on gameplay that fps skill or tactics. The damage system and weapons systems outclass any similar game I've seen, and the feeling of beating an opponent and knowing that it really was down to your own building ability is a very satisfying one.
Despite the somewhat ill-advised loot system, Robocraft is still a good game which receives regular updates, and the devs do tend to listen to the players. When you try the game for yourself, do remember that it is still in early access (despite it's level of polish), and that everything remains subject to change and improvement. That does not, however, mean that Freejam will ever spellcheck their item descriptors. Ah well.

When the original Max Payne was released, I thought it would be a very difficult act to follow simply because the highly violent and stylish "Shoot-em'-up!" theme of the game, made you feel as if you were in the Director's chair in a John Woo style film.
Well... all of that isn't enough to outshine the awesome third installment in the series. Max Payne 3 simply gets it all right. Its both what I loved about the series (slo-mo + bullet time) and now with useful cover mechanics and just an incredibly well put together story and game.
This game has exceeded my expectations.

A big con I've always had with this game is actually playing it. From personal experience, I've never had a play session without some form of internet lag, and on bad days it would run at about 4fps (as in, you could count the times the individual frames change, no joke). This was a problem even AFTER getting a better connection AND a better laptop to play it on.
Does that make it bad? F**K no.
Those fleeting moments in big servers when it DID run smoothly enough to play were few and far between, but were absolutely epic in scale and had me on the edge of my seat the entire time. It was a truly great gaming experience.
So, my thoughts? If you are a casual gamer and don't own a high end PC like me, I cannot recommend it fully as it will make your PC cry, Crysis style. But for those who have a high end gaming PC? SOLID recommend as it is a great experience when it works. It'll lie dormant on my games list until the day that I get a PC to run it
On that day I will be a very happy man

I am always searching for new Shootergames because i get bored-out often, and mostly too quickly to enjoy the games to it's full context. However not with Dirty Bomb!
Pro's:
Having played this game on and off for about a year or so now, i really enjoy the gameplay it offers because every game is not alike the previous one. The team shuffle between two games following up on each other works good so that you don't have to play against the same people all the time.
And it's mostly always balanced! (However there are those who vote-shuffle in-game too often as well). >> Do keep in mind tho that there are players above lvl 20+ that sometimes get put into a game full of players under lvl 20.
DB is very much an appreciated game, even more so if your team knows how to play their mercs. Even if they (or you yourself) are new to this game. Everyone can be a gamechanger!
Neg's:
Buying a merc you enjoyed playing in a free-rotation week can sometimes take a huge amount of time.
A smaller misfortune is the lack of customization, but if you have a decent loadout-card for a merc you like to play with, it can easily be neglected.
My conclusion:
A very different kind of FPS, enjoyable fast paced gameplay with each character having a different skillsets, very balanced gameplay.
I'd give it an 8/10 because of the system to buy mercs takes quite a while.

AW-some!!!
Just finished my first play through and enjoyed nearly every second.
First this is a huge install 50 GB and is built on the ID 5 engine used for the game RAGE.
So the visuals are fantastic.
The game starts during WWII and you are in a squad tasked to kill a Nazi codenamed DEATHSHEAD.
He is a true evil genius. He is making cybernetic Nazi super soldiers and winning the war revolves around stopping him. You and your team are shot down durring your bombing run and must make the raid on foot.
Characters are developed as you go and the two that stands out are a duo that act more like father and son than veteran and grunt.
Quickly things go from bad to worse and soon you are captured. The villian enters and forces you to make a choice between the two I just mentioned, the one you choose will die a most gruesome death- while the other is left with you- locked in a cell- that soon will be and oven- to die.
This makes two character "time lines" depending on who you choose- the story may develope in very diffrent ways...
As you escape you are caught in an explosion and catch a chunk of shrapnel in the head... (thats gotta suck)
Cut scene- credits- Game truely begins.
You wake 15 years later in a family run mental hospital....  (" I don't know...  It has always been my dream to open a nice little country psych ward were the troubled people of my country can come to get help, and terrorize my children.") -
IDK
Anyway, the daughter has taken care of you and grown fond of you as you watch time pass in voice- overed cut scenes. You learn that the hospital is where the Nazis come to get test subjects and when they shut it down one day all Hell breaks loose and you are given control once again.
One of the coolest things are knife takedowns. You have to sneak up behind a Nazi and hit the "takedown" key. (Some very brutal kills) One you actually slash the legs of the Nazi causing him to fall backward where you then perforate him chest several times. You get a gut reaction of "ouch"
Some of the K-9 unit kills are viceral too.
The whole world has fallen under Nazi rule and is now the new norm. It now is your job to undo it.
The game awards you with new guns now and then giving you the means to "upgrade" them. Usually with a scope or a new ammo type.
The gun mechanics are very standard and even with the ability to duel wield- I hardly ever did. Only a couple times did I even HAVE to. I played on normal difficulty.
The story was simple and to the point with very little attempts to deepen the plot or character development.
This may be my lack of finding the right cues or skipping them because of choices I had made.
Make sure you achieve all the goals in whatever chapter you are in once the plot moves along all side missions and hidden objects dissappear.
You can find hidden things throughout the game: glod objects, enigma codes, letters, newpaper clippings etc... that help to "fleshout" the world but not much. You can decipher the codes to get unlocks but I haven't tryed yet so I haven't a clue on what they are about.
Like I said I enjoyed this game. Worth 60 bucks to me and that is saying something.
I will play through again choosing the other timeline so see if it differs.
-GrAnD
**********************************************UPDATE********************************************************
Just finnished the second play through choosing the other timeline.
The only real change I saw was a secondary character swap, one being a mentally broken woman that goes out in a blaze of glory and the other a man who may have been Jimmy Hendrix.....
Still a fun game both times but I would have combined the two story lines and added content.
I did notice this time they left the end open for more gameplay....
I hope they do!!

The Nazis, immortalised in popular culture as one of the greatest villains in both fiction and reality return in Wolfenstein: The New Order and WOW, it's good to go up against them once again. The New Order manages to balance the old and the new; there is never a dull moment, plenty of shooting (and sneaking) and a surprisingly well done story.
The shooting gameplay is top-notch, you're able to dual-wield almost every weapon and the carnage that ensues is tremendous. Different types of enemies means different tactics to defeat them and you will have plenty of them and plenty of ammo. The stealth aspect of the game is brilliant. It does not feel out of place and it works wonders for when you need to dispatch certain enemies. Unlike proper stealth games, its fun to fail at stealth and get into another massive firefight. The story while a typical, resistance story is nicely done. The voice-acting is very good, a lot of effort has been put into bringing life to the main characters and to the Nazi enemies who speak proper German.
Wolfenstein: The New Order is easily the best game of the year so far and could be the best game in the Wolfenstein series. It's enlightening that an old IP can come back strong as ever. And its good to see that most who played the game think so too. The return to the oldest FPS IP is an experience like no other and indeed, its good to be back.

This game is an online FPS. There are three factions, each with slightly different weapons, and 6 classes, that are very different. In the game each faction is trying to take bases from the other two to control all the continents of the game world. Each continent feels different, from tundra to swamps. The classes are the Light Assault, which has a jetpack; the Heavy Assault, who gets a rocket launcher and shield; the Medic, who can heal people; the Engineer, who can heal vehicles, place turrets, and give ammo; the Infiltrator, who can become invisible, and has a sniper rifle; and the Max, who gets two different guns at the same time, and is healed by the Engineer instead of the Medic. I have performance issues at the lowest settings in areas with lots of people, but that is to be expected, because my computer is crap.

My Purchase Price: $59.99
I'd rate it: 87%
Pros:
- Excellent story (I know I was shocked as well)
- Stealth Mechanics: I've completed entire missions without a single shot fired, knife kills = very satisfying
- Levels: Open, multiple paths depending on story branchs taken early in game (chapter 2)
- Nazi era awesomeness: OVERLOAD! Everywhere is the feeling this game came dev which I've never heard of, grew up with a copy of Wolf3d and Spear of Destiny, only. They then spent the past 20 years perfecting their idea of what a Nazi controlled world would feel like in the 1960's.
- CGI: The quality of the story delivered by the cutscenes is a 10/10 in my book!
- Collectables: Finding every piece of Enigma codes, gold, back story (letters/newspaper clippings) is worth the hunt.
Cons:
- Lack of info: Not sure if this is a feature or a bug, there is a branch in the story line, end of Chapter 2 based on which of two lives you choose to save. Save one, in later levels you get the option to hot wire devices; save the other, you get the option to pick locks. However, you do NOT get the other option which is not listed, as such I spent 4 restarts on chapter 3 trying to get to a level behind a locked door that I needed a lockpick for :).
- HUD: Would like to have seen an option to disable the bright white dot, center screen, this has been fixed via a simple hud mod via Steam command line options for the game. I've played for over 5 hours with NO hud at all, very engrossing so far
- Load times: I'd like to see the 20 second level load times cut down, playing on a fast SSD with a top end Nvidia card = no matter
- AI: Once or twice I've seen, again not a huge deal over 5 hours, the enemy AI will freak out and attack you in the spot you used to be: Enter a room by running in and shooting, they still act like you're at the front door.
- Week one graphic driver issues: Running a 780 ti with the latest Beta drivers, still getting very random artifacting in game, usually in NPC faces, light green/pink glitches in the texture maps for 1 frame from time to time.
Conclusion: If you're an avid fan on anything Wolf3d, it's worth the premium price tag, this game is a true series relaunch to the last good Wolfenstein in my book: The 2001 Return to Castle Wolfenstein.

There is something terribly wrong with this game.
There isn't enough of it.
It isn't often nowadays that a game will send a tingle down my spine when I get my hands on it. Bioshock Infinity and Dishonored would be the last two, and W:TNO has joined them on that very small pedestal.
Obviously the graphics are brilliant. For 40GB worth of game you'd certainly hope so. High end machines necessary. Mine isn't too bad and I had a rather interesting where everthing would slow down into silky smooth slow motion - making the game really easy and dramatic to play, but completely removing any tension. Easily rectified though - exit game and start again. Done.
The animations are pretty good, but the moddelling and shading is where it's at. The sublte cell shading, similar to the effects of what could be seen in id & Bethesda's earlier FPS Rage and Bethesda's Dishonored, adds a slight comic book feel to the game, which is further amplified by all the DieselPunk Uniforms, Buildings, Vehicles, Robots, Mechs and RIDONKULOUS GUNZ! Everything in the environments is a little over the top. I guess you would say Uber. Hah. Very good.
Again the comic book feel is reinforced by the sheer gratuitousness of this game. Plenty of head-popping, chunk-blowing, shrapnel-tearing, body-bursting, edge-shoving, face-burning, skull-crushing, knife-throwing, limb-ripping, rubble-squishing, bullet-riddling, about a gajillion ways to knife someone from behind, and yes, you will eventually get your hands on what is essentially an Unreal Tournament InstaGib shock rifle (ahem, LaserKraftWerk, whatever). I even managed to drown a man in his own p155. That was very satisfying.
The sound effects are pretty standard, the voice acting on pretty much every single level is marvellous. The main characters have been cast brilliantly, veterans such as Gideon Emery make an appearance (his character, Fergus, being the owner of some quality material). The German speaking voice actors, like Nina Franoszek and Dwight Schultz are bang on, really hitting the mark, creating such brilliant characters.
The characters, THE CHARACTERS! Man...terrific job on the primary antagonists. Really good. Both Engel and Strasse are sufficiently sinister, both often stomach churningly evil - Strasse more the mad scientist and Engel the personification of Nazism. The scene in which Engel is introduced sets a pretty good precident of how unnerving she is. There isn't a huge amount of character development for the allies aside from B.J, Anya, Fergus/Wyatt which is a shame.
Throughout the game, B.J has these quiet little asides to himself, which makes a nice change from the completely silent person behind the floating gun or having someone talking at the top if their voice while sneaking up behind an unsuspecting victim. Brian Bloom does a fine job with Blazkowicz.
The soundtrack is sublime. Truly excellent. During the high octane, bullet chugging sequences you are immersed in grungey Unreal Tournament esque choons (back when UT music was the bee's bollox) while the rest of it sounds like some crazy, wonderful blend of The Black Keys and Frank Klepacki of C&C fame.
How does it play? Well. It plays well. It's remarkably simple, but it encourages you to think outside the box - take a look at a room full of nazi's and think of the best (or most fun) way of merking them all with the tools you have. The laser cutter opens up (literally) new attack routes and possibilities and you are normally presented with the differnt options that you would use to skin your cat anyway. All I'm saying is knee-slide-knife-throw.
The enemies are pretty predictable, the Panzerhund being the scariest (and sadly rarest) and the shrapnell shotgun guys the twattiest. The boss fights are pretty easy, nothing to worry about there, sadly does remove a lot of tension.
If you play this game like a bog standard FPS  - as if you were playing the original Wolfenstein - it will feel just like that, so be creative.
This game feel special. The atmosphere and universe that has been created. It's chilling and beautiful, and being thrust into a fight where you are under the underdog actually gives you a sense of hopelessness. And the way B.J has been portrayed makes the whole thing seem personal. And the game is LITTERED with easter eggs, showing it's heritage (one REALLY shows it), not to mention the collectables, some which may give you a titter, as it did me.
Christ listen to me, I know I've been gushing a lot and I'm kind of sick of it. So yeah, downsides.
There's not enough. Simple as that. You quickly lose track of where you are and why you're doing what your doing. The game constantly leaps from place to place, I'm here, now I'm here! Hah ha! Seriously, stop. Slow down. The problem is that a lot has been crammed into a finite amount of space. While in development, W:TNO was porobably never meant to be more than about 30GB. Instead there was just so much stuff to pry in as well as making the game look and sound as awesome as it is.
Understandably devs and gamers alike would be asking "what would *this* be like if the Nazis had won WW2?" and so on, so they had to take the best bits and leave whatever they could spare, filling the gaps with (albeit excellent) cutscenes and little snippets mid game.
There isn't enough backstory in the Nazi take over, a few newspaper snippets,  but still, not enough. The whole secret society of awesome inventions? Not enough backstory. Concrete mould? Mentioned as a major sabotage plot and then forgotten throughout the game. And there just isn't enough character development for any of the members of the resistance cell. There are some great concepts there that just weren't followed through properly.
Oh, and the resistance HQ in central Berlin - asscessible by 'stealth helicopters'...
1. You can see a stealth ANYTHING with your eyes - especially if it's a ♥♥♥♥ing helicopter.
2. You think the Germans, THE GERMANS of ALL PEOPLE, wouldn't notice the painfully obvious terrorist headquarters, let alone the four ENORMOUS, SUPER-LOUD, STOLEN, TOP SECRET helicopters flying from it on a daily ♥♥♥♥ing basis?! Stop it. Try harder next time.
But you can't blame the devs for leaving all this stuff out. They probably reached 30GB worth of data and thought "Sh!t...we've only got half our game here chaps, something's gotta go. And what they have ended up with isn't the longest game, nor is it revolutionary...but it has been made not just by industry heavyweights, but by people who love an adventure and a bloody good shoot up. It's almost a movie made by gamers and a game made by movie fans.
I love what they've done with this game. Not too mindless, not too thoughtful, very pretty, very gripping, very evil, very touching...and less than £40.

While I mostly completed the campaign with some ease, I would not say that it stalled me to the point of research particularly often, but it made up for it by telling the previously unexplained story of what was happening in the original Portal, you discorver more about yourself and how you got there, with querky characters that are fully voice acted, and if you have completed the campaign (or are just bored of it -not saying you would be-) you can go to the co-operative multiplayer section and enjoy solving puzzles with your friends (or random people over the internet) with an ability to message them directly in-game. If that is not your sort of thing, or you just find the puzzles too easy, then there is a fully interactive level creator, so that you can build your own test chambers using most of the equipment you see in the story, and to make it better you can even play them co-operatively too, while the story is roughly 6-7 hours (if you are competant -unlike me-), you will have alot of challenges to face as the story begins to unravel. The ending I found enjoyable even though I have only completed it on console (which does not have the level builder) only to find the bundle on a previous steam sale including both portal one and two. Like most valve games there are many console commands you can use if you get bored or are completing it again. My overall verdict is that Portal 2 is an enjoyable experience for those who enjoyed playing the original Portal or newcomers as little to none was explained in the last game, My score would be 9/10, an unique experience with a great multiplayer and a level builder, while it may be challenging for newcomers or the casual audience, the veterans of the game may pause for less time as they did for the first time they played the first game.     -RedWyvern

In a previous version of this review, I talked at length about how, in spite of some utterly broken mechanics, horrible shooting, and uniformly hostile attitude towards new or casual players, that the game was worth playing.  That a new player's first few bleak, infuriating hours being dropped into the middle of a warzone could be offset by the promise of some of the most incredible spectacles of warfare ever depicted in a game.
Yeah, well I was too generous.  This game is f*cking appalling.  In fact, it might be the single worst game I have ever played.  Not because it isn't utterly beautiful to look at, or isn't full of incredible potential; but because how much of its potential is squandered.  Mercilessly and repeatedly.
Your first experience of this game, past the hateful, broken tutorial, is being dropped into the middle of 'solo' play, which even Planetside's pathologically sycophantic community unanimously describe as 'really not very fun'.  It's a miserable, directionless zergfest of epic proportions, in which tactics play almost no role at all, and attrition reigns supreme.
You can join a squad, but all that really achieves is a few markers on your HUD and a measly exp boost.  Your squad will likely be as directionless, bored and confused as you are, because that's all you can ever be while playing the game this way.
The 'REAL' way to play the game is to join an 'outfit', or a clan by any other name.  This sounds like a great idea, but it's where the game's problems really begin to surface.  Unless you're a high-ranked player with excellent twitch skill and kill-to-death ratio, then you can be one of three things - a medic, an engineer, or a burden.  This hierarchy makes it incredibly difficult for new or less skilled players to actually enjoy the game.  Repairing turrets and healing other players is tedious and thankless, and considering most players who signed up for this game wanted to play an FPS, it strikes me as a gallingly bad investment of leisure time.
It's been said by the developers that the game experiences a huge amount of 'churn' in terms of new players - that an overwhelming majority of players give up entirely before they reach Rank 8.  Often in the past, on the Daybreak forums and on PS2's official Reddit, new players would air grievances similar to this rant/review, only to be branded as 'whiners and quitters'.  This outright hostility to new players is perhaps the blackest mark of all against this game.  While free-to-play, I nevertheless ended up regretting playing this game, not because it's a waste of money, but because it's a colossal waste of time.  I regret every minute I spent playing this f*cking atrocity.

Overall I would give the game a 3 out of 5.   The gameplay is good overall.  Graphics, mood, environment all are well done.  However, there are *A LOT* of cutscenes throughout the game and we're not talking short ones either.  For me these cutscenes really seemed to disrupt the game play.  If you are into a story then the cutscenes probably will not bother you too much.
The game does include some interesting areas and scenarios such as rope climbing up the side of the fortress while shooting nazis from the windows, and lunar scenario including a brief space suit walk, etc.
There are more than a few missions that seem to disrupt the game play by making all your guns disappear either by being 'captured' in some way or just for no reason you start a new mission without weapons (even though you just had them from the previous area).
Overall, the game is very linear in game play.  You can wander a bit in each level but pretty much you are limited to a certain path/ area.  Also, replayability for this game seems very limited.  I have no desire to play it over at a hard level due to cut scenes.  Some scenarios just seem a bit tedious, almost more a chore to play than actual fun due to the amount of grinding through endless nazies.
Sneak attacking and stealth kills are fun but ultimately you should expect to end up in a gun battle at some point.
*BIG TIME SPOILER ALERT*
Finally, the ending is completely disappointing in that you die after the final boss battle with the old nazi guy but things seem left undone.  The secondarily boss chick lady (who should of died earlier in the game) also seems to be left alive and that part of the story seems unfinished.
Get the game for the game play and story if you are interested.  However, don't expect too much from the ending.  I personally would wait for it to go on sale and catch it half price.

Simply put, this game it not worth 60 dollars. Once it has been out for a year, I would recommend anyone to buy it. The problem is that every new chapter I became more and more dissapointed with missed opportunities. I love that this game has lazer weapons, but the fact that you can sit behind a wall next to an outlet and just kill everyone hurts this game. I wanted to be rushing around shooting people with double assualt rifles, but why when I can just use an infinite ammo sniper? This is just one way the game messes up your power fantasy. I wanted to be on a bridge and snipe hoards of people running at me, I wanted to shoot nazis on the moon with super no-gravity jumps. Bridge to moon might seem like a far away comparison, but they are literally only one cutscene away. This game just skips so much over. The levels start to feel like a task because they aren't connected in any way. The story was pretty good, but its been a few days and I haven't thought about it, so the effect wasn't lasting or powerul. Also the texture quality is pretty bad, dual wielding weapons blocks half your screen, and you can't disable depth of field. If it goes on sale, buy it, there were some fun experiences in it, and could be considered a step in the right direction. Health and armor systems are awesome, you may start to question yourself (should have been expanded), and most of the guns are fun.

I just finished this game and am quite happy with my purchase. I was somewhat apprehensive at first being that it’s a ID tech5 game, it’s odd to me to have an engine that can look phenomenal at times and terrible at others, anyways enough about the game engine. Wolfenstein the New Order was an absolute blast with a good amount of game play. I finished it in almost 16hrs, although I’ll admit that I like to search almost everywhere for items, regardless 16hrs is a good game length especially when compared to MW3 or CoD:BO which cost the same and only come in around 6hrs. I experienced very few bugs in this game, figured I’d mention that. There was some odd yet funny nostalgia moments in the game that most should find pretty amusing. This game mixes a lot of different forms of game interaction together, there is some outcome based decision making, operation of vehicles, choice of guns-a-blazing or stealth to make it through a mission. When you add all of this up, along with a pretty solid story line, however at times odd you get a solid game. Will I play it through again? Probably not, however I will probably always wonder how my decision making affected the outcome vs. a different choice.
In conclusion: This is a good game, $60 good? Meh, but when compared to some other $60 choices this is top class. If you’ve got the $ to spare then spend away knowing that you’ll be satisfied, if $40 is more your budget wait and get a great game.

This game was good untill the update that ruined the weapons system.  If you have been playing this game for a while like I have, it is a huge problem because higher level weapons are not as available as they used to be.  Before, you unlocked weapons as your level increased, and then you could buy them with RP and get them.  Now, you get crates which follow this rule: protonium and diamond: slight chance at epic, generally a few rare's and multiple uncommons.  Gold and below: uncommons and commons.  The worst part is items are sold for 25% of their buy price so it is nearly impossible to buy new weapons with robits.  Now my second complaint: crates are awarded for team ranking.  Before, the money you got was directly related to your score, so I would get X ammount of money for my score.  Now I could get a score of 2000 ish in a league arena, that would get me somewhere around 100,000 RP enough money to get about halfway to buying a max level non-meagabot SMG.  Now, I get a score of about 2000, there are 4 players who have scores slightly higher ( greater than mine but less than 3000), and I get a silver crate, where I have probably less than a 1% chance of getting the item I want.  Now, while the fast and formidable update helped some with balence,  ROBOCRAFT RUINED THE MONEY SYSTEM.

It's like playing through an action movie. Very much fun as a shooter, even though I liked the atmosphere of the older games more. Still in the entire game I never felt like any surrounding had been made by "copy paste principle". The environment repeats rarely to never which is pretty unique to me. Gameplaywise I would say that, at least when playing on hard or higher difficulty, being in a firefight with 5 enemies really feels like you are in deep trouble. As the game says you need to have at least "ok" aim and use bullettime to get through the game alive, when you play on hard or higher difficulty, and even then there are scenes in which you die a lot. If you know the old games, Max still is the same guy. They did not change his temper or personality in general, besides him being older of course.
Overall I would say it is quite an experience, no matter if you have played the previous  Max Payne games or not. Also in my opinion it's a great game, gameplay- and storywise.
