This Wolfenstein is simply the best shooter of the recent few years. Everything about it just feels right.
The gunplay feels right- this is so important in a shooter, and Wolfenstein nails this for every gun. Everything has a nice heft, and you can shoot through cover, e.g. cover destruction as seen in titles like Stranglehold and....Stranglehold. You can dual wield every gun at the cost of being able to aim down sights. Dual AR/Shotgun/Rocket Launcher? Yes/yes/yes. You can sprint and slide and shoot while sliding. Ok, you slide like two feet if it's not under an obstacle, so it's not terrible useful, but you get style points.
All aspects of the sound are great- guns sound nice and full, knife attacks are rightfully 'squishy' sounding, and all the voice acting is excellent. The voice actor for Blazkowicz is especially good- he isn't given too many truly emotive lines, but his low-down heavy bass voice is perfect for the somber quips the game tries to sell, and it really is very fitting for an internal-monologue narrator voice.
The graphics, art style, and environmental design are excellent. While it's not Crysis levels of detail, it's still very good looking. The poly counts are good, and I haven't seen any obvious blurry textures so far. There also aren't any obvious flat surfaces like the type you might see in a 360/PS3 shooter, besides the admittedly high crate population. The environments are all very nicely designed and cluttered so they feel real. Even crates are often breakable for pickups, and they don't each contain just the pickup, but tinned clutter.
The level design and pacing are so well done- straight nonstop shooting can get monotonous, but this gets broken up by sections where pure stealth around is viable, or by mini-boss fights, or small setpiece/cutscenes. The level locations are all also very different, as each of the 16 chapters has a different feel to it. This plus the fact that each chapter is separated by story cutscenes instead of flowing into each other without interruption, adds to a feeling of genuine variety.
Lastly, the writing is absolutely excellent. It's a weird thing that no one expects of Wolfenstein, but I think it easily beats Bioshock: Infinite, a game people really expected to excel at storytelling. The fictional world and characters are exceedingly well done in this game, and they're all supported very well through letters, recordings, newspaper articles, and simply the levels of the game taking place in many varied locations. The relationship between the main characters is also far more believable and nuanced than in BI or any other shooter I can remember. I have to say it's not perfect- I mean, there are plenty of RPGs that have a deeper story, and some of Wolfenstein's cutscenes can feel a little disjointed, as if they didn't have enough time to really expand on them, but what is there is just fantastically executed, and the ending just might bring a tear to a few people's eyes.

I have never played any of the Wolfenstein games, so this review will be a first impression of the title.
I have only played it through once, I may play it a second time to see what can be different, as there appears to be choices of who to save, you can if you want to do it in stealth or full guns blazing. "Enjoyable full guns blazing, but can regret it when you get overwelming Nazi's and machines, not really a bad thing though."
The story is very good for an alternative history, having seen that my allies have failed to repel the Nazi's and they have won, made me feel like that some♥♥♥♥♥kicking is in order, save the people who live in fear of being test subjects and killed, but it is getting common with "ONE MAN WILL FIGHT THE WHOLE ARMY/COUNTRY TO SAVE THE WORLD, AND ONLY YOU CAN DO IT" thing, but oh well, its still very much enjoyable.
The gameplay feels very arcadey which kinds of ruins the story telling, which I have enjoyed from what I could pay atention from, you just mostly feel like shooting Nazi's and not listen to the story as much (or at all), which is a shame, the ending is good in my view, I would like to know if there is an alternative ending though.
Skills feel like that they are not needed at all, they just feel wasted, I focused mainly on stealthing the game, so that I don't have to worry about getting hoards of Nazi's after me, but as I got further into the game, stealth became very much useless and you are forced to shoot everything, even though I had unlocked nothing in dual wield or single wield, I was still able to kill those Nazi's with ease.
AI, oh boy...the AI is very basic in a way, as I have had many times that Nazi's are staring right at me in stealth, and just walk past me with no sound of alarm, you can just see their face staring right at you, they do this "is....someone," and keeps walking, either the Nazi's have really bad eye sight or their helmet goggles have too much tint of black, another bad AI was when you do get spotted, you can hear the Nazi soldier raises his voice in supprise, but the other Nazi's don't take any notic of him, if you kill him before he finishes his line, the alarm wont be raised.
The games collectables are easy to find once you have foudn the map in the level, which is very close by at the start, sometimes a bit later on, but the map will show you every tunnel and all the collectables to get, this does stop the fun of searching for them, but there are time that you have to find a certain item to be able to reach the next room, plus the enigma codes is something I think every fan of the Wolfenstein game would enjoy collecting, as if they solved the enigma they can unlock new modes and difficulty to the game, and I would most likely thing the very first Wolfenstein game.
Would I recommend this game to my friends? I would say that the fans would enjoy this game a lot, but for people who have not played the Wolfenstein games before, not as much, if they like arcadey feel to the game, then yes I would recommend this game to them.

Hands down better than any triple A first person shooter on the market. If you're sick of campers and the laser tag style of play games like CoD offers then you should be downloading this game right now.
I noticed some folks here complaining about bugs. Maybe these are old posts or they are just playing on an old rig. I personally have not encountered any of these, as far as I know, if I have they have been so few and far in between that I haven't noticed them.
There is no pay to win in this game, most of the items can be earned with certification points, which take time to earn. "Most" of the items that cost real money are cosmetic, helmets, camo, horns for vehicles etc. You can either pay money for weapons or take the time and earn the certification points to acquire them. If you're an avid player of FPS's this will be no problem for you. I'm thinking some of the folks screaming pay to win are going in as medics/infiltrators/engineers and charging into the frontlines thinking they are gonna kill everything they see. A medic that gets killed 100 times and only has 2 kills for themselves is more than likely doing their job properly and racking up cert points.
System requirements are not that steep. It's also available on PS4 if your PC is older. This is my basic setup:
CPU: AMD 6x 3.50 GHz
GPU: AMD R7 250X 1GB
RAM: 16 GB
Hardly high end... But it still allows me to run on Ultra settings @60 FPS with no drop in frame rate even at the most chaotic of times.
There are more classes to choose from than a lot of MMORPG's, such as support classes (medic and engineer). These are the best classes to start (earn certification points) with. New players should start on one of these 2 classes and use the certification points they earn on the class they want to use overall. You can earn certs on any class and spend them on any class or vehicle.
Flight in this game is not for everyone. If you try to jump in any of the air vehicles and fly it like you're flying a jet in Battlefield or Ace Combat or something similar, you're gonna have a bad time. Luckily there is a VR training center that lets you use any vehicle, air or land, so you can get the hang of it.
My only problem with this game is that outside of youtube there is almost no tutorial. A new player gets dropped in with no sense of direction, no understanding of the icons on the maps, and no way of knowing how to easily earn certification points to upgrade themselves or their vehicles. So if you plan on installing this game, I'd suggest heading on over to youtube while it's downloading.

Shooters of today are dumbed down and force you along a linear path which feels more like a chore than a game.  Wolfenstein The New Order is a call back to when shooters were supposed to be fun and engaging. You can dual wield any gun in the game and the stealth kills are different if you have one knife or two. You carry every gun from the start of the level to the end unlike other shooters with only two weapon swapping.  Not only can you backtrack for ammo and health but you can run around looking for collectables and newspaper articles which give you story. You can see how many collectables are in the level and where they can be found on the map, which is a nice touch.  The game doesnt hold your hand or bug you every five seconds about the mission and you can run around the level without consequence.  The sounds of the game are top notch and should be turned up.  The guns in the game have a fair amount of recoil and have the distinct sound of firing a weapon.  Everything just feels right when you are firing dual shotguns at your enemy.
The two downsides that i will say arent that great are 1.) The perk system is kind of tacked on and feels cheap but on the bright side if you die (or reload) all of the progress on the perk tree stays with you.  So you could grind out perks that you want and you dont have to progress the story if you dont want. 2.) There isnt any saving just checkpoints. On the bright side the checkpoints are very close together so you never lose a half hour of gameplay.
As the story unfolds you get to see what the Nazis were infamous for during WW2. This game shows and tells you a lot of very literal things that are historically accurate even if this game is set in fiction. The portrayal of what the Reich did to people and the fear, pain, and misery they instilled into the world is clearly on display. The times may be different (in game) but the evil things that the Nazis do is nothing new. This game, for me at least, makes me want to be a better person in spite of all the dehumanizing things that happen.  It makes me want to help somebody i dont know because its the right thing to do.
There was some setbacks at launch, but as with any new game it will be patched out.  The game feels right at home on the PC with no distinguishable console features.
All in all its one of the best run and gun games to come out in a long time.  You can see that the game wasnt just another carbon copy of CoD but a game made out of love for the genre. This game may not be the game of the year but it has a lot of heart. The hype and marketing campaign comes with any triple A game and while its not the be all end all of shooters it is a well crafted game that does the Wolfenstein name proud.  IMHO this game is worth the money.

So I'm a big Wolfenstein fan going back to the original 1992 version and there was no way I was going to pass this up.  The game overall is great looking; backgrounds and world look fantastic even in lower resolutions.  The game play is pretty typical of any FPS with the exception of the dual wield function which you can do with almost any weapon.  You can really do some damage when you fire with both of the assault rifles or shotguns at the same time, or better yet set one assault rifle to fire rockets and one to fire bullets.  The dual wield sniper rifles are a little silly but novel and fun to try.  You cannot mix and match (ie one shotty and one assault rifle).  Game play is mostly shoot'em up, but there are a number of areas where stealth is strongly advised and encouraged.  There is a pretty good selection of weapons but typically at the beginning of each level your weapons are removed and you have to start with what the game gives you for that level and what you can find during the mission.  Weapons include knives, grenades, pistols, assault rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles and the laserkraftwerk which is a laser rifle with a number of upgrades available (its cutting feature is also important).  All the rifles have alternate fire modes (ie rockets on the assault rifle, shrapnel ammo for the shotty etc.)
Controls are pretty standard.  One thing I didn't like was the slide function.  On a standard keyboard you have to hold down "W and SHIFT" to run forward, then tap CTRL to slide under obstacles.  It's fairly awkward and you will have to do it half a dozen times throughout the game, plus 3 times while killing an enemy to earn a perk.
Perks are a major feature of the game and are split up into 4 categories (Stealth, Tactical, Assault and Demolition) with 8 perks per category.  Earning perks gives you access to better weapon mods and features .  Killing enemies with knives in various ways and in certain numbers will earn you stealth perks while killing with grenades or rockets will earn you demolition perks as an example.  The one downside to this system is you generally must obtain one perk before moving onto the next.  So in the case of Demolition you must kill 10 enemies with grenades before you can work on the next perk which is to kill an enemy commander with a grenade.  Even if you already killed a commander in the first 10 enemies, it won’t count toward the new perk.  Perks are permanently part of your character once earned.
The game has a deep story and cinematics, most of which can be skipped on a second playthrough, but some you will have to sit through a second time (ie the train scene).  Most of the story is good, but gets a bit tedious in spots.  Fighting Nazis on the moon is tough to beat!
If you are a person who likes a lot of collectibles, this game has them in spades: enigma codes, gold pieces, health boosts, personal letters that give various peoples stories of the Nazi world etc.  They’re all relatively easy to find (I got 75-90% on my first play through), but a few are tricky and Steam guides are a big help.  There are a couple of others (concept art and characters) that are triggered automatically when you encounter a character or area of a map.  The enigma codes unlock other game play modes when you manage to crack them.
Achievements are all pretty easy to get; there are 50 overall.  All of the 32 perks generate an achievement when you get them, most of the rest are for collectibles and making it through various stages of the game.
Some of the downsides : too short overall, no multiplayer, AI is wak in spots (this is NOT Dishonored), highly linear (this is NOT Fallout New Vegas) whihc affects re-playability and the save feature is limited to game autosaves.  The autosave is especially annoying as it overwrites if you decide to replay a previous chapter from the menu.  If you do decide to re-play a previous chapter, do it once you have finished your current chapter so as not to lose any game play.
One word of advice with respect to the perk feature, keep an eye on it constantly and try to determine if a given situation you are in most suited to obtaining a certain perk.  I would even go so far as to recommend playing the first mission a few times over before moving on to try to pick up as many perks as possible.  Otherwise you may find yourself playing the game the way the perk system forces you to instead of the way you want.
I’m not sure whether or not this is worth $60.  I think the casual FPS fan would feel it is overpriced.  Probably $30 is a good trigger price.
As a final note unlike others I did not have any hardware issues (i7-960 Bloomfield, EVGA GTX 570, 12GB RAM and Asus P6X58D Mobo).  My system is about 3 years old.
This game needs to be more advertised. It's a really good game and I enjoy it immensely. But it needs more players.

This is one of the few games that can arguably be said to be worth the $60 asking price.  It's a high price, of course, above the price we PC gamers expect of new games.  However, it must be said that no part of this game is half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ none of it.  You can see flaws in many great games where they obviously cut corners or ran out of budget, here, everything just works, the shooting, the stealth, the story, the production values, and there is just a feeling of quality that permiates the game.  It feels like a more modern version of HL2, in a way.
Graphics
The graphics of the game are a wonder to behold.  I played this on an EVGA 760 Superclocked, and I noticed zero framerate studdering, no tearing, just smooth as butter.  People look very striking, the skyboxes are amazing, and pretty much all the textures look and feel excellent, adding to the feeling of immersion.
Weapons
All the weapons are pretty great, I won't spoil any of them, but they all feel like they have their useful situations.  They all have real heft and kick to them, and feel suitably powerful.  Weapons upgrades also help to round out the experience.
Gameplay
A welcome surprise is the presence of stealth gameplay in what I thought would be a typical 'shoot mans' game.  Much like in metro last light you can instakill enemies by sneaking up on them.  You also get a silencer for your pistol early on, allowing you to headshot enemies across the map stealthily, which is pretty great.  It feels a little like cheating, but it's still loads of fun to clear an area with only 4 shots and 3 stabbings.
Story/levels
Another element that I thought would be lacking is actually perhaps the game's most striking feature.  Each of the game's levels feel nessisary to the plot, nothing feels like filler, there is never any question as to what you are doing to advance the plot, and all your actions feel impactful and rewarding.  to reiterate, NOTHING FEELS LIKE FILLER!  There is also a lot of optional side content, and for the most part it is very high quality.
Overall, I was extremely satisfied with my purchase of this game.  I would recommend it without question to fans of the shooter genre, especially if it was on deal.
Warnings
There is lewd sexual content in here as well as some rather cringeworthy torture, though it's a lot breifer and more tastefully done than Burial at Sea 2's disgusting torture scene, that's for sure.  Basically keep the kids away from it, this is an adult game for adults, and elder teenagers I suppose.

Wolfenstein The New Order is a great addition to the series, adding a yet alternate story to an already alternate history. Where is actually goes from here in the telling of the iD Universe, not exactly sure.
Gameplay is quite smooth and still mainstains mostly the classic FPS, along with some more modern mechanics like peaking, sliding, etc. Controls labeling could use an improvement, i.e. switching to alternate fire on any weapons in left or right hands is not adequately labeled. The choice on some levels to go completely stealth covert or guns blazing is a nice addition ot the series.
Graphics are really awesome on character models and distant objects, however most static objects up close render in such a extreme low resolution it looks like some items like pens or notepads on a table liike like they were drawn with a crayon. Things like that shouldve just been a high res flat photo instead of looking like a texture from games in the circa 1999 generation
Storyline is well written, though the wolfenstein games never really had a full blown story ever (even RTCW had pretty much a straight forward mission dialog to get from point a to point be kill X, you didnt really interact with anyone). There is plenty of well placed comic relief near areas that potentially become aggrevating. Also the unexpected love interactions between our hero and his damsel, which is more comical than it is a romance.
Easter eggs are far and few but the ones that are there like treasures and enigma code documents are generally scattered in hidden places like anyother Wolfenstein game. Others like the Nightmare sequence is a really awesome, yet all too short, easter egg which should bring back some old memories for us early gamers (they changed the audio dialog, which I found really sad).
All in all I'd say for strictly a single player game (which i find the best for FPS titles) Wolfenstein The New Order is a great addition to the series. My only question that would remain is... Is this it for B.J. Blazkowicz?

: A solid FPS, and the only one on the market that
puts "massively" in MMO. Pick it up if you enjoy FPS games with specialized classes that fill niche roles, all of which is bundled wonderfully with excellent gunplay, awesome vehicle combat, a fully fledged build-it-wherever base system, and an amazing community. Also, did I mention it's
?
Where to begin?
I jokingly reviewed this game back in mid-late 2015, when I had about 450 hours of gameplay logged on steam, and covered what, to me, were the important points about each class. That review is gone now, because you're reading this one, which is my attempt at a legitimate overview of why you
to play this game
. That's the big kicker that gets most people, just how far flung from the norm Planetside 2 takes the FPS genre. No it doesn't reinvent the wheel, but it gives us something that no other FPS, not even the ARMA series, can provide:
. Battlefield players, ARMA players, take a step back before you jump into this beast, because this isn't a lobby shooter.
Planetside 2 is the most frantic, chaotic, and sometimes ludicrous entry to the FPS genre that has ever graced our monitors. I'll condense this review into individual parts for your reading pleasure, and do my best to explain how each works. The topics I'll cover are: Scale, Gameplay, and Playability.
There are four continents in the game excluding the beginner continent of Koltyr, which is locked to only allow entry up to level 15, which is when the game boots you into the real meat grinder. I personally have never bothered playing Koltyr, as it is optional, and cannot attest to it's size in comparison to the rest. The four continents in question are Amerish, Indar, Esamir, and Hossin. Each of these maps are so enormous, and filled with so many outposts, bunkers, power stations and the like, that even after almost 530 hours I have yet to visit all the locations on even
map. Arguably this boils down to the territory that your faction controls (which dictates when you get to see those places without being rendered a smoking stump), but such size has rarely been accomplished even in singleplayer games, and only the Just Cause series comes to mind with similarly enormous expanses.
Your main concern in the gameplay department is going to be centered around the five main classes, with the specialized sixth. These classes are:
: The sniper, the spy, everyone's favorite guy.
Infiltrators can cloak, scout out enemy positions, carry sniper rifles or any number of scout rifles (semi-auto, high powered, mid-range guns) or SMGs, and hack enemy terminals. They specialize in making you regret not checking every corner, and standing in front of windows. They are very squishy though, so if you plan to play one, be extra careful.
: To infinity, and beyond!
Light Assault is all about momentum, agility, and attacking from literally
angle (but not upside-down, then he'd be Batman). Light Assaults wield carbines, and are usually known for dropping C4 on enemies down below, thus leading to their moniker: C4-Fairies.
:
But seriously though, Engineers are the lifeblood of this game. They wield the same weapons as Light Assaults, but can also deploy shielded gun turrets for killing infantry, rocket turrets for killing vehicles, auto-turrets for... sucking... and small barriers to provide mobile cover to allies. They also give ammo to allies and repair structures, vehicles, and MAX units. Did I mention they have a lot of explosives? Because they do, and in many different flavors.
: You'll often hear people spamming the 2 macro to call for this guy.
The Combat Medic heals and revives allies, and has specialized grenades to make his healing AoE or his reviving even more AoEee. He also carries assault rifles, which are the bigger brother of carbines, and make him a mid-range monster. This is my personal favorite class <3
: Do you like gun? I like gun. Here, have all the gun.
Heavy Assaults are the fists, whereas Engineers and Combat Medics are more like the spine and ribs, and the LA's and Infiltrators are fingers which are always trying to touch you. You'd notice it a lot sooner if a Heavy Assault touched you though. They carry the
guns, like LMG's, burst-fire shotguns, plasma cannons, and rocket launchers. To top all that off, they have toggle shields which can absorb a whole extra health bar of damage. As such, they obviously specialize in gun, but also kill.
: It's Hulk after an NRA meeting.
The MAX is a specialized class in the game that requires the expenditure of nanites to use, which are the constantly regenerating pool of resources that you spawn vehicles, grenades, and equipment from for combat. The MAX is a bullet sponge that can equip anti-infantry, anti-vehicle, or anti-air weapons, one on each arm. Their size as infantry units lets them operate indoors where vehicles normally can't go, but they pack roughly the same firepower, and shred everything in their path. However, they can only be repaired by engineers, have no shields, and are easy targets for rockets or C4-Fairies. For these reasons it is best to treat them like a siege breaker, where teammates supplement your downfalls, and you tank all the hits for them.
These six classes all hold very specific roles on the battlefield, but are certainly not limited to them, at least most of the time. Beyond the infantry, there is an extensive vehicle and aircraft game which has a life of it's own, and promotes the development of some truly outstanding pilots and aces in the community. There is also a massive base building mechanic that was added in recent updates, which is a game in and of itself, one that I have personally taken part in and can endorse.
No, I'm not sure if "playability" is an actual word, and I'm too lazy to google it and find out. If it's meaning (my meaning) has gone over your head, I am referring to the "fun factor" of Planetside 2. We don't play games that aren't fun, and I certainly wouldn't mean to somehow misconstrue the flaws of this game. The issue is, that beyond the occasional bug or glitch, the game is not
hard or unenjoyable. Balance across all weapons and classes is fantastic, and that extends to the vehicular portion of the game as well. Where the concern comes in is the human factor.
When you first enter this game, you
be roflstomped into the ground, repeatedly. It doesn't matter if you're a veteran of FPS titles, because there is no game on the market except Planetside 2 that puts you in a field, with two hundred enemies collectively firing at you. This is all because the game is built around the players; the players drive the action, and dictate where, and when, things will happen. There are no NPCs, and there are no scripted events (barring Alerts, but that's just incentive to keep playing and is entirely optional). From the get-go you'll fight against people who have honed their aim and techniques over hundreds of hours, or perhaps years of their lives. Don't be discouraged though.
Everyone starts at the bottom, and if you accept that you're there, you can have a blast in Planetside 2. The community is something to behold, for better or worse, and I highly recommend you find an Outfit as soon as possible if you start playing. You won't get much milage out of the game without being a team player.
The final concern would be the grind, as it is a Free 2 Play game. I'll be quick, because my word count is too high, but it's nothing to worry about. If what you've read has made you curious, it's free, so there's no harm in trying.
Goodluck out there soldier!

This is a great game, especially since its free to download, but it isn't without its flaws. I would suggest that if you like what you see, download and try it. I do have alot to say about Robocraft that isn't positive, but it is a fun game for possibly the 4-12 hours of enjoyment that you can get out of it before the game becomes repetitive and manipulative. If you do manage to get past the early stage where it has you do the same chore of playing on team deathmatch atleast 20 times (no joke, the only option's are either team deathmatch or Ai bots), way more of the good side of the game opens up. Unfortunately after the new and better modes open up, the game starts to show off its quick and gimmicky cash grabbing trait that may harm any free to play users experience. For starters, many players that pay for premium in the game, have a high chance of earning DOUBLE or more ingame currency (in the form of sellable objects) than any free to play users. Another negative is that the small amount of legendary items that are in the game are overpriced on purpose to get you to pay to be able to get them almost instantly compared to other users that play for free. The legendary items are almost impossible to get if you play for free without putting in weeks into grinding ingame currency through the repetitive and small choice of modes. The reason that im mentioning the legendary items alot is that they are broken and literally will always make the team with the most legendary items win. I have heard that if you are a high enough level (like weeks worth) then the legendary items won't be as impacting and cheap to you but the reason that this group of items matter so much at a small level is that this game is unfairly balanced at choosing your opponents and allies. I also am certain that small algorithm's are in place to favour anyone that pays to make them feel special so that they get more and/or begin getting addicted. The game seems like a good spin on the 3PS/FPS genre but in reality it is an exact replica of the established and photo-copied 3PS/FPS addiction formula. The music is nice, polished and catchy, my favourite being Tihonium canyon. There is ingame options to change everything to fit your computer's needs (good sound and graphical settings). On the best settings you possibly can achieve, the game is beautiful and is up to todays standards. Some bugs might appear and may change/ruin your experience but not to many exist. If I gave it a rating, Id give it a 7/10.

What a fantastic game. I don't regret pre-ordering this one bit. This is what storylines in games need to be like. With well-developed characters, alternate timelines, and protagonists you actually despise, a lot of game developers could take a lesson from Wolfenstein the New Order.
Think about it. You can beat this game as quick as 10 hours, as long as 20. But you'll want to do it again based on a choice you make in the prologue that changes the story in a few different ways (including gameplay, to some degree). Because of how quiock you can beat this game, though, you'd think a lot of people would be dissatisfied. Heck, even I'm a bit disappointed by how short it is. And of course, many are still butthurt about no multiplayer. But the fact that the visuals, gameplay, and storyline are enough to counterbalance that? That's where developers need to take note. You don't need a massive sandbox to make a fantastic game (though it can be quite awesome). You don't even need multiplayer. All you need is a good story and good gameplay. Be original, and be compelling. Wolfenstein delivers there incredibly well.

Wolfenstein, the alternate universe or reality where the Nazis win World War 2 and rule the world. Under the command of General Deathshead, the Nazis are fearless and unstopable but, there is one person that can stop them, William "B.J." Blazkowicz.
The story of this game is about a soldier named B.J. Blazkowicz, he was in the war when the Nazis were still fighting World War 2. He and his squad attacked Deathshead compound and failed. Blazkowicz went to the loony bin for 14 years, until the Nazis closed down the asylum that B.J. was in. The family that kept Blazkowicz alive and healthy was killed but, one person, Anya Oliwa, a girl who he later ♥♥♥♥s. He and her, go to her relatives in Poland, nearby where they tell Blazkowicz that the war is over and the Nazis won. He asks if there is a resistance and they said no resistance, they are all locked up and he decided to break them out. With the resistance on his side, he hopes to change the war outcome to favor his side, the U.S.
The gameplay of this game is great, the weapons, how they play out, and the upgrades for them. The dual wielding in this game is suprisingly good, most games, their dual wielding is crap but, you are really accurate. IGN (Ignorant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s) said the only bad things about this game are the dual wielding and the quote on quote "Archaic gun/ammo pickup", Archaic means very old or old-fashioned. The gun pick is a bit stupid but, I wouldn't say old. I think every game has a pickup similar to that, and IGN shouldn't decrease the score of the game because of that. This game has a lot of replayablity, 5 game difficulties, plus other gamemodes by collecting collectables called Enigma codes, of course you can't have a Wolfenstein game without Nazi gold objects. Right now, I'm on my quest to collect all the collectables. I also did like the transition from 1948 to 1960's weapons, they looked a bit different but, they played differently.
The graphics in this game are really good. This game used the engine ID Tech 5, used in the game RAGE, which was a decent game but, most people called it "A visual display for ID Tech 5". This game looks a lot better than RAGE. Some textures are murky but, that maybe because I'm running the game on Medium. The weapon and character models are clear and smooth looking, no jagged edges. This engine, being two years old,  runs this game wonderfully. Console versions (Mostly current gen, Xbox 360 and PS3) come with 2-4 discs, that's how big the game is and how the graphics are. Loading times on some levels are a bit long, for example, the level where you have to derail a train, I died muliple times and the loading times took about 5-10 minutes, so after that, I was wise about when and where I died. But, loading times on the moon level took 30 seconds to a minute. So the loading times are an example of how the graphics are in this game.
Now, the sound, I thought were a good part of this game of course, what is a game without sound. The soundtrack of this game, mostly rock music, fit well with boss battles and intense scenes with waves of enemies. The gun sound effects fit well with the guns, the futuristic guns, such as the marksman rifle, sounded like how you would think a futuristic gun would sound like. I liked the futurisic feel of this 1960 period.

!NOTE! - If you don't want to read a detailed review, GO STRAIGHT TO THE PRO CON SECTION.
This game is probably one of the most satisfying Nazi killing game hands down! Visuals are fantastic, gameplay puts you in the zone, the music is so solid and amazing it fits the mood for every situation whether you're mowing down enemies, exploring a location or picking a stealthy approach, this game has a good bunch of everything.
However, one thing to note is the story. The entire premise is captivating, well executed and definitely makes you feel like the Nazi's are in power. But one thing is a small issue and is quite ironic: The story. While the story is there, it is good and puts you in the middle of it all, you forget the reason why you're doing anything you're being told on any point in the chapter. This is actually just a small factor in the game, as it immediately puts you back on track. Now where to start with the review...
The Premise: The Nazis won the war and they are definitely in power. Wolfenstein: The New Order executes every bit of this atmosphere so well it is scary. It almost feels historical! Except for the fact that they are extremely technologicaly advanced. Aside from that, this game is amazing when it comes to making it seem like the Nazis really do control everything!
The Atmosphere: Every mission and environment are different in their own ways both visually and game wise. They really put you in the situation and allow you to feel the weight of it all. Althought the paths you take can be very linear, the world is open enough for you to feel like you are really exploring. Among other things, the Nazis are also one of the biggest parts of this atmospheres(as if you didn't know already). They add a really good grim feeling to anything they're are around while also adding a nice touch of military strength. If the Nazis weren't as good as they looked, this game would be bland.
The Graphics/Visuals: Stunning in every way shape and form. Honestly, this game is Tomb Raider levels of good. Lighting, shadows, character models and texturing are all so well done. Some parts lacked like the Lunar Base and other textures but they never removed from the game. On top of that, all the Characters, Enemies and Robots look so amazing its insane. Every Nazi soldier looks awesome that when you kill them you can't help but look at them. Each character is also very well detailed that you want to stare at them.
The Gameplay: Very solid for a first person shooter, and it is to be expected. Controls for leaning might be a bit wonky but it is no biggy. It is as basic as you can get with controls. But the weapons and enemies is where the meat of it all is of course. You have a varied but formiddable array of weapons to your disposal and on top of that most of which can be dual wielded. They can be upgraded as you progress and allow for dynamic fighting. The enemies you encounter however are what determine what you should be doing. You could encounter a large wave of enemies and need some serious automatic fire power, so why not dual wield Assault Rifles? Heavily armored troops could jump in so mount up some laser weaponry. Enemies too far away? Marksman rifle. Don't wanna deal with them all at once? Grab your knives and stealth kill everyone. The vast amount of choices to engage enemies is surprisingly wide.
Another thing to expand on with this game is that you actually make choices, both linear and personal. The game can make you do small or large decisions that can ultimately change the game itself or do something to the immediate situation. Really good. And then you have engagement options which varies between stealth and destruction.
The Characters: All characters are voiced and designed well. Although they are not incredibly attachable they allow you to be immersed in the game. However, you don't actually get to see much of them unless you're in the safe house or "taking care fo the dirty laundry". Otherwise, characters are well done.
The Main Character: William J. Blazkowicz is a pretty awesome and badass character. Well voiced and well designed. No real backstory is provided, just his part in WWII. All in all, pretty good.
What is BAD about the game?: Well first off, the game itself isn't actually that bad, it's just some things that take away from the experience. As said before, you forget the story all together. Sometimes frames might drop here and there but it's no serious issue. But one thing I find is actually lacking and that is difficulty. Honestly, the game wasn't that challenging until you reach "Death Incarnate" and even then it is relatively easy. I would highly recommend playing on "Uber" your first go. It will be challenging and it actually makes you feel like you're fighting a Nazi armada.
Pros -
+Stunning Visuals
+Gameplay is Fantastic
+Dynamic Choices
+Static Choices
+Nazis look EPIC
+Weapon array might be small but usage is massive
+Atmosphere is superb
+Really does feel like Nazis control EVERYTHING
+Characters are well voiced and personality wise AWESOME.
Cons-
-Story can be quite forgettable. You forget why you're doing this.
-Frames can drop randomly and even freeze. Might just be me.
-Difficulty really lacks. Play on UBER to really enjoy the game.

I would like to start off saying that this review is coming from someone that has played ALL the wolfensteins, and yes that includes Spear of Destiny. I will be doing my best to avoid spoilers.
I thoroughly enjoy the game and i've played through the story (one side of it), and althought the story only has 2 linear paths, its based off a critical decision. Wolfenstein works this style of story telling to its strength. This game made me feel like i was playing one of the original games that made me love the series, the subtle humour, the tense action moments, jaw clinching survival through battles, and embracement of multiple mechanics. This game has great pacing in difficulty and very astetically pleasing.
I played this game on a Quad Core AMD and a GTS 450, according to the minimum requirements, i shouldnt have been able to run this game, however i ran it at 60fps without fail (up until the final fight where i had minor frame issues that were fixed once i tweaked a couple settings), and it was nice to finally run into a game where my rig was challenged, a game that finally put "PC Master Race" to good use.
I didn't run into any game breaking bugs, like most nvidia/amd users. Overall it was simple, i got home, installed on my secondary HDD and off i went into the world of Wolfenstein.
The game starts off Dropping you into WW2, and immediately it feels like you're back playing RTCW (with EXTREME graphics and AI updates). The guns felt metallic, and powerful; the movement was smooth and fluid, and it was highly immersive. The games greatest strength is also its greatest problem, the game changed its focus from what it has done in the past 3 wolfensteins being cult focused into more of a Twitch Based Shooter, much like the original Wolfenstein (as "twitch" as possible, back in those days).  Which was not what I was expecting, however it was nice seeing them go back to the basics of what made wolfenstein great. Not the women running around in Latex outfits (although noone ever complained about that), just a man on a mission, using impossible guns, fighting Impossible monsters.
The game progresses and gets the player immersed within a great love story that truly brings you in. I admittedly had to put the game down (much to my dismay), due to having a job; but when i came back, i had no difficulty getting re-acquainted with the characters and being back in B.J.'s mind and living the games experience.
Without spoiling anything, the story was great, the development was solid. I would have liked to see more variety in Enemy soldier skins (for example: women, black nazi's,), or atleast more indepth reasoning into the world that was created. The story could have been elongated by a couple missions where you have to try to live in the alternate history world they created instead of just jumping into this new world and starting a revolution.  That way, as a person, you actually feel that this change is needed, as opposed to what i noticed from the commentary by most civilians during the game, that were happy with the Nazi Regime taking over and how they were living their lives. Alas, i'm being nit-picky on that point, overall the story had great consistent message and didn't leave me wondering "Where did that come from?"
Now, lets get to some negatives:
-The AI is inconsistent, sometimes they will get stuck running into walls, running into doors, you can sprint while stealthing around, and overall they seem fixated on ignoring you.
-The maps, although feel non-linear, are extremely linear that you really only have 2 options; stealth, or non-stealth. Some levels only have the non-stealth option aswell, and with the issue above, stealthing is super easy.
-Hidden items, Yes this is also a plus.. But they are seemingly in random locations. I should just find a gold knife in the middle of a room where i was fighting some bad guys..
-Hidden Rooms. Due to the amount of references back to the old wolfenstein, and the intro levels having a few hidden paths, i figured later in the game, there would have been alot more of this. These kinda drop off in the favour of the "cut the fence/box/wall" mechanic.. where rooms arent hidden.. you just have to look for the particular texture and problem solved.
-Lack of Multiplayer, Although the focus on the singleplayer made this a huge plus, one of the greatest attitributes of the Wolfenstein Series is the RTCW: ET expansion, where multiplayer just took it to new levels and reinvigorated the series. Although I would suspect an expansion will be coming in the future that will include this feature, or hopefully it will be in a patch....
Overall, I did greatly enjoy this game, and the negatives i can find with the game itself are minor at best (and the AI bug helped me at one point where i ran into problems near the end.. ). I would strongly recommend this game on the PC platform for the FULL price tag. It is a AAA game, and was definately worth the $59.99 i paid for it. Thankyou for such a great game! I look forward to dumping more hours into it in the near future.

Okay I want to make one thing clear. This is by no means a bad game. I think that's something people just assume when they see the thumbs down, and don't actually read why. THIS is why I didn't reccomend this game. For starters, it takes the brave move of being a single player only. This alone doesnt bother me. But combined with the length of the game, which is rather short, and the lack of an open world, once you beat it, there really isn't much to do besides hunt achievements. Total completionists will have a good time with all the hidden areas and the whole second timeline to play around with, but for someone more interested in the story, there just isn't a whole lot there. I noticed there are supposedly extra game modes available via vodes you can find in game, and I havn't tried this yet. But unless those game modes are seriously well put together and fun to replay, my eyebrows will go only higher. But as I said. What game there is isn't bad at all. Its actually quite good. The story is interesting enough to keep me around, the combat is tight, the stealth is fun, though can be unpredictable. And this is what I look for in a good game. Several more hours of it would be enough to keep me happy. It usually takes me several weeks to beat a game, since I don't actually play very much, and I tend to just hop on and off. But with this game I managed to beat it in just 4 play sessions, and I don't think I was playing particularlylong on any of them.
Another, even more serious complaint is the overly heavy usage of cutscenes. Often forcing me to watch segments that would be very fun to play. Such as driving a car off a highway, or firing one of the wacky ball contraptions you find in the gameat the castle in the final segment. But instead I find that  only get to control walking down to the cannon, while the actual firing is taken from my control and done by the computer. Each individual cutscene is short, but there are so many o them, that depending on how fast you play the gae, I don't think it would be far fetched to say a third, or even more of it is just video. And again .This really wouldn't be a problem to me if the whle damn game was a few hours longer. And had better side quests. And an open world. And longer se-- oh I'm getting side tracked.
Anyway. This game has a lot of potential. And what game there actually is here is a blast to play. But in a world where multiplayer and/or open world is almost a necesity, it just doesnt have enough going on. I wouldn't reccomend buying this now, but once a sale roles around, or they (inevitably) lowerthe price, I'd say it'd be worth it then.

Overall the graghics in this game a quite good, but there is one thing in this game that is so unholy, it makes my brain hurt. Dear god the DOF. It is horrible. When trying to take out a guard only 15 or so feet away, and that entire area of the screen is just blurred out, it makes for precision gameplay, and long range stealth pretty much impossible (since as far as I know you cant get a silencer for your sniper rifle.) All they have to do to fix this is use REAL DOF. NOT JUST LETS BLUR OUT EVERYTHING TEN FEET AWAY FROM THE PLAYER. Real DOF means burring out areas that your not looking at, similar to how the human eye actually works, and focuses on thigs. This game just makes your character near sighted. This is especially bad in the safe house, where  for some reason it gets way more extreme. This didn't bother me at first: in fact I kind of liked it. It gave interesting visuals, and since there was nobody to fight, it didn't matter. But later on in the game, you actually DO fight in the safe house, and the DOF doesnt go away. And theres the fact that there's smoke through the entire hous in that scene, AND fire with a way to intense bloom effect. That entire level is just flat out tedious. I had to play through it several times, bue to getting shotgunned at pont blank by a guy I couldn't see. And DOF can't actually be turned off in the settings. Only changed in terms of quality. My theory is that they use it to cover up texture pop ins, and that all textures more than 15 feet away are actually mip-mapped to an unrecognizable blur, which would explain how my not-very-powerful LAPTOP managed to handle this game so well.
Anyway. I can't think of anything else I can say about this game, without getting in and analizing the story, (which isn't bad, but it's not great either) so I'll stop beating the poor thing's bloody corpse.

!NOTE! - If you don't want to read a detailed review, GO STRAIGHT TO THE PRO CON SECTION.
This game is probably one of the most satisfying Nazi killing game hands down! Visuals are fantastic, gameplay puts you in the zone, the music is so solid and amazing it fits the mood for every situation whether you're mowing down enemies, exploring a location or picking a stealthy approach, this game has a good bunch of everything.
However, one thing to note is the story. The entire premise is captivating, well executed and definitely makes you feel like the Nazi's are in power. But one thing is a small issue and is quite ironic: The story. While the story is there, it is good and puts you in the middle of it all, you forget the reason why you're doing anything you're being told on any point in the chapter. This is actually just a small factor in the game, as it immediately puts you back on track. Now where to start with the review...
The Premise: The Nazis won the war and they are definitely in power. Wolfenstein: The New Order executes every bit of this atmosphere so well it is scary. It almost feels historical! Except for the fact that they are extremely technologicaly advanced. Aside from that, this game is amazing when it comes to making it seem like the Nazis really do control everything!
The Atmosphere: Every mission and environment are different in their own ways both visually and game wise. They really put you in the situation and allow you to feel the weight of it all. Althought the paths you take can be very linear, the world is open enough for you to feel like you are really exploring. Among other things, the Nazis are also one of the biggest parts of this atmospheres(as if you didn't know already). They add a really good grim feeling to anything they're are around while also adding a nice touch of military strength. If the Nazis weren't as good as they looked, this game would be bland.
The Graphics/Visuals: Stunning in every way shape and form. Honestly, this game is Tomb Raider levels of good. Lighting, shadows, character models and texturing are all so well done. Some parts lacked like the Lunar Base and other textures but they never removed from the game. On top of that, all the Characters, Enemies and Robots look so amazing its insane. Every Nazi soldier looks awesome that when you kill them you can't help but look at them. Each character is also very well detailed that you want to stare at them.
The Gameplay: Very solid for a first person shooter, and it is to be expected. Controls for leaning might be a bit wonky but it is no biggy. It is as basic as you can get with controls. But the weapons and enemies is where the meat of it all is of course. You have a varied but formiddable array of weapons to your disposal and on top of that most of which can be dual wielded. They can be upgraded as you progress and allow for dynamic fighting. The enemies you encounter however are what determine what you should be doing. You could encounter a large wave of enemies and need some serious automatic fire power, so why not dual wield Assault Rifles? Heavily armored troops could jump in so mount up some laser weaponry. Enemies too far away? Marksman rifle. Don't wanna deal with them all at once? Grab your knives and stealth kill everyone. The vast amount of choices to engage enemies is surprisingly wide.
Another thing to expand on with this game is that you actually make choices, both linear and personal. The game can make you do small or large decisions that can ultimately change the game itself or do something to the immediate situation. Really good. And then you have engagement options which varies between stealth and destruction.
The Characters: All characters are voiced and designed well. Although they are not incredibly attachable they allow you to be immersed in the game. However, you don't actually get to see much of them unless you're in the safe house or "taking care fo the dirty laundry". Otherwise, characters are well done.
The Main Character: William J. Blazkowicz is a pretty awesome and badass character. Well voiced and well designed. No real backstory is provided, just his part in WWII. All in all, pretty good.
What is BAD about the game?: Well first off, the game itself isn't actually that bad, it's just some things that take away from the experience. As said before, you forget the story all together. Sometimes frames might drop here and there but it's no serious issue. But one thing I find is actually lacking and that is difficulty. Honestly, the game wasn't that challenging until you reach "Death Incarnate" and even then it is relatively easy. I would highly recommend playing on "Uber" your first go. It will be challenging and it actually makes you feel like you're fighting a Nazi armada.
Pros -
+Stunning Visuals
+Gameplay is Fantastic
+Dynamic Choices
+Static Choices
+Nazis look EPIC
+Weapon array might be small but usage is massive
+Atmosphere is superb
+Really does feel like Nazis control EVERYTHING
+Characters are well voiced and personality wise AWESOME.
Cons-
-Story can be quite forgettable. You forget why you're doing this.
-Frames can drop randomly and even freeze. Might just be me.
-Difficulty really lacks. Play on UBER to really enjoy the game.

You can't really call yourself an RTS fan without playing this masterpiece of the genre first. It may seem a bit basic - train a load of soldiers and build a load of siege engines in order to systematically remove every other player from the map - but the complexity comes from adapting to various different styles of map, as well as learning how each different civilisation works. For example, the Britons have some of the best archery units in the game, but their mounted units are lacking in response. On the other hand, the Teutons have a unique unit that can take a lot of hits but is extremely slow, so they essentially need ranged escorts. And then there's dealing with being krushed (a.k.a. rushed with knights) and being able to reach the Castle Age in under 20 minutes. Oh, and don't even get me started on the absolutely wonderful soundtrack - something that I didn't hear until I got this version, no thanks to having to use a No-CD patch.
However, while this is an incredible game, I feel like Microsoft haven't done enough to call this a true HD edition. Yes, technically it is in HD and this improves the game significantly, but otherwise it has little in the way of improvements, and it's therefore quite expensive for what it is. If you're never going to play multiplayer then try to find it cheaper on Amazon or something, and download the Forgotten Empires mod separately. Otherwise, get it when it's on sale, because fifteen quid is rather a lot of money to be spending on a game that's over 15 years old.
In conclusion, absolutely get this game (when it's cheap) because it is one of the greatest strategy games ever created, alongside Civilization IV and Command & Conquer: Red Alert. And to those idiot critics who say the game doesn't play very well, you deserve several slaps.

I would like to start off saying that this review is coming from someone that has played ALL the wolfensteins, and yes that includes Spear of Destiny. I will be doing my best to avoid spoilers.
I thoroughly enjoy the game and i've played through the story (one side of it), and althought the story only has 2 linear paths, its based off a critical decision. Wolfenstein works this style of story telling to its strength. This game made me feel like i was playing one of the original games that made me love the series, the subtle humour, the tense action moments, jaw clinching survival through battles, and embracement of multiple mechanics. This game has great pacing in difficulty and very astetically pleasing.
I played this game on a Quad Core AMD and a GTS 450, according to the minimum requirements, i shouldnt have been able to run this game, however i ran it at 60fps without fail (up until the final fight where i had minor frame issues that were fixed once i tweaked a couple settings), and it was nice to finally run into a game where my rig was challenged, a game that finally put "PC Master Race" to good use.
I didn't run into any game breaking bugs, like most nvidia/amd users. Overall it was simple, i got home, installed on my secondary HDD and off i went into the world of Wolfenstein.
The game starts off Dropping you into WW2, and immediately it feels like you're back playing RTCW (with EXTREME graphics and AI updates). The guns felt metallic, and powerful; the movement was smooth and fluid, and it was highly immersive. The games greatest strength is also its greatest problem, the game changed its focus from what it has done in the past 3 wolfensteins being cult focused into more of a Twitch Based Shooter, much like the original Wolfenstein (as "twitch" as possible, back in those days).  Which was not what I was expecting, however it was nice seeing them go back to the basics of what made wolfenstein great. Not the women running around in Latex outfits (although noone ever complained about that), just a man on a mission, using impossible guns, fighting Impossible monsters.
The game progresses and gets the player immersed within a great love story that truly brings you in. I admittedly had to put the game down (much to my dismay), due to having a job; but when i came back, i had no difficulty getting re-acquainted with the characters and being back in B.J.'s mind and living the games experience.
Without spoiling anything, the story was great, the development was solid. I would have liked to see more variety in Enemy soldier skins (for example: women, black nazi's,), or atleast more indepth reasoning into the world that was created. The story could have been elongated by a couple missions where you have to try to live in the alternate history world they created instead of just jumping into this new world and starting a revolution.  That way, as a person, you actually feel that this change is needed, as opposed to what i noticed from the commentary by most civilians during the game, that were happy with the Nazi Regime taking over and how they were living their lives. Alas, i'm being nit-picky on that point, overall the story had great consistent message and didn't leave me wondering "Where did that come from?"
Now, lets get to some negatives:
-The AI is inconsistent, sometimes they will get stuck running into walls, running into doors, you can sprint while stealthing around, and overall they seem fixated on ignoring you.
-The maps, although feel non-linear, are extremely linear that you really only have 2 options; stealth, or non-stealth. Some levels only have the non-stealth option aswell, and with the issue above, stealthing is super easy.
-Hidden items, Yes this is also a plus.. But they are seemingly in random locations. I should just find a gold knife in the middle of a room where i was fighting some bad guys..
-Hidden Rooms. Due to the amount of references back to the old wolfenstein, and the intro levels having a few hidden paths, i figured later in the game, there would have been alot more of this. These kinda drop off in the favour of the "cut the fence/box/wall" mechanic.. where rooms arent hidden.. you just have to look for the particular texture and problem solved.
-Lack of Multiplayer, Although the focus on the singleplayer made this a huge plus, one of the greatest attitributes of the Wolfenstein Series is the RTCW: ET expansion, where multiplayer just took it to new levels and reinvigorated the series. Although I would suspect an expansion will be coming in the future that will include this feature, or hopefully it will be in a patch....
Overall, I did greatly enjoy this game, and the negatives i can find with the game itself are minor at best (and the AI bug helped me at one point where i ran into problems near the end.. ). I would strongly recommend this game on the PC platform for the FULL price tag. It is a AAA game, and was definately worth the $59.99 i paid for it. Thankyou for such a great game! I look forward to dumping more hours into it in the near future.

Okay I want to make one thing clear. This is by no means a bad game. I think that's something people just assume when they see the thumbs down, and don't actually read why. THIS is why I didn't reccomend this game. For starters, it takes the brave move of being a single player only. This alone doesnt bother me. But combined with the length of the game, which is rather short, and the lack of an open world, once you beat it, there really isn't much to do besides hunt achievements. Total completionists will have a good time with all the hidden areas and the whole second timeline to play around with, but for someone more interested in the story, there just isn't a whole lot there. I noticed there are supposedly extra game modes available via vodes you can find in game, and I havn't tried this yet. But unless those game modes are seriously well put together and fun to replay, my eyebrows will go only higher. But as I said. What game there is isn't bad at all. Its actually quite good. The story is interesting enough to keep me around, the combat is tight, the stealth is fun, though can be unpredictable. And this is what I look for in a good game. Several more hours of it would be enough to keep me happy. It usually takes me several weeks to beat a game, since I don't actually play very much, and I tend to just hop on and off. But with this game I managed to beat it in just 4 play sessions, and I don't think I was playing particularlylong on any of them.
Another, even more serious complaint is the overly heavy usage of cutscenes. Often forcing me to watch segments that would be very fun to play. Such as driving a car off a highway, or firing one of the wacky ball contraptions you find in the gameat the castle in the final segment. But instead I find that  only get to control walking down to the cannon, while the actual firing is taken from my control and done by the computer. Each individual cutscene is short, but there are so many o them, that depending on how fast you play the gae, I don't think it would be far fetched to say a third, or even more of it is just video. And again .This really wouldn't be a problem to me if the whle damn game was a few hours longer. And had better side quests. And an open world. And longer se-- oh I'm getting side tracked.
Anyway. This game has a lot of potential. And what game there actually is here is a blast to play. But in a world where multiplayer and/or open world is almost a necesity, it just doesnt have enough going on. I wouldn't reccomend buying this now, but once a sale roles around, or they (inevitably) lowerthe price, I'd say it'd be worth it then.

Overall the graghics in this game a quite good, but there is one thing in this game that is so unholy, it makes my brain hurt. Dear god the DOF. It is horrible. When trying to take out a guard only 15 or so feet away, and that entire area of the screen is just blurred out, it makes for precision gameplay, and long range stealth pretty much impossible (since as far as I know you cant get a silencer for your sniper rifle.) All they have to do to fix this is use REAL DOF. NOT JUST LETS BLUR OUT EVERYTHING TEN FEET AWAY FROM THE PLAYER. Real DOF means burring out areas that your not looking at, similar to how the human eye actually works, and focuses on thigs. This game just makes your character near sighted. This is especially bad in the safe house, where  for some reason it gets way more extreme. This didn't bother me at first: in fact I kind of liked it. It gave interesting visuals, and since there was nobody to fight, it didn't matter. But later on in the game, you actually DO fight in the safe house, and the DOF doesnt go away. And theres the fact that there's smoke through the entire hous in that scene, AND fire with a way to intense bloom effect. That entire level is just flat out tedious. I had to play through it several times, bue to getting shotgunned at pont blank by a guy I couldn't see. And DOF can't actually be turned off in the settings. Only changed in terms of quality. My theory is that they use it to cover up texture pop ins, and that all textures more than 15 feet away are actually mip-mapped to an unrecognizable blur, which would explain how my not-very-powerful LAPTOP managed to handle this game so well.
Anyway. I can't think of anything else I can say about this game, without getting in and analizing the story, (which isn't bad, but it's not great either) so I'll stop beating the poor thing's bloody corpse.

Does anybody remember the time when video games were about doing? Not what a lot of fancy games have now with their set-pieces and linear levels and platforming sections. Some nostalgia freaks would call that "the good old days", but I would like to just say that it is what video games are about. It is what they are supposed to do, and what
happens to do very well.
I still remember the sound of the old Polish man in the game telling me "Kill all the Nazis" right before handing me a gun to blow their brains out with. This sort of mentality has two major plays within the game.
The first way this mentality applies is through the games atmosphere, dialogue, story, and character interactions. The game takes every opportunity to be very open that it is a "dumb shooter", and does not take itself too seriously. It is full of humorous lines poking fun at the average gamers' behaviour when you do something that would be weird to do in real life, but people do in games all the time. This makes the game natural, and connect with the player, making light about otherwise boring and mundane tasks in the game. These random pokes at the gamer do not come at the expense of the main character, whereby Mr. Blaskowicz never leaves his characteristic self to do things that he would never do. Which, his normal self of course is a dual assault rifle wielding human tank of Nazi killing death.
That leads to the second way the particular line of dialogue exemplifies the game: The game and its gameplay. The levels are pretty large to say the least, with lots of differing pathways and areas to explore, and go about completing fighting the Futuristic-Nazi scum. Think
size and style, but bigger, a lot bigger. All of this is crafted in heavily stylised, and excellently modelled and textured environments, that look absolutely gorgeous to be covering in a fresh coat of blood. Which happens when your head gets blown off by two autoshotguns firing miniature flak rounds out simultaneously. Yes, yes you can do just that. Dual wield any two weapons in the game (with the exception of the two handed weapons) at the same time, and rip through your foes at an astonishing rate. Of course this does not replace the good old fashioned iron sights, which are complimented nicely by a leaning/stationary-viewing key system that is smooth to the touch; the same goes for the rest of the keyboard inputs, making you leap, lunge, duck, run, and throw weapons with utmost fluidity.
This comes at a price however: the id tech 5 engine. Many gamers, mainly AMD users, seem to have issues running the game at all, or running it well once it is running. Considering this is a AAA contemporary release at the time of writing this, this is not surprising as game requirements are going up, and many people would expect to be able to run it on old systems would be disappointed. But the game leaves the gamer disappointed in other ways as well, mainly how the game handles some particular parts of the itself. One way it fumbles itself is sometimes the game will throw a “serious” part at the player (I can only think of one off the top of my head, and while it was sentimental and a legitimate plot point, it felt out of place). Another way the game messes up is with rather disappointing boss fights. While they are impressive to look at, and awesome to take down, they seemed a little weak compared to how some of the super soldiers in the game would kick your butt over and over and over again until you rage quit. This does not ruin the game, but this dichotomy does slightly take away from the experience.
Some honourable mentions before I finish: The game has a stealth system, which is a little broken like in most games, but still viable for the most part. Nothing more satisfying than one shotting a Nazi with a throwing knife. As well, the OST is very atmospheric, and fitting for the game, lending itself well to the experience the player will feel throughout. The game has a lot of collectables to collect, including new difficulty modes you can unlock. The game has a perk system to make playing on higher difficulties marginally easier. The game uses limited regenerating health (just to a low threshold, like 20% of your hitpoints), and uses the health system where you need to find med kits to replenish your health (even allowing you to overheal yourself!). The game has a lengthy campaign lasting from 9-20 hours, with multiple endings and plot divergences. Lastly, the game's beds are just pure awesomeness.
If you could not tell by the thumbs up recommendation, I would recommend this game. It is a good old timey inspired, arcade shooter that is a boat load of fun to wade through pools of blood in. Killing Nazi's has not been awesome.

-Highly respectable business model. Not pay-to-win. Guns that can be bought for real money are mostly sidegrades, but even the upgrades take skill. Weapon customization can not be bought with real money, and that is the most important aspect of offensive capability.
-Subcommunities are diverse in skill level (casual to borderline professional), so there's a place for everyone to join.
-Playerbase generally mature and friendly.
-Very well optimized
Cons
-Occasionally, you find a bad egg in the community. Sometimes they're spamming voice chat with obnoxious noises, sometimes they're incredibly rude for no reason whatsoever, or sometimes they'll bash all of their teammates for having lost a base (see: rage). Just mute them.
-Very steep learning curve and will take some time to get used to. It can be very frustrating; notice how most of the negative reviews are from people with <10 hours in the game. However, it's completely worth it once you get the hang of it.
Other thoughts:
-People are talking about the playerbase "dying", but I still see many people in firefights. It really doesn't seem that way to me.
-If you're not the most patient person in the world (let's be real: we all kind of are, as gamers), then you can make the learning curve more bearable by playing as a support class (engineer, medic). Stay in cover and observe people to learn. And, by goodness, if somebody asks for an ammo pack, res, heal, or repair, you give it to them if you can. If you're feeling brave, take out your gun and join the offense to practice, so as long as nobody needs support.
-Battles can last a LONG time. I've had instances where we everybody was trying to push the stalemate of a capture for two hours. It's easy to get sucked into a large firefight lie this, so don't hop into large battles if you have things to do IRL. You can do short half-hour play sessions as long as you stick to smaller battlefields, though.
TL;DR/Conclusion
This is a freakin' epic, free, and awesome game that you should totally downlaod.

An epic first-person shooter which is basically a war simulator. Unlike most online fps games, Planetside 2 is based around an actual war across 4 huge continents between 3 empires: The Terran Republic, The New Conglomerate, and The Vanu Sovereignty. Instead of playing game matches, you simply join the game while the never-ending war goes on and you choose a spawn location and jump right into action. This game combines 3 types of combat: infantry, ground vehicles, and air vehicles. All these have to work together in order to capture enemy bases. No one player ever stands out in the war and teamwork is most important because nothing can beat a well-organised squadron of soldiers. Eventually, this leads on to a single faction capturing a continent, then everyone joins the battles in other continents. Also, all of this is free and all items can be unlocked without spending any real money.
The only downside of this game is that new players are at a big disadvantage compared to those who have played for a while. However, if you don't mind dying a lot at the start and barely ever dying when you get better, then this game is for you.

The Little Mod That Could.
A Franchise Refurbished, Yet a Missed Opportunity.
The age of empires series is one of fame. After 13 years it can still be purchased (along with its expansion, The Conquerors) at Wal-Mart and Office Depot. This "new" title is an attempt at sprucing up one of the most beloved games of the franchise. It is amazingly rare to see an old property being brought back to life and updated, especially by a parent company that is only looking forward to the next big buck, and are willing to drop any title not making 500% profit (AOE Online was scrapped after a year in the wild, and much needed updates to many games still hang in limbo at EA). Only the bigwigs know what made them bring this one back, but we are glad to see some dust wiped off of our past every once in a while. Developer "Hidden Path" was contracted to shine up the series fav and bring it into the new age of gaming, they fixed important things and they didn't fiddle around where it wasn't needed, but they missed a couple of points that would have made it into a new age RTS diamond.
First of all, I must thank hidden path for finally raising the unit cap, but why only 500? While it is a good 2.5x higher than before, our machines are 250x more powerful than the Pentium II 200mhz it was originally designed for. I can only guess that much of the core engine remains as it was, and 500 was the highest they could go without breaking it. Even though the cap has been raised, you can still only select 20 units at a time. Was it something that was overlooked? not likely. Here is another notch in the theory of a stretched engine. They just couldn't do more without overhauling the back end.
While we are on the graphics, The reason it has HD in the title is the ability to hit 1920x1080, (and beyond for multi monitor rigs) whereas the original topped out at 1024x768. I agree with the general consensus in that the overhauled building and unit models are amazing, but once again the elderly engine comes through showing us no shadows, no zoom, and no visual effect updates. These are an almost standard feature of today's even bargain bin games that they missed completely. Does it detract from gameplay? Not really. Could they have spent a little more time bringing the graphics engine into this decade without effecting gameplay? yes.
The multiplayer. What can I say here? Game Zone worked (kinda) back in the day, but thankfully we have learned from those early days and have integrated the game wholly into Steam's online network with only a few launch bugs and some early lag issues (to be continued). What this means is a front row ticket to a beautifully seamless multiplayer before-game matching experience, but completely removes the LAN option that, like me, so many young geeks had permanently set up in their basements just for this. Inclusion with the Workshop will make mod and map finding a breeze, and I believe the good outweighs the bad here, but somehow there is still a bad taste somewhere in my mind from losing our offline multiplayer. (single play is still allowed offline).
The music score has been redone, but I can still pound the number keys for WOLOLOOO and "I Need Wood". No complaints there.
All-in-all it was well worth the money, and it is the authentic Age Of Kings/Conquerors experience, but the lack of improvements to the gameplay, and the surface improvement to the graphics makes this game feel more like a decent mod than a blockbuster.
(For further fiddling- the mod "Forgotten Empires" does everything this HD remake does, plus adds hours of single player campaigns, and a good dozen fixes)
