NOTE: I've seen people complain about technical issues for AMD. I have an R9-290 and I have had *zero* issues on very high/ultra.
+ The graphics are gorgeous. Very smooth.
+ The gaming itself is fun, and it is more than just the bad guys you gotta watch out for. I liked the fact that there were traps and the like in the environment, meaning that you have to watch your step in-between fights, too, in certain places.
+ The story is pretty good. I'm not going to lie: it isn't a masterpiece, but for an FPS game it is far and above better than what you're used to.
- I've had some issues with the AI. I want to be clear that there haven't been big issues with the AI, for the most part it has worked pretty well, especially in combat where the AI generally speaking is working well. The major issues is how detection works. Sometimes I knife someone in the back from behind in broad daylight and the other guards don't notice anything even if they are 10 m away and his body lies there. Other times I am moving in complete shadows in the dark underground and some guard spots me from 100 m away. It's inconsistent in that regard, the stealth mechanic in the game is not really there. Then again it isn't generally supposed to be a stealth game but there are areas where you can use it, or at least, it is *designed* in some areas where stealth is an option.
- The story. While it is far and above better than most of what I've played, it became pretty, eh, obvious what was going to happen already by the beginning of the game. There were really no major surprises. Also, some of the script had a pretty low quality in its narrative quality. I wasn't expecting a masterpiece, but some of it was just a bit bizarre and out of date. Like the time you're fightning bad guys on the moon and he starts talking to himself how he was swimming in the water when he was a kid, out of nowhere, and then suddenly cuts himself off and never picks up the thread. Bizarre and incoherent.

This game has been one of the highlights of my year so far, Right now its easily the best first person shooter of the year.
Lets start with the good:
-The game mechanics are tight, good, old school gun play mixed with some stealth options, There are PLENTY of ways to kill Nazis, and plenty of ways for the curious player to get a leg up on them, Want to take cover and shoot around it? You can do that, Want to just charge them and gun them down dual wielding quad barrel fully automatic belt fed assault shotguns? Totally can do that, Want to pick them off from a distance? You can do that too. Want to dual wield sniper rifles? Knock yourself out, you can do it. The levels never feel small or constrained (Unless erm.. They're supposed to, No spoilers)
-The environments are fantastic, lots of variety here without giving too many spoilers away, You get to go all over the place and shoot Nazis and every environment is quite nice to look at
-The story is pretty darn good, Far better than most other FPS games released lately (Looking at you CoD) Is it complex? No, But thats not bad, its a simple story told very well. And of course the cast of characters, both good AND bad is quite well established and rounded out
-The game also does a spectacular job immersing you in its setting, The music, the newspapers, advertisements, even the announcements and propaganda serve to make you feel like you ARE in this world.
-Playtime is very good, There are at least 2 possible storylines i can see, and it took me 11 hours to finish one of them, without nabbing every collectable in sight, From my understanding getting a bunch of the collectables unlocks more modes, Not sure what they are, but i am fairly intending to find out.
-Difficulty on the second highest setting was good, I never felt "cheated" when i got killed and it provided a strong challenge
-Lack of multiplayer to me is a good thing. Even thought RTCW and Enemy Territory were fantastic I am actually more happy to have a game that didnt feel like it had to shoehorn in multiplayer, These days it seems like everything gets MP and the single player experience suffers...
Now the game isnt perfect.. For one, idTech 5 is showing its age, even if they've tried hard to update it, theres still the pesky "popping textures" at times, and the engine is straining under what its trying to deliver, Textures can look blurry at times, and performance is somewhere in the "eh" category, I managed 50-60 fps at 1440p with all the details cranked up pretty high, Sadly the game doesnt, and probubly will not, support SLI (its a limitation in idTech 5) But that said, when i sat back and just got myself into the game, none of these things mattered.
There are some bugs, I heard AMD users are having a lot of issues, I had a few problems with Triple Buffering but once i turned that off everything worked fine from start to end.
At the end of the day this game is a refreshing shot in the arm that I havnt felt in the FPS genre for a long time, I doubt the new CoD can beat it (although thats comparing apples to oranges in a way..) But we shall see, For now I highly recommend you get this game and get a good taste of what people my age missed about the golden years of FPS games

They made one change that drove half the playerbase away and since then the game has been consistently going downhill.
In case you're wondering, that change was a patch entitled "Team Orders". It was released back when tiers were still a thing, and its namesake was the only good thing in the update. It flooded the upper tiers with new players because of how they changed the upgrade system, and that drove half the player base to just uninstall the game. Ever since then, it's been a downward spiral. When they lost those players, they panicked because they were all the ones paying a ton of money for premium memberships. So, about 8 months later (roughly 14 months ago) they added loot crates to the game as a cash grab. That drove even more players away, so they panicked again and started trying other things. Each update after those two has been designed to try to convince new players to sign up and old players to come back. So far, it hasn't worked, so they keep trying even more drastic changes. This has made the game a total♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥at this point.
Unless and until the developers change their policy from damage control to actually trying to better their game, I'd avoid Robocraft like the plague. And this is coming from someone who has historically supported a lot of their more controversial changes.

Wolfenstein: The New Order was everything I could have wanted from a single-player focused first person shooter. The story was engaging and ramped at appropriate moments, and the pacing seems to take some inspiration from movies in where the plot gets shoved along in things that wouldn't be as interesting to get to the good parts. The story takes some leaps of faith when doing Tarantino transitions, but honestly they are shorter leaps of faith than what the player had to do in some levels.  It works; Wolfenstein is long without many noticeable lulls and offers a lot of options in each level when it comes to branching paths (some of which are dependant on what you did in the first chapter).
The writing is pretty good for what I was expecting. Some characters are developed more than others, but for how many people get thrown in the mix there's a decent balance. The scope of what occurs during the game is huge, to say the least.
The game features some light stealth mechanics that are simple, but work. They are by no means advanced, but they get the job done and allow you to complete objectives without being seen if player agency wills it. The combat itself is solid, and harkens back to the unlimited weapon inventories of Wolfenstein, in which there's less weapons overall, but you're carrying all of them at once. Every weapon can be dual-wielded, with the exception of turret weapons, grenades, and weapons you only possess one of. There's a decent cover system, and all weapons have some alternate function.
The game features a lot of puzzles or situations featuring the cutting tool, which is a game mechanic to saw through chain link fences and thin metal plates to get into different areas or open some containers. The plates even act as cover against most weapons, except for laser turrets (they chew through them). In a way, it's Wolfenstein's gravity gun. It's interesting to use, and the tool gets upgraded multiple times, even becoming a capable weapon in its own right.
There's a level of detail regarding the world that is excellent. Everything is controlled by the Nazi regime, even pop culture. The level of technology over the time span was also interesting to see in concert with the totalitarian government control. Poking around and listening to dialog gives a bit of insight into just how twisted the world has become.
There were some graphical glitches and pop-in textures, but aside from that, there wasn't really anything detrimental to my overall experience with the game. The game was a blast and ended with a bang, faithful to the source material to the end.

The Little Mod That Could.
A Franchise Refurbished, Yet a Missed Opportunity.
The age of empires series is one of fame. After 13 years it can still be purchased (along with its expansion, The Conquerors) at Wal-Mart and Office Depot. This "new" title is an attempt at sprucing up one of the most beloved games of the franchise. It is amazingly rare to see an old property being brought back to life and updated, especially by a parent company that is only looking forward to the next big buck, and are willing to drop any title not making 500% profit (AOE Online was scrapped after a year in the wild, and much needed updates to many games still hang in limbo at EA). Only the bigwigs know what made them bring this one back, but we are glad to see some dust wiped off of our past every once in a while. Developer "Hidden Path" was contracted to shine up the series fav and bring it into the new age of gaming, they fixed important things and they didn't fiddle around where it wasn't needed, but they missed a couple of points that would have made it into a new age RTS diamond.
First of all, I must thank hidden path for finally raising the unit cap, but why only 500? While it is a good 2.5x higher than before, our machines are 250x more powerful than the Pentium II 200mhz it was originally designed for. I can only guess that much of the core engine remains as it was, and 500 was the highest they could go without breaking it. Even though the cap has been raised, you can still only select 20 units at a time. Was it something that was overlooked? not likely. Here is another notch in the theory of a stretched engine. They just couldn't do more without overhauling the back end.
While we are on the graphics, The reason it has HD in the title is the ability to hit 1920x1080, (and beyond for multi monitor rigs) whereas the original topped out at 1024x768. I agree with the general consensus in that the overhauled building and unit models are amazing, but once again the elderly engine comes through showing us no shadows, no zoom, and no visual effect updates. These are an almost standard feature of today's even bargain bin games that they missed completely. Does it detract from gameplay? Not really. Could they have spent a little more time bringing the graphics engine into this decade without effecting gameplay? yes.
The multiplayer. What can I say here? Game Zone worked (kinda) back in the day, but thankfully we have learned from those early days and have integrated the game wholly into Steam's online network with only a few launch bugs and some early lag issues (to be continued). What this means is a front row ticket to a beautifully seamless multiplayer before-game matching experience, but completely removes the LAN option that, like me, so many young geeks had permanently set up in their basements just for this. Inclusion with the Workshop will make mod and map finding a breeze, and I believe the good outweighs the bad here, but somehow there is still a bad taste somewhere in my mind from losing our offline multiplayer. (single play is still allowed offline).
The music score has been redone, but I can still pound the number keys for WOLOLOOO and "I Need Wood". No complaints there.
All-in-all it was well worth the money, and it is the authentic Age Of Kings/Conquerors experience, but the lack of improvements to the gameplay, and the surface improvement to the graphics makes this game feel more like a decent mod than a blockbuster.
(For further fiddling- the mod "Forgotten Empires" does everything this HD remake does, plus adds hours of single player campaigns, and a good dozen fixes)

I can't remember how long ago it was that I bought Age of Empires, but I still have 1, 2 and Mythology on CD/DVD. The only real reason I bought the HD version here on Steam was the convenience of not having to load in and out a disc all the time. In truth the game is solid, it's the game that you all remember. The AI was never very clever, but AOE2 took the next step on from AOE. It's a decent balance of build, strategy and has (had) a half-decent multiplayer too. This HD version takes the original and makes a few minor surface tweaks. It's slightly better looking, but it all looks pretty much the same.
There is one tiny problem. The pricing here on Steam. I was fortunate enough to get this version through a Humble Bundle, but I'd NEVER pay £14 for a copy of the game. Even $14 is too much. The HD 'extra' isn't something that really justifies the extra spend. If you're after this game get the original on disc or keep an eye out for sales. Paying the extra for the HD really doesn't seem worth it. The original disc still runs fine on my Alienware 14, it doesn't always look wonderful, but it's perfectly playable. My opinion is that it's just not worth the extra cash for something that isn't that improved.
Additionally, the new 'Forgotten' Campaign certainly isn't worth the extra money. There are literally thousands of user generated maps and campaigns that you can get out there for free.
If you've got AOE2 already on disc, keep using that. If you've never played AOE get it on disc (it's probably cheaper), or wait for a sale somewhere.
To be clear I'm recommending the game over the HD extra stuff here on steam.

Wolfenstein The New Order is one of the better first person shooters of the past (half) year. It has a nice science fiction story about what would've happened if Germany won WWII after all. It starts off semi realistic but the action and settings become more over the top halfway through the story. The shooting aspect feels very solid and dual wielding guns is a nice touch, even if it isn't all that accurate and becomes less helpful later on in the game when tougher and more enemies appear.
The stealth aspect was, for me personally, the best part of the game. Enemies are sometimes stupid and they won't even spot you when you're practically hugging them and other times they see you when they're not even supposed to but knifing enemies (and especially throwing knives) just feels awesome and satisfying. I was actually disappointed every time I was (incorrectly) spotted.
Levels are also less linear than the previous Wolfenstein games so you can sometimes take a different road. These seperate roads aren't long but they give a nice illusion of freedom. An illusion the Wolfenstein games absolutely need to keep it more fun.
The perk system is also a nice addition and a bit different than what you're used to. Perks can be unlocked only in a certain order and it's entirely up to you what you want to do first. Do you want to unlock the stealth perks first, or the more explosive perks ? It gives you freedom in how you want to play the game, which is refreshing. Even if the backbone of this system is still the same as in any other game using perks.
The voice acting is excellent, and the soundtrack kicks in nicely when a shootout is about to begin. Nothing to complain about here. The graphics on the other hand don't feel very next(/current)-gen, but are still good (especially the characters), and texture streaming is still a problem with this engine and this impacts the overall experience. Performance in general seems to be terrible, even with the most high-end systems. But you can still get it to run at a solid 60FPS with a little tweaking here and there.
Wolfenstein The New Order took me 10 hours to complete, which is pretty long for a shooter these days. And if you read the entire review you don't have to ask me why I would recommend this game to anyone. It has my seal of approval. *Stamp*

Wolfenstein: The New Order harkens back to what FPS games used to be about. Before red dots, tactical vests, grittiness and the hold your hand and wait for your team approach modern FPS have taken to; there was simply one guy goin nuts shooting as many Nazis in the face as you can while looking for secrets strewn about This game encapsulates that very well without getting too stagnant or boring. It has yet to become boring charging into a room dual wielding auto shotguns and destroying everything in your path, and i have yet to encounter a part of this game that was cheap or that i didn't want to play again. The mechanics of the game work great and dont ever seem like a gimick that has gone too far. The stealth system does show some lapses in AI as they cant see other dead bodies but i tend to use it as a means to get good position to mow down everyone while dual wielding Assault Rifles.
The only bad remarks i can make about the game are the lack of variety of the guns you get as they fit your basic generic formula and while the gun models look cool and are interesting in of themselves i would have liked to see them go further with it. Zanier things like Tesla guns, flamethrowers, and multi-barreled chain guns take a back see to more practical weaponry. This doesnt limit the fun to be had with the weapons you're given but it would have been nice to see them go off the charts on something, the only weapon that does this is starts as a tool for cutting open grates but once upgraded is paramount to one of the Prawn's weapons from District 9.
The other thing i find  complaint with is the story, B.J. Blazkowicz is portrayed with more humanity than the lifeless speechless vessels we've grown accustom to in recent shooters but only in the cut scene's. Once out of them Blazkowicz goes back to being mostly silent, sharing a quip or two while ruthless murdering Nazis. This somewhat clashes with the character who just moments before was waxing poetically about a future with kids or how this war has taken its toll.
That coupled with a world left unexplored leaves the story a little bit lacking. Ever since the first trailer i was imagining we'd actually get to see the world under Nazi regime, instead here it seems like its just an excuse to explain why there's Nazis everywhere. Sure there's newspaper clipping and things strewn about describing the Nazis rise to power but in playing it the world was never really humanized, i was hoping to see what life in this universe would be like. The closest we get to it is a "hub" world between missions and i use that term loosely. Best i could compare it to would be if Deus Ex Human Revolution only gave you the Sarif building to explore instead of all of future Detroit. If anything i would appreciate some DLC where we see just how hostile the world has become.
Regardless of my gripes this is still a good game that I would recommend to anyone who likes classic arcade style shooters, or still has a bone to pick with digital Nazi's. The game play is what should be focused on here and if you like the sense of empowerment charging into a room guns a blazing brings, over chest high cover and waiting for your health to recharge you're going to like this game too.

One of the best games I've played, it draws a lot of influences from Half Life and other more involving FPSs.  There's a lot going on in this game and it's well worth taking the time to look through the newspaper cuttings on the wall, listen to the audio logs etc; this is one of the few games that has left an impact on me.  The Nazi domination and complete control left me deeply unsettled, it's not a thing you'd expect from a shooter.
As with Rage, the shooting/fighting mechanics are great (I'm not a fan of the id Tech 5 engine though) once you get your settings tweaked.  On a GTX670, I finally ramped up almost everything to high and switched off in game vertical sync.  The game was smooth with no texture pop-in, no strange flashes and no artifacting.  I didn't measure the fps, but there was no discernible lag.  The game crashed once when cutting through a crate, no problems thereafter.
I really recommend this game, it's the closest thing to a modern version of old-school shooters, including some great secrets.  I'm about to dive back in on Uber.

It was a tough decision to not recommend this game. The first half is pretty solid story- and diversity-wise and the production quality is obvious. Unfortunately, most of what the creators tried to do fell flat in the long run.
I'll start with my biggest gripe: the world. The game world *looks* quite good. However, there's no way to describe it other than "empty". You essentially fight your way through enormous bases devoid of people (and moving things in general)--except for the soldiers you'll find at scripted encounters approximately every hundred yards. The parts of the game containing other people provide no interaction, even to overhear them discussing something.
The first half of the story is good; after that it becomes quite predictable. There are side "quests" you can participate in to collect baubles to then learn something else about the personality of characters that rank around "meh" on the complexity scale (with one or two exceptions). Though the game never mentions it, these side quests are only good for the down time between scenarios; once you start another mission, they disappear forever. The game's entire goal is, in effect, to kill one man--and I guess to save the world from the Nazis but, since about 12 people exist in said world, that was never a very compelling motivator. All that being said, I did like the English guy ;)
The developers tried to do a lot and the extra features felt thin as a result. While the *concept* of choosing an engagement style is a cool one--complete with "perks" to improve yourself in your chosen "field"--I found it ultimately fell flat, at least on the hardest mode. My choice was, generally, to use the appropriate engagement style for a given scenario or "room", or die. Sneaking about was necessary in specific (obvious) scenarios to avoid extra troops being summoned; in all others, the enemies already know where you are at all times, even if they just magically appeared from a spawn point. The dual-wield "run and gun" style was novel for a while--until it just meant being very inaccurate and wasting ammo. As for the perks, you'll basically get them all eventually if you find the game challenging enough to invoke all the mechanics.
Finally, in terms of difficulty, I found the game far more frustrating than challenging. With the exception of a few scenarios I had to play over and over (and bloody over again) to get through, it was pretty much a walk-through on the highest difficulty.
Having said ALL THAT, if AAA FPS titles are your jam, it might be worth your time. This game is not at all BAD, it's just not AMAZING either.

I went into this game with no expectations one way or another, and I left incredibly impressed.  Wolfenstein is an excellently executed single player only FPS that does more than simply line up a shooting gallery for you to run through.  Yes, there's tons of nazis that need killing, and yes, you still fight giant mechanical monstrosities, but I was actually more impressed by what they did with the characters.  BJ has the look of a man who's seen far too much, and there's this undertone about the horrors of war that carries nicely through the piece.  They do a lot to humanize BJ as more than just a standard FPS dude, and it plays very well.
The gunplay is very solid, and interestingly supports both a more run-and-gun playstyle along with a stealthier silent-takedown approach.  The level design is consistently strong with multiple set-pieces and varied locations throughout.  My only complain at the moment is that there's no DLC for me to buy!

This game surprised the hell out of me.
I was a bit let down in the initial level as it felt pretty cookie-cutter shooter to be honest, but I am glad I persevered because it totally comes into its own. The combat allows you to choose whether or not you want to play a run-and-gun, cover-shooter or stealth based game when you come across a group of new enemies, this variation means you aren't forced into dreary "tactical" fights. Also, if you get bored of stealthing through a section, you can just pull out double machine guns and go crazy!
The story was another surprise for me because I really enjoyed a lot of the characters and the voice acting was great. The game has a bit of a sci-fi background which definitely made it more interesting for me as a lover of sci-fi.
On the negative side; There wasn't a lot of variety in terms of weapons and enemies, this didn't actually ruin the experience for me, but I was a little let down initially when I realised this. None of the boss fights were particularly exciting or clever, but again they weren't frustrating and they were worked in pretty smoothly. I have read about issues with screen tearing during the game, but didn't have any problems myself.
Absolutely think it's worth checking out, even if you want to just wait a while for it to come on sale.

This game surprised the hell out of me.
I was a bit let down in the initial level as it felt pretty cookie-cutter shooter to be honest, but I am glad I persevered because it totally comes into its own. The combat allows you to choose whether or not you want to play a run-and-gun, cover-shooter or stealth based game when you come across a group of new enemies, this variation means you aren't forced into dreary "tactical" fights. Also, if you get bored of stealthing through a section, you can just pull out double machine guns and go crazy!
The story was another surprise for me because I really enjoyed a lot of the characters and the voice acting was great. The game has a bit of a sci-fi background which definitely made it more interesting for me as a lover of sci-fi.
On the negative side; There wasn't a lot of variety in terms of weapons and enemies, this didn't actually ruin the experience for me, but I was a little let down initially when I realised this. None of the boss fights were particularly exciting or clever, but again they weren't frustrating and they were worked in pretty smoothly. I have read about issues with screen tearing during the game, but didn't have any problems myself.
Absolutely think it's worth checking out, even if you want to just wait a while for it to come on sale.

===Not a shooter with a brain and/or soul, but definitely a shooter with a heart.===
Wolfenstein pre-dated Doom. Now ponder that for a moment. What you're playing is history. History that will hopefully be made again if the game sells well enough to warrant a sequel, and I do hope you buy this game because I want to know how it all plays out since the game ends on a cliff-hanger, the almost Half-Life 2 Episode 2 cliff-hanger.
This game is one of those ultimate male-fantasy games. It just nailed pretty much everything right. It is also a tale of revenge. You play as an alpha-male with a soft heart, you get a hot chick, you travel around the world and to the moon, you get some downtime there and there, you kill Nazis and robo-Nazis, destroy their accomplishments, unravel their secrets, inspire the resistance, etc.
It's a roller-coaster of a shooter with some old-school and some "new-school" mechanics that is outrageously fun, brutal, gripping that, after 16 chapters, will leave you yearning for more.
I kept thinking about RAGE as I was playing this though (not even Bioshock Infinite came to mind). No wonder, this is still the ID Tech 5 engine which, sadly, still has ways to go in terms of rending the world around you with no texture popins (Ahem Rage, Ahem). I would also still like to see my legs. Otherwise, the engine delivers. Blown off heads, sometimes big set-pieces, multiple ways of approaching the target, tons of ricochet/explosion/smoke/bullets flying everywhere along with pieces of concrete whizzing by. I also love that this time (unlike in RAGE) you play as a character with a voice as well as inner thoughts. I always wondered why so many games out there fail to deliver on the inner narration when your character thinks of something or encounters something in the world. It took Bioshock franchise 3 games to finally create a memorable character (whose face you sadly do not get to see in the game, still).
Now why do I mention Bioshock again? Well, I've noticed some subtle philosophy behind this game. The war is over, well, all wars are over now, nations do not fight each other anymore because there are no more nations. The technology put the man on the moon in 1951. There is Colonization of Venus is underway. Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Aeronautics along with Eugenics, racism, suppression, slave labor, camps. It is the New Order. All you see is conformity/normality and honest idealistic beliefs (probably reserved for Germans only). And then there is a third choice, resistance.
And that's where B.J. Blazkowicz and his friends come in. Now how exactly did the Nazis manage to conquer the world and reach Peru? Well, play the game and find out. However, with all those bad things I mentioned I can't help but play a devil's advocate and ponder that in a few more generations of the New Order the assimilated people would no longer know of the good old days. Fast-forward few more generations and people would simply take the world as it is. A technologically advanced civilization the fruits of which are reserved for the top 1%. As you read letters written by the British they will mention that even though the war was lost they have now experienced 6 months of peace - without any terrorist activity, where they can walk the streets of London without being scared for their life. Now that's where the game is trying to throw the player off a bit, I believe. However, we have very little knowledge of how the outside world fares.
I don't want to get too deep into this but I'll say this, buy the game, support the dev, and enjoy.

The strongs:
* A cool story well deserved by the artistic directing, characters with strong charisma.
* Old school feeling "me shoot, me kill!" VS "sneaky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" : your choice, both are rewarded adequatly.
* Humour.
* The audio, especially the music, is pretty good.
* Multiple paths maps (even if still limited by the corridor like movements)
* Cool featurettes, secret doors and easter eggs.
The bads:
* idTech5 : Virtual Textures are a nightmare for memory bandwith, I/O and CPU workload at the point it can run awefully on very high end rigs.
* Virtual textures : poor details at near distance.
* Lazy culling : culling of dynamic objects is asynchronous : say hello to objects popping out!
* The AI is quite stupid if not fully scripted ( balanced by a higher difficulty become acceptable but its not to expect by default )
* A small number of the sequences are completly unfair for the player due to graphic overload and invisible walls (why ennemies are able to shoot you perfectly by 500m when in a dense fog where you can't see through, and why am I sometime unable to jump over 1m ?)
* Audio sources are attenuated at very short distances, even cut, and mixed inconsistently which causes difficulties to hear a few dialogues and correctly localize gunshots.
* I totally dislike the way the mouse wheel for weapon selection has been handled
* Final boss sequence is too much scripted and feels unfair.
Overall, the gameplay is quite enjoyable and the players interested by story telling will find a nice one here.

This game boasts a rather unique alternate history setting where the Nazis have somehow gained great technological advances that allowed them to win the war. You play as the valiant American War Hero B.J. Blakowicz, who falls into a coma while performing a raid on a Nazi controlled castle. It is up to B.J. and the resistance to crush the Nazis and take back the world. You get several various weapons, following the structure of older FPS games where you pick them up and unlock them as you go, but only the more unique weapons. You generally start every level with a knife, two handguns and another weapon, obtained in the story so I won't spoil it. I am personally having a blast with this game, even though I am playing it on the hardest-but-one diffficulty of "I am Death Incarnate," the hardest diffficulty of the first Wolfenstein games. It's fast, it's fun, and it's free.  While it doesn't bring anything new or groundbreaking to the genre, it's easy to get into and get going.  The different characters/classes are fun (though a few are annoying *cough* Proxy *cough*) and offer a variety of playstyles (even between the different characters of the same class).  The side objectives  provide some additional action and are an interesting idea (you don't need to complete them, but they can give you team a competitive edge).  I also like the card/loadout system as well, as it gives you something to work for but isn't game breaking if you don't build up your loadouts.
The only down side is that there are only really two game modes, Execution (team DM) and Objective (one team attacks objectives whle other defends) and maps are a bit limited (Execution has two, I think... and Objective has five).
Overall, if you're looking for something to kill some time and want a fast-paced FPS, you can't really go wrong with this well-executed (and free) little gem.

I encourage you to try this game out if you can play with friends and you're ready to die a lot to learn this game. It can have its moments that no other game can come close to recreating, but lacks any real driving force behind the giant battles which leaves you wanting so much more from the game that has failed to deliver for 2 years.
Planetside 2 features large, 600 v 600 v 600 battles on large 8km x 8km maps with a dozen bases that can easily fit the largest battlefield maps in them. Battles can be an intense fire fight as players use tanks, bombers, and variety of troop transports to gain ground and territory. These battles can be a lot of fun... IF a lot of variables are just right.
Battles often have one side heavily out numbering the other, spawn camping the smaller group in their spawn while they wait for a cap timer. When big battles do happen, they rarely continue between bases. When one side loses the majority of the players scatter as the winning force then swoops in to take the connecting territories with no resistance util they get bored and try to find another fight.
The game seems afraid to give any direction to the players. this leads to new players wondering where to go or do. Its a game where coordination is required, but gives no tools to the players to do so. squad and platoon leaders have very little tools to keep a squad together or hand out objectives. The devs did start to implement a mission system to help with this, but stopped half way through and theres no word when they'll finish it.
A lot of key features are also half implemented. Resources are used in the game to purchase vehicles and consumables for infantry. however, there is no way currently to get low on resources through normal play for very long. Players gain a steady rate of resources. there is no way to impact that rate when there should be to provide secondary objectives to players behind enemy lines.
I could go on and on on how many things are half implemented or missing from this game that would make it a truly great game. However, the devs at SOE really fumbled it up bad. One of the former leads, Matt Higby, even admitted to some mistakes early on that cost the game dearly in design choices and in handling development of the game.
While i don't recommend spending any money on this game, if your interested you should check it out since it's free. just don't expect too much depth.
Pros:
- Huge Battles with hundreds of players
- Runs well considering whats going on (on some computers)
- local, squad, and platoon voice chat in game
- Playing with an outfit leads to some awesome moments you can't replicate in any other game
Cons
- Incomplete game. 2 years after release the game is missing SO MANY features, a good amount of them could be considered key or core features too
- Lack of direction means battles or a cluster♥♥♥♥ as people wander around killing each other wondering what to do
- No real depth in any of the game's systems. Once you know how to kill efficiently alone or in a group you'll get bored quickly.
- Runs poorly (on some computers), inconsistent stability across different machines.

The Rating System: Good refers to the obvious positive qualities, the Bad is reserved for nitpicks and gripes that don't necessarily ruin the experience, the Ugly is for the worst parts of the game, meant for serious consideration before purchase.
The Good:
The game plays very smoothly, it has excellent optimization with plenty of options. The controls are simple and easy to understand once you find their hidden, "optional" keys. For example the, "switch between primary and secondary" action isn't bound to anything by default. Until I found it, I would panic constantly as I was forced to go through a weapon juggling routine every time I needed to switch between secondary and primary, which led to several deaths just from that alone. I hit my stride once I found it and the other options like it. If the controls aren't agreeing with you, take a long hard look at the options menu, there's likely something there to help. It's good that they didn't go one way or the other and made these things optional, but the more intuitive options should be on by default, or at least something you can choose between in the tutorial map.
Something I like is how the game rewards you with slight XP and cash bonuses for your performance, but your performance is not linked only to your kill/death ratio. You can top score your team by focusing primarily on the objective, resupplying with ammo, healing and reviving teammates, there's loads of ways you can be a valuable player on the team besides purely killing.
The weapons and gear are comfortable and behave how you would expect, and all 13 classes have a special ability that can be tide turningly effective if used properly. The gameplay itself consists of your standard FPS multiplayer fare, but the rounds are very short and loud, the kind of thing that feels exhausting after only 30 minutes just because there's so much going on. It's like potato chips versus a pizza: One requires you to stop on occasion to get up and grab another slice, allowing you time to enjoy it as well as notice how full you're getting from it. The other is sweet and all in one handful, meant to be eaten quickly one after the other until you've eaten the entire bag and feel slightly sick. That's a praise and a criticism at the same time, as it's definitely fun, but it's a very repeatitive and exhausting kind of fun. It's great in short bursts, like Ruffles cool ranch.
The Bad:
Dirty Bomb is flawed fun, with some things that get in the way. I find the main menu interface to be cluttered and confusing, a mess to the eyes that takes a long time to figure out, with too many redundant menus. It takes a lot of messing with menus just to change a single loadout card for example, when that process could be much quicker and simplified.
It's true what they say, you're going to get your♥♥♥♥♥kicked when you first start playing, but a part of why that is, is because players who've spent the most money or the most time can have 3 passive upgrades that give big advantages such as bonus health after dying, bonus movement speed, bonus melee damage, etc. While it's possible to get these things for yourself via hours and hours of grinding or with real money, it's very unforgiving to new players who don't have a single passive upgrade and just the two starter classes to play.
The Ugly:
I really dislike the card system it uses. If I get a really good upgrade with an ugly skin, I'm forced to use it anyway or be at a disadvantage. If I want to only use one of the weapons on the upgrade card but not the other, too bad. You can only use the game's pre-made loadouts, there is absolutely no creativity allowed with this system. The prices on these cards are outrageous at that, 5,000 credits or 3 dollars for a single card! Imagine without random item drops or trading, where you HAD to buy individual weaponry. It's nice that you can at least buy a specific card, but it's still a very restrictive system that requires weeks of grinding (all while being outgunned in every match you're in), because of the cost. You either get to spend your weeks of credits on a new loadout, or save for a month just to unlock a new character to play.
On that note..
The game has plenty of random crate drops, but because of how expensive classes are, chances are likely that it's not even for a class you have. You only get 2 classes out of the 13 class roster to start. They range from 30,000 - 50,000 ingame credits, or 10 bucks a pop. This is a LOT to ask for something that should be accessable from the start to help level the playing field for new players just trying to find what they're good at, and yet another reason why new players have such a short lifespan. It's hard to learn what a class does when you can so rarely have access to them. They could fix most of the game's balance issues by removing class purchasing entirely, making the skinless cards dirt cheap, making cards only drop for classes you have, or introducing Steam trading and community market support.
I'm unsure if this is really something to count against the game itself, but I would want to know something like this before purchasing a game, so I'll include it incase you do too. The Dirty Bomb community has a LOT of negative, quarrelsome and stereotypically rude players in it, the kind that people who aren't "gamers" tend to think of when they hear that phrase, who go into temper tantrums and spit homophobic slurs every four seconds. There's a client side mute function, but it's very weird. You hold Tab to show the scoreboard, then press left click to make your mouse pointer show, then select a player's name off the scoreboard to mute them. There's also vote kicking, but nobody ever seems to vote kick the rude players. Thankfully the devs are working on the game often enough that that may become a non-issue in the future.
These kinds of people - as is often the case - are NOT the majority and if you don't think this applies to you, then it probably doesn't. That being said, there is certainly a large enough pool of these kinds of players to make it worth warning about. This problem may stem from both the high skill requirement it takes to survive a second in this game, as well as the fact that failure results in very few credits. When a round can average about 600 credits out of 50,000 for just one new class to play, there's going to be a lot of pressure to succeed.
Final Verdict: 5/10
Functionally fun gameplay marred by its awkward user interface, abundance of hyper aggressive players, needlessly expensive loadout system with all but 2 of its 13 classes locked behind paywalls. It's fun enough to recommend, but it's not for everyone, and very hard to get into. I don't mind spending money on TF2 for its user friendly design, and the fact that the only things you "have" to spend money on are cosmetic. Things like classes should be free, or at least very cheap or unlockable through normal play. Pay to win is an ugly term, and it's hopping right up to that line when players with WAY more money or time to put into the game, get way more basic gameplay options than the standard 2 classes with only 1 strict loadout a piece.

I'm not one for getting offended by things. But portrayals of Nazis in pop culture have always been disconcerting in many ways, turning them from a real life nightmare into something on par with zombies and vampires - occult/dangerous Other things that aren't beholden to the rules of society proper. So if you're not really into the ideas of Nazis as villains on that level, then this probably isn't for you.
This game is largely good in its humanization of the Nazis, which is appropriate because the scariest part about them was not the horrific atrocities they committed, but the rhetoric and ideology they used that convinced people to join them and become complicit in the eradication of their fellow man.
The game vacillates wildly in tone at times, however, especially with regard to Blazkowicz's interactions with Anya. Her portrayal isn't flattering, for the most part. Although, in other occasions with her and with the other characters, a tremendous amount of effort was put into making them feel well rounded. The most impressive parts of the game for me were the occasions of stillness when you could talk to people fighting with you, thereby getting to know their stories. And the characters are excellent, oftentimes leaving one feeling hopeful for humanity in spite of their circumstances. Incidental dialogue between Nazis themselves and the German people are also very humanizing, which was a welcome addition.
I'd recommend it, for the most part. The shooting is solid and feels significantly weighty. Machinegames did a great job on a technical level, which is consistent with some of their key members' previous work at Starbreeze. There is a certain amount of texture pop-in that happens in much the same way as it did in Rage, so I'd put a portion of the blame for that in idTech 5 idiocyncracies, though I'm far from an expert in that.
It's a good game - the only question one needs to ask beforehand is how comfortable does one feel fighting cartoonish Nazis? And it is a question worth asking. For my part, I accept that it's a complicated representation put forth by the game, but I think that it does more than anyone would have expected with regard to making sure that it's characters - good and bad - are sufficiently plausible. I feel like it's a decent accomplishment, though not an unprecedented one, as similar themes can be seen (in just as complicated a manner) in Tarantino's

It's solid, polished and when the gun fights are going down it's magnificent, fluid and testing. The boss fights are testing at points too with audio hints and clues if you get a little stuck working out what to do. The main point to make here is the boss fights are well designed with an old school approach in mind. They require some quick reflexes, fast thinking and a little intelligence/perception to work out what to do. I love this, I really do.
The sound track is like silky smooth milk chocolate to the ears. The music fits the ambience of the levels/scenarios and really gets the adrenaline pumping during gun fights. The sound track changes on the fly depending on how much action is going on at any given time and never seems out of place. It invoked emotion in me. If I made a mistake while taking the stealth option and was forced to bring out the akimbo assault rifles the music adapated fueling my adrenaline and passion for mowing down nazis! MEIN LIEBEN!
The graphics are sublime, just stunning. The effort that's gone into the detail, polish and art style really fits the game. Nothing seemed out of place and no detail was spared on static props. It runs like a dream on my system:
AMD FX (Piledriver) 8350 (8 Core) 4Ghz
16gb 1333mhz DDR RAM
Nvidia GTX 670
The reports of the AI being a bit poor, in my opinion, don't hold any water. The enemies are actively taking cover, rolling/sprinting/sliding behind cover, flanking, making smart use of grenades and forcing you out into the fight.
Luckily, I have also encountered no bugs, no crashes and no funnies. I know this isn't the case for everyone but I can only speak from my own personal experience.
It took me, around, thirteen hours to complete the game on Death Incarnate, which is quite reasonable considering your average mainstream game these days are clocking in at around six hours.
The game rewards your play style too. If you want to stealth as much as you can (like me) you can and will be rewarded for it. If you'd prefer to go in all guns blazing (and I'm now going to replay it with the alternate timeline using this method) you will be rewarded for doing so. I like this and I wish more games gave you this option.
I cannot recommend this game enough if you're from the generation which grew up with id, Unreal, 3D Realms, Apogee and Monolith. I'm 99.9% sure you're going to love it and even be charmed by the little touches which blend modern technology and techniques with properly good old school mechanics which started the genre.
I give this 10 Llamas of Super Coolness out of 5 Jam Sandwiches.

I have been a fan of Wolfenstein since the first time I ever played it. I started mostly with Return to Castle Wolfenstein, pretty much the godfather of FPS's and worked my way through the games as I could to the, I think, 2009 game that some people didn't like, which I may say I did like.  Now let me get this out of the way and this is mostly just a heads up for some people, I bought the retail copy so I got disks, the box had 4 disks in it, which I thought was weird for a 40+ gig game and for good reason, if you get the retail copy you will still need to download 10+ gigs, I think it was like 10.7 or something, I cannot remember.  I understand some people may not have a problem with that, but I had to wait an extra day just to play it.  This may not even be a problem for most people though, unless you have download limits or what not, just a heads up. Now to the review.  As most people that have heard of this game know its about the Nazis winning the war and classic hero BJ is there to kill Nazis.
The story is pretty good, although don't expect it to be the best thing ever written. It is very good and unlike most war focused games, this one actually shows the civilian cost, and the effect people have with the Nazis in control.  The gameplay is fun and I felt tactial at times. Most levels you have the choice of how to engage, there are certain units that if they spot you they will call in reinforments, which can be a pain.  So you can either go guns blazing and take out everyone, or take the stealth routine.  I tended to be as stealthy as possible, but when spotted went guns blazing.  Also this game has a perk system which is kind of cool.  Each of the trees has different slots, all can be earned by doing a certain challenge such as get so many headshots, or kill 2 people with one grenade.  There are a couple trees to earn each skill for and once earned never go away, unless you start a new game.
The AI was kind of buggy at times, not anything that bad to where the game couldn't be played or wasnt fun, just sometimes guards would be looking straight at me and not set off an alarm or shoot at me, but other times the AI would work together to murder me.  I played through the game on the medium difficulty so I could get a decent challenge but still be able to beat the game without raging.  The guns are fun and some can get upgrades which just make a great gun even more fun to use.  If you like collecting things then this game will keep you around for a while.  Of the collectables I can think of off the top of my head you have: Letters written to different people which give you cool histroy and sometimes tips, Gold items that are just around, and the last I can remember are code fragments.  If you get all the pieces of one code you can then decode it, through trial and error, paying attention in game I think there are hints in some levels, and the internet.
The reward for finishing the code? Unlocking a new game mode adding more replayablity to an already good game.  I have around 11 hours or so in the game and finished it in 2 sittings, but decided to give my laptop a break after 9ish hours straight.  The game also managed to have some humor and have a serious tone and some sad moments.  The only really challenging part of the game for me was the final boss fight, I would say much about it but after dying a few times you should figure it out like I did.  I had the settings on Ultra and it looked pretty amazing. Do the side missions also, they arnt listed as missions but if you see them you will know what I mean, and explore every region you can because you can find some cool stuff hidden around. As a big fan of the Wolfenstein series this game was great and kept the old school feel which i miss in most modern games. I highly recommend this to fans of the series or fans of FPS's in general, also there is no MP in case you were wondering. I loved this game, also I get access to the upcoming Doom beta so thats a huge plus too.

It definitely has a Team Fortress 2 vibe to it, which I love. I was able to draw similarities between the classes here and in TF2 from the initial cutscene which immediately put me in the right mindset for objective play. I chose to play as Aura the medic to play on my TF2 experience and came to find that I appreciate the time I spent as a medic in The Division a little more since the medical mechanics are very similar.
If I had to choose one thing to dislike about this so far, it would be the lack of a party system. Yes, it's true that TF2 also lacks a party system, but it's significantly easier to find a joinable lobby with 2-4 players there than in here. The lobbies in Dirty Bomb fill up far too quickly, and even if 2 friends manage to get in, chances are they'll be on opposite teams. It might be nice for some to have that result to spice the game up a bit, but when your buddy specializes in being the Mobile Minigun from Hell and you were his Medic, it turns into a bloodbath with no hope of winning. Not fun.
I love that the cases you earn don't cost anything to open!
I sort of dislike the fact that you can buy other cases with real money which can be borderline pay-to-win if you aren't careful with the types of weapons you put in there, but I can't fault you, the Devs, for using this to support your beautifully crafted game. Buying cases is totally okay as long as there isn't anything super OP in it. We already have the Heavies for that.
So, 8/10 overall. It's a solid game, but the lack of it acknowledging you're friends with someone in a game where the players are made of rice paper (compared to other games) and teamwork is an absolute necessity keeps it from being rated higher.
*Side Note: There are already Medics out there who play with their patients.. Taking out the defib, charging it, and turning it away to let go before doing it again. Teammates also ignore members who are down even when there are no threats around. Perhaps an incentive to pick up fallen comrades could help fix this.
-------
The above is what I wrote for feedback the other day. Immediately afterwards, there was a spree of games where my minigun friend and I were thrown in a lobby on the Bridge with players who were level 68 and 75. Normally in these types of games, we pay very little attention to levels since that is not always an accurate indicator to skill. Well, that statement was partially correct here. We weren't able to determine their skill at the game because we were getting fried by their Flame and Frag grenades which seemed to instantly kill us regardless of where we were in relation to the grenades. Because they were spamming them, it was impossible for our team to even leave spawn. The cherry on top was the airstrike that dropped -in our spawn area- a few seconds before the match ended.
On the Dome, there was a player who was sporting a Gold card (second rarest loadout type with first being Cobalt) which had a shotgun as the main weapon. We're unsure if this was an intended mechanic or if this kid was hacking, but as players were coming into view of the objective delivery area this kid was on the opposite wall and downed everybody with a single body shot each. Not even a guy on our team with a Cobalt loadout was able to take this guy down. Basically an OP Sniper-Shotty was dominating this game and even claimed to only be 7 as if that helped his case. 7 years old and level 75? Yeah, totally legit.. If this kid was hacking, we did in fact report him, but if it wasn't a hack then the Devs need to talk to whoever is balancing the combat system right now and rebalance it.
Neither of these situations is helped by the fact that every merc, including the Heavy, seems to be made of rice paper. It's like there's no reason to have a health bar in the first place because you go down in one or two shots, and then you have to wait for the next spawn wave which can be up to 15 seconds. It doesn't seem like much, but it's a lot of time in an FPS game where every second is precious for defusing a bomb or getting the objective to the chopper.
The moral of the story is we need a party system and a proper matchmaking system based on skill level to help prevent this sort of thing. Or even better; a matchmaking system that looks at your card rarities in active use and bases your match on that.
Despite these drawbacks, it's still a very well-made. smooth game even compared to games that cost money. My friend and I did some thorough exploring of the maps, and we could not find a single "perfect" spot to camp. There was always a place to shoot in on the area (with the exception of a few corners here and there that served no real advantage at all). The only problem in this area is there is no absolute way to leave spawn safely. If the enemy team manages to pin you down on your spawn, you are at their mercy unless someone gets cocky and gets picked off. Even then, there is little chance of leaving, let alone taking back the game. With the grenade example above, once you're pinned, it's game over.
The game does sport a large variety of classes/mercs to play as, but they don't tell you on the front page that you have to pay for these mercs (besides the default two and whoever is in free rotation) with real money or spend 50,000 credits per merc. The average good match (by good I mean 5k-9k XP) usually pays out 200-500 credits.
So if you somehow manage to play 100 matches which pay out nearly 10k XP and 500~ credits each, then you can buy yourself one merc with in-game currency. This of course does not take into account any of the three side missions that you complete which can reward either 500 or 1k credits each and changes every 3 hours or so. There's only a handful of maps and the objectives formula is always the same, so prepare yourself for some mind numbing if you plan to grind to earn your mercs.
Overall there are a lot of drawbacks in this beta and you're probably better off playing something like TF2, but this is still better than something like Nether and has its own feel and playstyle to it. That's worth upvoting to me. I'm told that things get better when you hit level 7 and open a special case that the game gives you, but I haven't gotten there yet since the XP system is on the slow side. I will stick with my 8/10 rating for now and update when I've hit that point.

Where to begin? This is one of the best (if not the best) first person shooters I've played in a long time. It excels in terms of visuals, storytelling, and most importantly of all, gameplay. The action is violent, bloody, over-the-top, and exceptionally fun. During most portions of the game, the player is free to choose whether to be stealthy, or to simply run-and-gun. If you enjoy stealth, feel free to sneak around dozens of Nazis, silently picking them off one by one with knives and/or silenced firearms. If you prefer running and gunning, then go right ahead, and experience the fast-paced and very dynamic gunfights.
One of the coolest things about this game is that you can dual-wield any weapon, providing that you find and pick up two of them (it's usually not hard to find two). Imagine running around with two fully-automatic shotguns, or two huge combat rifles with outfitted with rocket launchers. Is this over the top? Is this unrealistic? Yes, and yes. But that doesn't matter one bit, because it's fun as all hell.
In terms of writing and character development, I found much more than I originally anticipated. Given that the Wolfenstein games have rarely had any more depth than "here's some Nazis... go shoot them", I was pleasently suprised. These kinds of action games really don't need detailed stories and interesting characters; but Wolfenstein: The New Order gives you these things anyway, and it does so beautifully.
In short, I honestly have practically no negative things to say about this game. (I did notice one particularly annoying bug with the game's 5.1 audio, but it's not a huge deal. Changing the Windows audio config to stereo resolves the issue.) The lack of multiplayer is (for me at least) a non-issue. In fact, if anything, it is a breath of fresh air. The developers clearly wanted to focus on delivering a lengthy and fun campaign, and it pays off big time. I highly enjoy this game, and I recommend it to any fan of the FPS genre. Easily worth the $60 that it costs at the time of writing.

After having finished the game and collecting a good amount of the hidden collectibles I must say this game is better than your average shooter. Underneath that hardened nazi killing machine is a man plagued by the deaths he has seen caused by his enemy Deathshead. The story can be likened to Quinten Tarantino's Inglorious ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s with the humor and dark parts blending in very well together. The AI in the game however is not the best and can increasingly become stupid in many cases however as I had found out later on in the game on the hardest difficulty level, you will die several times by not paying close attention at where the enemy is. The graphics themselves are decent though not amazing, but in reality I would choose gameplay over graphics which this game definitely has. I personally did not come across any glitches or bugs during my playtime and there really isnt anything I did not like about this game, heck there is even a second timeline in the game that I am beginning now. The finale in the game will definitely get or adrenaline going too (Sorry no spoilers are allowed here). All in all, Wolfenstein The New Order is a great shooter (Which is longer than most) and definitely a fantastic reboot to the series. Hopefully this is a game that will continously get better and better if and when another installment is made in the future.

This was horrible timing. I started playing PS2 right before they decided to run it into the ground.
Sony was just beginning to break even, was about to port it to Playstation 4 (Sony's console!), which means relatively little development effort for unlocking a vast new customer base. And what do they do? They sell it, to an investment company. Probably an attempt to not sully the name. (I can't avoid being cynical about this.)
So the game was full of issues, needed lots of work. And what do they do as one of the first actions after the sale? ... Get rid of half the dev team. BEFORE they bring the game up to a decent state. WHILE they had the added work of console-porting. ... And now every new update introduces more bugs, makes the game worse and worse. It feels like an Early Access alpha.
Every time I spent money on it, it felt like being punished for it. Horrible business approach. They had a sale on all infantry cosmetics. I bought plenty. A week later they frickin changed the looks! (And why? For IFF reasons they say! Visual identification is pointless in most situations anyway in a twitch shooter like this, and you have markers above friendlies anyway, and many camos are also supposed to be functional, but no longer. This is not just noob-pandering, but to an extent that makes no sense. - More catering to the braindead is to follow.) That was one of the first things. The last was when I had just unlocked the flak turret for the Lightning tank with plenty of points that took me quite a while to accumulate, and also bought a bodykit for the tank. A day later they messed up tank and turret controls by introducing a quarter second input lag! Drunk rubber-band style.
Why? Because they consider PC p(l)ayers not worth the effort to give proper controls, so they do something unheard of: They port a game to console, but not by creating a second version. No, PC players have to deal with the console version. They try to emulate mouse controls on top of a game controller input system which didn't exist at first. They say the alternative of two systems would be too much administrative work.
Doesn't that feel nice? PC players have financially supported the game all this time and that's what they get: Step back for the esteemed console crowd now. They take priority.
This is really PSN me off.
They also release for-money cosmetics that are actually unfinished. You might buy a whitish bodykit for an aircraft and then suddenly: It was meant to have camo-texture, so we fixed that now. Other cosmetics might have tons of clipping, so there's no quality control. (This content is player-created, too, not even their effort. They just have to damn check that it fits properly before asking money for it, but that seems too much to ask.) They even revise models, add tiny details, and forget to fix the blatant screwups. And they make the effort to revise some weapon models and on the new ones the camo textures are barely visible anymore. They really do everything they can think of to dis paying customers.
And they have that general policy: No refunds. (Not even if it's in part their fault, and no automated undo-system either!) Sounds so much like punishment for fools. Well, by now I finally learned my lesson. All my incredible leniency and tolerance and good will have finally been crushed. I had intended to invest even more in the game, liking the style, but they crushed that. They crossed a line.
And their business policy goes farther downhill, as various announced changes indicate  (the usual MMO crap - turning a game into a heroin selling scheme), all the while their ingame shop - the thing that is actually supposed to bring money in - is an appalling piece of lackluster design that misses so damn many opportunities for bringing money in in a decent way. They even treat their discounts like secrets. (What, you're not following them on Twitter? Well, that's YOUR problem, isn't it? ... Oh wait.)
People saying that Planetside 2 deserves to be saved because it's the only Battlefield style MMO is something that will only be used against them, too. PS2 doesn't need saving, it needs rescuing. But it might not be worth the effort.
I'm now in the ugly situation of having invested a considerable amount of money out of passion without having gotten opportunity to actually enjoy the game for a significant time. I settled for playing it for free from now on, since paying money is optional (which makes their business policy of discouraging monetary investments even more facepalm-worthy), but even with that approach, there are still plenty of antisocial players to♥♥♥♥♥♥you off by trying to ruin your day. People on your own team working against you for their own egoistical benefit, and as usual for MMOs, no appropriate, effective tools for dealing with that. It ruins my spirit when such scum joins a team game.
The reward-for-effort system is quite well-developed by now (yet antisocials don't care), balancing is quite alright, too. Without all the mentioned funspoiling issues, the game would actually be great, and something I could enjoy a lot. There's tons of buff/nerf threads on the forums, but personally I could enjoy the game regardless of possible imbalances currently existing. That's the whole reason why I spent a lot of money on it. Because I saw it was a good game and didn't encounter all the crap yet. Some of it I couldn't, since it only got implemented later. They actually have horrible bugs on the test server and eventually decide to move them to the live servers. It's as if they want to test new bugs properly before they release them, to make sure they are effective and work as intended. As I said, it's hard not to be cynical about what happens with that game.
I should have stuck to my resolution of not playing an MMO again, as well as to my contempt for Sony. But I thought: Maybe I just need to be more accepting and re-evaluate my priorities. Well, yet another mistake. I am repeatedly being taught a life lesson that the more crap you tolerate, the more crap you get.
They seem to be more geared towards tricking you out of your money (e.g. make you buy twice - like FIRST discount on vehicle items, THEN EXTENDING the palette of available options with new fancy stuff right after that) than make it appealing for you to spend it without regret.
UPDATE: More than a year later and almost all the bugs, small or big, annoying or just looking bad, are still there. But you have some base-building now. Wow. -_- A lot in this game seems like late alpha / early beta. The gaming world would be missing something without this battlefield MMO, but it keeps easily destroying my temptation to spend more money on it.
Anti-griefing measures are still totally ineffective, too.

I dont often pay full price for SP games on Steam, but nostalgia grabbed me, and since it has been out for a week, I have only heard positive feedback.
What a great game.  Good storyline.  Great graphics.  Rails moments are fast and like they should be.  Weapon options will make you smile.  Stealth is fun.
Did I mention dual wielding Automatic-Firing Shotguns?  Nancy Panzerhunds that eat thru walls?  Die Kafer?
The destructible terrain is very staged... looks great and acts great but feels off.  Blowing up sheet metal walls earlier with a 2 handed laser, then later not able to make a mark on a barrel or a guy hiding behing a tarp was funny... dem tarps..
Graphics:  8/10
---The graphics function at a high level.  There is an issue with a detail pop up, from what I understand only Nvidia cards.  I am on a gtx770 and the fill in is noticable but doesnt break the game at all.  It happens usually just at a "starting" area as the world populates.  Then its gone for the most part.  Once in a while Ill do a double spin or something and I see the detail on a wall pop in late.
Sound: 9/10
---Wow.  This is a LOUD game.  Just... turn it up.  Im on 5.1 and the stuff you hear alone with the speaks up loud is awesome.  The dogs jumping thru the walls...OHSHEET! /ESC go outside let heart settle down.
Control: 5/10
---Right down the middle WASD basic control with filler around it.  Nothing broken nothing new.  I have 2 "control" problems that are going to be subjective haha.  The slide?  I have a hard time doing W, Left Shift + Left Control just before you need to slide under a low point - usually with a 4 legged juicer on your tail.  And my second problem with control is those times you need to hotwire something.  Trying to get those wires together is hard!  I let my 13 year old do it EVERY TIME.  Haha >.>
Saving is checkpoint based.  Reach a certain point and it saves automaticly for you.  Prepare to play some areas over and over.  Healing is food/bandage based.  You come across glowing  food or health based type that grant a certain amount of health up to 100.  You can get more food and "overload" your health up to 200.  This extra hit points slowly ticks down as you look for trouble or engage.  There is also a shield stat - same idea, find random items or get them from bosses to add to your shield stat.
Weapons can be accessed via mouse scroll up/down bringing up  a circular dial that you can continu to scroll to what weapon combo you wanted.  I found doing the same with the number keys faster.  You can dual wield most anything - knives, pistols, shotguns, and rifles.   I have not seen a sniper rifle yet.  Basic grenades for the most part.  Basic logical rules apply to weapons: pistols/shotguns lack range, rifles can be cumbersome in tight corridors etc.
Stealth is similar to dishonored but stripped down a bit.  Basic crouch and go slow, hope to reach baddy before he turns around BOOM sliced knee, turn and knife through eardrum.  Very few different takedown animations.  You can use silencers on pistols, even when dual wielding.  Seems to be thoughtful to someone wanting to stealth to a certain point.  You will find grates and pipes and planks to walk on.  I found myself having a blast stealthing around and eventually tripping onto something bad and just getting swarmed somehow fighting my way out of a total mess.
Great game.  If you dont buy this now, thats ok, just know that you will in time.

What's not to like right?  Wolfenstein 3D, a first person shooter developed by Bethesda and Id (and others), should be the best thing since sliced bread?   Well, it's not, at least for me.
What I really liked about this game was the atmosphere and the story development.   It drew you in and made want to keep playing, which is good, because the gameplay is certainly repetitive.   Unfortunately, that's about all I have to say that's good about the game.
Wolfenstein brings in a bit of a cool concept, a perk tree that you get from achieving certain milestones in the game, for example, killing a commanding officer via stealth will award you the "Scout" perk/trait.   The problem is that this tree is really quite simplistic and it really feels like a wasted opportunity.   The game would have had so much more depth with a borderlands style tree where you can select stealth or marksmanship to suit how you wanted to play.   It'd also mean that I'd probably be playing the game a second time instead of uninstalling it from my PC.
Missions are decent.   You know what you're going for and they are major story plots.   But the side missions are quite frankly  horrible.   Find someone's ring?   Find someone's toys?  And they wouldn't be so bad if they weren't all exactly the same.   Talk to generic NPC, hear story, go find item, give item, get nothing in return.
But the major failing point in this game is that the AI is just plain horrible.   Like really, really bad.   Stealth is a joke, because they can look right at you say "What was that?" and then if you nimbly move out of line of sight, they go on, as if nothing has happened.   Big mechanical baddies will sit there, content after seeing another Nazi's head be blown off by a silenced pistol.   And if they're not being stupid, they're running in place on invisible walls or huddled in some corner cause their waypoints weren't mapped well.
Horrible and quite frankly unacceptable from a game builder such as Bethesda.  Heck, Oblivion IV had better AI, and that's what, 10 years ago?
Wolfenstien is fun, don't get me wrong, but it's such a disappointment given who was involved.   It's like getting a dinner by Gordon Ramsay and getting a TV Dinner.
I wouldn't reccomend purchasing this game at 59.99.   It's a solid purchase at half that price (24.99).
