Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game is alive and kicking? I mean a proper alive, not the "oh we just updated the graphics for nostalgia's sake" so that some game artists can make a decent living. My previous review was written around the time the HD edition was released and I was banking on only nostalgia to validate my purchase -- but now there's been a new expansion and the competitive scene seems to have massively grown to the point where this is a viable RTS, online games and all. Video tutorials going in depth for each civilization, new strategies and tactics being developed today (this review being written on the 30th of December, 2015), and not quite 24/7 Twitch streams but still enough content during prime times to gain a following. Who'd have thought?
I've included my older review below, but it was mostly a self-indulgent tale of how I came to start playing this game and my appreciation for its revitalization -- but I never imagined that it would get to this point.
-----
I'll be honest, nostalgia was the biggest factor in my purchase of this game.
Age of Empires happens to hold a rather special place in my personal gaming history as it's one of the first purchases I immediately regretted. This was because I had accidentally purchased the expansion pack instead of the main game, thus was unable to play.
Now, there used to be a time where internet speeds were nowhere near fast enough to download nor even update games in a timely fashion (this was before youtube could even dream of being a thing). Game developers had to save any extra content they wanted to add onto a game and release it in a seperate box. Usually, these packs would contain a lot of content in order to create more value that could offset the cost of a physical release. The Sims franchise is about the only series that continues this tradition.
So, some innumerable years ago (only because I refuse to count) I was embarrassed because I had spent my allowance on the wrong game. This isn't really the focal point of my nostalgia, but to fully understand it I need to probe the depths of what memories I can find before I had a computer.
Backtracking further into the past, there was a point where I observed someone playing the original Age of Empires -- I think it was at a friend of the family's house. This happened at an age before I could be reasonably trusted to handle a computer, but like the supposed effect of playing Mozart and other classical musicians to a baby the image of this game burned itself into my subconscious somewhere. That or I simply couldn't stop talking about it. Maybe I substituted the normal games of pretend and imagination with my toys for more structured games and called it 'Age of Empires,' but trying to remember any of this is a rather futile effort. I'm not sure why or how but this game simply stuck with me.
I remember passing by a display of computer games some years later and immediately recognizing the title. There was a rush of excitement as I took hold of the box and confirmed what my memories were telling me. Yes, this was the sequel to that game you remember from so long ago. Yes, you do have the system requirements to play the game. Yes, this could happen today.
Turns out I was blinded by excitement, as previously mentioned. Eventually I did grab a compilation pack that included AoE II, AoE II: The Conquerors expansion, a gold edition of the original AoE, and a sound track. Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥did I play those games.
Playing now, I realized how terrible I used to be at the game. I'm not sure how I got through the campaign, except by sheer determination and just playing it over and over again. That and cheatcc. It's an old-school no-holds-barred RTS. The proper game was far too difficult for my past self, but at that age I could enjoy myself for days with the little laser riflement and the RPG-weilding cars as I simply cheated my way through the campaign and single-player content. Maybe I shouldn't be so harsh on the 12 year olds shooting untold numbers of faceless soldiers in games like Call of Duty, I was commiting time-travel genocide at that age. Over and over and over again.
But now that the story's done, there's an interesting competitive scene (still?) revolving around the game that surprised me. Found a ton of videos on youtube of people playing rather masterfully and it encouraged me to revise tactics and actually start beating some of those levels I found impossible (even on Easy). That being said, I'm still getting wrecked by the computer every now and then. The more things change, the more they stay the same.

Fun game that plays a lot like ET and Wolfenstein. However, they have had the same maps live for 3 years now with only 2 new maps (still in development) and no community tools to make new maps. New development also seems to be nonexistant as they removed the characters from everyones account last year, then made people re-buy the newly tweaked characters but didn't really offer much of anything new. Development just moves so slow - founders who bought into this game almost 3 years ago have seen very little new content and are still playing the same few maps the game started with.
PROS:
- Super tight shooter gameplay with fast action and maps that funnel the action towards objectives and tight areas.
- Fun and balanced classes with the old school 4 class system at the foundation.
- The only game to come close to being a new Wolfenstein or ET Multiplayer experience.
- A shooting game with clear objectives and pupose beyond blowing away the enemy. Team play is an absolute must and matches feel super epic because of the objectives and the classes.
CONS
- Little to no new content over 3 years.
- Super slow development.
- No community tools to make new maps even though the game is on Unreal engine and Unreal tools are available for free.
- No MOD support.
- Matches can be aweful and time consuming if players don't understand objectives. Thankfully all maps except Dome are straight forward and easy to learn and fun to play.
In closing I would point out that Dirty Bomb is a superior shooter to COD and Battlefield (IMO), if you like your shooter game to have some sort of direction and purpose and you enjoy expending maximum effort and team play to get the job done on any map. The gameplay is so tight and so much fun when teams understand the map. However, the DEV team has flip flopped a few times over the last 3 years of the game being in development, new dev is super slow with the devs facinated with making the Pay options work better, and there are no community tools available yet to make maps or MOD the game, which is sorely needs (more maps and MODS). Hopefully development will pick up or they will put some tools in the communities hands so that we can make more content, and make it faster to extends this games life. There is also one very bad bug they have never fixed, if players get it they can never play the game again without running the game in Safe mode. Splash Damage seems unwilling to address teh bug (over a year old) so now I have uninstalled the game since I got tired of fixing it through Safe mode. :)

What a great game.  Good storyline.  Great graphics.  Rails moments are fast and like they should be.  Weapon options will make you smile.  Stealth is fun.
Did I mention dual wielding Automatic-Firing Shotguns?  Nancy Panzerhunds that eat thru walls?  Die Kafer?
The destructible terrain is very staged... looks great and acts great but feels off.  Blowing up sheet metal walls earlier with a 2 handed laser, then later not able to make a mark on a barrel or a guy hiding behing a tarp was funny... dem tarps..
Graphics:  8/10
---The graphics function at a high level.  There is an issue with a detail pop up, from what I understand only Nvidia cards.  I am on a gtx770 and the fill in is noticable but doesnt break the game at all.  It happens usually just at a "starting" area as the world populates.  Then its gone for the most part.  Once in a while Ill do a double spin or something and I see the detail on a wall pop in late.
Sound: 9/10
---Wow.  This is a LOUD game.  Just... turn it up.  Im on 5.1 and the stuff you hear alone with the speaks up loud is awesome.  The dogs jumping thru the walls...OHSHEET! /ESC go outside let heart settle down.
Control: 5/10
---Right down the middle WASD basic control with filler around it.  Nothing broken nothing new.  I have 2 "control" problems that are going to be subjective haha.  The slide?  I have a hard time doing W, Left Shift + Left Control just before you need to slide under a low point - usually with a 4 legged juicer on your tail.  And my second problem with control is those times you need to hotwire something.  Trying to get those wires together is hard!  I let my 13 year old do it EVERY TIME.  Haha >.>
Saving is checkpoint based.  Reach a certain point and it saves automaticly for you.  Prepare to play some areas over and over.  Healing is food/bandage based.  You come across glowing  food or health based type that grant a certain amount of health up to 100.  You can get more food and "overload" your health up to 200.  This extra hit points slowly ticks down as you look for trouble or engage.  There is also a shield stat - same idea, find random items or get them from bosses to add to your shield stat.
Weapons can be accessed via mouse scroll up/down bringing up  a circular dial that you can continu to scroll to what weapon combo you wanted.  I found doing the same with the number keys faster.  You can dual wield most anything - knives, pistols, shotguns, and rifles.   I have not seen a sniper rifle yet.  Basic grenades for the most part.  Basic logical rules apply to weapons: pistols/shotguns lack range, rifles can be cumbersome in tight corridors etc.
Stealth is similar to dishonored but stripped down a bit.  Basic crouch and go slow, hope to reach baddy before he turns around BOOM sliced knee, turn and knife through eardrum.  Very few different takedown animations.  You can use silencers on pistols, even when dual wielding.  Seems to be thoughtful to someone wanting to stealth to a certain point.  You will find grates and pipes and planks to walk on.  I found myself having a blast stealthing around and eventually tripping onto something bad and just getting swarmed somehow fighting my way out of a total mess.
Great game.  If you dont buy this now, thats ok, just know that you will in time.
Thanks for your time.

What's not to like right?  Wolfenstein 3D, a first person shooter developed by Bethesda and Id (and others), should be the best thing since sliced bread?   Well, it's not, at least for me.
What I really liked about this game was the atmosphere and the story development.   It drew you in and made want to keep playing, which is good, because the gameplay is certainly repetitive.   Unfortunately, that's about all I have to say that's good about the game.
Wolfenstein brings in a bit of a cool concept, a perk tree that you get from achieving certain milestones in the game, for example, killing a commanding officer via stealth will award you the "Scout" perk/trait.   The problem is that this tree is really quite simplistic and it really feels like a wasted opportunity.   The game would have had so much more depth with a borderlands style tree where you can select stealth or marksmanship to suit how you wanted to play.   It'd also mean that I'd probably be playing the game a second time instead of uninstalling it from my PC.
Missions are decent.   You know what you're going for and they are major story plots.   But the side missions are quite frankly  horrible.   Find someone's ring?   Find someone's toys?  And they wouldn't be so bad if they weren't all exactly the same.   Talk to generic NPC, hear story, go find item, give item, get nothing in return.
But the major failing point in this game is that the AI is just plain horrible.   Like really, really bad.   Stealth is a joke, because they can look right at you say "What was that?" and then if you nimbly move out of line of sight, they go on, as if nothing has happened.   Big mechanical baddies will sit there, content after seeing another Nazi's head be blown off by a silenced pistol.   And if they're not being stupid, they're running in place on invisible walls or huddled in some corner cause their waypoints weren't mapped well.
Horrible and quite frankly unacceptable from a game builder such as Bethesda.  Heck, Oblivion IV had better AI, and that's what, 10 years ago?
Wolfenstien is fun, don't get me wrong, but it's such a disappointment given who was involved.   It's like getting a dinner by Gordon Ramsay and getting a TV Dinner.
I wouldn't reccomend purchasing this game at 59.99.   It's a solid purchase at half that price (24.99).

After 5+ years, for those who are playing it for the first time, it's still an amazing experience that won't decay over time. 10/10.

Just the facts (and opinions):
+ Love narrative focused FPS games and when they don't do the "obligatory" tacked on multiplayer they get a plus in my book. It's all single player focused gameplay and story
+ Very memorable & well written cast of characters. NPCs dialog is sharp, fun and well done. Every NPC has their own distinctive, well written personalities that will stick with you
+ Secrets! Every level/section has secret areas you can find with collectibles and powerups
+ Great perk system. Instead of giving you perk points, you unlock any one of the many perks by completing objectives, for example, stealth killing 5 NPCs grants you a perk
+ No pressure gameplay. You will run around and kill lots of baddies. This is not Metro where each fight must be carefully calculated. Run in, gun 'em down & move on. It's refreshing in it's simplicity. That's not to say it's an easy game, you will be challenged, but you don't need to over think it.
+ Optional stealth objectives. Some areas can be entirely cleared by being sneaky
+ Multiple paths. Most levels/sections have multiple ways to an objective. Do you take the vents? Go underground? Run around the backside?
- Check point system, no free saves. The check points are pretty generous but this is a bummer none the less
- Linear. I don't mind this much but open games are always preferred
- Very long intro/prologue level. Overly long IMO but once you pass it the game picks up

The first half of this game is absolutely extraordinary, allowing a variety of playstyles from you to choose from, which, alongside open areas, adds up to be an amazing experience tailored to your own playstyle. Then comes the second half. The second half resorts to the game throwing every enemy they can at you. The challenge is definitely needed in today's games, but it completely rids you of a playstyle choice. Enemies no longer can be stealth killed, or manuvered around, so each section gets dumbed down to "1. Use most powerful gun and empty bullets into armored enemy until they are dead. 2. Acquire new enemy. 3. Repeat steps 1 and 2 until room is cleared. 4. Advance. 5. Repeat entire sequence." This also gets very frustrating as well, as inevitably, you will run out of ammo. At that point, you get killed by some over-armored shotgun spamming Nazi, and have to start over. To summarize the second half, enemies can no longer be stealth killed, or avoided, leading you into bottleneck situations that require you to abandon any tactical essence about the second half, and resort to emptying round after round into seemingly invincible enemies who do the same thing to you, but ten times more effectively. I find myself feeling like completing the game is a chore, and do my best to resist the temptation to go back to the earlier levels, which are infinitely better.
I give this game a 5/10, as the first half is a definite 9, but the last half is a struggling 1.
Not worth the $60 I paid, but maybe a lower price would make this game more appealing to play.

Slick and polished.  Well made FPS.  Took me 20 hours to complete, took my time and enjoyed the details.  Satisfying combat.  The turret gun is fun...liquifies the enemy.  B.J. Blaskowits is well done and likeable with a very likable demeanor.  The game ran flawlessly for me at all maxed settings...including high spec adjustments via Nvidia Inspector.  Not a single crash or problem, so I don't know why others have had issues...???   Nice weapon designs.  Nice animations and characters.  Good story too.  Kinda high priced compared to much larger games like Dark Souls 2 which is HUGE and less money.  But I have to say I have no complaints.  It was worth it to play the game.  Pretty good replay value too because there are two diferent time lines you can opt to take.  Perhaps the only thing I might have desired more of in the game, was 1. A bit longer, especially perhaps the segment on the Moon, and 2., Perhaps a few more enemies, perhaps some Nazi 'creatures' / monsters...which I think would have fit right with the game.
Compared to the last game, 'return to castle Wolfenstein', it is a better game in most respects, however, I myself very much liked the 'occult' aspect, and since the Nazi's were in fact into the occult, I think it would have been pretty cool to have given some of that into this game too...???
Overall, the game is very well polished and exhibits nice design and attention to detail.  The mechanical robot dogs made no sence to me though, because, it would be utterly stupid to create a robot dog whose weaponry were teeth like a dog, instead of some kind of lazer or energy weapon.  The 'armored' dobermin dog, however, WAS well done and DID make sense.  Advice : Play it on one of the top two difficulty settings, otherwise you won't really sweat much and thus you will not be subject to any type of immersive feeling which B.J. most certainly WOULD experience given the situations he gets into.
Final note :  If your budget is tight, and, say, you can only afford to spend money on a single FPS game, I'd say it's FAR bettet than anything that's come out for a while.  However, if, say, you want to get an immense amount of game for your money, wait for a sale and instead opt for Dark Souls 2...which is rediculously huge for the money.  I bought both.  I hope they make another one of these, the ending leaves it open for another instalment.
Also, I'd play it with keyboard and mouse.  I tried playing it with my xbox controller and using a stick to control aim is utterly worthless.  With a mouse you get utter precision and control.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Ah, Good Old age of empires. I played the original version of this game for many hours when I was younger. I'll try to be as unbiased as possible in this review.
First, a word to any veterans that may be considering the HD version: KEYBINDS. If you had all the old ones memorised, you are going to have to rebind them. They don't use the original keybindings in this version.
Now, for those that have not played before...
A brief overview of what is possible.
-Random matches are basically an "anything goes" type of round. There are multiple ways to win, Not just by combat.
-Deathmatches start you with high resources and are a battle to the death.
-Regicide (a personal favorite) is a game variant in which you must protect your king while hunting down the enemy kings.
-Wonder race is quite simply, the first person who is able to build a wonder. If you were "wondering" what a wonder is, that basically is a monument made by your race. It can also be used to win a random match, however you must defend it for a length of time for it to work in that game mode.
-King of the hill (I believe is what it is called) is a variant in which you must protect a neutral wonder in the middle of the map for x amount of time.
-Capture the relic is a single relic on the map which must be captured to win. Both king of the hill and capture the relic can be VERY fast paced matches depending on your opponent.
Now, something for both vets and newbies alike:
-Treaties! - if you struggle fighting "rush" tactics in rts games, the DLC for this allows for you to set a time limit in which everyone is friendly. This prevents people from rushing you and gives newer players a chance to see how others play.
-Increased population limits! The old version had a limit of 200. The max now is 500 and there are even some forge mods that allow you to go even higher (although I wouldn't recommend it for your own sanity)
Now, I thought this was going to be great... I was wrong...
-New map size!... I thought this was going to be AWESOME at first. I was horribly dissapointed when I saw the tremendous amount of lagg this causes during multiplayer rounds. Stick to giant and you are fine. LUDAKRIS is 4 times larger than giant, and for some reason it laggs like a MOFO. It gets even worse if you add an AI to the map.
Now, My final verdict..
Overall gameplay - 8 / 10. The reason I don't give it a 10 is due to the fact that I'm not that big on the campaign. I could live, eat, sleep, and breath the multiplayer but I find the campaign boring at best.
Community - 7 / 10. For the most part you run across fairly nice people. Of course, every game has a few rotten apples playing it.
Diversity 9 / 10. Unlike some games where you see "cookie cutter" builds and races, Pretty much anything is viable on here. There are a few things that could use some rebalancing but, if you have a brain you can still counter most of them.
AI (Computer Players) 10 / 10. You want a challenge? put those suckers on max difficulty. You'll be running home to your grandmother crying by the feudal age.
Nostalgia 11 / 10. Nuff Said.

Well it is free, so yes I do recommend it. Anyways here's all the good with the bad.
The good: Alright so the good it's free, and you can do so many things in it. Game mechanics wise, it's almost like a futuristic, pure player versus player version of Grand Theft Auto, and there's THREE factions fighting instead of two, and the factions are much deeper than the whole admittedly shallow Red Team vs Blue Team thing. Don't get me wrong, lots of great games use the Red Team vs Blue Team thing, including one of my favorites of all time, but I like how Planetside 2's factions go way deeper.
And yes, that's just as good as it sounds.
Since the amount of player is so huge, and there's things like repairing/healing/offering ammo reviving, even some lock on weapons, players of all skill levels can contribute. If your aiming or dodging skills are slightly below average, you can partially compensate for this by going light assault or infiltrator, and take enemies down by surprise... I feel like my aiming/dodging skills are at least a little subpar, and I like being able to use strategetic ambushes to compensate for that, and yes, it works.
When I play Planetside 2, I tend to main in either SMG infiltrator, semi-auto scout rifle infiltrator, and then sometimes albeit less often, a light assault, medic, magrider gunner, or magrider driver, depending on the circumstances. Sometimes a Max unit, but to be honest I personally get quickly bored of playing as a Max often times, in spite of all this talk of them being gamebreaking.
Infiltrator gameplay can be a nice, playstyle, in spite of all the stereotypes of the "Rambo-Wannabe-Infiltrator", you can just leave motion detectors near where your faction is mostly taking cover in, and then go off, and focus more on battling the enemy yourself, or taking advantage of the enemies distractions. Sometimes wraith flash infiltrator with the right weapons can be quite fun as well.
Or though I hardly ever play it, there's the option of Heavy Assault for direct combat, or engineer for vehicles/repairs/ammo support, or COMBAT medic who has the most versatile weapon in the game.  There's also four different continents you can go to.
The bad: It requires a very good computer, and consumes a huge amount of resources, and it can be difficult, or impossible for some to get a consistently decent FPS. The factions mechanics, even their looks to some degree, could use some more diversity.
I think Vanu players should be able to purchase cosmetics that would either replace bodyparts with cyborg parts, or visibly turn them into genetic mutants... I mean, well they ARE supposed to be the transhumanist faction! Likewise, I think TR players should have the options of wearing cosmetic armor belts, and cosmetic guns built around their character, since they are all about using so many bullets. Lastly, NC should have the cosmetic option for lets just say "Mining fashion", as they do use repurposed mining gear as armor.
I think it would be a small but significant faction difference immersion booster, if the TR had a high tech judges gavel melee weapon, the NC had a very high tech mining pick weapon, and the VS had a laser claw melee weapon. I doubt these will ever be added but I think they'd be great add-ons.
Also too much about the VS seems to be... Being in between the TR, and NC, as in, firing faster than one faction, slower than the other, and hitting hard than one faction but not as hard as the other faction... And not having their own defining trait. Also the flash handles very badly, and driving up hills in it can if you ask me, be much more harder than it should've been. Updates, and new features being implimented can take an extremely long time as well. Key examples being the stalker cloak, that fast burst jetpack for the light assault.
Also the infiltrator was supposed to be given a recon drone but that whole idea seems to have been cancelled or something.
Some other downsides, that you may consider subjective... Well downsides to me anyways are the following. Now, I know Planetside was BUILT around friendly fire, so removing it would destroy it's balance, so I realize SOE shouldn't remove it for that reason... Although personally, friendly fire is something I dislike, but that's just me, and it's something I can cope with in Planetside.
Often times when you're going around capping bases, you're either getting steamrolled so hard, your platoon leader asks you to redeploy a minute in advance, or you're steamrolling so hard the enemy platoons just stay inside of their spawn or re-deploy and you can be sitting around for minutes waiting to cap multiple bases in a row with almost no fighting going on, and not even needing to watch your back very much... To me this can get quite boring, and is an unfortunate consequence of the games mechanics.
Also glowing landmines are a bit silly... Though to be fair, they did often fall through the ground a lot in the past making them a bit hard to see. Another big one, like a lot of players, I feel like the way a lot of bases were designed made vehicle players not able to contribute as much to their faction, and that's something I didn't like.
Here's the biggest downside of them all if you ask me: One world or two words combined... Redeployside. Earlier in the game it wasn't as much this way from what I could tell. But due to certain changes, a lot of platoons are redeploying every few minutes, okay maybe an exagguration but not far from that.
Some people like this or don't mind it, on the other hand it actually bothers me, and some other people a lot. Because we feel like it makes vehicles less important. There's fewer vehicle convoys than there used to be from what I can tell, and modern Planetside 2 platoons are much more heavily redeploy-a-holic-infantry oriented, than the platoons of the days before that became so prevalent.
To me it takes away the immersion, and is unfair to vehicle oriented players as well. Keep in mind you're talking about someone who generally heavily dislikes Click-This-Map-To-Travel mechanics. In some ways I'm very much an immersion player, and I dislike map-click-travel systems for that reason.
Conclusion: yes if you ask me, Planetside 2 is a good game... Especially for one that is free to play. Although sometimes, when I don't have much time to play, or I'm seeing almost no combat for a really long time (often times due to platoons redeploying so much,  I end up playing TF2 instead). Yes I recommend this game... Hopefully your computer can run it okay.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a great "rebooting" of the series.  While technically not a total reboot, the developers have talked about how they are trying to take the legendary series in a different direction.  And to be honest I think it is for the better.
Instead of having zombies and "magic" they have replaced that with more of a futuristic Sci-fi feel, but not with aliens.  Machine games makes use of an underground Jewish thinktank to produce these crazy technologies.  While probably just as likely as alien visitations being the reason for the Nazi technological advances it feels more realistic somehow.  Machinegames also really went out of the way to remind us about how terrible the Nazi's were.  Even including some pretty hardcore scenes and references that even someone with a basic WII history knowlege will recognize.  The actual story though is pretty bland.  While I feel like they did a good job building up BJ Blazkowicz(the character you play), through flashbacks and his mid level muttering.  They basically left out developing all of the other characters around you.  And the actual story was basically a terrible action movie.  In fact just think Bourne Identity and you will probably be pretty close.  That all said though most players are not going to be playing this game for the story, but instead for the gameplay.
Wolfenstein is a welcomed return to a simple shooter.  By that I mean it was a great single player shooter experience with really just the basic extras we have come to exepct and nothing else.  It seems like recently all I have played is a bunch of open world, RPG elemented infused, huge perk tree, squad based shooters, or some combination of that.  And while those games are all good and there are reasons that adding those elements to the FPS and even 3rd person shooter games, sometimes I just want a return to a game that resembles those old classics.  And that is what Wolfenstein really does well.  It was almost a welcome relief.  Now the game does have a perk system, but instead of giving you points to level up it just gives you perks based on your preformance in the game.  There is only one real choice in the game and to be honest it doesn't have that big of an impact on the experience.  There a little more than a half dozen guns and almost all can be dual wielded as well as having alternate firing modes.  The actual shooting, gore, and graphics were up to par.  In fact because my computer could handle it, Wolfenstein on the PC actually is a really good looking game with great effects on the highest settings.  Although playing on the PC it sometimes had some pretty noticable screen tearing and such, however that could be due to my specific setup.
Ultimately what really sets the game apart is it's ability to be both a stealth shooter and a rampage style shooter.  The player can play as either and I didn't really feel like there was a penelty for playing as both throughout the game.  Sure I didn't unlock the top perks but I got to play the levels how I wanted to.  This execution is really rare and I want to commend Machingames for executing this.
Well if you have read this far I congradulate you.  Basically in the end Wolfenstein is a damn good shooter.  But the bar has been raised so high for games that only are single player shooters that I can't really say this game is worth 60 bucks.  This is mainly because of it's lack of narrative, character development, and immersion.  Maybe 5-8 years ago this would have been a no doubt about it recommendation.  But today this is almost a pass because of titles like Bioshock, HL2, and others.  I would say that if you are an older FPS player like me and you are sick of these modern shooters you will totally enjoy this game.  If not maybe just pick it up on steam sale.

Let me get this out of the way first: DO NOT PLAY THIS FOR THE STORY! The lore, world, and characters are interesting, but the plot and dialog will make you cringe at times.
But we didn't come here for the story, did we? How does it play? It's a fascinating game to look at from a design perspective. the game give you  alot of choice as to how you want to play. It has three main gameplay styles: stealth, COD-tactical-shoot-from-cover-down-sights, and a more traditional run-and-gun hold down the fire button until the enemy is dead. Even the "perk" tree exemplifies this (don't worry, the tree functions more like achievements, and they stay active throughout the game). 3 of the 4 trees give perks tailor to each play style. But one playstyle doesn't fit every situation. You'll find yourself switching between styles on the fly, mainly because of the level and enemy design. Some levels are COD-like, with an open area with a bunch of waist high cover, while other areas are Halo-like, where several hallways lead into and out of each other, and occasionally levels have cyrsis-like arenas. The game really gives the player a lot of options. Take a look at the guns for instance: by the end of the game you have about 5 distinct weapons. But most of the weapons can be dual wielded and have different fire modes. That means you have a total of 15 different ways to take down an opponent. Here's an example of what I'm talking about. One part of a level was beating me pretty badly. It was basically a fight up a hill with a lot of waist-high cover (I mainly did badly because I didn't take advantage of the dynamic cover system). Even in this COD type scenario I have options. Snipe the guy blowing up my cover? Take potshots with my assault rifle? Agh! An enemy is right on top of me! Quick: dual wield and gun him down. Eventually I closed the distance and fired my shotgun on full auto at everyone, but the entire time I was thinking: "there has to be another way to do this." This brings me to my next topic: secrets. turns out I was right.
I replayed the level hunting for secrets and I found a path that had me attacking the hill from ABOVE! This game has secrets everywhere of every kind. It has useless collectibles, to collectibles that unlock game modes, to health/armor buffs, to weapon upgrades, to weapons you would get later in the game, to ammo caches, to flanking routes. Sometimes the secrets area just hidden in a crate, others times they're in areas of the level you didn't even know you could get too. The game often shows you a secret, but doesn't tell you how to get it. Sometimes the collectibles are labeled on the map, but the map only tells you the general location. Weapon upgrades, and caches are not labeled, so the level design give you "hints" by putting items on ledges and behind glass. It's a single player game that encourages replay.
Is it worth it? I'd prefer a 50$ price, but it's definitely worth it. If you're a fan of first person shooter you need to play this game at some point. If a friend has it play it at their house! (But don't pirate). Wolfenstein doesn't do anything amazingly new, but it combines old school and new school mechanics in a fascinating way. The game puts things into a...New Order.

You see, everybody hates this game because of the recent "Epic Loot" update. The removal of balance and the Tech Tree. The way you now don't earn the currency after each game, and [/i apparently] you get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t in every protonium crate. At first I thought it was really crappy, and almost quit the game, but I remembered how much time I had spent in the game and how much fun I had, so I didn't quit. It was hard starting off- getting pwned by LOML's, but soon I realized how hard Freejam worked on the game and that we should all be appreciative of the fact that this game is free to play.
I personally love this game. I'm addicted to it. I love how every single roobot, depending on what you place where, and the weight of all the objects impacts the physics of your robot. I love building robots and the idea to let people upload robots they create with the CRF. I'm sure the *cough cough* seven, I think, people at Freejam love this game and are motivated to keep working on it, but are depressed by all these negative reviews. All of you players out there just don't know how good the coding and physics and connection and cloud saving and everything good about this game, you're only inferring the negative. This game can unleash your true imagination- and even use it in battle with players who have done the same thing! (Still, if you have a weak imagination and know how to make a hovering platform with guns, don't feel bad! That's what the CRF is there for.)
Every game has its cons, though, and here are my thoughts on the few downsides of this game.
1. Balance
The game's matchmaking seriously needs new balance. People are making tiny helis with a single LOML, so the can be in the low level group, and have a top-tier weapon. Some new ways of balance would be:
Limits to using Legendary Weapons with a low CPU robot (perhaps you could start using them at 1000 CPU)
Bringing the Tech Tree back
Maybe even completely replacing the matchmaking system with something more balanced
2. Rage Induction
I will admit, it's pretty rage inducing when your flyer loses a single wing and you no longer can fly, you just go around in circles until you hit the ground. However, there is a solution for everything.
Making a new module similar to the Power Booster that combines all your robot's health into one ( so you can't lose a wing and go down, it splits the damage on your wing among all other robot parts)
Or perhaps you could do the above for all robots, without having to create a module.
This isn't a big problem, but it would be nice if one of the above were done.
3. Premium access
This is a problem for nearly everyone and it's one of the main reasons that people hate Freejam and think they want our money. But it is true, premium costs too much. Seriously, like $1.19 PER DAY?! What is that?! That costs more than World of Warcraft subscription!
This is my only major problem with the game. There are solutions, though, if Freejam isn't in a financial crisis.
Reducing the price of Premium Edition
Giving out Free Premium Codes more often (I like how you give them out in the first place, but it's only once in a blue moon.)
Increasing the given time of Free Premium codes (Perhaps to 3-7 days)
If Freejam fixes these minor problems, the game could be much better, most people would stop sending negative reviews and more people would play again. Thank you for reading, I apologize if the post was too long.

tl;dr 8/10; this is as good as the original, but DLC is really what makes it, though it's a bit overpriced, so get it on sale.
A classic RTS resurrected, this is a good buy. I say good in order to avoid "excellent", because to be honest with the standard the game is as the title says: an HD version of AoE2.
Because of that, it's got the same features as the original game just in HD. The HD is good, but is best seen on things like water and fire. Units are all the same, no changes here. Pluses though are the inclusion of the Workshop and hosting the servers on Steam, as I know it's hard to find matches for the original version. The inclusion of achievments as well is a plus for those into that thing, as well as trading cards.
The Forgotten is really where this version shines though. The inclusion of new campaigns and civilizations are great, as well as the new techs in the Castle Age. They went a bit wild with the renaming of units and making some new ones (like a seemingly pointless AoE1 Broad Swordsman and "Nordic" and "Eastern" Swordsmen), but I digress. Campaigns have no narmy VAs sadly but are fun nonetheless with okay storyelling.
The Encylcopedia was expanded for The Forgotten civs. Sadly this meant that the standard HD edition's encyclopedia is messed up. You can interchange between both the Forgotten and HD edition instantly though.
However a problem occurs with how faction changes and patches don't carry over between the two, though this only really affects Campaigns (if you have Forgotten you can just play the same civs in MP with the changes). So low pop limits, old tech trees, and stuff still occur in the original campaigns.
Another problem I have is the price tag of $29.99. It's a bit too much for a re-release in my opinion, since you can pick up the original version (including Conquerors) for at most $10 somewhere else. The Forgotten DLC is $14.99 as well so my suggestion is just get both on sale if you're going to get it at all.
The game's great as the original though and the Forgotten is fun. I still recommend this game to anyone who wants to play this great game once more. I know I play it regularly, and I have more reason to with this on Steam.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a great "rebooting" of the series.  While technically not a total reboot, the developers have talked about how they are trying to take the legendary series in a different direction.  And to be honest I think it is for the better.
Instead of having zombies and "magic" they have replaced that with more of a futuristic Sci-fi feel, but not with aliens.  Machine games makes use of an underground Jewish thinktank to produce these crazy technologies.  While probably just as likely as alien visitations being the reason for the Nazi technological advances it feels more realistic somehow.  Machinegames also really went out of the way to remind us about how terrible the Nazi's were.  Even including some pretty hardcore scenes and references that even someone with a basic WII history knowlege will recognize.  The actual story though is pretty bland.  While I feel like they did a good job building up BJ Blazkowicz(the character you play), through flashbacks and his mid level muttering.  They basically left out developing all of the other characters around you.  And the actual story was basically a terrible action movie.  In fact just think Bourne Identity and you will probably be pretty close.  That all said though most players are not going to be playing this game for the story, but instead for the gameplay.
Wolfenstein is a welcomed return to a simple shooter.  By that I mean it was a great single player shooter experience with really just the basic extras we have come to exepct and nothing else.  It seems like recently all I have played is a bunch of open world, RPG elemented infused, huge perk tree, squad based shooters, or some combination of that.  And while those games are all good and there are reasons that adding those elements to the FPS and even 3rd person shooter games, sometimes I just want a return to a game that resembles those old classics.  And that is what Wolfenstein really does well.  It was almost a welcome relief.  Now the game does have a perk system, but instead of giving you points to level up it just gives you perks based on your preformance in the game.  There is only one real choice in the game and to be honest it doesn't have that big of an impact on the experience.  There a little more than a half dozen guns and almost all can be dual wielded as well as having alternate firing modes.  The actual shooting, gore, and graphics were up to par.  In fact because my computer could handle it, Wolfenstein on the PC actually is a really good looking game with great effects on the highest settings.  Although playing on the PC it sometimes had some pretty noticable screen tearing and such, however that could be due to my specific setup.
Ultimately what really sets the game apart is it's ability to be both a stealth shooter and a rampage style shooter.  The player can play as either and I didn't really feel like there was a penelty for playing as both throughout the game.  Sure I didn't unlock the top perks but I got to play the levels how I wanted to.  This execution is really rare and I want to commend Machingames for executing this.
Well if you have read this far I congradulate you.  Basically in the end Wolfenstein is a damn good shooter.  But the bar has been raised so high for games that only are single player shooters that I can't really say this game is worth 60 bucks.  This is mainly because of it's lack of narrative, character development, and immersion.  Maybe 5-8 years ago this would have been a no doubt about it recommendation.  But today this is almost a pass because of titles like Bioshock, HL2, and others.  I would say that if you are an older FPS player like me and you are sick of these modern shooters you will totally enjoy this game.  If not maybe just pick it up on steam sale.

The most incredible gaming experience I have had since Planetside 1 !!!!!!
Hi folks,
When the first Planetside game came out in the early 2000s, I was intrigued, not because I am a big fan of FPS type games, but that it was a MMO FPS.
Moreover, the only FPS I played and enjoyed previously was Unreal Tournament, and the idea of a "persistant world" with a purpose above and beyond the standard small map games of UT and other FPS games.
The BOMBSHELL!
Picture this....the "first time" I ever played the first Planetside game, I was in awe of the Galaxy Drop Ships and how they each carried almost a dozen players; but moreover, imagine the sight of seeing 12 or more of these ships taking off fully loaded...
Then, everyone dropping out of all these ships and more at around the same time filling the sky above the targeted fortress with hundreds of players.
As I landed....NOTHING.....and I mean NOTHING could have prepared me for what I experienced...
There had to be hundreds if not a thousand players beseiging a fort defended in both land and sky by similar numbers of opposing players.
When I landed, i was fortunate to be near a boulder, for the air was alive and buzzing with thousands...maybe tens of thousands of tracers bullets, lasers and other types of projectiles.
The fire was so thick, it was impossible to move out, as trying to do so instantly got you killed.
As this inferno of tracers overwhelmed my senses, try to imagine the "sound" of this mayhem!
It was "pew pew" madness as the sounds of this immense battle rang in my ears.
For an hour, this went on, and the sky was filled with dog fighting ships and reinforcing drop ships, and the constant scene of some of these ships crashing into the area....it was spectacular!
When we finally assaulted the fort, I honestly believe half of us were cut down, and the battle for the interior of the fort raged another hour and then I was killed.
I did not go back to this battle....as I was exhausted and still could not believe the epicness of it it all.
Now although, that battle was never matched in its intensity and granduer during my play time in the first Planetside, I am sure there were other battles just as good and if not better, that I had missed. For at the time, i was involved in so many games, I used to switch around alot.
FAST FORWARD!
This past weekend I finally decided to play the new version of this game, Planetside 2...its free, unless you buy a bunch of cosmetic stuff or bundles that include some unlocked equipment, which frankly I feel is a waste of money, but thats me.
Anyway, imagine my joy when the very first time I hopped on a Galaxy Drop Ship: which now sport all kinds of custom paint jobs, I dropped into a huge battle that was just as good as the one I previously mentioned, but even better.
The sound...omg the sound...so many players were battling it out that the sounds of battle was literally a deafening ROAR!
And the intensity was easily 4x more intense the original game I had experienced.
Even when the number of players in a battle was less thatn what I had previously experienced, it still seemed more intense.
IN CONCLUSION, I have played the last two "Battlefield" games, and as good as they are, I feel Planetside 2 is BETTER....and is practically free, so give it a try!
I played almost all day Sunday, neglecting all other things in life and came away so satisfied, it might just be time for me to buy some custom paint jobs etc.
If there is one thing I dont likw with Planetside 2, is the fact that the conflict areas seem to fill up quicker than the first game. Moreover, because this game is free as opposed to the first game which is sub based; you will get stuck in a waiting queue because the zone is full, and then get sales pitched to buy a membership (subscription) to avoid the que.
Now before you get angry like I did at first, please remember this game although free, is not provided as a "public service"...NO, it was made like most games to make a company money.
And there is nothing wrong with that at all.
Thus, having to pay for "something" to get something in return is totally logical and fine.
In fact to be honest with you, the queue was only 2 minutes...so no big deal.
However, I am concerned what these ques will be on a Friday or Saturday night.
Despite that, if there was ever a game to shell out a subscription for, it would be this one, as you definately get your moneys worth.
And even better, should you not want to pay a dime, this game still offfers more than any other free game.
Give it a try! Moreover, join a Guild/Outfit!

Let me get this out of the way first: DO NOT PLAY THIS FOR THE STORY! The lore, world, and characters are interesting, but the plot and dialog will make you cringe at times.
But we didn't come here for the story, did we? How does it play? It's a fascinating game to look at from a design perspective. the game give you  alot of choice as to how you want to play. It has three main gameplay styles: stealth, COD-tactical-shoot-from-cover-down-sights, and a more traditional run-and-gun hold down the fire button until the enemy is dead. Even the "perk" tree exemplifies this (don't worry, the tree functions more like achievements, and they stay active throughout the game). 3 of the 4 trees give perks tailor to each play style. But one playstyle doesn't fit every situation. You'll find yourself switching between styles on the fly, mainly because of the level and enemy design. Some levels are COD-like, with an open area with a bunch of waist high cover, while other areas are Halo-like, where several hallways lead into and out of each other, and occasionally levels have cyrsis-like arenas. The game really gives the player a lot of options. Take a look at the guns for instance: by the end of the game you have about 5 distinct weapons. But most of the weapons can be dual wielded and have different fire modes. That means you have a total of 15 different ways to take down an opponent. Here's an example of what I'm talking about. One part of a level was beating me pretty badly. It was basically a fight up a hill with a lot of waist-high cover (I mainly did badly because I didn't take advantage of the dynamic cover system). Even in this COD type scenario I have options. Snipe the guy blowing up my cover? Take potshots with my assault rifle? Agh! An enemy is right on top of me! Quick: dual wield and gun him down. Eventually I closed the distance and fired my shotgun on full auto at everyone, but the entire time I was thinking: "there has to be another way to do this." This brings me to my next topic: secrets. turns out I was right.
I replayed the level hunting for secrets and I found a path that had me attacking the hill from ABOVE! This game has secrets everywhere of every kind. It has useless collectibles, to collectibles that unlock game modes, to health/armor buffs, to weapon upgrades, to weapons you would get later in the game, to ammo caches, to flanking routes. Sometimes the secrets area just hidden in a crate, others times they're in areas of the level you didn't even know you could get too. The game often shows you a secret, but doesn't tell you how to get it. Sometimes the collectibles are labeled on the map, but the map only tells you the general location. Weapon upgrades, and caches are not labeled, so the level design give you "hints" by putting items on ledges and behind glass. It's a single player game that encourages replay.
Is it worth it? I'd prefer a 50$ price, but it's definitely worth it. If you're a fan of first person shooter you need to play this game at some point. If a friend has it play it at their house! (But don't pirate). Wolfenstein doesn't do anything amazingly new, but it combines old school and new school mechanics in a fascinating way. The game puts things into a...New Order.

Let me just by saying what a game.  For me this goes beyond what i expected.  No only have i only completed one timeline and there are 2, and there is secret stuff, took me about 16 hours.
make no mistake this is an adult game, There is gore and its nice, it never goes over the top imo, and it fits because you feel absolutely no remorse for what these nazis have done.
This game was just amazing, the gameplay is awesome and meaty, the guns feel and sound amazing, this is the most fun ive had in all the wolfenstein games and in an fps in a long time.
This game has some really interesting and likeable characters, you get to know quite abit about, some more than others.
The story is really interesting as well, it really caught me in, makes you hate the living guts of these nazis. You will just want to see them and their empire taken down.
Its a really fun and engaging rollercoaster, You never spend to much time in one place, i could easily have settled for more time in the various places you get to visit. but lets just say you get around. You arent just running around castles. Its quite the journey.
Megatextures this time around looks a lot better. Its still not Crysis 3 texture quality, but its way WAY beyond rage, i didn find myself ever stopping up like i did in Rage to look at a horrible low res texture that caught my eye.
If you like Wolfenstein and played the Original Wolfenstein 3d, i would recommend this even more, this isnt just your average shooter. You really get to learn and know what motivates B.J who he is and what he stands for. And i gotta say, he is the type of person i imagined all the way back when playing the original in my childhood.
The game does have some regenable health, but its the best mix between oldschool and newschool that ive tried. You regen up to 20 health never more, you max is 100, but you can overcharge it, yes thats right you can go far up 150-200+ health, it degrades showly over time, that means you dont just spam and pick up everything, you let it be until you need it, depending on your playstyle, more on that a bit later. There is armor as well, that goes up to 100. which is really nice, you can find armor in the levels or take it off dead opponents.
There is secrets as well, which you can find completely on your own, or get a bit of help as where aprox they are in you silently kill the officers. which makes you want to explore around. There is lots to find, enigma codes, treasure, letters, armor upgrades, weapon upgrades and so forth.
Then there is the play styles, you can play this game with quite a bit of choice,  But in the higher difficulties you will need to use a bit of everything, else they will kill you. Lets jus say you will learn to not engage shotgun guys in close range really fast.
You can go around and stealth kill, go full head on, or you cover and yes its real cover, no snap to cover 3rd person crap, its move up to something and you can actually lean around corners, i dont think ive seen this since the FEAR games. but finally proper lean is back. Then there is the perks, which ever playstyle you choice or jack of all trades, you will unlock perks, from carrying more ammo, to reloading faster to doing more dmg. Its kinda fun.
Over all i find this game does a very good job and combining oldschool and newschool. into something i enjoyed. no QTE evens SPAM E to open door. or some crap. which is nice.

Ah, Good Old age of empires. I played the original version of this game for many hours when I was younger. I'll try to be as unbiased as possible in this review.
First, a word to any veterans that may be considering the HD version: KEYBINDS. If you had all the old ones memorised, you are going to have to rebind them. They don't use the original keybindings in this version.
Now, for those that have not played before...
A brief overview of what is possible.
-Random matches are basically an "anything goes" type of round. There are multiple ways to win, Not just by combat.
-Deathmatches start you with high resources and are a battle to the death.
-Regicide (a personal favorite) is a game variant in which you must protect your king while hunting down the enemy kings.
-Wonder race is quite simply, the first person who is able to build a wonder. If you were "wondering" what a wonder is, that basically is a monument made by your race. It can also be used to win a random match, however you must defend it for a length of time for it to work in that game mode.
-King of the hill (I believe is what it is called) is a variant in which you must protect a neutral wonder in the middle of the map for x amount of time.
-Capture the relic is a single relic on the map which must be captured to win. Both king of the hill and capture the relic can be VERY fast paced matches depending on your opponent.
Now, something for both vets and newbies alike:
-Treaties! - if you struggle fighting "rush" tactics in rts games, the DLC for this allows for you to set a time limit in which everyone is friendly. This prevents people from rushing you and gives newer players a chance to see how others play.
-Increased population limits! The old version had a limit of 200. The max now is 500 and there are even some forge mods that allow you to go even higher (although I wouldn't recommend it for your own sanity)
Now, I thought this was going to be great... I was wrong...
-New map size!... I thought this was going to be AWESOME at first. I was horribly dissapointed when I saw the tremendous amount of lagg this causes during multiplayer rounds. Stick to giant and you are fine. LUDAKRIS is 4 times larger than giant, and for some reason it laggs like a MOFO. It gets even worse if you add an AI to the map.
Now, My final verdict..
Overall gameplay - 8 / 10. The reason I don't give it a 10 is due to the fact that I'm not that big on the campaign. I could live, eat, sleep, and breath the multiplayer but I find the campaign boring at best.
Community - 7 / 10. For the most part you run across fairly nice people. Of course, every game has a few rotten apples playing it.
Diversity 9 / 10. Unlike some games where you see "cookie cutter" builds and races, Pretty much anything is viable on here. There are a few things that could use some rebalancing but, if you have a brain you can still counter most of them.
AI (Computer Players) 10 / 10. You want a challenge? put those suckers on max difficulty. You'll be running home to your grandmother crying by the feudal age.
Nostalgia 11 / 10. Nuff Said.

This game encompasses old and new, a throw back to the health and armor system that seems to have been lost on most shooters these days. The gunplay is absolutely fantastic, it feels smooth and fresh like it did in RAGE but better in my opinion, I haven't felt this satisfied with a shooter since Half-Life 2: Episode 2. The sounds and music transitions with the cut scenes are absolutely beautiful and the voice acting is really well done.
With hints of Tarantino style story telling, the game pulls you through both sides of the spectrum when it comes to feelings and responses, like a rollercoaster of rage and punishment. I can safely say this is the first time a game has really put me through a process of "Oh god that is awful, why am I looking at this" to "I really want to rip that persons head off" It's a game that, to many, doesn't seem to take itself seriously, but it does - in its own special way. It's a hard thing to go into an alternate path of history and for it to be taken seriously. While Wolfenstein The New Order may miss it at some points, it nails it to a cross on a frequent basis. While I was playing I constantly was thinking about the story and how it seemed to be an analogy of insanity & rage. The level of absurdity you go through was extremely satisfying, you get the feeling that its completely ok to go over the top to wipe a Nazi out, that you could not accept that they became such a power and you would do everything to wipe them out with no remorse.
I'm currently going through the second playthrough at the moment. There is a point early on in the game where you make a choice and it ends up giving you a specific experience with characters because of that choice. You have altnerate methods of accessing locked areas, and new secret areas that you will come across, as well as acquiring weapons at earlier points in the game, all depending on the choice you make early on. It's an interesting twist to the game, and definitely can make a second playthrough worth it to some extent - may update when im finished with the second playthrough.
Overall Wolfenstein The New Order didn't play the usual harp strings of emotion, it took its own path - while this path may not fit for some, I have a feeling many will really get a kick out of it, and find it extremely satisfying. I wish there was more to play, I really hope MachineGames continues to dig into the Wolf universe, this is the first Wolfenstein single player experience that I REALLY loved, even over RTCW (with the exception of its multiplayer ;p)
also MachineGames, if you're listening - get on the phone with Splash Damage and work with them on making Enemy Territory in this universe ;)

What I expected from this HD-Remake was to improve the visuals of the game, make it available for online play again, cutting out bugs and redoing some parts of the HUD. But all this game does, is offer you the option of playing it with a higher resolution (something that in my opinion could have been done way more efficiently by releasing a patch for the original). Okay, so, i really did like this game, and ill be honest, there are still some aspects i like, for example:
The Fighting mechanics are still decent, you know, shoot at someone they take damage and part of there bot is blown off, leaving them disabled, whereas in some games, you get shot at and you still have full capabilities.
Now, to the not so good, and better said, the awful UPDATES to this game.  So, the devs adding guns are blocks and stuff is good, but it is the core fetures they change that is bad.  A little ways back we had a buy/sell system using rp, or robopoints.  You would get RP at the end of the battle depending on how you did.  But recently, things have changed.  We now have the system of, depending on your placement in the game, you get a loot crate.  In the loot crate you can get items.  The thing is, you get a small amount of items and NO money.  In order to progress or get things you actually want you have to sell what you get and selling is NOT rewarding.  You sell things at up to a 90% decrease in price, so you gain little profit, and chances are you will not get decent gear in the chest.  This means it is EXTREMELY difficult to progress. They also removed a feature that, in the beginning, would place you in matches with people of about the same teir as you.  This is done through using a given amount of points that your bot had from the things you put on it.  This was from t1 to t10.  Later on, they changed it to just have it be that you would be placed with people that are around your same point average.  Now, however, you are placed with bots that have the same CPU as you.  CPU is basicly how many blocks you have.  Each item has a differant CPU.  But this means that someone who only placed 1000 normal blocks, no guns or anything, can get into matches where pthers have actually put time into there bot only to lose from trolls.

This game is retro breeze from the past but in a positive meaning. Take this game as an equivalent to
movies. If
showed up 15 years ago, everyone would be annoyed and bored in a way like "jeez, not these crusty clowns again, please!". But nowadays, when everything must be shot with shaken camera, every plot has to have at least 3 twists and main antagonist is pictured as internaly disrupted guy who deserves our sympathies, it has just hit the audience with the force of 10 has-been bad-asses. And so did the Wolfenstein.
This game is pure linear corridor one with a couple of tiny options to finish the task - there are always 2 or 3 ways at the maximum how to reach the checkpoint, and so it is with the playstyle: you can be Sam Fisher, the Terminator, or both. Nothing more, nothing less. But it is great and entertaining.
The plot is suprisingly very dark and serious. I don't know why I expected the plot will be ironic, over-the-top humorous story about stupid and impotent Nazis against Duke Nukem style bad♥♥♥♥♥ I assume it could be because of
movie from which Wolfenstein borrowed some ideas for sure. Speaking of which, this game is full of pop-cultural references to movies like
,
etc. for example, but anyway, the plot is neat, the atmosphere is brilliant and the ending is satisfying. And did I mention that B.J. is a fricking bad♥♥♥♥♥
Now the negatives.
Unfortunately, this game is not polished. It suffers from time-to-time crashes, microstuttering is almost everywhere (especially in interiors) and AI is poor and sometimes suffers from bad pathfinding. There is also weird checkpoint system - sometimes, when you die, you are spawned behind the spot you died so you do not have to face those enemies who killed you before.
Crashes and microstuttering will be fixed in time for sure with patches and new gpu drivers, but I am quite sure AI and checkpoint system will stay as it is now, which is sad.
But hell, this game kicks♥♥♥♥♥anyway! I am looking forward for the sequel.

Fundamentally Wolfenstein is all about having fun gibbing Nazis; any of the constraints placed upon the character are those which are necessary to make a game challenging. Not out of a misplaced emphasis on 'realism'. Wolfenstein is very self aware. It succeeds in maintaining an ironic disposition to its plot which lends itself to the whimsy that is inherent to Super Soldier gunning down a Nazi Goliath with a giant laser gun. In this way it blows Battlefield and Call of Duty out of the water. That being said it also succeeds, for the most part, in juxtaposing its ridiculousness with a competent emotional subplot.
TLDR: Self-aware game that knows its players just want to gibe Nazis with lazers. Its decent emotional subplot is the cherry on top, rounding off a great game without stealing the show.

Like many of you (probably), I grew up playing things like Wolf 3D, Doom, Duke 3D, Rise of the Triad, Blake Stone, Hexen, Heretic. That's out of order and I think I did manage to avoid Quake somehow, but whatever. I was something like 4? I did this until I was around 8-10 and my parents got me a N64 instead of a computer so I got into Mario, Zelda, the usuals. so I've been out of the FPS loop for awhile. Just starting in 2012 or so did I really start diving into the Bioshocks, Metros, Singularity, I even gave Wolf 09 a spin. I enjoyed most all of them except Singularity, haha. Unfortunately, never a Starbreeze game. So even though I was hopeful for this title I didn't really know what I was getting into with that pedigree thrown around since it doesn't mean much to me. But I was hopeful regardless, and it looks like my blind faith paid off pretty well.
It's really fun to kill Nazis. Not really a better way to put it. Watching them fall apart as you overwhelm them, using all the different weaponry, scoping from cover or guns blazing, or clearing out a whole floor with a silenced approach was pretty great. Even though it was highly useful for my Uber playthrough, I wish the thrown knifes and silenced pistol weren't so broken. I ended up avoiding using the pistol in the later half of the game because it was so boring. The knives were similar but a notch harder to acquire and aim so I used that whenever I felt like it. I love how the perks reward you for playing the game in multiple ways, instead of just being acquired skill poiints into a tree or something. It was a little distracting and silly when I found myself failing a checkpoint so that I could work on different perks, but that's on me I suppose. One of my favorites was the one that healed you for doing the melee takedowns. Something satisfying about gunning down a nazi and not wanting to wait for the reload animation so I would just run up to him, slit his throat. and get some health back. Once I learned how powerful the scoped LKW was, that was also and enjoyable tool in the arsenal.
The game starts with some really open map design which gives you a lot of freedom to do those things I mention. However, somewhere around chapter 10-11 it ends up becoming a bit more straightforward, where the game seems to send you from "arena" to arena. This is still really fun, and a lot of the encounters have enough paths and levels that it doesn't feel constricting. It was just not as good as the first handful of chapters in this respect. However, I do think that the later locations are much more interesting in general. Chapter 12, for instance, was my least favorite and really soured me with how it was organized. However, it was also a pleasure to just look at and move around in.
I think the game has some really great smoke/dust effects, is it just me?
I'm not as high on the narrative. While the game doesn't feel as disjointed as some other titles, I have to remind myself about how things connected from one chapter to another. At one point you get on a train and end up in a uboat and it just felt a bit abrupt. BJ seems to survive a ton of♥♥♥♥♥♥that doesn't really make a lot of sense, but maybe it's just some sort of protagonist invincibility. A lot of the characters just don't play as much of a role in order for them to be memorable to me. I played on the Wyatt timeline (that's not really a spoiler right) and having to play alongside him early on cemented his relevance so to speak. Some of the other characters were just not important until chapter 15. While I'm saying all this though, it's not like I want more cutscenes (I think the extent of the narrative and frequency of cutscenes was fine.), so maybe I'm unsure about what I actually want here. I do think that the..cinematography, if that's the right word, was pretty good. It reminded me actually of RE5 in that way (not in quality, but in the "camerawork" and things like that.) I apologize if I sound a bit silly here. I'm not sure how to put it into words.
Not super high on the new BJ either. He was kind of unremarkable to me. I don't really get the "favorite protagonist" accolades that I've seen. He does have a pretty interesting design and voice and isn't as generic as he might initially appear. I guess I enjoy that he's subtle (when not sprint sliding dual shottgunning a nazi troop). We don't really hear him yell or scream much nor does he get too dramatic about anything. The inner musings were generally nice and well written, some very memorable lines. Broke your♥♥♥♥♥♥ Some of them felt like they were trying too hard to make him seem somewhat detached. Buoy . And I felt like the poetic use of the count to four line had worn itself thin by the end of the first chapter.
I can't wait to play on easy to just have the leash slackened so that I can just use whatever I want and cover the floors in gibs in the most stylish ways possible. I was disappointed in the number of push wall type secrets, but I reserve the right to backtrack on that statement due to the possibility that I simply just missed them. Most everything was just kind of lying about, Speaking of, there's something satisfying about just running into a room with Nazis firing on your♥♥♥♥♥ spamming the pickup button to re-up on health, armor, ammo, whatever, and then turning around and using whatever you just managed to scrap together. Much more rewarding than hiding behind cover until the red jelly goes away. At first I thought that the 20 health increments for the regen was too broad, but I suppose on Uber I ended up appreciating it a fair bit. Being able to pick up items by walking on them would be nice I suppose, but later on in the game it didn't really bother me that much.
That chapter 14 boss was a neat spectacle but I wish there was more to it. The chapter 16 boss was fitting and grounded. By that I mean it wasn't ridiculous and over the top, but still sufficiently momentous that it was a satisfying ending to the journey. It will be interesting to see to what extent the alternative timeline changes things up. It's a good excuse to go back on easy and collect stuff.
Edit: The home base stuff was forgettable, enough so that I needed to add it in to mention it. Fluff.

The features that set this above and apart all others are:
- Very fair pricing: With minimal play time, it\'s possible to get a 50,000 credit hero permanently unlocked in 1-2 weeks. If you play each game mode every day and win once, you get 2,000 credits everyday and you can get 1,500-3,000 if you complete the objectives that cycle every 3 hours. No change in power above bronze cards.
- High skill requirements: There\'s very little auto-aim (1 turret class) and a lot of hip-firing skill is required. Against snipers, small HP mercs move fast and there\'s ample flanking paths. Tank classes are usually balanced by slow movement or needing medics and fire support characters to feed them.
- Massive focus on teamplay: Success is highly dependent on your team having a medic, fire support, engineer, assault and recon. At high levels you\'re going to need serious co-ordination between your team.
- You can still carry: Despite the requirement for team-play, a good player is easily recognised in Dirty Bomb. You may not win but you\'ll make the other team pay hard. With enough skill, a medic could keep the entire team healed and push the opposition back.
- Varied heroes: All mercs are functionally distinct and highly balanced. Each merc has specific loadouts and skills that contribute to the game.
- Server browser: Wish other games had this.
Negatives are:
- Matchmaking: Sometimes you\'re going to up against stacked teams.
- Loadout system: You have a fixed loadout that others may not like as it forces them into a specific weapon / augment they may not like. Fortunately, bronzes are relatively cheap.
- RNG: You can select the hero that you want to get a loadout, but the cheapest path requires RNG. Special events also have a lot of RNG involved. However, you can buy a bronze loadout you want with in-game credits for 17,500 credits.
- Minor glitches: I\'ve had a little rubber banding here and there. High ping players seem to teleport around every now and then. Nothing major.
- Hackers: Relative to other F2P shooters, though, Dirty Bomb has a very low hacker problem. That said, it\'s not like there\'s no cheaters ever.
