Like many of you (probably), I grew up playing things like Wolf 3D, Doom, Duke 3D, Rise of the Triad, Blake Stone, Hexen, Heretic. That's out of order and I think I did manage to avoid Quake somehow, but whatever. I was something like 4? I did this until I was around 8-10 and my parents got me a N64 instead of a computer so I got into Mario, Zelda, the usuals. so I've been out of the FPS loop for awhile. Just starting in 2012 or so did I really start diving into the Bioshocks, Metros, Singularity, I even gave Wolf 09 a spin. I enjoyed most all of them except Singularity, haha. Unfortunately, never a Starbreeze game. So even though I was hopeful for this title I didn't really know what I was getting into with that pedigree thrown around since it doesn't mean much to me. But I was hopeful regardless, and it looks like my blind faith paid off pretty well.
It's really fun to kill Nazis. Not really a better way to put it. Watching them fall apart as you overwhelm them, using all the different weaponry, scoping from cover or guns blazing, or clearing out a whole floor with a silenced approach was pretty great. Even though it was highly useful for my Uber playthrough, I wish the thrown knifes and silenced pistol weren't so broken. I ended up avoiding using the pistol in the later half of the game because it was so boring. The knives were similar but a notch harder to acquire and aim so I used that whenever I felt like it. I love how the perks reward you for playing the game in multiple ways, instead of just being acquired skill poiints into a tree or something. It was a little distracting and silly when I found myself failing a checkpoint so that I could work on different perks, but that's on me I suppose. One of my favorites was the one that healed you for doing the melee takedowns. Something satisfying about gunning down a nazi and not wanting to wait for the reload animation so I would just run up to him, slit his throat. and get some health back. Once I learned how powerful the scoped LKW was, that was also and enjoyable tool in the arsenal.
The game starts with some really open map design which gives you a lot of freedom to do those things I mention. However, somewhere around chapter 10-11 it ends up becoming a bit more straightforward, where the game seems to send you from "arena" to arena. This is still really fun, and a lot of the encounters have enough paths and levels that it doesn't feel constricting. It was just not as good as the first handful of chapters in this respect. However, I do think that the later locations are much more interesting in general. Chapter 12, for instance, was my least favorite and really soured me with how it was organized. However, it was also a pleasure to just look at and move around in.
I think the game has some really great smoke/dust effects, is it just me?
I'm not as high on the narrative. While the game doesn't feel as disjointed as some other titles, I have to remind myself about how things connected from one chapter to another. At one point you get on a train and end up in a uboat and it just felt a bit abrupt. BJ seems to survive a ton of♥♥♥♥♥♥that doesn't really make a lot of sense, but maybe it's just some sort of protagonist invincibility. A lot of the characters just don't play as much of a role in order for them to be memorable to me. I played on the Wyatt timeline (that's not really a spoiler right) and having to play alongside him early on cemented his relevance so to speak. Some of the other characters were just not important until chapter 15. While I'm saying all this though, it's not like I want more cutscenes (I think the extent of the narrative and frequency of cutscenes was fine.), so maybe I'm unsure about what I actually want here. I do think that the..cinematography, if that's the right word, was pretty good. It reminded me actually of RE5 in that way (not in quality, but in the "camerawork" and things like that.) I apologize if I sound a bit silly here. I'm not sure how to put it into words.
Not super high on the new BJ either. He was kind of unremarkable to me. I don't really get the "favorite protagonist" accolades that I've seen. He does have a pretty interesting design and voice and isn't as generic as he might initially appear. I guess I enjoy that he's subtle (when not sprint sliding dual shottgunning a nazi troop). We don't really hear him yell or scream much nor does he get too dramatic about anything. The inner musings were generally nice and well written, some very memorable lines. Broke your♥♥♥♥♥♥ Some of them felt like they were trying too hard to make him seem somewhat detached. Buoy . And I felt like the poetic use of the count to four line had worn itself thin by the end of the first chapter.
I can't wait to play on easy to just have the leash slackened so that I can just use whatever I want and cover the floors in gibs in the most stylish ways possible. I was disappointed in the number of push wall type secrets, but I reserve the right to backtrack on that statement due to the possibility that I simply just missed them. Most everything was just kind of lying about, Speaking of, there's something satisfying about just running into a room with Nazis firing on your♥♥♥♥♥ spamming the pickup button to re-up on health, armor, ammo, whatever, and then turning around and using whatever you just managed to scrap together. Much more rewarding than hiding behind cover until the red jelly goes away. At first I thought that the 20 health increments for the regen was too broad, but I suppose on Uber I ended up appreciating it a fair bit. Being able to pick up items by walking on them would be nice I suppose, but later on in the game it didn't really bother me that much.
That chapter 14 boss was a neat spectacle but I wish there was more to it. The chapter 16 boss was fitting and grounded. By that I mean it wasn't ridiculous and over the top, but still sufficiently momentous that it was a satisfying ending to the journey. It will be interesting to see to what extent the alternative timeline changes things up. It's a good excuse to go back on easy and collect stuff.
Edit: The home base stuff was forgettable, enough so that I needed to add it in to mention it. Fluff.

Reviewers complaining about graphical issues have their settings all at max, I noticed that turning the frame "buffer" to 32 instead of 64 removed ALL of those issues with no loss to the great graphics, texture popping never happened to me at max settings. Its like a wonderful cross of Dishonored with a FPS, you can either be sneaky or lob grenades everywhere and there is a simple but fun "Perk" tree to work on (you unlock things as you kill xyz x times using y). A good old fashioned story (no risks to the writing) with solid characters. Besides, who doesn't want to punch a Nazi scumbag off a bridge, or vaporize them, or otherwise make silly ninnys out of them? This did a good job of making you really hate the villians. As far as realism goes, it is certainly a bit OTT in terms of what the Nazi's could have acheived, but gets the point across pretty well. Good length, fun story, good replay value, does not have multiplayer and doesn't need it (MP =/= art, go play CoD/BF).

Well I had a much longer review in mind, but halfway through I found out that Steam only allows so many characters. Thanks Steam!
So to sum up what was going to go into my review.
Pros:
Gunplay is fast and fun. If you have the weapons for it.
No regenerating health.
Secrets.
Levels are not liner hallways. Although in later levels they turn into them.
Weapons sound and feel good.
The setting is interesting and fun to explore.
You get to kill Nazis.
Cons:
Game takes guns and armor away at the end of every level rendering secrets pointless.
Game takes health away from you arbitrarily through cinematics.
Introduces characters but never builds them up, only to kill them off.
Uninteresting villain who only appears at the beginning and end of the game.
Lack of diversity in weapons.
Pointless stealth system.
Rock dumb AI.
Uninteresting story that fails to suck you in and get you invested.
Unnecessary focus on a Gimmick Weapon that serves no real practical use.
I really felt this game could have been good, and it has a solid game play base to work with. Unfortunately they messed up by putting too many restrictions on you, such as taking weapons away, damaging you in unavoidable cinematics ect. It feels like a game that doesn't trust the player. When you play a game like Serious Sam or DOOM it feels like the developers have a little bit of trust in you. They know you know where to go. They trust you to fight the boss with a certain weapon or that you will figure it out. With Wolfenstein you can play the game. But in the end you're going to play the game THEIR way. You're getting that new gun when THEY say you can. You leave the helicopter when THEY say so. You can only fight the boss with the weapons THEY want you to. It never feels like you have a choice in the matter and if you don't play their way,
Then game over.

This game is brilliant, there isn't too much I can pick a fault with, I have never experienced the problems that many users have reported.
The gameplay is solid, good chunky fun, and playing through the game at medium was no challenge, so if you're an experienced shooter player then make sure you play on "I am death, incarnate!" diffculty or "Uber" as any less will make you feel unchallenged. I epsecially love the duel wielding and the different upgrades for your arsenal that you can pick up along the way.
The collectables add replayability value to the game, (as if it needed extra) and will keep you searching for them guides online. The downtime between missions is great, and meeting the different people within the resistance is great, it adds a personal feeling to the game, and the easter egg in the resistance headquarters is brilliant!
The soundtrack is brilliant, and you can find collectable records in the game so you can listen to a 60's Nazi take on well known western music of the real world. In each level you play you will unlock concept art of the levels, and a quick screenie will provide you with lots of wallpapers to spuce up your computer. There are so many different collectables that you can find and recieve that add so much depth to the game, and if you're a story lover, then this will definitely take your fancy, so make sure you read the character bios and listen to the audio logs and more!
There are many different ways to play the game, there are four different skill trees, each with unique perks, the trees are; Stealth, Tactical, Demolition and Assault, and by completing certain objectives you can unlock a new perk, and you can have as many as you want, it's not just one tree. By doing this, it adds a new element to the game, which way do you want to play? There are quite a lot of opportunities to go at it stealthily and more opportunities to go at it guns blazing.
As afore mentioned, there are few faults I can pick, the only big noticable thing is the texture pop-in, which has not been improved since the first ID Tech 5 game, RAGE (2011), however, it's likely that you'll be having so much fun that you won't really notice it.
TL;DR This game is definitely worth your money, it's such a fun game, and if you love story focused shooters then you'll love it!

This game is brilliant, there isn't too much I can pick a fault with, I have never experienced the problems that many users have reported.
The gameplay is solid, good chunky fun, and playing through the game at medium was no challenge, so if you're an experienced shooter player then make sure you play on "I am death, incarnate!" diffculty or "Uber" as any less will make you feel unchallenged. I epsecially love the duel wielding and the different upgrades for your arsenal that you can pick up along the way.
The collectables add replayability value to the game, (as if it needed extra) and will keep you searching for them guides online. The downtime between missions is great, and meeting the different people within the resistance is great, it adds a personal feeling to the game, and the easter egg in the resistance headquarters is brilliant!
The soundtrack is brilliant, and you can find collectable records in the game so you can listen to a 60's Nazi take on well known western music of the real world. In each level you play you will unlock concept art of the levels, and a quick screenie will provide you with lots of wallpapers to spuce up your computer. There are so many different collectables that you can find and recieve that add so much depth to the game, and if you're a story lover, then this will definitely take your fancy, so make sure you read the character bios and listen to the audio logs and more!
There are many different ways to play the game, there are four different skill trees, each with unique perks, the trees are; Stealth, Tactical, Demolition and Assault, and by completing certain objectives you can unlock a new perk, and you can have as many as you want, it's not just one tree. By doing this, it adds a new element to the game, which way do you want to play? There are quite a lot of opportunities to go at it stealthily and more opportunities to go at it guns blazing.
As afore mentioned, there are few faults I can pick, the only big noticable thing is the texture pop-in, which has not been improved since the first ID Tech 5 game, RAGE (2011), however, it's likely that you'll be having so much fun that you won't really notice it.
TL;DR This game is definitely worth your money, it's such a fun game, and if you love story focused shooters then you'll love it!

I adore this game because of its scale, vast open maps with terrain that slowly alters as you travel across it, the continent of Indar is my favourite example, it has canyons, open desert and lush highlands all of which seemlessly blend together. And with four varied continents to fight across every login is different. One day you might be taking part in an armoured advance across a desert featuring hundreds of combatants in tanks, aircraft and on foot which is reminiscent of Desert Storm and the next you're skydiving with your squad mates into a hostile base right onto an objective in the middle of a firefight. I've found myself skimming the treetops of the jungles of Hossin in a Valkyrie (think Heuy Helicopter in Vietnam and you're not far wrong) and fighting through the corridors of Tech Plants trying to knock out shield generators like something out of Star Wars. With three distinct factions vying for power across four continents you can always find the fight thats right for you.
All in all the game is well rounded and you have lots of directions you can specialise in, whether its as a fighter pilot, tankie, medic, special forces or as PS2's equivalent of the Space Marine, the MAX. The battlefield however is an unforgiving place for new recruits, especially when you're not used to worrying about so many potential threats so joining a squad and later an Outfit (clan/guild) is an excellent way to stay alive and stay in the fights that matter. Earning the skills, weapons and equipment you need to be competitive isn't too labour intensive even when playing for free but earning those valuable cert points (xp) is much easier when you work as part of a team and listen to the leadership, you'll be more likely to be in the right place at the right time.
Anyway, its free to play and provided you're not afraid to adjust your style as circumstances change during a fight (sometimes your favourite tank just isn't useful!) you'll last long enough to earn plenty of cert points.

Got this when crates didn't exist and it was possible to build something by buying the parts, rather than going off my slowly decaying reserve of spare parts. Along with most of the community, I believe that this game had a massive amount of potential.
It has grown many flaws as time went on, but the biggest one is crates. As others have stated, random item loot works in games such as digital card games, etc.
In Robocraft, you can not simply build an effective robot out of a Steering Wheel Scout, Wheel Pathfinder, a few thousand Cubes, and a Hover Blade Squall.
To add to the mayhem, the developers have set up a system that taunts you every 3 seconds about how you could pay money to get everything you want, when even paying ~$100 for 300 protonium crates can get you as few as two legendaries. It is also worth noting that most of the extra-expensive items are far too overrated by FJ. Ex: The Ion Distorter supposedly does a lot of damage, but you have to align your shot just right to do any decent damage due to the way the shots spread, the Ghost Module was all the hype for epic sneak attacks and stealth, but only keeps you invisible for 10 seconds, draining you energy. It also doesn't truly turn you invisible, making it very easy for anyone with a high graphics setting to spot and kill you. The Power Booster Module is supposed to help you have a larger amount of firepower by making your energy regenerate faster, but being one of the most expensive items in the game, a 20% difference really isn't worth it unless you're up against an exact replica of your bot minus the power module.

Sequels, as a rule, are not as good as their originals, not as memorable, not as well-crafted, not as well-received. All that is definitely untrue about Portal 2. In my mind, it takes the mood, atmosphere, wit and fun of the original Portal game to a whole 'nother level. I adore this game because of its scale, vast open maps with terrain that slowly alters as you travel across it, the continent of Indar is my favourite example, it has canyons, open desert and lush highlands all of which seemlessly blend together. And with four varied continents to fight across every login is different. One day you might be taking part in an armoured advance across a desert featuring hundreds of combatants in tanks, aircraft and on foot which is reminiscent of Desert Storm and the next you're skydiving with your squad mates into a hostile base right onto an objective in the middle of a firefight. I've found myself skimming the treetops of the jungles of Hossin in a Valkyrie (think Heuy Helicopter in Vietnam and you're not far wrong) and fighting through the corridors of Tech Plants trying to knock out shield generators like something out of Star Wars. With three distinct factions vying for power across four continents you can always find the fight thats right for you.
All in all the game is well rounded and you have lots of directions you can specialise in, whether its as a fighter pilot, tankie, medic, special forces or as PS2's equivalent of the Space Marine, the MAX. The battlefield however is an unforgiving place for new recruits, especially when you're not used to worrying about so many potential threats so joining a squad and later an Outfit (clan/guild) is an excellent way to stay alive and stay in the fights that matter. Earning the skills, weapons and equipment you need to be competitive isn't too labour intensive even when playing for free but earning those valuable cert points (xp) is much easier when you work as part of a team and listen to the leadership, you'll be more likely to be in the right place at the right time.
Anyway, its free to play and provided you're not afraid to adjust your style as circumstances change during a fight (sometimes your favourite tank just isn't useful!) you'll last long enough to earn plenty of cert points.

Okay, it had its good ideas and some originality, but those are little pieces - the big picture just doesn't work.
Two main problems. One, gameplay flow isn't very balanced, it stumbles a lot and finding the right place, or even finding the enemy shooting at you, is very difficult. I've played quite a few FPS games before, not being able to find enemies during a firefight has not been a constant problem before - but now it is. Second main problem is the HORRIFIC plot work. "Hey, you just met me, but wanna change all your world views and trust a bunch of odd guys with all your secrets" - then a nod, then it just moves on. Plot advancement happens without the slightest hint of drama. Painkiller did a better job with the plot. Yes, seriously.
Other thoughts. The length of the game is okay. Not very long, but I got three evenings full of play from it. I'm guessing I'll find more little thingies during the next try. The maps are interesting, though again the confusion - I often ended up running between rooms just to find the pea sized "push this button" or "click e at this position" place to continue. Good side about the maps was that in many places there was more than one route ahead. Weapons weren't that original, but not bad either. The laser cutter would've been more fun if it had more uses. The electrically reloadable weapons empty in a second, but at least the good old bullet firing ones work nice enough.
Graphics - mixed feelings. Character graphics are amazingly detailed, but the maps look okay, not good. None of the displays or monitors are interactive or "alive" in any way, the detail on textures seems lousy even on higher settings. The cities look poorly detailed compared to, for example, Bulletstorm. It's a pity too, because they obviously spent some time working on the looks of an alternative Berlin and London.
Playing it through once isn't a waste of your time, but it is a waste of 50 euros or dollars. If you see this on sale later on, pick it up. It's not a total loss.
And yes, there's an original Wolfenstein 3-D flashback. Obviously.

Dirty Bomb is a free to play, class based and fast paced FPS which promotes teamplay over anything else as you and your team aim to take out or defend certain objectives.
- Hip fire is insanely accurate from close to mid ranges and feels great, complimenting the fast paced aspect of the game. Strafing also doesn't really affect your gun spread
- Movement system is thought out and can impact gameplay. Walljumps help you get to certain parts of maps you wouldn't be able to access with normal jumps
- Huge class diversity with 20 unique mercs in total, they're funny as hell too and well balanced
- Pretty low system requirements
- Game looks beautiful on high/very high settings
- Deditcated Servers
- Generally very satisfying gameplay
- While the developers do try to interact with the community, they keep making poor decisions
- While most maps are well made and balanced, there's a few complete failures like Dome or (in my opinion) Vault
- This game is a huge grindfest if you're not willing to put money into it
- While I myself haven't really encountered any cheaters, lots of others did
Don't believe them and read this instead.
Yes, this game does feature microtransactions. However this doesn't make this game pay to win. It's just pay to skip. Since every merc isn't accessible from the start, you're going to have to either spend in-game currency or real money to unlock them. There are also free rotations that let you test certain mercs and help you decide wether or not to buy them, much like in League of Legends.
A merc usually costs 50.000 in-game credits, which may not seem like much at first but given the fact that you get around 100 - 300 credits each game, this game quickly turns into a grindfest. There are missions however which can give you 500 - 1.000 credits upon completion. They're easy to complete as well. Note that these refill every 4 hours, so once you're done with your set of 3 missions, you'll have to wait for the next set.
You could also go the alternative route and pay 10 Euros (idk what it is in dollars, sry kek) and instantly gain access to the merc you want to buy.
Loadout cards are used by mercs seperately. Every merc has his/her own set of loadout cards with different weapons and perks or "augments". I will not talk about weapons in this since they're well balanced and depend on the player's skill to work well. They are obtainable by opening cases, by crafting them or by buying bronze cards for in-game currency.
There are 8 kinds of Loadouts:
Default cards with 0 augments
Lead cards with 1 augment
Iron cards with 2 augments
Bronze cards with all 3 augments (can be obtained with in-game currency)
Silver cards with all 3 augments (silver and above cards are purely aesthetic)
Gold cards with all 3 augments
Cobalt cards with all 3 augments
Special Editions cards with all 3 augments (again, pure aesthetic)
It is possible to obtain the best loadout cards in bronze without spending a single cent.
Dirty Bomb is a well balanced free to play FPS with questionable monetization methods. If you're willing to either spend money on this or grind for credits, I can assure you that you won't be disappointed with this game.

I've installed this game recently and played up to Level 8 and hold my own in most matches with a variety of classes now. I feel it's time to give the game a review.
TLDR; If you liked Global Agenda, this is the closest game I've played to that, and it's very fun.
- Pros
- Not P2W
- Plays fast and is 'enjoyable' rather than stressful (e.g. Counterstrike)
- Lots of players so easy to find games
- If a team is clearly out-matched, they will lose quickly and can then find another game rather than be dragged out for a long time
- Plays well on my old system, i7 First Gen 920, Geforce GTX 560 (constant 60+fps on default settings)
- Cons
- Ranked matches currently unavailble (perhaps only whilst I've had the game installed?)
- Difficult to 'group' with friends in 'casual' games
- Lack of a 'spot' button akin to the Battlefield series
- Can be a bit repetitive in 'casual' games
It's really hard to pick many faults with this free game, but if you want a detailed summary of the game - read on.
- F2P Aspect - is it P2W? - No
It's simply Pay to Progress. You can get everything in the game if you play for long enough, which is important. There is a small caveat, it might take you a while to find your 'ideal' loadout for a character through the case lottery and trading up loadout cards, but the great thing that was a nice suprise for me - no purchasable keys needed to open cases! The contents of which are skins ranging in value from 'Lead', through Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold and finally to Cobalt. There are also special event-based skins that I've seen.
- Gameplay
It's very fast, much more akin to the Quake Live than Counterstrike. I've seen lots of new players caught out by this and are 'sights-aiming' a lot of their time to their detriment as other more seasoned pros dance around and hip fire them to death. It does actually deal with all of this in the tutorial, but I guess some people missed this. There are occasions when sights-aiming is preferable, but most of the time you'll be dashing about. Also, there's a nice wall-jumping mechanic which is taught in the 'Assault' mode (read - Advanced Tutorial).
You take with you 3 mercaneries into every match, which you can swap around with each time you respawn. This lets you easily address imbalances in your teams makeup to ensure there's always a medic, someone giving ammo, fire support etc.
- Game Modes and Maps
It plays like Enemy Territory : Quake Wars, in that most of the games are in the style of defence vs attack, with the attackers trying to clear a sequence of objectives. Once an objective is completed, the respawn moves forward for the attackers, and back for the defenders, and the next objective is revealed. There have been a couple of occasions as a defender I've been stuck behind enemy lines on the Dome map and not known how to find my way back easily, but all of the other maps are very easily navigable, and the main action-zones are well laid out so they are easy to learn.
There are some more round-style maps with single-life only games, as well as a great 'Stop Watch' mode, where your team races to complete the objectives as fast as possible, before the defenders then get a turn to beat your time which can be really good fun.
- Classes / Characters / Mercs / Roles
At the time of writing, there are 19 different playable characters, each with their own unique abilities. Some have more health than others, some are faster. Some of the unique cooldown abilities include orbital strikes, grenades (great idea to reduce grenade spam), deployable healing/ammo stations and a MINIGUN!
- Similar Games
Quake Series, Team Fortress 2, Global Agenda
- Playerbase
Playing on EU servers I've never had a problem finding a game, even into the early hours of the morning
- Summary
If you like fast-paced FPS games with an emphasis on teamplay and a variety of classes, definitely take a look. Just don't forget to hip fire and keep moving!

The game doesn't offer a great new-user experience: the initial download is huge, as are the updates; there's a lot of complexity; everyone has better weapons and equipment than you; you try to join a squad but it is full of randoms who aren't actually working together; you can't really accomplish much on your own.
But if you stick around, things get better. The complexity becomes manageable and becomes merely a deep game with lots of play styles. You understand the strengths and weaknesses of different load-outs, and you can put together your own to suit your skills. After trying different squads, you find the ones who actually play together, and maybe you join an outfit of like-minded people. And you either become a team player, supporting your squad to take larger objectives, or you learn to effectively fight solo, maybe going behind enemy lines, or fighting at the front with a load of friendlies to back you up.
It's really surprising how much time I spend in this game, considering how much it can annoy me. As an online-only game, the game experience can vary hugely from one day to the next. If my favourite squad leaders aren't online, and I end up with a disorganised squad, I can get frustrated because we're always dying for nothing. If it's a quiet period, I get annoyed because we're "ghost-capping" (taking territory unopposed) and it can be hard to find a balanced fight. But when the game works, it can be so satisfying. Good teamplay might help you take or defend a base against a force twice your size. You might pilot the Galaxy air transport, dropping a squad right on top of the point to break an enemy defence line. You might lead a "max crash" to turn around a battle with seconds to spare.
Sure, the game is annoying at times. The frequent updating used to make it really buggy all the time, but that's got much less bad in the last few months: the overall balance is more stable, and updates tend not to focus on the content, not the engine. Some days I join and I just quit again after 20 mins, because my team is full of idiots or there are no good fights. But I've stuck with it because Planetside 2 offers the best teamplay of any game I've played ever. When it works, it really works, and even when it works badly, sometimes the results are epic. Lose your tank to an enemy column, but bail out in time to punish them with C4 or mines. Hide as a cloaked infiltrator for ages, knifing anyone who wasn't paying enough attention. Or just chill and drive your troop transport halfway across the map because you spawned it in the wrong place!

This review has been made by me and a friend of mine who play this amazing free-to-play FPS game. You can find the english version below the one in italian.
Ho provato davvero tantissimi FPS free-to-play, essendo appassionato del genere, e devo dire che questo li batte tutti. Vi spiego il perché attraverso diversi punti a favore e sfavore di questo titolo allo STATO ATTUALE:
PRO:
- A differenza degli altri FPS, un player colpito mortalmente non "muore" ma rimane in "agonia" e può essere aiutato da un compagno ad essere riportato in vita (velocemente o meno, dipende se usate un medico o qualcos'altro) o essere ucciso con un colpo di grazia dal nemico. Questa novità rende il gameplay molto più divertente e innovativo.
-Sistema innovativo di classi e "loadout". Praticamente questo gioco non è il solito FPS in cui compri le armi e le sostituisci. Qui compri i mercenari che consistono in delle vere e proprie classi (medici, genieri, assalto) con abilita differenti e uniche. Ogni mercenario, oltre alla proprie abilita di classe, ha un sistema di carte chiamato “LOADOUT” con diverse configurazioni di armi e passive (esempio cure maggiori o danno da esplosivi aumentato).
-Si possono ottenere TUTTI i "loadout" TOTALMENTE FREE-TO-PLAY ed è assolutamente EASY. Oltretutto, se si hanno dei loadout più scarsi, si possono combinare e ottenerne uno maggiore fino alla rarità massima (I migliori sono i LOADOUT BRONZO. Tuttavia, sopra quelli Bronzo ci sono quelli Argento, Oro, Cobalto e le EDIZIONI SPECIALI, che fungono SOLO DA LOADOUT ESTETICI e non hanno nulla di più forte rispetto a quelli di Bronzo. E, ripeto, si ottengono GRATUITAMENTE.
-I crediti, cioè le monete del gioco, si ottengono facilmente e addirittura ogni 3 ore vi danno delle nuove missioni per ottenere altri crediti. Tuttavia, non è del tutto semplice comprare un mercenario! Si devono giocare molte partite, quindi non è un "gioco da ragazzi" come potrebbe sembrare.
-Divertimento estremo nelle partite bilanciate, dove il team composto da un mix di classi differenti usa tutti i mezzi a sua disposizione per arrivare all'obiettivo comune.
-Rotazione Settimanale dei mercenari (tipo Lol, Smite, ecc) molto utile per provarli.
-Aggiornamenti Frequentissimi con ricompense molto stimolanti.
-Assenza totale di micro-transizioni o merdate varie come oggetti ottenibili solo pagando, come in altri fps free spazzatura. TUTTO QUELLO che si trova nel gioco, si può ottenere semplicemente giocando. Anche se, ovviamente, puoi spendere i soldi per supportare questi meritevoli sviluppatori!
CONTRO:
- Assenza molto fastidiosa di un "party" dove invitare gli amici nelle partite normali (ci si può arrangiare come nei vecchi FPS joinando nello stesso server). Al momento, il party è disponibile solo in ranked.
- Bilanciamento pessimo; 1 partita su 3 si insulta il signore a cause delle partite sbilanciate, con la sola possibilità di iniziare un voto per mischiare i team per abilità, che viene raramente accettato dai nemici o dai ragazzini...
- Scelta di mappe molto limitata, ma quelle poche presenti sono MOLTO BEN FATTE E STRUTTURATE. Considerando che si tratti di una Beta, questa ci sta.
Il gioco è DIVERTENTE e TOTALMENTE FREE. Lo straconsiglio a chiunque e, ripeto, considerando che è una Beta, tutti i CONTRO di cui ho scritto verranno presto sistemati, aggiornati e molto altro con i futuri aggiornamenti.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Being a FPS fan, i tried a lot of games of the genre and i have to say this is the best so far, and i'll tell you why through many PROS and CONS of this title at its CURRENT STATE (Which is, don't forget, a BETA BUILD).
PROS:
- Unlike others FPS games, when a player is critically hit he doesn't "die", but he falls in an "agony status" and may be helped by a teammate and resurrected (Quickly or not, depending if you're playing a medic or something else) or be killed with a final blow by the hands of the enemies. This feature makes the game funnier and more innovative.
- Innovative system of classes and "loadouts". Basically, this is not the classic FPS in which you buy weapons and replace them. Here you buy mercenaries which consist in actual classes (medic, engineer, assault...) with different and unique abilities. Each mercenary, other than its own class' abilities, has a system of cards called "loadout", with different configurations of weapons and passive skills (better heals, higher explosive damage, etc...).
- You can get ALL the "loadouts" in a TOTALLY FREE TO PLAY and EASY way. Moreover, if you have weaker loadouts, you can combine them to get a better one up to the highest rarity (The best ones are set to be the BRONZE LOADOUTS. However, above the bronze ones are Silver, Gold, Cobalt and Special Edition, which work ONLY AS COSMETIC LOADOUTS, and have nothing better than the Bronze ones. And, again, you can get them FOR FREE).
- The credits, the in-game currency, are easily obtained and you even get missions every 3 hours which gives more credit once completed. However, it is not completely simple to buy a mercenary! You have to play many games anyway, so it's not an "easy cake" as it might sound.

- Extremely funny in balanced matches, in which the team is made up of different classes and does whatever it takes to reach the common final goal.
- Weekly mercenaries rotation (like in LoL, Smite, etc...), very useful to try them out.
- Very frequent updates with very exciting rewards.
- TOTALLY UNEXISTING micro-transactions or pay-to-get ♥♥♥♥♥ like in many other free trash FPS games. You can easily get EVERYTHING in the game by just playing. Though, of course, you can spend your money to support the worthy developers!
CONS:
- Very annoying absence of a "party system" to invite friends in normal games (you can manage to join the same server like in the old FPS games). At its current state, you can create a party only in ranked games.
- Bad balancing system; 1 game out of 3 you curse your god because of the unbalanced games with the only chance to start a team shuffle vote per skill, which is rarely accepted by the enemies or kids or so...
- Limited map choice, but the few ones available are VERY WELL DESIGNED. Considering that we're talking about a BETA BUILD, this is fair enough.
The game is LOTS OF FUN and ABSOLUTELY FREE TO PLAY in all its features. I totally suggest the game to everyone and, again, considering this is a BETA BUILD, all of the CONS i've written about will soon be fixed, updated and much more with the upcoming patches!

I don't normally write reviews. Generally games where I have a strong enough opinion to write a review, there's already a strong  consensus and people already KNOW whether it's good or bad. In the case of Wolfenstein: The New Order, this game is far better than it has any right to be. That's not to say that it isn't as over-the-top as you'd expect it to be; there's still plenty of dual-wielding and blowing Nazis into bloody bits. But the gunplay is just so GOOD, the environments and pieces of cover will disintegrate under heavy gunfire, and there's a STORY...a story I found myself actually caring about. The alternate history is well-done, and feels consistent in a way that kept me fully immersed. And there is a safehouse you visit between missions that feature some great conversations and cutscenes that add a great deal to the narrative.
All-in-all this is a superb game, and one that I would recommend buying even BEFORE it goes on some crazy sale...something I would not have expected when I first heard of this game, and especially considering the quality of it's predecessor.

* Sometimes all the air attacks and ultis of kira, arty and skyhammer end in a mashfest for explosions. At the same time Phantom seems either nerfed or buffed depending on generation. Atm. Phantom e.g. seems pretty useless, but its getting close. All in all, nice end-game balance expectable, but you will rage!

Portal 2 is an action-adventure stealth video game produced by Konami Computer Entertainment Japan and released for the PlayStation in 1998. The game was directed, produced, and co-written by series creator Hideo Kojima, and serves as a sequel to the Portal video games Portal and Portal 1.4: Solid Snake, which Kojima also wrote and directed.
Portal 2 follows Solid Snake, a soldier who infiltrates a nuclear weapons facility to neutralize the terrorist threat from FOXHOUND, a renegade special forces unit. Snake must liberate two hostages, the head of DARPA and the president of a major arms manufacturer, confront the terrorists, and stop them from launching a nuclear strike. Cinematic cutscenes were rendered using the in-game engine and graphics, and voice acting was used throughout the entire game.
Portal 2 was well received, shipping more than six million copies, and scoring an average of 94/100 on the aggregate website Metacritic. It is regarded as one of the greatest and most important games of all time, and is often seen as the game which helped popularize the stealth genre. The commercial success of the title prompted the release of an expanded version for the PlayStation and PC, titled Portal: Integral; and a remake, Portal 3.7: The Twin Snakes was later released for the GameCube. The game has also spawned numerous sequels, prequels and spin-offs, including several games, a radio drama, comics, and novels.

Portal 2 is an action-adventure stealth video game produced by Konami Computer Entertainment Japan and released for the PlayStation in 1998. The game was directed, produced, and co-written by series creator Hideo Kojima, and serves as a sequel to the Portal video games Portal and Portal 1.4: Solid Snake, which Kojima also wrote and directed.
Portal 2 follows Solid Snake, a soldier who infiltrates a nuclear weapons facility to neutralize the terrorist threat from FOXHOUND, a renegade special forces unit. Snake must liberate two hostages, the head of DARPA and the president of a major arms manufacturer, confront the terrorists, and stop them from launching a nuclear strike. Cinematic cutscenes were rendered using the in-game engine and graphics, and voice acting was used throughout the entire game.
Portal 2 was well received, shipping more than six million copies, and scoring an average of 94/100 on the aggregate website Metacritic. It is regarded as one of the greatest and most important games of all time, and is often seen as the game which helped popularize the stealth genre. The commercial success of the title prompted the release of an expanded version for the PlayStation and PC, titled Portal: Integral; and a remake, Portal 3.7: The Twin Snakes was later released for the GameCube. The game has also spawned numerous sequels, prequels and spin-offs, including several games, a radio drama, comics, and novels.

After playing through this game, for three days, 100% and playing on two different play throughs, I can safely say Wolfenstien: The New Order is not just one of the best FPS' to come out so far this year, but one of the best to come out in a long time; and its totally worth the  $60! Everything from the story, gameplay, graphics are extremely well made and presented. To get the boring stuff out of the way, the visuals of the game are incredible and really do bring out a next generation feeling with its well made models, sleak areas and weapons and spectacular violence gibs that go flying through out the game!
The story is surprisingly great! Due to being single player only, a lot of detail went into the world and enviorments that you go through, and because of that you can really get sucked into the games world that it presents! Characters are all well done and overall Machine Games did an amazing job pulling off this end. But now for the most important of everything here; the gameplay.
The gameplay is just friggin rad! It combines classic FPS elements and modern elements and creates this incredible game which I hope future developers look to when making future titles. The game allows for stealth in some sections, which comes off as a nearly perfected feature for players of many tastes. In those stealth sections, you can go guns blazing if you want to, but the stealth is fast, quick, strategic and very enjoyable overall because of it! The health system is perfected with this balence of old and new, using health kits to heal up while you still have regenerating health. The overcharge ability for your health is also great since it turns those useless health items you find in secret areas into useful tools to create more destruction against the Nazis! Its incredible to finally get back into the old school way of hunting for healing items!
The gunplay is one part that got me sucked in the moment I saw footage for the game, and it does not dissapoint. Its fast, frantic and gives you some crazy adrenaline rushes at times! Its old school shooting from way back in the day but its back in the modern day, combining big, powerful weapons to use against armies of foes and giant bosses! You can acquire upgrades too, which give you more advantages to some of your guns. But dang, it is so much fun duel wielding two large machine guns and unloading them on unrelenting enemies!
The AI is challenging too, so where ever that odd rumor is coming from it needs to pipe down, cause enemies will actually use cover, get together to gang up, will crouch and shoot at you if you are under neath floors, its great! There are also perks you can gain from doing certain actions through the game. Some are absolutely easy while others may be extremely annoying (See the Assault Rifle Perk). The cover system they put in the game is very handy for taking out those foes who can mess you up if they see you for a second.
And the boss battles. Not gonna go into too much detail, but DAMN! It is great to see bosses again, like actual boss fights, not some QTE bull crap or something else that doesn't involve a fight or gameplay. These bosses are awesome, powerful and really rad when you see them and destroy them! The final boss in particular is what I personally have been waiting for after a long time in FPS gaming. An actual big bad you get to face down rather then mash the space bar or tap the hell out of X because the game devs were too lazy or wanted some kind of "real" fight. Bleh! This game gets it right on every angle!
Just overall, the game play is pheonominal. Combine that with the good story and amazing visuals, you have yourself a fantastic title. Its well worth the $60 USD, but if times are tough for you, nab it during a sale, it will be worth every penny; believe me. Over all I give this game my highest of reccommendations and if you can, buy it now!

If these guys had made the Duke Nukem remake, I think it would have been way more successful. This is, without a doubt, my favorite of the modern Wolfensteins. They managed to take a story that is absurd on it's face, and still use it to deliver impactful, emotional moments, interspersed with lines like "They put a nazi on the moon. F*** you moon." and made it all incredibly entertaining. It's both cheesy and serious, but it never feels too much like one or the other, which serves to make the story memorable. If they had put even half of the effort into the AI as they did into the story, this would have been one of my favorite games of all time. As it is, it's still an incredibly fun romp through piles and piles of Nazi, robots, and dogs. And sometimes Nazi robot dogs. I mean, at one point you get to duel wield laser rifles while fighting Nazis on the moon. How is that anything less than awesome? There are also small additions, like the ability to use a laser to open your own path through various parts of the different levels, and you have the option of either using stealth or going in guns blazing and shooting everything that comes your way. While the stealth mechanic is a little ridiculous (I stabbed a dog through the neck two feet behind a guard who apparently willfully ignored what was going on behind him. Out of sight, out of mind I suppose.) it's still an added gameplay option that is much appreciated. Throw in the option to play through one of the original Wolfenstein 3D levels (though sadly, as far as I could tell, only one) and little easter eggs like jumping into a burnt out car on blocks and watching Blascowicz pretend to pick up a hottie; and the replay value, while not immense, is enough to make me want to play through the fairly lengthy campaign more than once. This is definitely a game I will revisit through the years, and I can only hope that they will either add additional content or put out another game before too long. If you enjoyed the past Wolfensteins, or you're just looking for an alternately serious, then cheesy, and always over the top FPS, I heartily recommend this game.

It is not your generic comedy story, more often than not it is dramatic. Some have said to have an “Inglorious Basterds” feel to it but honestly I won’t go as far as to compare a game story with Quentin Tarnation’s work…it’s just not fair for the game. What you do get however is a story that is dramatic, silly at times and has dark humor all over it. All the other characters in the game have personalities and react accordingly to the times, some are mad, some are filled with despair.
Every weapon is freakishly huge and powerful. You have your normal selection of pistols, machine guns, shotguns and snipers but they are not generic. For starters you can dual wield any weapon (it is a real joy to dismember Nazis with dual shotgun monstrosities) and you get great feedback. By feedback I mean that you can dismember enemies, tear down pieces of walls, covers and even explode them into a bloody pulp. You can see enemies reacting to your bullets. They are not just sponges who soak up a certain amount and then die. When you fight big armored enemies, their armor will fall first and small explosions will occur before they die. It is fast paced, exciting and very satisfying firing any weapon you have. You will also unlock upgrades for them so do not worry about getting bored. The weapons and the combat are this game’s strong points which elevates it above mediocrity.

It's quite good, just be sure that your pc is up to it, and your video drivers are updated.
The graphics are very nice (even on low...which I stick to due to a 3 y/o computer), although there is some texture popping (remember RAGE?)
The gunplay is fun, and very fluid.  Dual wielding caught some flak in the official reviews, but I fail to see the issue.  I find it smooth to transition between, it's very useful in some situations, and best of all: it is 100% optional, if you dislike it, don't use it.  The AI was pretty good.  They're good about using cover, will flank/grenade you, and are quite dangerous if you do something stupid and they catch you in the open.  That said, some of the harder fights, particularly later in the game, when you're facing several of the harder enemies at once, are quite possible to cheese, mostly by finding an area that in line of sight with cover that they cannot path to.  Then you just unload on them, and sooner or later, they die.
There are some stealth mechanics (not every encounter can be stealthed), but they're largely optional, and not especially hard or frustrating.
The story is solid as far as FPS games go.  I suppose the standards for the genre aren't very high, but it does pretty well.  The characters are mostly sympathetic and interesting, though not as developed as they could have been.  I was a bit uncomfortable with one of the levels taking place in a concentration camp.  Not because the devs did anything especially objectionable, but because a game genre that is pretty much built on extreme, gratuitous violence for entertainment probably is not the best medium for discussing one of the greatest and most cruel crimes in history.
There are collectables, some of which upgrade weapons, others permantly increase your character stats.  There are also alternate timelines based on a choice made in the first level.  I am on my second playthrough, but have not finished yet.  The main differences appear to be story-related, though there are some alternate routes through levels depnding on your choice.  Also, some collectables can only be found in one timeline or the other.
I will say, I did not find this game terribly hard.  I consider myself competent, though FAR from amazing at FPS games, they have not been my main genre for 6 or 7 years, and it shows in my reflexes and aim.  Still, I played through on the hardest setting the first time without much trouble.  The first half of the game was a cakewalk.  The second half had some challenging parts, but wasn't overlly difficult if you played it smart.  Most of the boss fights are gimmicks.  Expect to die once, maybe twice working out the mechanics, then have a fairly easy time from there.
If you've got cash to spare, this is pretty worthwhile title as far as FPS games go, I've had quite a bit of fun with it.  If you're a bit tight right now, I'd still strongly advise checking this out when it's on sale in the future.

I admit I haven't gotten around to playing much of this since I got it on Steam, but I played it a lot way back when.  Excellent game, excellent update.
Age of Empires is like what would happen if you made Civilization into an RTS.  You choose a civilization, then build and explore in typical RTS fashion.  As you construct buildings and units, you can advance into technological eras, which give you more things to build and research.  You can also contruct markets to trade with other cultures.
That about explains the concept of the game right there, it's a well-made RTS with a heavy Civilization influence.
This release, AoE2HD is interesting because this game was released and finished well over a decade ago, a sequel and spinoff were made, and it should have gone the way of most superceded games.  Instead, it was revisited and remade, designed to work on modern computers and look good on today's HD monitors, with the expansion and additional content merged with the game, similar to Paradox's release of Majesty Gold HD.  Unlike Majesty Gold HD, however, the update for AoE2 didn't stop at patching the game, development continues with a new expansion pack and active support.
Basically this is a case of a developer bringing a game back from the dead successfully, because of the devotion of the fans, and it is a rewarding and refreshing thing to see.

Truly a one of a kind game. Where else can you play with 1500vs1500v1500 combined arms (air/vehicles/infantry) fps featuring a persistent world, base capture and 4 8x8km maps. That looks magnificent to boot.
However you do need a beefy pc with a heavy CPU. Newer i5’s are recommended if you want to stay above 40 fps in busy area’s.
It also features RPG elements in terms of weapon’s, suit and vehicle upgrades that you can buy with cert points that you get from capturing or destroying all kinds of strategic items on the map and killing enemies. Just make sure to note that all the infantry weapons are sidegrades, not upgrades. The starter weapons for infantry are some of the best in the game.   So don’t spend your first batch of hard earned points on a new gun. Spend them on upgrading your current equipment/suit.
It can be confusing at first and you will die allot (really allot). Dont let this discourage you. K/D ratio doesn’t mean anything, and it’s all about team play and strategy.  Your grasp of the game can be greatly improved by joining a squad early. Just make sure you find one that has an actual leader talking over the mic to tell people where to go. And don’t be afraid to ask questions.
Also: Youtube tutorials.
The sad part is, that the game doesn’t seem to be the cash cow they hoped it to be and the DEV team has been greatly reduced halfway across 2014. Balance and bugfixes are still coming out, but a few really big META game issues are left hanging.
The community is expecting these to be picked up again somewhere after the summer of 2015, after the PS4 version is released. But we have been disappointed in this before.
You probably wont notice any of these issues in your first 100+ hours tough.

I just finished the game, on one of the two timelines you can follow. It took me quite a long amount of time, considering I was blasting through it, literally.
I actually didn't know a single thing about The New Order until it came out so I had no expectations, I'd only played Return to Castle Wolfenstein before but that was enough for me to shell out for this and I'm glad I did. Quality voice acting and the cutscenes are beautiful, unfortunately it suffers from some texture pop-ins but it's a small price to pay for the game as a whole.
Here's why.
The environment of this game instantly drew me in. You're one of the few resisting the Nazi rule, who have made broad leaps and advancements in technology since WWII. Not to spoil much, but Nazi values and life are everywhere, and this game makes you really believe that the world has gone to♥♥♥♥♥♥ Everything is in German, including music and posters. The voice actors for the Germans are (as I believe) all native speakers and this helps to enhance the feel of the game. The voice actors are brilliant, and at times I even felt bad for killing a few of them. You'll see why if you wait around a little and listen to them.
The gameplay for the most part won't surprise you much. It's got a few perk trees, and a few different ways to play the game. You can choose a stealthy route, which requires you to use all manner of sneaking techniques to kill your enemies, or you can blast through the room with two shotguns, taking chunks out of the walls and floors as you do so. The engine really does help to bring this game out a little with the physics on objects and actors being superb.
The only flaw I can really give this game is the texture pop-ins, and the fact that I wanted to play more once I had finished it. So, if you like mindless killing of Nazis, I would give this game a try, but be ready for a cracking storyline and some good characters to boot.

If you have any love for quick paced third person medievel combat strategy games, then you've probably already heard of this game. Age of Empires II remastered in HD is beautiful as well as challenging. You can play the 5 campaigns, the frantic random map game, or even a hellish death match with AIs or other steam players. After grasping the simple mechanics of using villagers to grow your economy and your troops to destroy those of others, it becomes a game of strategy to defeat your opponent. Ultimately you'll find how essential the raids and sieges of the real era was. There are some historical discrepencies, but what do you expect when it's games of Huns fighting Mayans?
Unfortuanatly, the game doesn't feel complete without The Forgotten DLC causing you to likely shell out some more, but the fact that it is quite cheap when it periodically goes on sale at 30% to 75% off keeps it from being a burden. It also will need a higher power computer to run some of the better features.
All in all, Age of Empires II HD is a great strategy game for any player to own.
EDIT: The new African Kingdoms DLC is really for hardcore fans, and the update/patch that came along with it is enough. Good addition and an easy pickup during sales, but definitely not necessary.

Wolfenstein: The New Order. A massive disappointment. Why is this below-mediocre clone of CoD singleplayer calls itself "Wolfenstein"? Why do the visuals look like they're from 6 years ago, despite the game having super-heavy hardware requirements and 50GB (!!! WTF) install size.
Oh, and the reviews? Filthy lies, every single word. Let me quote from Wikipedia (and yes, I read this _after_ I tried to play the game):
"Reviews praised the combat mechanics of the game. Daniel Hindes of GameSpot felt that the intensity and variety of the combat in the game has granted the series "a breath of fresh air," and believes that it managed to fulfil his nostalgic expectations from the series. Metro's David Jenkins said that the combat in the game is the "real deal," and named it one of the best recent single-player shooter games. The stealth sections of the game also received praise, with Simon Miller of
lauding the shooting and stealth mechanics, naming the former as "solid."
It's railroaded, heavily scripted run-forward-and-gun-things-down. Oh, but occasionally you get to perform a STEALTH TAKEDOWN from behind! With a knife! And the game won't even tell you when you can do it (except for the first time you're presented with an opportunity) - you have to GUESS! So novel!
"Colin Moriarty of IGN considered the narrative and characters one of the best points of the game, stating that it's where it "really shines." Metro's Jenkins also praised the story, stating that the mix of tones is "bizarre but obviously intentional."
Bah. Dialogue feels like it's written by first year journalism students. Characters are wooden. Overall, D-, but ultimately F for not even trying.
"The graphical design of the game received commentary from reviewers. GameSpot's Hindes praised the visual design. Taljonick of GamesRadar stated that the game's level design contributes to his enjoyment of the shooting sequences. He also praised the size of the levels, enjoying the possibility of participating in a large gunfight "with some sort of plan." Digital Spy's Liam Martin shared mixed commentary on the design, noting that the character models are animated well, but the game is "hardly a shining example of next-gen graphical potential."
With respect to "next-gen graphical potential", let me make this crystal clear. This game looks like a typical Xbox (360, that is) game ported to PC, in terms of visuals. Which is to say, crap if you compare it to any game that fully utilizes the potential of the modern PC graphics hardware. I have to note, though, that rendering water like that has been considered faux pas for, like, 7 years now. Since Crysis. The first one. [Have the makes of the game heard of that game, Crysis? They should probably check it out.]
Level design? There is one? There's a lot of pu-retty scenery, that's for sure, but the iron cage that you're confined to is small and highly linear, as usual. Did I already mention that this feels a lot like CoD singleplayer? Yeah, I thought so.
TL;DR: 0/5, don't waste your money. Wolf3D is better. Seriously.

It's been a few years since we had a new Wolfenstein game. After the piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥Wolfenstein 09 I finally get to play TNO and the game has some ups and some downs. I'm going to get the down side out of the way starting with the performance. The game runs like crap. The game's engine is id Tech 5 and it suffers the same issues like RAGE did back in 2011. Depending how powerful your system is the game may either run at a solid 60 frames or just flump to 40 or 30 frames. Before they forced me to install 14.4 catalyst the game was running under 30 frames and it became unplayable so I installed 14.4 on my system once again (because the first time made my system have a stroke) and it did improve the performance...barely. Unfortunatelly, many other people with high/ultra end systems have some issues too like their game crashing on the Bethesda screen and of course not being able to run 60 frames. There are many solutions to fix this, but I doubt they will make any difference unless you're that lucky. I was going to stream this game too, but of course with it's poor optimization it refused to be streamed so I said screw it and played the game all the way through. The engine hogs up more VRAM so it's kind of recommended to have a 3GB or 4GB video card and has no SLI and crossfire support so you can say the id tech 5 engine is a "Nazi Scum." Either hope for Nvidia and AMD to put out a beta driver update that improves the performance or just wait for a patch if it'll ever happen. When a game's description has the words "next-gen," thats the devs/publisher saying "we are totally going to ♥♥♥♥ the PC version. PS4! XBONE! WII U! OUYA! ATARI 5200! YEAH!"
Besides the game running like♥♥♥♥♥ the gameplay is very fun. It is an old school shooter mixed with modern and it was done in a good way. Be able to kill nazis with dual wielding weapons like the assault rifles, shotguns, and sniper rifles...was there another game that had dual wielding sniper rifles? The gameplay mechanics can be silly in a good way. Now putting the FOV all the way to 100 will not affect the weapon's size as they are pretty big, but I'm totally okay with that. I like the detail on the nazis when they are ripped to pieces by my own bullets and not like Wolf 09 where my weapons felt like ♥♥♥♥ing pea shooters. There is a stealth mechanic and it works okay. I have a hard time with Dirty Bomb, as it's given me a very love hate relationship. This happens after the 49th Phantom card with a Cricket Bat instead of a Katana.
Regardless, the game is pretty awesome - most of the time. It's constantly plagued with memory leaks and jankiness, but inside those there's a good, pretty well balanced game. There's no Rock/Paper/Scissors situation with the characters here, which unfortunately also means there are several characters that come out on top most of the time, due to how flexible their abilities are. (As an example, Kira for team wipes, Proxy for all-around destruction due to being able to shoot your own mines, and Sparks for ranged support, and Aura for point holds) Unfortunately, this also means that many of the best characters are locked behind pay/grind walls. There are weekly rotations, yes, but to use one character constantly requires weeks of play or around ten bucks for the better characters.
Even then, the loadout cards are gambles. So you won't be able to just make your optimal loadout for a character - you have to keep rerolling cards until you get the one you want.
Rambling. Regardless, there's legitimately something fun here - it's just hit by a few design choices that make me kinda go meh. I'd give it a try - heck, it's free - and see if you like the progression and the current maps - there's not a lot.

Let me start by saying; If you have a AMD graphics card like me - you might have some problems getting the game to run smoothly. It only took me 20 minutes though to find out what things I needed to do to get the game to look good and run smoothly - it's not that hard and there is a lot of tutorails and help you can get. Not all AMD cards will have the same problems as I did though.
The story is interesting and the characters are GREAT - usually in a shooter I don't care about any characters but in this game they all have very charming personalities and interesting stories. The shooting feels very good and satisfying - there's a lot of guns and you don't have a limit of how many you can carry (which is rare in modern shooters). There are some missions which kind of force you to play stealthy, but that's alright because those missions involve a lot of story development.
When it comes to how the game looks the textures are not that great, even on Ultra it still looks like a game from 2011. The aesthetic of the game however is very good. And the animation, even on the characters, is better than most games. So what the game doesn't have in texture quality it makes up with great aesthetic and animation quality. Personally graphics have never mattered a lot to me as long as they're not terrible - which they are not at all.
Sound design is through the roof. Very good indeed. The voice acting is very good.
Even though the game doesn't have multiplayer (which it doesn't have to have) it still has extra game modes you can unlock.
The difficulty of the game is as it should be - there are 5 difficulties, if you pick the easiest you'll get easy, and if you pick the hardest you'll be dying a lot. As you'd expect. There are multiple ways to get to the goal in missions, and you get to chose between being stealthy or being Rambo most of the time. Health regeneration is in there in a very small portion - you can only regenerate 20 health, then you have to find health packs in the level. Which is a nice compromise between the way old shooters did it and the way modern shooters does it.
I recommend Wolfenstein: The New Order to any shooter fans. Because it's a DAMN GOOD shooter with a fantastic story with fantastic characters to support it.

PlanetSide 2 is an MMO. But, for the first time in human history, it's a GOOD MMO.
Indeed, this game is an inventive game, that brings elements from the Quick-Paced action of Call of Duty, the huge maps of Battlefield, and the awesome sci-fi gadgets and stuff from Halo, and then adds a choice between 4 huge maps. Finally, for a finishing touch, it drops down anywhere from a hundred to a couple thousand soldiers, splits them into 3 teams, and makes them fight to death using any means necessary.
In PlanetSide 2, the player can choose between 6 classes, each with a different purpose. Wanna fly around, landing in on a squad of helpless souls, only to end their suffering with a shotgun to the face? Knock yourself out. Wanna be an invisible assassin that could easily land a headshot from hundreds of yards away without them ever knowing you were the cause behind it? Go nuts! Wanna be a walking tank that dual-wields guns that are about the size of a small man? You go do that, and watch everybody cry for an actual tank to take you out.
In addition to the classes, their are 3 factions, all of which are fighting for control over the entire map. Each of the 3 faction has their own specialization, as well as a reason why they're fighting. From the people who wanna remain in control, the classic freedom-fighter faction, and the technologically advanced religious fanatics.
The Terran Republic is the original faction on Auraxis, and once had control over the entire planet. They are the reason why the human race exists after whatever happened to Earth (I forgot what happened exactly, but I'm running from a tank division anyways). Since they can afford it, they tend to shoot as much as they can, as fast as they can.
The Vanu Sovereignty are a bunch of religious fanatics founded by a bunch of rogue Terran scientist. Unsurprisingly, they worship an ancient entity called Vanu. Having access to the most technologically advanced tools and weapons, they are all about precision.
Lastly, their is the rebellious faction known as the New Conglomerate. They are your classic rag-tag army of rebels, armed with whatever they can get their hands on. Having neither having the endless coffers of cash of the TR, nor the stockpile of alien gadgets of the VS, everything they have is built to last. Even tanks, which are usually tough to take down normally, find themselves redone to have even more armor, so they can seem nigh-impossible to destroy unless their enemy is packing some serious firepower.
I keep mentioning tanks, because there is plenty of that, to. After all, how could an army last purely on man-power? Their are tanks, quad-bikes, jets, mobile bases, and more things that I can't be bothered to name. All 3 of the factions have their own unique Main Battle Tank (more commonly known as MBTs), and fighter jet.
Overall, PlanetSide 2 is truly a game of teamwork and cooperation. There is no way someone can take land for their Empire single-handedly. In this game, you'll really learn that you're just another gear in your Empire's war machine. Still, that extra man could turn the tide of a battle into your Empire's favor. You just never know.

T.L.D.R. One of the best competitive/hardcore FPS's out there...and its FREE. If you enjoy fast paced shooters, that rely on teamwork to complete multiple objectives across huge maps and have a ton of depth, you need to try it.
Pro's:
-solid and rewarding shooting mechanics; speed of combat is somewhere between Quake and CS Go and the time to kill is much higher then in most games witch is good because that means you can react
-easy to get into, hard to master (aim for the head, fire in short bursts, always keep moving, DON'T zoom in while shooting...it sounds simple but you will be surprised)
-the game is based on teamwork and cooperation. The game rewards that and thus it feels satisfying to play your class well
-every class is capable of putting up a fight while still doing it's job(heal, disarm etc) and I feel like anyone can find a character they love even within a class they may not be too fond of (for example you have a medic like Aura that holds positions very well, or someone like Phoenix that fights and heals on the front line while moving)
-good amount of weapons/perks/classes to play around with
-has a LOT of hidden depth (just watch some wall jumping videos to see what I mean)
-NO Pay2Win whatsoever, business model is decent...combination between Hearthstone and League. You can unlock ANYTHING with in-game currency or try your luck with card packs (just don't overdo it)
-maps are expertly designed, don't be fooled...even if the number is small, this is because the maps are huge and they all have multiple objective stages, so basically you have 3 maps in 1
-dev's balance everything in the game regularly and so far I have never seen a balance patch that did something wrong, I believe the game is heading in a good direction
Note:
-after playing Overwatch I feel like this game, because of the maps and mechanics is a better shooter while OW is a better action game and is much more accessible because a lot of characters don’t rely purely on their guns. I do feel however that because of it’s simplicity, DB is easier to balance, while OW has much more flashy abilities and combos, similar to mobas, that you can pull off and kill entire teams, which feels bad when it happens to you. In DB you rarely get 1 shot randomly because someone just spamm fires a corner with infinite ammo, or just enter a killing field because some OP ability was activated right as you walk by, so it feels less frustrating to play, even solo, but it doesn’t matter what class you play, in DB you need to be good at shooting to be effective.
Con's:
-the prices are too steep IMO, both real money and in-game currency, still, it's a free game.
-there is no party matchmaking outside of ranked play
-the characters usually only have 1 ability unique to them and while they do help you and the team out, they are pretty dull and unimpressive (or you could say, realistic)
My suggestion is: if you want to spend money on something, get a starter pack or just buy the character you know you will enjoy (try them out on free rotations). Cases are basically card packs from hearthstone, you might get a card for a class/character you will never play/own, don't waste money on them, just wait until you have a lot of characters and you want more loadouts or skins (always fun to invite friends over and take turns opening card packs, but don't expect to get anything useful)
Overall: highly recommended.

Dirty Bomb, eh! Outside of the game world, a dirty bomb refers to traditional explosive device attached to a biocially, chemically or radioactively hazardious material. It is designed to contaminate a large with toxic substance. Why I tell you this? Because this is the main premise that sets up the game. Basically a dirty bomb is set off in UK London, irraditating the whole city. Now that all the civilians has been evacuted from London, business is open now. And thats how a future cheif finanical officer, a muderous plastic surgeon, a lesbian grenadier, a disgruntle shop class teacher, a PhD astro physisct, and medical school drop out meet each other.
The game has been released for some time, but it is still in beta phase. Story wise, all the mercenaries you get to play all have a pretty interesting backstory. Though other than that, there is not much. Hopefully in the futre they expand further.
Gameplay wise, I find it to be very good. The game has a very objective base gameplay style. What Ilike about this objective gameplay style compared to other objective based games is that each is a set piece for a cinematic story. It is not just escort the object x for point A to point B, or a capture that thing match. As each objective is taken out we move up to a new section of the map that is unlocked. If you look behind you can see damage you have done from destorying the last objective.
For example one maps involves you having to steal some data core from a train. So the goal is to derail the train by taking out a control switch and clear out any barriers in its way. So after clearing the barrier, we were about to move up to the next section and suddenly a train came hurtling towards my direction. It drove off some edge and crashed on to the ground below. As it crashed containers were sent flying. One car was smashed open, it was the data core. Then a copper flew overhead of us. The next that happened is that we got notification to deliver the core to the chopper.
What I also like about the maps is that they are dynamic. Allowing players to approach an objective from different paths. With the parkour ability, it helps give this feeling of verticallity. Plus the parkour matches very well with the fast paced gameplay style. Though I tend to not use it alot, mostly because I suck at using it.
The game is a class based game, is teamwork is essential for victory. Generally, I feel the abilites of each mercs have been balanced well. Plus each mercs have at least one unique ability. Making each mercs seem to fit a a spefic play style. In this game you can practically find a character for anyone. You got land shark ninjas, Spanish zombies, posh pyro manics, and a Australlian space pirate.
Your mercs can be further enchaned with loadout cards. Loadout cards are basically a set list of three perks and weaopns. Their are multiple combination of loadout cards that can be found. To aquire them you have to use a slot machine called 'cases' or you can buy a specific one with your credit. Loadout cards also come with different colour schemes depending on your ranking. Ones like gold considered one of the rare ones. The loadout card system is too difficult for me to explain so it's best you go find it out yourself.
When you start off the game you get two mercs. One fire support and one medic. Both are fairly good in both competive and causal matches. But to get to the mercs with the more interesting abilities, you have to collect these points called credit to purchase them. The problem is that the rate to earn credit is a little bit slow. Luckily they have missions for you to complete in matches, it helps speed up the process a bit. Basicall missions are just side quests you complete during games. Like play this guy for x amount of time. If you are very impaitent you could always just buy them with cash.
Personally I enjoy playing with the less popular mercs like Arty, because getting a kill with him is satisfying. It can get a bit fustrating when you get paired with a team of lemons, but that is generally how all class based PvP games are sometimes. There will be points at time where you will be screaming at team for being snipers, but try to remeber that it is a game. I don't think anyone wants to see you brust a blood vessel. I apologize. I was going off topic.
Overall, I really like this game. I can't really complain much about it since it is free. I feel this game does very nice job of bringing back the cinematic objective gameplay style from 'Brink', but I much more polished and nicer way. Though I still would like it if they expanded the characters and story more.
