Wow, just wow. Blown away. The Swedish team at MachineGames has a nice pedigree for me. The founders are from Starbreeze Studios, they were the key members that made Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay and The Darkness, two shooters that did very well and are some of my favorite story driven FPSs.
I was hoping they would put Wolfenstein back where it belongs, at the top. I really liked Rage and the direction it was taking but it was lacking something. MachineGames found out what that something was and Wolfenstein The New Order has that classic shooter feel without feeling "stiff."
The story is fantastic and the characters are all memorable. What stood out the most was the way they portrayed B. J. Blazkowicz (the main protagonist). He was the main character from the original Wolfenstein 3d also and I feel they couldn’t have portrayed him better. I love his monologues. Also I liked how there are 2 timelines. Depending on a what choice you make in the beginning the game will feel a little different. That was also a nice touch. I won't say more than that though.
The guns are great. They feel awesome and they are different and shine when you use them at the right time. Brings back the feeling from classic shooters when you used different weapons for different enemies to conserve ammo. You could run through the game with the assault rifle but you would run out of ammo a lot I feel. There are also gun upgrades you come across when you play through the campaign. These upgrades are also kept across playthroughs. Also the dual wielding is lots of fun. Running through tight corridors dual wielding auto shotguns splattering Nazis faces along the way felt good. The perk progression is cleverly organic and is based on your play style. As you you play, the way you kill and the weapons you use unlock perks that give you passive bonuses. The perks are little things like faster sprint while dual wielding, a larger grenade pouch, etc. After completing the game the perks remain in effect giving you a chance to survive on Uber difficulty.
There were a few times the AI was a little derp but it more often was deviously efficient in putting the pressure on. I played the game on “I Am Death Incarnate!” (a step above normal) and there were plenty of times the AI put me down with well timed flanking and pressure. After beating the game I went to the chapter select (hell yeah!) and tried a few of the easier difficulties and the enemies seem to go down faster but aside from that were still lethal.
The music is awesome and feels like a classic id game. You got nice metal tracks to kill Nazis to. The sound effects were awesome and the voice acting was well done and made all the characters more memorable.
Wow, 40 gb not wasted. The game is gorgeous. I don't know what the game looks like on consoles and I haven't a single **** to give. On the master platform this game is fantastic looking and runs a lot better than Rage. I’m running 2 GTX 780 TIs in sli. I turned off sli and ran the game on Ultra w/vsync to see how it played. A few times I had to restart from a checkpoint the game would lag (frame rate tanked to like 2) as the textures tried to catch up. Enabling VT Compress in the advanced graphics options fixed this issue. I did not have this issue while in SLI (more graphic mem to go around). To be honest I couldn’t tell the difference with VT Compress on or off. The game is breathtakingly beautiful, I cant stress this enough. I’m in love with the idT5 engine and I cant wait to pay Doom (4).

I had a feeling this game was going to be awesome but what sealed the deal for me was the Doom Beta. I am pleasantly surprised by how good this game is above my expectations. Wow, just wow. Blown away. The Swedish team at MachineGames has a nice pedigree for me. The founders are from Starbreeze Studios, they were the key members that made Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay and The Darkness, two shooters that did very well and are some of my favorite story driven FPSs.
I was hoping they would put Wolfenstein back where it belongs, at the top. I really liked Rage and the direction it was taking but it was lacking something. MachineGames found out what that something was and Wolfenstein The New Order has that classic shooter feel without feeling "stiff."
The story is fantastic and the characters are all memorable. What stood out the most was the way they portrayed B. J. Blazkowicz (the main protagonist). He was the main character from the original Wolfenstein 3d also and I feel they couldn’t have portrayed him better. I love his monologues. Also I liked how there are 2 timelines. Depending on a what choice you make in the beginning the game will feel a little different. That was also a nice touch. I won't say more than that though.
The guns are great. They feel awesome and they are different and shine when you use them at the right time. Brings back the feeling from classic shooters when you used different weapons for different enemies to conserve ammo. You could run through the game with the assault rifle but you would run out of ammo a lot I feel. There are also gun upgrades you come across when you play through the campaign. These upgrades are also kept across playthroughs. Also the dual wielding is lots of fun. Running through tight corridors dual wielding auto shotguns splattering Nazis faces along the way felt good. The perk progression is cleverly organic and is based on your play style. As you you play, the way you kill and the weapons you use unlock perks that give you passive bonuses. The perks are little things like faster sprint while dual wielding, a larger grenade pouch, etc. After completing the game the perks remain in effect giving you a chance to survive on Uber difficulty.
There were a few times the AI was a little derp but it more often was deviously efficient in putting the pressure on. I played the game on “I Am Death Incarnate!” (a step above normal) and there were plenty of times the AI put me down with well timed flanking and pressure. After beating the game I went to the chapter select (hell yeah!) and tried a few of the easier difficulties and the enemies seem to go down faster but aside from that were still lethal.
The music is awesome and feels like a classic id game. You got nice metal tracks to kill Nazis to. The sound effects were awesome and the voice acting was well done and made all the characters more memorable.
Wow, 40 gb not wasted. The game is gorgeous. I don't know what the game looks like on consoles and I haven't a single **** to give. On the master platform this game is fantastic looking and runs a lot better than Rage. I’m running 2 GTX 780 TIs in sli. I turned off sli and ran the game on Ultra w/vsync to see how it played. A few times I had to restart from a checkpoint the game would lag (frame rate tanked to like 2) as the textures tried to catch up. Enabling VT Compress in the advanced graphics options fixed this issue. I did not have this issue while in SLI (more graphic mem to go around). To be honest I couldn’t tell the difference with VT Compress on or off. The game is breathtakingly beautiful, I cant stress this enough. I’m in love with the idT5 engine and I cant wait to pay Doom (4).
Lets be honest, I bought Zone of the Enders 2 for the MGS: Sons of Liberty demo and this this is not very different. I had a feeling this game was going to be awesome but what sealed the deal for me was the Doom Beta. I am pleasantly surprised by how good this game is above my expectations. It stands on it own as one of my favorite Story Driven FPSs of all time. I was expecting a 7-8/10 and I got a 9/10. I feel the people at MachineGames knocked this one out of the park. I will keep an eye on this studio and impatiently await their next title.

My "Hundred Hour" review:
Dirty Bomb has become my guilty pleasure. Not because I'm embarassed to play it, but because I always leave feeling guilty for having done so. The game feels like it's so close to being a very solid, fun game, but is hindered by a misstep or two. First the good I suppose:
Pros:
Great graphics and graphic style, players easy to distinguish from enviornment.
Appropriate sized teams, didn't fall prey to the hunger for 24+ player servers which causes mayhem.
Decent objective modes, though I would have liked to see something other than a CS spinoff for the newer one.
Fun, fast paced games.
It's free
Cons:
The loadout system is a mess. It shouldn't even exist. Unlocking a Merc should give you one loadout, without needing to add extra nonsense in to the game that just confuses players to be honest. Opening cases should give cosmetics or something other than crappy loadouts, forcing you to buy the one thats signifcantly better for the merc anyway.
It feels like too much was taken from the gunplay. I may have played Counter-Strike for the better part of a decade, but I'm not here to compare the two, or wish DB was more like CS. On the contrary, I came to DB to escape the seriousness and toxicity of CS. However, in CS, regardless of all the nuances and strategy, the game is built around gun-play. Your life depends on your aim. In DB I don't get that feeling ever. I know thats bound to happen in a game with player abilities and airstrikes etc, but it feels too cluttered by those abilities and doesn't feel like the better aimer comes out ahead.
I unfortunately think DB missed it's golden window to gain a solid player base. I think that regardless of the Devs efforts, future patches are just going to see lower and lower player counts. It's really a shame because I feel like it was a few tweaks away from being a great game.
I'm sure this seems like a mostly negative review, but I do honestly recommend this game. It is great fun, and I will continue to play it every so often. I just wish it hit the right marks when it had the chance.

Winning and loot are now handed out based on who won, it used to be about how well you did and that upsets me because getting into the game is that much more rediculously hard. you may only use one weapon type at a time, this limits just how useful you can be at any given time but makes some sense. Lastly the thing i am most upset about is medics were made nearly usless, they can't deal the little amount of damage they did before and now everyone has an automatic heal when not taking damage like in CoD so the whole class recieved a kick in the nuts.
If you like team based combat, building, and puzzle solving then you may get some good hours out of this, it takes investment though and is vastly improved by playing with a friend.
The weapon variety has also exploded since it first came out, theres so many different stratedgies you'll probably find one you like, but also then find the team it absolutly doesn't work against, this happens and it just part of the game. your team mates and enemies make all the difference, but mostly try to have fun.

One of the few games on the market capable of producing combat on a truly massive scale, and definitely the best. Four completely open world continents, three warring empires, six in depth classes, infantry, aerial and armored combat, all come together to create an experience like no other. And best of all, it's completely free. No single class feels more overpowered than the others, (with the notable exception of the Max, which has numerous heavy restrictions on it to prevent it from being abused) and the game actually rewards you for playing support classes, unlike many others. And for a free to play game, it is remarkably well balanced. As a free player, I never felt as if I needed to purchase a subscription in order to keep up with paid members. The default guns are some of the best in the game, (Especially so for the Vanu Sovereignty) and most purchases you would need a subscription for are cosmetics. All in all, this game is a unique and addicting experience, full of base raids, air strikes, tank columns, crushing the New Conglomerate in every single large battle, jumping out of gunships with your platoon, high octane combat, and true massive warfare. 10/10 BTW, join the Vanu, we have the best guns and coolest tanks. Stay away from the NC, they're useless.

After the demise of AoEO, this game is a nice bit of nostalgia to fill the void. While I can't particularly get into the dated multiplayer(even though it has a "thriving" community), a good RTS campaign is always a great time filler.
The original game and expansion need nothing new said about them. They are classics.
Unfortunately, there are some issues with the new Forgotten expansion. More like a set of fan campaigns, they feel decidedly less professional than the original campaigns. No unique voice acting, some strange choices that bring to mind old school questionable attempts at original Starcraft "RPG" maps(clicking on individual units to advance dialogue... really?), and just an overall tediousness to the design of the missions.
And as a complete achievement ♥♥♥♥♥(though primarily on console) I would be remiss to not mention this game's ... um, let's say... "daunting"... set of achievements. Thousands of games played, tens of thousands of buildings lost(not destroyed by you, but LOST by you), etc. It's fairly ridiculous to say the least.
In short, the original game is amazing and worth picking up. The modern additions, not so enticing. Definitely worth playing, but if you have the original retail game sitting around like many people unless you just really feel like getting in some multiplayer on the title, stick with what you got. If you don't have the original or never played it, a definite buy.

With new dedicated multiplayer, expanded resolution, built-in Twitch support, and ongoing support community, this game is a must-have for real-time strategy fans. One of the finest titles of the Age of Empires series has been given the support it needs to enhance the game for long-time fans, as well as introduce new players to the series. With most of the initial bumps smoothened, Hidden Path and Skybox have done a great job in bringing this game back for the modern gaming community.
The Forgotten Expansion is a must-have too. Incredible scenarios, new civs, and continuous support from the mod's development team has made The Forgotten one of the finest add-ons to any game I've played.
My only mark against it is the lack of functionality of its Workshop. While AoE2 HD has a diverse Workshop community, getting mods to appear in-game is a lot more difficult than it should be. Often, the "subscribe" button doesn't seem to initiate a download, and many times mods simply aren't loaded. It's a shame, since this is pretty much the only major flaw in an otherwise great reboot.

Hello I'm Cosmic and welcome to the latest addition to the Wolfenstein franchise, Wolfenstein The New Order. This new sequel to the much beloved FPS franchise has been developed by Machine games who are a Swedish developer formed in 2009 and hold experienced developers who worked on both Riddick and the Darkness video games.
So finally we are back in the shoes of the Nazi killing machine that is William 'B.J' Blazkoviz. Those familiar with the previous Wolfenstien titles will know that Blazkoviz is the reoccurring main protagonist. Once again your pitted against General William Strasse more commonly known as Deathshead. The New order takes place in an alternate reality of 1960 where the Nazi's somehow found advanced technology that allowed them to win world war 2 and thus take over the world. Blazkoviz was injured in 1946 at an assualt on deathshead compound and spends 14 years in a polish mental hospital. Once he awakens he sets of to find the resistance and take the fight back to the Nazi world regime.

Despite the slew of strategy games that I've played in the past ten years, there is no game that I have returned to with a greater passion than Age of Empires II. Its arcadey gameplay style does not detract from the epicness as you advance from the Dark Ages to the early Renaissance. Watching your population grow, armies expand, and cities grow is as exciting as commanding armies in large one-on-one fights. Sounds and visuals may be dated, but still entertaining. The availability of Mods and minigames designed by other fans makes the game worth so much more than $20.
If there's one complaint, it's that not enough people want to play the Forgotten Expansion online, which is a shame as the expansion improves the gameplay with more civilizations, maps, and game modes. I highly recommend that history and strategy game fans pick up the full Age of Empires II HD + Forgotten Expansion during a Steam Sale when the price drops to around $10. I've been playing this game for quite a while now, on and off, and I really cannot recommend it enough. This game is 100x better when you play in a good platoon and outfit, and 100x better yet when you play with friends. But don't get me wrong, I typically play it alone simply because it is, unfortunately, quite a demanding game, and not all my friends' computer can run it. So lets start off with the basic gameplay quality - speed.
Most of the demand is placed on the CPU, but if you want to enjoy the beautiful (if VERY slightly unrealistic graphics), you'll want to have a good GPU. On my i7 5829k + 2x GTX 970 Gamings, it gets anywhere between 174fps in near-empty regions, to 34fps in massive 96+ vs 96+ battles (though keep in mind that this is with a tiny +0.2GHz overclock, for a total of 3.5GHz). If you have any form of a decent (~£20-£30) CPU cooler and can go up higher, it should never drop below 60fps. Graphical settings don't seem to affect with game too much, even with only 1 GTX 970 - the difference between lowest and ultra settings is about 10-20fps, and the visual change is huge. The problem is the client-side processing that puts heavy strain on your CPU.
Now let's get fun factor. This game has 6 classes:
Infiltrator (can use temporary cloak as sniper/weak gunner, or perma-cloak but only use the sidearm)
Light Assault - fast guns with very low recoil, and jetpacks
Heavy Assault - Powerful guns that can also be fast, but with huge recoil. Can use different forms of "nanite-mesh" (activated shield) to defend themselves
Engineer - has the same starter gun as a light assault, but no jetpack. They acn, however, fix vehicles and Maxx suits. Best used as drivers or Maxx supporters
Medic - has a suprisingly powerful starting with really low recoil and high quality scopes to choose from. Heals players. Best used as for the start, because they can earn the most points quickly, letting the new player unlock weapons and upgrades for other classes/vehicles.
MAXX - uses two powerful guns, controlled independently, on each arm, and has two health bars instead of the typical health and shield bar - this, however, means that they cannot regen their shields (since they don't exist). Can only be healed by an engineer.
There are three empires:
The Vanu Sovereignty (purple/cyan) is based around exploiting alien technology. They use plasma/laser rifles (don't worry, not the weak♥♥♥♥♥♥from the Fallout games), and because of that they have barely any bullet drop over large distances. Their faction-specific fighter jet, the Scythe, is by far the most manouverable plane in the game, and (I believe) has the cheapest first new weapon you can buy - only 100 certs (I think the other faction's first is 250 certs).
The Terran Republic (red/black) is the original faction. They look like they should be the toughest guys... But, in fact, they are not. Their weapons have the smallest cone of fire (least bullet spread over distance, highest accuracy), they have the largest magazines, and some of the fastest-firing weapons in the game - including the minigun. Their faction-specific fighter jet is the Mosquito. It is the faster jet in the game. Plus, you get awesome voiceovers when you kill one ("Swatted a mosquito", "Splat").
The New Conglomerate (blue/yellow) are the rebels. They don't have large clips of ammo - they don't need to. They instead have the hardest hitting weapons, and the hardest armour on all their vehicles. Their snipers also get access to my absolute favourite sniper rifle - the AF-8 RailJack. Whereas most sniper rifle's bullets travel slowly so you need to aim a far in frontof & above your enemy, the RailJack instead has a longer delay between the pull of the trigger and the firing of the weapon, but they it travels super fast and hardly drops at all (I only aim at most 5mm above my enemies from hundreds of metres away). This counters the idea of aiming in far in front of your enemy, because you can instead just trace them with your rifle, and it'll hit them. Their faction-specific figher jet is the Reaver - it's slow, possibly the slowest of the bunch, but it has the faster Afterburner (limited speed boost that recovers for a bit after use), and the strongest armour of the three.
I would say that planes aren't something for new players, though - they're not only difficult to control, they are also VERY easy to shoot down by experienced pilots and any turret. But for this, we have the Training Facility - it holds no enemies, but lets you test every weapon/vehicle/upgrade without having to spend any certs. It also has no real enemies, just player-like dummies. TIP - new pilots should head to Amerish or Hossin - Amerish has the most new pilots, so you're less likely to get screwed over flying, and both contintents have a LOT of trees for cover from fire or tracking missiles.
The game gives you 3 free character slots, so you can easily play as each empire (like I do), but more are unlockable if you want to play on characters (if, say, you want to play on different servers).
The game is amazing, but it can have moments of waiting around for certain classes (though that only seems to happen when playing alone). The long-range Infiltrator (sniper), for example, when you're waiting for the enemy to come in-range when they attack, or to appear in the courtyard, or when you're attacking an enemy base and they're all hidden inside. This can be countered by the recent addition of the "stalker" infiltrator, though. But, of course, you could equally change to any of the other classes to get some more action.
Speaking of action, this game is packed with it if you join a platoon (which is simple, 1 button when you log in). And it definitely has it's moments. I'd talk about mine, but I'm not very good at action-packed descriptions, so instead look at the other reviews here.
The tutorial is quite crap, but there is a metric ♥♥♥♥ton of amazing ones online. I'd suggest looking at Angry Joe's Angry Army training that he recorded. Extremely useful stuff for new and experienced players.
A lot of people here will say that it's pay-to-win. Definitely not true - the first weapons you start with will, a lot of the time, be the best weapons you use. The devs seem to have picked the most commonly used fighting types, and gave the weapons that use them to you as a starter. The only thing new weapons change is the style of gameplay. For example, the Vanu Heavy Assaults start off with the Orion. A lot of people (myself included... Sometimes) like to replace it with the Flare. The Flare does more damage... But it is far slower in fire-rate, letting you play a bit more like the NC faction. For a lot of people (myself included... Sometimes) the Orion is the best weapon for most situations, whereas the Flare can be used once you aquire a better aim. The only things you can only use real money for are cosmetic customisations. Points can be hard to earn at first, but you'll soon(ish) be earning hundreds every hour or so, or more (I'm just not a very good FPS player. T.T)
During the day, multiple platoons travel across the 4 continents, engaging in massive, spectacular firefights and seiges that feel entirely scripted, better than in any movie, yet it's all done through organic interaction, no scripts involved. At night, remnants of the platoons and lone wolf players (like me. :3) that tugged alone with them take the bases over, usually facing off very few opponents in assassin-styled standoffs.
Like I said before, I cannot recommend this game enough. If I forgot something, please leave a comment and I'll explain that too. :)

Here's the interesting thing about Wolfenstein: The New Order. It's good for about the first two thirds. Like, really, legitimately, genuinely good. As you traverse the game's world, from the narrow confines of Nazi castles to the vast expanses of National Socialism-inspired, Albrecht Speer-like monstrous concrete cities, you find yourself taking it all in and saying: "Wow, these guys really did their homework!"
And then the ♥♥♥♥ing sewer level happens. And it all goes to♥♥♥♥♥♥from there.
Here's the thing, boys and girls -- much like Far Cry 3 before it, TNO is an excellent example of how to construct complex characters in a whimsical fantasy world. You're never inundated with too much exposition on how things got to be the way they did (and hint: they just did, because Nazis), which renders your protagonist as a thoroughly unreliable narrator. This scenario isn't helped any by the fact that B.J. Blazkowicz, the returning protagonist of the previous fifteen million iterations of the series, suffers a severe head trauma early on in the game. This presents an interesting quandary for us, the gamers: is B.J. really killing all those Nazis, or is everything just playing out in his head as his neurons are firing their final, Jacob's Ladder style? The latter interpretation explains so much about the game's narrative structure, particularly how certain characters are rendered alive even though they are chronologically older than both my grandparents put together -- or, indeed, how certain other characters (COUGH Caroline Becker COUGH, no spoilers there) make the miraculous recovery from the malaise of ♥♥♥♥ING DEATH.
But narrative complexity, involved and storied though it may be, is clearly not the focus here. The focus is killing Nazis. I mean, this IS a Wolfenstein game, and as such, there's a contractually mandated NPS (that's Nazis Per Second) rate at which you must progress through the game, painting the walls with a decidedly Jackson Pollock-esque splatter of blood, brains, and ichor. And, shockingly, for roughly sixty to seventy percent of the game, it's really good times. The weapons in your orchestra of destruction range from the sneaky to the loud, but all are decidedly mundane, eschewing the decidedly more amusing Particle Cannon, Tesla Cannon, and Flamethrower in favor of shotguns, rifles, and machineguns. This move, in my opinion, is the game's first misstep, as one of the more positive features of 2009's Wolfenstein was the variety of creative ways in which you could ruin National Socialism's day -- and trust me, few things are as viscerally gratifying as setting a Schützstaffel commando on fire, zapping him with a Tesla coil, and putting a bullet in his scrotum for good measure.
I do not, I repeat, do NOT need therapy.
All kidding aside, Nazi hatred as just part of being human. They are the universally reviled evil, so therefore it is a crying shame that Machine, TNO's developer, sheepishly resorts to the most fundamental tools of destruction. As for the enemies themselves, while their numberless atrocities and innate predisposition towards pure, unrefined evil makes them easy targets to splatter against various surroundings, their variety peters out within the first three hours or so. More disappointing (and ultimately frustrating) are the stealth sequences the game occasionally forces on you. While we are at it, new rule, Machine Games: if you're planning on putting stealth segments into your game, please make sure they are adequately integrated. Give the gamers options to track enemies' movements and so forth, rather than just artificially dumbing their AI and IQ down so that a Hauptmann literally stepping over a downed Unterfeldwebel's corpse and into a pool of his blood doesn't just go "Huh. I wonder what kind of bratwurst the dining hall is serving today" and go about his business. Sadly, the stealth elements really take you out of the game's sense of flow, and ruin the progression somewhat by giving you an inconsistent difficulty level and forcing you to reload when said Hauptmann finally gets wise to all your taffing about and calls down five hundred ♥♥♥♥ing guards on your♥♥♥♥♥
The part where the game really screws the pooch is the ending (as mentioned above, it's the sewer level that kicks this in motion). It's as if the game forgets the "fun" component that was so central to its first two acts, and decides to kick you in the balls by confusing challenge with difficulty. Whereas the early portions of the game are interesting to look at, play around in, and destroy, the latter parts are exercises in frustration. Even the detour to the Moon, in the game's casual nod to "Iron Sky," fails to capture the pulp fiction nature of the game up to this point. All of the sudden, the story begins taking itself much more seriously than it has before, and culminates in a profoundly disappointing ending, much to my chagrin. While sequel-baiting is fine and good and all, when you build up your main villain to be so degenerate and cruel that he Absolutely Has To Die™ at the end, you can't just yank the rug out from under the gamers' feet and have him♥♥♥♥♥♥block your revenge boner! A few loose ends abound in the plot, and the fade-to-black nature of the conclusion leaves one with the biggest pair of blue balls this side of Modern Warfare 2's single-player campaign.
Speaking of the CoDs, this game will draw an inevitable comparison to Activision's flagship franchise, as both are military shooters. Where TNO really steals the show from CoD is its focus and length. With most single player campaigns clocking in at barely 4 hours, TNO manages to extend the joy to 6-8, depending on your playing style and skill level. I must confess, however, that at least a full hour of that time is spent scavenging ammo from your fallen enemies. That's right: every time you need to replenish your stocks, you have to press E. Press E. PRESS E. PRESS ♥♥♥♥ING E FOR ♥♥♥♥'S SAKE GOD DAMN YOU MACHINE GAMES THIS ISN'T ♥♥♥♥ING HARD! Just... just... make the player automatically pick up any ammo he walks over. I mean, seriously, how did this one play out in your minds? Did you honestly imagine people playing this game going: "Hmm... ammo. Ya know, I might just need less ammo for this next segment. Think I'll give this ammo clip a pass." Seriously, what in the ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥? Even the original Wolf3D had automatic ammunition pickups, you asshats! Also, while the game is devoid of any multiplayer (thank ♥♥♥♥ing God), there is some incentive for replayability. Various in-game actions reward B.J. with perks, which can be tailored to fit a specific play style. Of course, this part of the game is also broken in a weird way: the stealth perks are among the easiest to achieve, and yet they are also the most useless. On average, you get to spend maybe, MAYBE ten percent of the game killing Nazis silently. And yet, while I was able to fill out my Stealth perk tree, I had to struggle like a salmon going upstream to get even the most basic Heavy Weapon perk, which should be deftly accomplished by blowing up two Nazis with one grenade. Seriously, what the ♥♥♥♥? I know I'm better at games than this. Such technical issues abound throughout, are too numerous to mention, and while they don't ruin the game, they definitely make me wonder what the hell the dev team was thinking as they were putting their code into action.
To conclude, while TNO is by no means bad (it is a B effort at worst) its lack of ambition reduces its impact to mediocrity. This is especially obvious when contrasted against the inspired narrative structure and the occasional nudge-nudge-wink-winks to previous titles in the series. At full price, I can't recommend this game. Wait for it to drop down to twenty bucks, and then it might be worth your dollars, depending on how strongly you disagree with the tenets of National Socialism.

Overview: Planetside 2 is the largest FPS MMO I have ever seen. I have put in over 1000 hours into this game ~350 on Steam and at least 700 on the client from their site. If you enjoy working with teams(Platoons/ Squads) to battle the enemy. Then this game is for you
~~~Pros~~~
+3 Factions help to prevent stalemates, they happen but usually end quickly
+Some, not as much as many of us would like, faction specific  weapons that help create diverse battles ensuring that  each battle is unique
+Hundreds of players no matter the time of day and some fights are hundreds of players on both sides in a small area
+ 4 continents with many bases on each(continents are ~7km x ~7 km each)
+Membership or station cash are not needed for anything other than cosmetics allowing players to get everything without paying a cent
+Tons of fun to have
+Hours of content
~~~Cons~~~
+Company layoffs in early 2015(time of writing) have stalled progress
+Many ideas were put on a roadmap for development but with such a large game they were pushed or forgotten about
+Bugs! so many of them While most are not game breaking it gets a little annoying after a long period of time(They are working on fixes ATM)
+Not optimized all that well. While it can be played on any decent gaming PC, to max it out at 1080p @ 60FPS with everything on Ultra you need an extremely high end PC. However don't let this deture you. I built my glorious rig just to be able to play this game. On Ultra @ 1920x1200 I get 30-60FPS with a 3.5ghz quad core intel i7 with a GTX780. When it drops is usually because I'm in a huge war zone with hundreds of players, vehicles, and aircraft. But the somewhat poor optimization does not help it in this area
~~~Rating~~~
Give it a try! It is free what do you have to lose? I recommend this game to everyone I meet. This game despite the bugs is a shining example of the power of PC games compared to consoles.

text:
Wolfenstein: The New Order review:
Pros:
+ Keeps the classic gameplay of Wolfenstein 3D but more improved.
+ Objective markers only appear when you come near it, no handholding.
+ Dual weapon mechanics is just functional and kickass.
+ Health and armour system keeping it classic with abit of regeneration.
+ Vehicle sections are not too long or too short, also very functional and fun.
+ Every level was unique in some way, completely different textures and buildings (explains the 40GB install size)
+ Proper boss fights.
+ Soundtrack fits the situations perfectly.
+ Enemies are fun to kill while still being a challenge.
+ Secrets that make you want to replay the game for.
+ Destructible cover, game telling you to not coward like a ♥♥♥♥♥.
+ Extremely well done story.
+ Cutscenes make the game feel like and movie with stunning visuals and so on, you won't even feel the need to skip it. Also some of the cutscenes will make you cry.
+ Every friendly character is likable, none of them will annoy you.
+ Antagonists are hate-able (in a good way) and getting revenge from them is just the best feeling.
+ BJ Blazkowitz is the best protagonist I've played so far, kills loads of people and doesn't be a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥about it, is funny, has a heart and isn't a egomaniac (Yes I am looking at you Duke Nukem).
Cons:
- Lag issues
- Texture loading problems
- Crashes sometimes
- There was one time were it reloaded to a checkpoint for no reason
- Death animation is clunky
- When map is reloaded, weapons that were dropped previously on the floor will not re-spawn.
- Stealth is as broken as Metro 2033's stealth system (This game is about guns blazing so wouldn't be much of a problem)
- The ending was a huge plothole. Really they should atleast say what happens to the world next.
Verdict: 8.5/10

It's a fairly solid game overall. I can live without multiplayer; unless the game is a dedicated multiplayer game, MP seems like a crappy, tacked-on afterthought anyways. I prefer a solid SP or MP game rather than two sub-par halves crammed together.
As far as the game goes, id Tech 5 is a wicked engine. Some deformable terrain, damage realistically displayed on enemies (sometimes graphically so, as the energy weapons later on will show), without being terribly system-demanding, and always seemed smooth. I find it worth noting I never once had any glitches or slowdown in this game. Truly a rarity these days (especially when Bethesda is involved, COUGH COUGH).
The story is quite interesting, and even though some of the characters are a bit flat and undeveloped at times, and there's a couple of instances where for the sake of plot you need to suspend your disbelief, it's fairly believable. Plus, you get to shoot space Nazis on the ♥♥♥♥ing Moon. With lasers. It's like Stanley Kubrick directed 2001: A Space Odyssey with Nazis in it. And lasers.
The gameplay is top-notch. Everything is fluid, from movements, to context sensitive abilities like vaulting, and the stealth/cover systems are as about as non-cumbersome as you can get. You're not stuck to surfaces, and can transition quickly from cover to cover. Not that it's necessary to; unlike that one section everyone remembers from Return to Castle Wolfenstein, stealth in this game is entirely OPTIONAL. It may make your life easier, such as in taking out Commanders to prevent them from calling reinforcements, but you can also just dual-wield and mow down everything that lives. Gunplay in this is absolutely BRUTAL. Dismembered limbs, exploding heads, exploding bodies, stabbing people in the face, chest, temple, leg...if you've ever wanted the definitive Nazi-killing simulator, The New Order is it.

After 30 hours of playtime and 100% of achievements completed on 'Uber' difficulty, I feel I am ready to rate Wolfenstein: The New Order. Between the well-crafted levels and deep character driven story-telling, this game is easily one of the best modern shooters. The Nazi regalia art deco style thrived off creative and believable level design. That is to say, the graphics are stunning and tuned to the story as much as old great titles a Half-life or Golden Eye were. There is such fine detail that the weapon models are different for the era and location.
The characters brought the game to life with beautiful true to the moment animations. The animations were cinematic throughout the game. The tempo and pacing of the voice acting over the animations were fluid and felt real. The outlandish game had a believable band of characters that truly came to life beyond previous standards.
The mechanics offers fairly tight shooting while the gameplay offers various styles of play; Stealth, Run-and-Gun, Explosives. You could go cover hopping while dual wielding rocket launchers or silently takedown enemies with special knife attacks or equipping a silenced pistol to avoid alarms. However, you can mortally wound a foe by throw a knife into his foot.
The AI was ok. The soldier enemies used cover well and the heavily armored foes close the gap and cause a lot of trouble for your health bar. I did encounter enemies that tried to throw grenades through pillars killing themselves and anyone nearby.

The maximum difficulty felt like less of a challenge and more of it took a lot of bullets to kill everything other than yourself making shotguns the bane of your existence.
All in all, I know I raved about the story-telling being amazing, and I mean it. On my first play through I felt like I was watching a two-hour film you would gladly pay $20 to see. Instead, I got a 15 hour experience for $60 dollars, that I could watch again with different mechanics, levels, and characters.

Classic shooters like DOOM, Shadow Warrior and Duke Nukem are slowly being killed off by generic and linear first person shooters. We were treated to quite some reboots and re-imaginings of classics lately, like Rise of the Triad, Duke Nukem Forever, Shadow Warrior 2013 to name a few. Some were good, but some were severely lacking their original vibe (for example regenerating health or a weapon carrying limit). Hearing about
rekindled the old flames inside me that enthousiastically was waiting to bring some of those classic shooters in a modern coat, but I remained sceptical, because the line between a classic shooter and a modern-day parotic reboot is surprisingly thin. I expected it to be a seven-out-of-ten game based on what I had seen and heard about it, and for the first two hours of the game it was exactly that. After that, however,
downright blew me away and immediately did everything right in a matter of minutes, raising my final score to a nine out of ten.
The Pros:
· Classic shooters and killing nazi's fit together like pancakes and Nutella: it may be a bit sticky and eye-rollingly cliché at first, but damn is it good and satisfying.
· A high-quality story with fantastic voice-acting and an sickly interresting main villain like we rarely/never get to see in modern-day shooters anymore.
·
's gameplay feels authentic without ever feeling like you've already seen it all. Guns handle very well and have a great feel to them, stealth options allow you to approach certain situations differently without  giving you the feeling that you have to go down that certain path, levels flow from tight corridors into larger open areas, and so on. It's jam-packed with features that are bound to attract almost any kind of gamer.
The Cons:
· Every item has to be picked up individually. For example, you can't just run over weapons to collect their ammo or run over armor to wear it. It's not the biggest problem in the world, but I felt like it interrupted the game's pacing at some points.
· For a single-player only game, I personally think 40 GB is a whole lot of space to spend on it. Not that it affects the game in any way, but some people simply can't spend that much space on installing a game. (Even though it's not really a gameplay-related downside, I decided to list it anyway just so you're aware of that. Hell, I have to list SOME downsides.)
The Visuals:
· A-f**king-mazing. Stunning lighting, very solid animations, indrecible textures, fantastic overal design and so on. Definately one of the prettiest games in recent memory.
Final Verdict:
·
is easy to love and hard to hate. Some of its minor flaws can easily be overlooked with the high quality it delivers, as it finds the perfect way to bring a classic shooter in a modern-day coat without losing ANY of its charm. 9/10.

I noticed that many of the reviews here were written before the authors finished the game. I would be singing the same tune as most of these people, but the latter third of the game is nothing but a disappointment.
The developers definitely tried to instill a bit of personality into BJ, our protagonist. He's no longer the hunk of nothingness from the prior games. BJ is now a thoughtful human being. Not a critical moment passes without an internal monologue delivered by him. These moments are a nice touch. His supporting cast is also decent. Some of the characters are quite intriguing. Unfortunately, not much is done with most of these characters. While some are quickly killed before you get a chance to know them, others are cast aside and left with little to do towards the end of the game. Even the main antagonist was given this treatment. He's only seen in the first and last level.
Although the attempts to instill some humanity into the narrative is admirable, it's also heavy-handed at times. Too often is the player reminded of the protatgonist's predicaments. We understand that BJ is a man with a conscience, but he does not have to be in agnony throughout the entire game. The presence of a forced romantic subplot doesn't help. Their motivation for engaging in said romance is never explored. It just happens after a large body-count. Wolfenstein's story is one that's yearning for some subtlety. There's potential, but it's not quite there.
The level design is possibly the saving grace of this game. There's a fair balance of stealth and combat in the earlier levels, where the stealth routes felt natural, and stealth sections were even spaced between combat scenarios. However, the levels denegerate into sheer chaos in later levels. This would fine, but as the game advanced, the environments also became more bland. While earlier levels were located in interesting locations, like an asylum and a concentration camp, later levels predominately took place in the interiors of generic military structures. Additionally, the officers that you must eliminate to prevent the arrival of reinforcements don't have much of a presence in said later levels, taking away a layer of depth that the game desperately needs.
Wolfenstein is a game that I really wanted to like. The developers definitely tried to reinvent the franchise with a more human and personable story, but between the ham-fisted dialogue and the amount of missed potential, I can't recommend Wolfenstein. It would be a fine game to pick up when it's on sale, but not for full price.

After 30 hours of playtime and 100% of achievements completed on 'Uber' difficulty, I feel I am ready to rate Wolfenstein: The New Order. Between the well-crafted levels and deep character driven story-telling, this game is easily one of the best modern shooters. The Nazi regalia art deco style thrived off creative and believable level design. That is to say, the graphics are stunning and tuned to the story as much as old great titles a Half-life or Golden Eye were. There is such fine detail that the weapon models are different for the era and location.
The characters brought the game to life with beautiful true to the moment animations. The animations were cinematic throughout the game. The tempo and pacing of the voice acting over the animations were fluid and felt real. The outlandish game had a believable band of characters that truly came to life beyond previous standards.
The mechanics offers fairly tight shooting while the gameplay offers various styles of play; Stealth, Run-and-Gun, Explosives. You could go cover hopping while dual wielding rocket launchers or silently takedown enemies with special knife attacks or equipping a silenced pistol to avoid alarms. However, you can mortally wound a foe by throw a knife into his foot.
The AI was ok. The soldier enemies used cover well and the heavily armored foes close the gap and cause a lot of trouble for your health bar. I did encounter enemies that tried to throw grenades through pillars killing themselves and anyone nearby.
Often considered related to AI is the difficulty options. There are five to choose from harkening back to the original Wolfenstein in theme. I only played the 'Uber' difficulty so, I don't know how much the experience differs. The maximum difficulty felt like less of a challenge and more of it took a lot of bullets to kill everything other than yourself making shotguns the bane of your existence.
All in all, I know I raved about the story-telling being amazing, and I mean it. On my first play through I felt like I was watching a two-hour film you would gladly pay $20 to see. Instead, I got a 15 hour experience for $60 dollars, that I could watch again with different mechanics, levels, and characters.
I highly recommend this game. Fair warning, this game is rated 17 plus. Contains a lot of violence and gore. Also, has some, believe it or not, tasteful sex scenes.

Classic shooters like DOOM, Shadow Warrior and Duke Nukem are slowly being killed off by generic and linear first person shooters. We were treated to quite some reboots and re-imaginings of classics lately, like Rise of the Triad, Duke Nukem Forever, Shadow Warrior 2013 to name a few. Some were good, but some were severely lacking their original vibe (for example regenerating health or a weapon carrying limit). Hearing about
rekindled the old flames inside me that enthousiastically was waiting to bring some of those classic shooters in a modern coat, but I remained sceptical, because the line between a classic shooter and a modern-day parotic reboot is surprisingly thin. I expected it to be a seven-out-of-ten game based on what I had seen and heard about it, and for the first two hours of the game it was exactly that. After that, however,
downright blew me away and immediately did everything right in a matter of minutes, raising my final score to a nine out of ten.
The Pros:
· Classic shooters and killing nazi's fit together like pancakes and Nutella: it may be a bit sticky and eye-rollingly cliché at first, but damn is it good and satisfying.
· A high-quality story with fantastic voice-acting and an sickly interresting main villain like we rarely/never get to see in modern-day shooters anymore.
·
's gameplay feels authentic without ever feeling like you've already seen it all. Guns handle very well and have a great feel to them, stealth options allow you to approach certain situations differently without  giving you the feeling that you have to go down that certain path, levels flow from tight corridors into larger open areas, and so on. It's jam-packed with features that are bound to attract almost any kind of gamer.
The Cons:
· Every item has to be picked up individually. For example, you can't just run over weapons to collect their ammo or run over armor to wear it. It's not the biggest problem in the world, but I felt like it interrupted the game's pacing at some points.
· For a single-player only game, I personally think 40 GB is a whole lot of space to spend on it. Not that it affects the game in any way, but some people simply can't spend that much space on installing a game. (Even though it's not really a gameplay-related downside, I decided to list it anyway just so you're aware of that. Hell, I have to list SOME downsides.)
The Visuals:
· A-f**king-mazing. Stunning lighting, very solid animations, indrecible textures, fantastic overal design and so on. Definately one of the prettiest games in recent memory.
Final Verdict:
·
is easy to love and hard to hate. Some of its minor flaws can easily be overlooked with the high quality it delivers, as it finds the perfect way to bring a classic shooter in a modern-day coat without losing ANY of its charm. 9/10.

I noticed that many of the reviews here were written before the authors finished the game. I would be singing the same tune as most of these people, but the latter third of the game is nothing but a disappointment.
The developers definitely tried to instill a bit of personality into BJ, our protagonist. He's no longer the hunk of nothingness from the prior games. BJ is now a thoughtful human being. Not a critical moment passes without an internal monologue delivered by him. These moments are a nice touch. His supporting cast is also decent. Some of the characters are quite intriguing. Unfortunately, not much is done with most of these characters. While some are quickly killed before you get a chance to know them, others are cast aside and left with little to do towards the end of the game. Even the main antagonist was given this treatment. He's only seen in the first and last level.
Although the attempts to instill some humanity into the narrative is admirable, it's also heavy-handed at times. Too often is the player reminded of the protatgonist's predicaments. We understand that BJ is a man with a conscience, but he does not have to be in agnony throughout the entire game. The presence of a forced romantic subplot doesn't help. Their motivation for engaging in said romance is never explored. It just happens after a large body-count. Wolfenstein's story is one that's yearning for some subtlety. There's potential, but it's not quite there.
The level design is possibly the saving grace of this game. There's a fair balance of stealth and combat in the earlier levels, where the stealth routes felt natural, and stealth sections were even spaced between combat scenarios. However, the levels denegerate into sheer chaos in later levels. This would fine, but as the game advanced, the environments also became more bland. While earlier levels were located in interesting locations, like an asylum and a concentration camp, later levels predominately took place in the interiors of generic military structures. Additionally, the officers that you must eliminate to prevent the arrival of reinforcements don't have much of a presence in said later levels, taking away a layer of depth that the game desperately needs.
Wolfenstein is a game that I really wanted to like. The developers definitely tried to reinvent the franchise with a more human and personable story, but between the ham-fisted dialogue and the amount of missed potential, I can't recommend Wolfenstein. It would be a fine game to pick up when it's on sale, but not for full price.

Well, I gotta say there isn't a lot of positive stuff here to say. I like the core gameplay of Robocraft but everything else around it is dull, patronizing, or worse trying to claw at my pocket book to the point what I do like about it is cheapened enough to not make me want to play. I will give you a quick overview of each problem I have, then details on what happened. Please note these thoughts are coming from an older woman who is just getting back into video games, so my opinion might not matter as much as I do not think this game is targeted at people like myself.
On the quick:
-Not very useful
-Teaches the player things that are learned within the first minute of game play
-Does not teach from the ground up
-Uses premade assets (bot almost finished)
-Does not give me information about WHY I should build the way it wants me to
-Does not let you keep the blocks used to make the robot.
-Crate it gives you for it doesn't give you the back row of items, it is insulting
-Constantly flashes "Well done. Nice job" at you, extremely patronizing
-Treats you like a small child
Overall I have nothing positive to say about the tutorial, I don't even like how the items it gave me was presented. It made me feel like the game thinks me a small child, as if I cannot figure out the most basic of functions and gameplay. It doesn't teach me anything particularly useful nor does it reward you proper.
Look at how rude this is, giving me a crate and keeping half of it locked:
When I went into the tutorial it prompted me to do some extremely basic things, things like place a leg on the bot then place six cubes to finish the bot's arm. My biggest problem with this is how I already know all of this, I have figured this stuff out within the very first minute of gameplay when I started it up so perhaps it is mildly useful to someone who hasn't played at all? It seems like someone would normally do exactly as I did and simply mess around with the blocks and make something (I started playing a few days before the update). This tutorial does not teach me how to build a robot from the ground up, it doesn't even let me keep the blocks used in the tutorial. To make matters worse it is amazing patronizing flashing "Well done. Nice job" over and over like I am a small child needing to be complemented for every action I take. Finally you take this bot and are thrust into a small training mode that lasts about 20 seconds, the game tells you how to move and shoot, all in text boxes like before while building, then tells you to blow up a rather impressive looking robot covered in cosmetics.
On the quick:
-Much higher difficult than player vs player matches
-Much less rewarding than player vs player matches (1 item vs 3)
-Takes just as long as player vs player matches
-You will fight better robots than your own mostly
-Is worthless to all degrees given you must:
A) have a constant internet connection and cannot play offline
B) Have an easier time playing against players anyway
Again, nothing positive to say.
Now I’ve only recently started playing, only with three days and a slight handful of hours under my belt. That being said I think I’ve been doing pretty good, have some matches:
I think I’m doing pretty well for myself. That being said the AI match I played was significantly harder than those I have been playing against players. Normally my matches are complete dominations with the enemy team barely scoring a few points. This AI match however was a lot closer and took A LOT more effort out of me, and for what? This:
Really? Just this? I am rewarded with a single item? I fought several bots built better than my own that all aim better than I do, struggling in a match that takes just as long as one vs players and I only get 1/3rd the reward? Why have this at all? I believe the developers of this game have taken a massive misstep in creating these AI matches, they are entirely worthless to me as I cannot play them while offline because Robocraft requires a constant connection to the Internet and they reward me less for more work.
Pros:
-Fun for those who like the rush of the gamble
-Although random, it is possible to get nice things very quickly
-Fun for those who like surprises?
-Gives me cosmetic items (I got a flag a few times) other mobile games won’t give free cosmetics
Cons:
-Does not properly feel rewarding
-Locked item row is constantly trying my patience, psychological warfare
-Does not give me blocks proper (struggle to make robots)
-Due to items selling for very small amounts getting anything without pulling it from a crate is hard
-Even getting the best crate does not grant very nice things (I have gotten many purple crates but only one purple item, is this normal?)
-I do not know what to do with almost every block I get save for normal blocks/smgs
-I personally am not a fan of gambling
-Without premium they are not fun almost at all.
I do not have much good to say about getting crates. What little I have to say that’s good doesn’t even apply to me personally but I wanted to put SOMETHING positive down. The only real good thing I can see in crates is getting really big fun items randomly without much work. So far I have struggled to make basic robots, I do not get almost any cubes, the basic foundation of robots and have to sell weapons which do not give enough cubes. A basic SMG sells for 80, that’s only eight blocks. If blocks cost 1 instead of 10 this would not be a problem ever. Blocks that do things (like guns) do not sell for enough for me to get just simple blocks; this means later on in the game when I want to get other blocks that do stuff, such as guns, legs, or even this new mini-gun it's going to take an increasingly long amount of time. Unless you get more items as you level up? I do not know if it gets better.
The other big problem I see is the constant psychological pressure to get me to spend money. I did not see it at first when I had the free 3 days of premium, but now that my premium time has run out every match feels stressful at the end, even if I did well because I know I’m going to miss out on a bunch of items that my near empty bank of items desperately needs.
Simply put, the game is not fun without premium, at least for me. I struggle to get enough blocks, I struggle to get weapons, and I struggle to get movement items. I simply do not get to make any robots save for tearing apart the basic ones I started with and reconfiguring it over and over. This is not fun, from my perspective. Getting a crate for the match, losing half your items, losing half the rarity of that crate for losing the match; this all stacks way too much unfun punishment on the player. The sheer punishment levels here are astounding.
My most important thought on crates:

This game has amazing writing; dark humor; an evil AI; several multiplayer campaigns; intuitive puzzle features; an insane artist; a british robot;  a level editor... and no cake :(.
9/10 needs more cake.

First and foremost, I'll start with gameplay, as that's often what's most important. As far as gameplay goes, Wolfenstein, for me, was like a blast from the past in terms of how the shooter played out, and felt between the level design, health system, and so on. Allowing overcharge of health like in the old dooms, as well as the pickups of armor, it really felt nostalgic. But then they upped it, allowing you to for example remove armor pieces/helmets from nazis/machines, and wear those. Health can come from food as with the other wolfenstein games. Level structure felt a lot like Return to Castle Wolfenstien; linear, but open enough to explore/find secrets, which was a very good thing.
The shooting itself was great, though I found the dual wielding a bit unwieldy; couldn't zoom in without switching off dual wielding, and often times you just didn't have the health/armor to really make use of it unless using some SERIOUSLY heavy weaponry. Generally I found myself preferring the single gun setup.
The stealth system was neat because it wasn't needed at all, but encouraged. You could take out enemy 'commanders' to silence reinforcement calls if you did it stealthily; doing so also makes a lot of the secrets show up on the map, allowing you to find them easier. (they appear as ? marks, so it's not exact where they are, just the general area. Easy to figure out, but not an exact give-away).
A few negative aspects were sometimes with bosses it was a lot of trial and error; it wasn't wholly clear how to beat a few of them without trying a few times, or surviving long enough to get some radio advice from npcs.
Overall the gameplay, levels, ect, was over the tops and extremely fun. I enjoyed it thoroughly, and may play-through a second time, which is rare for me.  As far as realism though; don't expect it. You're practically a superhero in terms of durability and agility.
Despite being such an over-the-tops shooter, the story was surprisingly 'down to earth' in terms of moral, feeling, characters, and overall just narrative. It was very, VERY good; something somewhat rare in shooters, but a very good treat. The character's had good voice acting in my opinion, and overall made me feel attached/sad/joyed/excited and so on. The plot twists, enemies, all of it fit together in a splendid package, and the story was a rare treat as far as shooters, and games in general go.
Generally I have no problems as far as sound goes, i'm not picky. In this, it was just as good. I would of liked if the bigger guns sounded as big as they looked, but that's excusable for me.
The graphics were not completely modernized, though had a consistant look in terms of textures/theming/ect, and overall they did the job they were meant to well enough, even if they were not top of the line.
On the downside, optimization was a big downfall in this one; the requirements are far higher then most games I've seen and the graphics didn't match up to most of them, as a result I'd say the optimization could use some work.
Overall I'd say this game was worth it; it was short, ten hours when I only got about half the secrets, and one playthrough; but for me, that's like going to the movies 5 times, for the price of 3 times. So I'd say it was worth the money given the story, gameplay, and entertainment value.
If you dislike short-ish games, don't care about story, or overall just don't like shooters, this isn't gonna change much for you, but it was a nice treat as far as shooters go, and if there is a sequal I'll surely be picking it up!

What is there to say, the real grumpy, old, grandad of all FPS shooters has finally come out of his nap! But does he hold up, surrounded by all of the Battlefields and Call of Dutys, or should he be sent to retirement home before he hurts himself?
I think it really does and here is the scoop, bringing you all the good AND the bad about this game:
And as always TL;DR is at the bottom
Are you tired of all this advanced/future/space/star realistic warfare shooter? With sidekick characters without character yelling orders at each other like a old married couple?
This game is for you!
Devs did a good job making locations and enviromens feel authentic and memorable. Some places will probably amaze you, others will even make you feel uncomfortable. In other words - game atmosphere is pretty spot on.
Can't forget characters though, and these are  sympathic, memorable characters with lots of personality that will make you care about them. Even our main protagonist gets a solid personality. You will "hear" his thoughts, he can sometimes interact with other characters in more ways than *nazi, stab, dead*, hell, he even gets few lines here and there!
I would't go so far as to say that this is "The Last Of US" level of character development and atmosphere but it is still pretty damn solid.
Also, don't want to spoil anything but, your choises count, so choose wisely!

But hey! Realistic you say?! There are lazers and mechs and aliens in this game, I hear you cry.
Well, some of the weapons are kinda futuristic lazer-ish, and yes there are robots in this game, but yet, it all seems somehow grounded in reality. Robots are big, loud, bulky. No super jumps or nanosuits or stuff like that. Also, aliens don't exist... at least in this game
Anyways, let's talk about guns, guns are fun right?
Wolfenstein series of games always had some crazy guns mixed together with a little bit of crazy science, so what do we have here?
Well, most of the weapons, even though designs are a bit different, did in fact have a real life counterpart that was used in WW 2. Anyways, they look cool, they sound great and they make enemies dead, so why bother with something else?
But mom, this is Wolfenstein, I expect better!, you keep whining.
Did I say that you can also upgrade your guns? And that they can be used akimbo?
Speaking of Akimbo, this is no realistic Call of Duty simulator, where you only have akimbo pistols and SMG. This game is so badass that it throws realism in a window, spits on it and let's you dual wield basically everything you see - pistols, assault rifles and heck, even fully automatic shotguns!
Want to feel big, manly and empowered? Grab those 2 assault rifles with grenade launchers and go ahead and fullfill your n00b tube dream of the century, because well... you can.
Don't want to go in guns blazing? You can sneak around as well! Just put on silencer on your pistol and grab some throwing knifes, be all like mad ninja or something if you want.
Do all that and you might end up with earning a perk or two! There are few perk trees like Stealth, Tactician etc that you can earn by blowing up, stabbing and shooting enemies.
If you are really careful and use your eyes and brains to look around on occasion, you can find collectibles, gold and enigma codes. Those unlock concept arts, game modes and well, virtual gold... Get rich while saving the world because... ladies love that... amiright? ;)
But all that is nothing without cool enemies to fight! you whine endlessly.
Well, even though previous games in Wolfenstein series did have bigger variety of enemies to fight this game keeps it pretty straight forward and simple.
You have your standard Nazis, the SuperSoldier Nazis, Commander Nazis that always cry for reinforcements if not silenced, the SuperRoboDeathDog Nazis, failed experiments Nazis and some non-transforming Robo Nazis - these will probably keep you pretty busy.
On the A.I. front, they all do your basic sosial stuff like, duck and cover, shout outs about your current location, covering fire, grenade throwing and smacking you in the face if you're to close to comfort. They do however, on a few occations, forget that you're in front of them, looking at you, wishing for all this fighting to stop... Heck, it only happened on a night mission, maybe they were tired?
Sounds scary? Relax crybaby! You still got your regenerating healt!
Oh, wait, you don't... Or, it does regenerate a little bit, to a certain point, but when it doesn't... well, time to remember how med packs in an old scholl shooter work! You can even find and eat food if you're really desperate. Hell, player can make our favourite hero of the day steal food from Nazi dogs if his health are low enough! I'm not even kidding...

One of my first moments in the game was cresting a hill with a squad I had hoped in with to see the full might of our armor collum in the canyone bellow, with more than 30 MBTs and numerous other light and medium vehicles with scatered infantry, while further ahead Our air Support started thining their numbers and claiming the Sky, Once the battle actualy started I found myself quickly dodging from one piece of cover to the next, while franticaly trying to lay down supresing fire so the rest of my squad could move, all the while tanks from both sides firing all around, and Engineers setting up MGs on the walls in front of us. I would look above whatever crate or wall I was hiding behind just to see nothing but tracers and rockets flying above me, while numerous teamates fell trying to reach my position, and I wasnt even at the front.
By the time the battle was over it had been 2 hours, I had lost count of how many times I had died, or how many I had killed, it didnt matter, it was finaly over, we could set up shop, lick our wounds and prepare for the next, cause there would be a next, weather it was them attacking or us. Ah, Age of Empires 2. One of my most favorite games of all time. Unlike the majority of the reviews, Im gonna hit the highlights throughout the game, and not focus on "crashing multi player" like everyone seems to have issue with.
Ok, the best deal on Steam is the Age of Empires 2 HD with the DLC The Forgotten included. Ive played THOUSANDS of hours on an old disc, and have completed the majority of the original campaigns. Finally, I didn't play it much. It was just old and had lost some of that exciting thrill. But once I bought AoE2 HD with the Forgotten DLC, the game feels completely new again, as the new civilizations bring all new units, building style, campaigns, and that thrill of a new game.  Even with the original civilizations, and campaigns. This truely brings a real medieval town building experience, and it is quite easy to see people settling down somewhere, starting a town, and calling it Hungary...truely an experience to see what a medieval king had to go through.
Here are the highlights I saw:
Population limit increased to 500 to better build armies and navies.
The new civilizations make the game feel like its an all-new game, not a updated version of an old game
The campaigns have a more in-depth story to them in the game and in the story
Clicking on the characters to make them speak and sometimes have conversations in-game is a nice idea!
Campaigns are SUPER challenging on standard difficulty(the easiest difficulty to choose from)
It also discourage's the use of cheat codes as NO Steam achievements are gained if ONE code is used.
Being able to play online WITHOUT cheat codes for proper strategy.
Music is awesomely epic!!!!!!!
Things that could be good or bad, depending on your view:
No voice-over during the story reading before and after campaign levels, though if you had to pause during that, it saves the story till your not busy.
The multi player finding system. You just select the settings you want, it search's and you gotta hope it finds a game. If not, tough luck.
Down part of the game:
Game is LAGGY during multi player games cause my computer wasn't "connected" to my friends device and would cause lag. Felt a bit ripped off there.
Lag seems to be most when population limit is 500.
A dirty word in-game. Its always been so clean and family-friendly(excluding Attila the Hun campaign and now the Dracula campaign) but I never did complete the Aztec campaigns either.
The price. It is ridiculous. I got it on sale during the Mid week Madness sale. But it needs to be lowered some. But you do get excellent game quality.
Overall, excellent game, the battles are well balanced, unless of course you have 100 troops against 30. The 30 wont kill any of your troops, most likely. The civilizations are also well balanced, so all are strong as the other. Its up to you to maximize there power over the other and ultimately, the winner will be the best general/king/emperor ;) I'd suggest keeping multi player local until you have the grasp of the game or the lag disappears. For old, veterans, this is a whole new ballgame. For new players, buckle up for a wild ride through history!

Disappointing, to say the least, especially since I already owned the original version of this game and had it running on Windows 7. For me, nothing has changed.
Those two points aside, this game is classic AoE. If you haven't experienced it, and you like RTS, give this a shot to see how us old timers played. If you're familiar with this title, jump in and enjoy the memories.

For those of you who ignore the reviews of this game beware. I bought this game out of nostalgia with steam money earned from other games while AoE was $5. I don’t necessarily regret buying the game, but I was very disappointed that everything the reviewers said came true after only 5 hours of play (offline I have around 15 hours).
The game grinds to a literal halt when more than 100 units are on the screen. You might think this is during battles, which does happen, but this was just when I had grouped the units and moved them. When the fighting started I had trouble moving people to the right spot. Additionally, changing my video settings didn’t improve this.
Online fighting possesses the same trouble as before. Lots of lag and DC.
The controls and unit AI have not been improved at all. Not that I was expecting this but I was little disappointed the devs couldn’t at least make unit movement a bit more intelligent. Such as a unit moving from point A to point B and not run up to enemy units before turning away or run away when you’re attacked (workers).  The different stances are really only good if you are keeping an eye on the units or they have a wall to fight behind. For example, defensive stance is great to hold a position but the units get confused when hit with enemy ranged units that are far off out of their assigned area. Moving large groups in any formation has not been improved at all. Again, I was not expecting any of these improvements when I bought the game but after so long since the original release I expected something more.
All in all, I would not recommend this game for anyone but someone who played the original. In my opinion, this shouldn’t cost more than $10 normally. Asking $20 is ridiculous considering how little was added to the game in what matters. Who cares if content is added if gameplay and the online experience have not been improved. You won’t enjoy what is added.
EDIT: Things can change. People do try. Much improved since I wrote this. Except the price, stick to the discount if you can.

This game is 100% p2w. The only two ways to get parts for your robot are crates and a shop that is so overpriced that some of the parts you can purchase require at least 24 hours of grinding. The crates give you randomly selected parts based on the rarity of the part. Crates are purchasable, but otherwise are only obtained by playing in matches. You get a crate that has a certain chance of giving rarer items based on your position on the leaderboard. Even if you get the highest tier crate, you still have a very high chance of getting very common items. It is nearly impossible to build the robot that you would like to build because it is very difficult and time consuming to get the resources to buy the parts that you need and it's very unlikely that you will get what you need in a crate.
In light of some very recent reviews, I felt that I needed to add this. These reviews have been defending the game by saying that the things you can purchase in the game do nothing but speed up the process of grinding for items. While this is not completely true, as some "dlc" packages have come out that give you specific items, I will consider this to be true while writing this review. The grind for even mid -tier items is so long that anything promising to shorten it is pay to win. I saved up for 3 days with the free premium I got when I opened my account. I earned approximately 205k  in-game currency. I sold every single item I got in every single crate that I got. I even resorted to selling every block that I got(these are with 1 in-game currency each) to achieve my goal of 200k. That 200k was enough to buy one mid-tier and one high-tier item. I often was the recipient of the highest-tier crates(about 1 in every 2 rounds). The other half the time I got second or third tier crates. I calculated my average income per round(again, after selling every single item ) to be around 1k per round. I played for several hours on each of those three days to reach that result. After my free 3-day premium ran out, I got roughly 200 in-game currency per round. Because of the increased chance of getting good items and the increased number of items from premium, my yield was increased roughly 5 times. I fail to see how this isn't p2w. To make the game even more p2w, you have the option of spending tons of money on high tier crates. This completely removes the need to grind at all. Again, I fail to see how this isn't p2w. What would take me about 15 days of grinding without spending money took me 3 days with premium and could've taken even less time of I'd skipped the grinding altogether. Again, how is this not p2w? I cannot recommend this game to anybody looking for a free game that they can spend some time playing. Stay away unless you're willing to spend at least $60 USD per month.
