Ah, Age of Empires 2. One of my most favorite games of all time. Unlike the majority of the reviews, Im gonna hit the highlights throughout the game, and not focus on "crashing multi player" like everyone seems to have issue with.
Ok, the best deal on Steam is the Age of Empires 2 HD with the DLC The Forgotten included. Ive played THOUSANDS of hours on an old disc, and have completed the majority of the original campaigns. Finally, I didn't play it much. It was just old and had lost some of that exciting thrill. But once I bought AoE2 HD with the Forgotten DLC, the game feels completely new again, as the new civilizations bring all new units, building style, campaigns, and that thrill of a new game.  Even with the original civilizations, and campaigns. This truely brings a real medieval town building experience, and it is quite easy to see people settling down somewhere, starting a town, and calling it Hungary...truely an experience to see what a medieval king had to go through.
Here are the highlights I saw:
Population limit increased to 500 to better build armies and navies.
The new civilizations make the game feel like its an all-new game, not a updated version of an old game
The campaigns have a more in-depth story to them in the game and in the story
Clicking on the characters to make them speak and sometimes have conversations in-game is a nice idea!
Campaigns are SUPER challenging on standard difficulty(the easiest difficulty to choose from)
It also discourage's the use of cheat codes as NO Steam achievements are gained if ONE code is used.
Being able to play online WITHOUT cheat codes for proper strategy.
Music is awesomely epic!!!!!!!
Things that could be good or bad, depending on your view:
No voice-over during the story reading before and after campaign levels, though if you had to pause during that, it saves the story till your not busy.
The multi player finding system. You just select the settings you want, it search's and you gotta hope it finds a game. If not, tough luck.
Down part of the game:
Game is LAGGY during multi player games cause my computer wasn't "connected" to my friends device and would cause lag. Felt a bit ripped off there.
Lag seems to be most when population limit is 500.
A dirty word in-game. Its always been so clean and family-friendly(excluding Attila the Hun campaign and now the Dracula campaign) but I never did complete the Aztec campaigns either.
The price. It is ridiculous. I got it on sale during the Mid week Madness sale. But it needs to be lowered some. But you do get excellent game quality.
Overall, excellent game, the battles are well balanced, unless of course you have 100 troops against 30. The 30 wont kill any of your troops, most likely. The civilizations are also well balanced, so all are strong as the other. Its up to you to maximize there power over the other and ultimately, the winner will be the best general/king/emperor ;) I'd suggest keeping multi player local until you have the grasp of the game or the lag disappears. For old, veterans, this is a whole new ballgame. For new players, buckle up for a wild ride through history!

Well. Where do I begin?
The first mistake they made was using ID Tech 5, which is a rather poor engine. Textures aren't great, and the game does feels somewhat like a console port. (mainly because of the 60fps limit, clunky menus, and unskippable intro movies).  The weapon sounds, animations and overall presentation of the game are great.
MachineGames claimed they were going for an old school game, which is mind boggling because it is but it isn't at the same time...
Why does health regen in blocks of 20? Why is the AI extremely dumb? (Like really, really, stupid) You can literally walk past some of the AI and they wont notice you. The AI is so stupid you can use bad stealth to land 1 hit 1 kills on all of them, even on the hardest difficulty. Why can you dual-wield EVERY GUN? I love dual-wielding pistols and smg's, but I am sorry, dual-wielding shotguns and assault rifles is gimmicky, and makes the game way easier than it already is. (It's a fun gimmick though)
That's another thing. This game is tainted with cutscenes every 5 minutes. (Good cutscenes mind you) Sure, the writing I must admit is awesome, but again has its minor inconsistencies. The voice acting is top notch though, and it's topped with a somewhat powerful story line, but overall the game is just way too easy. I am playing it on the hardest difficulty, and most enemies go down with 2 upper torso shots with a pistol. The only thing the difficulty levels effects is the damage enemies deal to you, and how many of them there are.
The only thing old school about this game is the fact that you can carry every gun. That's it. No quick save. No nothing.
It even has a stupid CoD Style hot key knifing and grenade system - which is hardly old school. Although they can be selected on the weapon wheel too, like an old school game. At least it gives you the choice I guess.
Overall I am conflicted about this game. I want to love it, I like it a lot, it's fun, it's written well, it's very good, but it just isn't as old school as they claimed it would be. This is the type of game you don't pay full price for, but you don't pay peanuts for it either.

Wolfenstein: The New Order Summary
The word of the day for Wolfenstein: The New Order on the PC is "restrictive." We have learned a lot about this game, and what we've learned is that this game suffers in many ways. It suffers as a game that reminds us of a focus on the console experience, rather than the PC gaming experience. It suffers as a game that reminds us of RAGE again, with many issues not learned, or ignored from that game three years ago. It's best if we break each topic down, then we will talk about performance, and then about what video cards play best at what settings. In no particular order:
60 FPS Cap - Wolfenstein: The New Order suffers from an imposed 60 FPS game cap. It is not disabled by turning off VSYNC, and there are no in-game options to turn off or increase the maximum framerate from within the game. This is normally a thing we see on console ported games, but sometimes it is done for other reasons. The fact stands that this is not a PC oriented option and in no way helps PC gaming. There are gamers with 120Hz displays who enjoy that level of gameplay. There are users of SLI and CrossFire who want all the performance they paid for to be there when they play games. This imposed FPS cap is unacceptable for PC gaming.
No AA Options - A staple in any PC game, antialiasing. This game lacks AA options or unique forms of AA to push the gaming industry forward. No control over shader AA, traditional MSAA, or SSAA. No alpha transparency AA options either. This is a common sense feature that should be in any PC game.
Graphics Options linked to VRAM Capacity - This game suffers from having its graphics options linked to VRAM capacity. On video cards with 3GB of VRAM, or more, the "Ultra" setting and optional customize graphics to maximum values are present. If you have a video card with 2GB of VRAM, "Ultra" is no longer there. We can imagine if you have less than that, it will decrease optional settings even more.
When a game like this sets itself by VRAM, rather than performance, what ends up happening is exactly what we've experienced. All the performance, for every video card, will be close to that 60 FPS framerate cap because one cannot push the settings higher and sacrifice performance for higher in-game settings. It's an imposed limit that forces a certain level of performance dependent on VRAM capacity, and not what the GPU is actually capable of accelerating.
No Aspect Ratio - Something as simple as forcing a different aspect ratio from inside the game is not there. Naturally, you don't need this for consoles, but for a PC this is a feature that is nothing but common sense. This game detects the aspect ratio of your display, and you are stuck to those resolution settings with in-game options. This does not favor PC gaming.
Those qualities above limit the game, now let's talk about other things this game suffers which decrease the gameplay experience.
Texture Pop-in - This one is one of the most annoying issues with this game, and it was present in RAGE. Unfortunately we cannot show you with screenshots. PC Gamer has some animations that shows this problem quite prominently. There has been three years since that game, and you would think someone would have listened and fixed this problem in a 2014 game, but nope. As you move the camera left or right, up or down you notice the textures loading in. It's so slow at doing it that sometimes you see textures loading in a quarter of a way into your screen. It is a major distraction, makes the game feel cheap, and kills the immersion of gameplay. This is a problem that cannot be ignored, we thought it was a one-off with RAGE, but apparently it's native to id Tech 5. This does not give us warm feelings about what to expect with Doom 4.
Article Image Article Image Article Image
Article Image Article Image Article Image
Inconsistent Texture Quality - This is also something else we encountered in RAGE and is still a problem in this game as well. In the same scene or frame you can have some textures looking detailed, and others looking downright flat, un-detailed, and just plain bad. It's a big issue, and it makes the game look inconsistent and unfinished. One again its kills the game’s immersiveness.
OpenGL - OpenGL 3.2, really? There have been six newer OpenGL releases since 2009, yet this game uses an API based 5 years ago. NVIDIA's and AMD's video cards both support OpenGL 4.4, released in 2013 and are primed and ready to show us what modern OpenGL can do. This game does not exploit that and does not move OpenGL gaming forward.
Performance
Due to the nature of this game detecting graphics options based on VRAM capacity, most video cards will operate between 40-60 FPS. We think it breaks down like this:
AMD Radeon R9 290X and GeForce GTX 780 Ti. You will have no issue running at 2560x1600 with the highest possible settings the game supports. You will have performance to spare, and either card is a draw in terms of gameplay experience.
AMD Radeon R9 290 and GeForce GTX 780. You will have no issue running at "Ultra" settings at 2560x1600. The GTX 780 will be technically faster, but it won't matter, the gameplay experience will be the same.
AMD Radeon R9 280X and GeForce GTX 770. You will find the GeForce GTX 770 to be faster, but it will be limited to "High" settings due to VRAM. The R9 280X will be able to run at "Ultra" at 1080p and even 2560x1600, though that might be a little too graphics demanding. The best setting for the 280X will be 1080p and "Ultra" settings. The GTX 770 can run at 1080p at "High" settings, or 2560x1600 at "High". 280X can also run 2560x1600 at "High".
For video cards below the 280X and 770 1080p is going to be the sweet spot. If the card has 2GB of VRAM, "High" settings will be playable down to a certain level of GPU, and we think it will be pretty far down the value tree. If you have a 3GB card you might find "Ultra" playable at 1080p.
Overall, this game is not a huge burden on video cards, nor does it require the latest and greatest and most expensive to have a good gameplay experience. In our experience an AMD Radeon R9 280X is probably your best value, that extra RAM will allow "Ultra" at 1080p and allow you to play at higher resolutions at "High" settings.
The Bottom Line
We hate to be harsh, we had hopes that Wolfenstein: The New Order would be better. We had hopes that the issues discovered in RAGE would be fixed. We had hopes this would be a forward looking, PC oriented game. In all cases, we were let down.
This game is not a forward looking PC game. It lacks basic settings and features PC games need. It has too many restrictions and too many negative graphical issues that harm gameplay. This game has the same issues RAGE had, it is as if nothing was learned, or no one cared. The gameplay is somewhat fun if you are looking for a fast paced first-person shooter, with a hollow storyline and immersion breaking graphics.
We have been itching and scratching to update our gaming suite, waiting for a game here in 2014 that is worthy to add. We are still waiting. We are now five months into the year, and there has yet to be a game that seems next generation to us on the PC gaming platform. Wolfenstein: The New Order will not be evaluated further from us, nor is it worth to add to our gameplay suite. That said, I'll play through the rest of it on my own gaming time just to complete the experience and nostalgia of this series, and that's about all there is to say about this game. All of us here say save your money as the new Wolf is only suitable as a bargain bin purchase.

For those of you who ignore the reviews of this game beware. I bought this game out of nostalgia with steam money earned from other games while AoE was $5. I don’t necessarily regret buying the game, but I was very disappointed that everything the reviewers said came true after only 5 hours of play (offline I have around 15 hours).
The game grinds to a literal halt when more than 100 units are on the screen. You might think this is during battles, which does happen, but this was just when I had grouped the units and moved them. When the fighting started I had trouble moving people to the right spot. Additionally, changing my video settings didn’t improve this.
Online fighting possesses the same trouble as before. Lots of lag and DC.
The controls and unit AI have not been improved at all. Not that I was expecting this but I was little disappointed the devs couldn’t at least make unit movement a bit more intelligent. Such as a unit moving from point A to point B and not run up to enemy units before turning away or run away when you’re attacked (workers).  The different stances are really only good if you are keeping an eye on the units or they have a wall to fight behind. For example, defensive stance is great to hold a position but the units get confused when hit with enemy ranged units that are far off out of their assigned area. Moving large groups in any formation has not been improved at all. Again, I was not expecting any of these improvements when I bought the game but after so long since the original release I expected something more.
All in all, I would not recommend this game for anyone but someone who played the original. In my opinion, this shouldn’t cost more than $10 normally. Asking $20 is ridiculous considering how little was added to the game in what matters. Who cares if content is added if gameplay and the online experience have not been improved. You won’t enjoy what is added.
EDIT: Things can change. People do try. Much improved since I wrote this. Except the price, stick to the discount if you can.

I been playing this game since August 2012, before you even heard of it(sorry had to be a hipster). I know the ins and out of this game, and I gotta say it's my favorite Game of All Time and a unmatachable multiplayer experience. I was anticipating this game since it was rumored to be called Planetside Next, I was a big fan of Planetiside back in 2003.
Like I said it's Skill To Win. After all this time I been playing, I am still using the free begginers gun. In fact most of the best weapons are the Free guns, there is a lot of meh guns you can pay for. The game is very very balanced, sure I want some changes but overall the balance is amazing considering how many players/how many factors there is in the game.
Easy to make Progress/Certs(AKA Fake money). It rewards you if you are a good player! Like I said it's skill to win, you can easily make 70-100 certs in around an hour if you are good enough. If you gets constant points thru out your play thru. The Expensive Guns cost 1000 certs, so basically you have to play for around 10-15 hours and you get that gun....Unlike League of Legends where you have to play for 30-40 hours to get for most expensive IP champs( I admit Champs have more animations/uniqueness than the guns).
Rank Levels mean nothing in this game!!!!!!! It's Not WoW. A Level 1 BR can destroy a level 100 BR if good enough. So unlike most MMO's this game leveling is pretty balanced. Like I said most of the free weapons are the best weapons overall, so what the game does is sell Sidegrades. What Sidegrades are is basically selling a playstyle, so one gun may be better upclose but it sucks at distance. Thats pretty much it, you are paying to change the style of gameplay by sacraficing something. There is some upgrades however, like leveling up your armor doesn't give you any negative effects but the advantage at most it gives you, it's probably 15%, hell it could be less. You could easily destroy somebody if good enough...So yeah don't expect WoW/League of Legends advantages where a season vet with all the runes or higher level has a huge advantage over new players or recent level 30 LoL players.
I been hearing players mentioning Implants as Pay 2 win. This is simply false. They mention how we have to buy Chargers(BS!!!) I never bought a charger, I simply get charger drops by playing the game. I get so many charger drops, that I have like 70 of them lol. I also only use tier 1 implant, I never feel at disadvantage with people with higer tier implants. The Implants are very very minimal advantages.
Gameplay = Amazing....The game is always at war, no bad lobby times like every other game in existant, waiting to start. The action is constant, depending on how you like to play of course. You can be a camper but let me tell you, this game benifits rushers as much as campers. I never camp and destroy campers simply rushing. The game has a good balance between twitch combat/camping combat. So you can be Rambo in this game or just lay back and be more tactical, once you understand the game, you will find the balance of how to play.
Cliffs:
Pro's
-Skill To win(Early Guns are usually the best)
-Easy to Progress for F2P players.This game rewards skill, you can easily get around 70-100 certs in an hour if you play good enough. The most expensive guns take 1000 certs so youll take around 10-15 hours. LoL players take around 30-40 hours to get most expensive IP champs(Yes Champs are way more unique than guns but just goes to show how its easy to make certs).
-Level in this game means nothing(new player can destroy old player)
-Side Grades. Most of the weapons on this game are sidegrades meaning you are sacraficing something in order to get something more specific.
-Upgrades are very minimal. The actual upgrades like upgrading armor have no downsides but its very minimal like 15% advantage. Don't expect typical MMORpg progress....A Level 1 will destroy a lvl 100 in this game easily unlike MMORPG's.
-Implants are not Pay 2 Win!!!! I have never bought Implant chargers, NEVER!!!!!I get free drops simply by playing the game. Not to mention I use Tier 1 implants which are the cheapest, I never feel at a disadvantage.
-Fast Chaotic Gameplay with non stop action, No Lobby times(Will make you hate games with Lobies where you are forced to wait).
-Twitch Rambo Skill Gameplay/Camper Gameplay with Guns is perfectly balanced! Whatever you gameplay style, if you are good enough, you will have success. Im twitch player who perfers to run and gun, and I dominate in this game but if you are a camper you can also do very well. You just need the right game IQ to know which approach is more viable.(don't expect camping fest since being a Rambo is super effective).
Cons
- No Pay 2 Win. No reason To pay. I list this as a Con because I believe some people actually want a game where money matters more. Where money buys you way more time in terms of how long you take for progress.
-No real content Updates since Launch. The game got alot of fixes in terms of bugs and overall gameplay but rarely have we gotten real content. We basically only gotten 1 vehicle, 1 Aircraft, and 1 Continent since Launch, that to me is unacceptable.  We get countless of weapons but that isn't a huge content adder IMO. So yeah, they added so little Content when it first Launched, I have to be realistic and say don't expect much unless PS4 version is a huge success.
-Upgrades/Progressing character in this game are every minimal(will♥♥♥♥♥♥off Typical MMORPG players). So yeah don't expect when you are lvl 100 to be a god compared to peasent lvl 1's. You won't be. All the upgrades you get in this game will be very minimal.
- Meh Cosmetic items. Don't expect alot of cool looking armor sets/helmets/ or cool looking paint jobs on armors...I wish the Art team will try harder.
BottomLine: Get this game if you want a Skill 2 Win game with 1000 Players fighting eachother with no lobby or downtime and just pure action.
BTW I have this game outside of STEAM, I have way more than 500 hours on it.

Update:
Decide to give it another whirl and it now appears that the developers are trying their best to destroy their own game. Otherwise they are so insanely stupid that they need to locked away in a padded cell where they wont hurt themselves or anyone else. It's just amazing how bad it is now.

Well. Where do I begin?
The first mistake they made was using ID Tech 5, which is a rather poor engine. Textures aren't great, and the game does feels somewhat like a console port. (mainly because of the 60fps limit, clunky menus, and unskippable intro movies).  The weapon sounds, animations and overall presentation of the game are great.
MachineGames claimed they were going for an old school game, which is mind boggling because it is but it isn't at the same time...
Why does health regen in blocks of 20? Why is the AI extremely dumb? (Like really, really, stupid) You can literally walk past some of the AI and they wont notice you. The AI is so stupid you can use bad stealth to land 1 hit 1 kills on all of them, even on the hardest difficulty. Why can you dual-wield EVERY GUN? I love dual-wielding pistols and smg's, but I am sorry, dual-wielding shotguns and assault rifles is gimmicky, and makes the game way easier than it already is. (It's a fun gimmick though)
That's another thing. This game is tainted with cutscenes every 5 minutes. (Good cutscenes mind you) Sure, the writing I must admit is awesome, but again has its minor inconsistencies. The voice acting is top notch though, and it's topped with a somewhat powerful story line, but overall the game is just way too easy. I am playing it on the hardest difficulty, and most enemies go down with 2 upper torso shots with a pistol. The only thing the difficulty levels effects is the damage enemies deal to you, and how many of them there are.
The only thing old school about this game is the fact that you can carry every gun. That's it. No quick save. No nothing.
It even has a stupid CoD Style hot key knifing and grenade system - which is hardly old school. Although they can be selected on the weapon wheel too, like an old school game. At least it gives you the choice I guess.
Overall I am conflicted about this game. I want to love it, I like it a lot, it's fun, it's written well, it's very good, but it just isn't as old school as they claimed it would be. This is the type of game you don't pay full price for, but you don't pay peanuts for it either.

I've been playing the game a few weeks now and I feel like I'm in a good spot to write a review, so here it is.
Planetside 2 is a MASSIVE online FPS, up to 6000 players at a time battling over multiple continents with tonnes of unique bases using anything from devastating laser missiles to huge Galaxy dropships. Anyway, now that you know this I'm also going to tell you three things before you jump over to the download page and excitedly watch the meter full up.
The game is intensive, I have a fairly decent computer and I can only run it on the lowest settings if I want to have a nice, smooth experience, don't bother downloading it if you can't run a lot of less intensive games.
Play with freinds, or find someone to play with on the planetside forums before you start. On your own the game isn't as fun, when you're with other people the game is more fun and you feel like a proper organised unit making a difference (If that's what you want to do) or the group of people flying Reavers upside-down at the warpgate instead of the one lonely person sat there waiting for something do to.
The game has a learning mountain, not a curve. You are thrown into a tutorial that teaches you very little and then dropped into a huge fight. You will die. Lots. As long as you don't get frustrated and instantly ragequit you'll notice what makes this game amazing. What I mean by this is the seventeen tanks blasting at eachother with huge packs of infantry rushing towards the enemy base while the defenders make their last stand, planes blast eachother from the sky and bombs rain down pelting the tanks as Liberator gunships arrive at the fight. Imagine something like this, then imagine this is happening across most of the map, and there's four different, diverse continents.
Anyway, if you are ok with all of that, this game is worth playing, it's free so there's no reason not to. Dive in for a few hours and if you don't like it you diddn't spend any money anyway. I'll move onto some general pros and cons now.
Things I love:
The scale, there's no game which can compare, if you have trouble imagining this, think battlefeild times 100, it's mental.
The vehicles, there's around 9 vehicles which all have different playstyles, it's a lot of fun and all of them are customisable, that Sunderer that's being used to get rid of pesky aircraft could be used to shred through infantry, repair and re-supply allied vehicles or even go and fight other armour if it wants to.
The customization, the guns cost a lot but it's F2P so it's understandable, when you get a weapin though you have loads of different scopes, ammo types, underbarrel attachments and different ammo types and that's just the guns. There are different classes for each situation all with different loadouts and abilities. You can change your armour type, weapons, looks, grenades, bombs, health kits. Everything can be changed to some extent and that's why it's brilliant.
The community, the community is really good, don't be afraid to ask for help because a lot of the time they will be willing to take you in and send you back out as an expert tanker, pilot, Infiltator, whatever you want, there's someone to teach you, hop in game and ask or go onto the forums and have a look around.
Cons:
Frustration, the game makes you angry when you are playing seriously, you're on a twenty killstreak and then that damn OP infantry farming ESF rolls up and wipes out your squad. This is only worse for new players as they have no clue what anything does, that Raven that just destroyed their first tank may apear as some kind of OP  broken glitch to them.
Apart from that I can't think of anything that isn't in any other free to play game, not everything is easy to get because the Dev's have to keep the servers up, but everything apart from cosmetics are earnable and you can't actually straight out buy anything but weapons and some attachments, the only way to get Certification points (The in game currency) is to earn them, they can't be bought, the only buyable way to speed this process up is through boosts that are purchasable so that guy with the fully kitted out Light Assault had to work for it just like you did. There is a daily boost when you first play each day so you get more points and there isn't really a problem with earning them. There no balance issues which I have noticed yet and the game is just a lot of fun.
Thanks for reading and I'll see you all on Auraxis!

Wolfenstein: The New Order Summary
The word of the day for Wolfenstein: The New Order on the PC is "restrictive." We have learned a lot about this game, and what we've learned is that this game suffers in many ways. It suffers as a game that reminds us of a focus on the console experience, rather than the PC gaming experience. It suffers as a game that reminds us of RAGE again, with many issues not learned, or ignored from that game three years ago. It's best if we break each topic down, then we will talk about performance, and then about what video cards play best at what settings. In no particular order:
60 FPS Cap - Wolfenstein: The New Order suffers from an imposed 60 FPS game cap. It is not disabled by turning off VSYNC, and there are no in-game options to turn off or increase the maximum framerate from within the game. This is normally a thing we see on console ported games, but sometimes it is done for other reasons. The fact stands that this is not a PC oriented option and in no way helps PC gaming. There are gamers with 120Hz displays who enjoy that level of gameplay. There are users of SLI and CrossFire who want all the performance they paid for to be there when they play games. This imposed FPS cap is unacceptable for PC gaming.
No AA Options - A staple in any PC game, antialiasing. This game lacks AA options or unique forms of AA to push the gaming industry forward. No control over shader AA, traditional MSAA, or SSAA. No alpha transparency AA options either. This is a common sense feature that should be in any PC game.
Graphics Options linked to VRAM Capacity - This game suffers from having its graphics options linked to VRAM capacity. On video cards with 3GB of VRAM, or more, the "Ultra" setting and optional customize graphics to maximum values are present. If you have a video card with 2GB of VRAM, "Ultra" is no longer there. We can imagine if you have less than that, it will decrease optional settings even more.
When a game like this sets itself by VRAM, rather than performance, what ends up happening is exactly what we've experienced. All the performance, for every video card, will be close to that 60 FPS framerate cap because one cannot push the settings higher and sacrifice performance for higher in-game settings. It's an imposed limit that forces a certain level of performance dependent on VRAM capacity, and not what the GPU is actually capable of accelerating.
No Aspect Ratio - Something as simple as forcing a different aspect ratio from inside the game is not there. Naturally, you don't need this for consoles, but for a PC this is a feature that is nothing but common sense. This game detects the aspect ratio of your display, and you are stuck to those resolution settings with in-game options. This does not favor PC gaming.
Those qualities above limit the game, now let's talk about other things this game suffers which decrease the gameplay experience.
Texture Pop-in - This one is one of the most annoying issues with this game, and it was present in RAGE. Unfortunately we cannot show you with screenshots. PC Gamer has some animations that shows this problem quite prominently. There has been three years since that game, and you would think someone would have listened and fixed this problem in a 2014 game, but nope. As you move the camera left or right, up or down you notice the textures loading in. It's so slow at doing it that sometimes you see textures loading in a quarter of a way into your screen. It is a major distraction, makes the game feel cheap, and kills the immersion of gameplay. This is a problem that cannot be ignored, we thought it was a one-off with RAGE, but apparently it's native to id Tech 5. This does not give us warm feelings about what to expect with Doom 4.
Article Image Article Image Article Image
Article Image Article Image Article Image
Inconsistent Texture Quality - This is also something else we encountered in RAGE and is still a problem in this game as well. In the same scene or frame you can have some textures looking detailed, and others looking downright flat, un-detailed, and just plain bad. It's a big issue, and it makes the game look inconsistent and unfinished. One again its kills the game’s immersiveness.
OpenGL - OpenGL 3.2, really? There have been six newer OpenGL releases since 2009, yet this game uses an API based 5 years ago. NVIDIA's and AMD's video cards both support OpenGL 4.4, released in 2013 and are primed and ready to show us what modern OpenGL can do. This game does not exploit that and does not move OpenGL gaming forward.
Performance
Due to the nature of this game detecting graphics options based on VRAM capacity, most video cards will operate between 40-60 FPS. We think it breaks down like this:
AMD Radeon R9 290X and GeForce GTX 780 Ti. You will have no issue running at 2560x1600 with the highest possible settings the game supports. You will have performance to spare, and either card is a draw in terms of gameplay experience.
AMD Radeon R9 290 and GeForce GTX 780. You will have no issue running at "Ultra" settings at 2560x1600. The GTX 780 will be technically faster, but it won't matter, the gameplay experience will be the same.
AMD Radeon R9 280X and GeForce GTX 770. You will find the GeForce GTX 770 to be faster, but it will be limited to "High" settings due to VRAM. The R9 280X will be able to run at "Ultra" at 1080p and even 2560x1600, though that might be a little too graphics demanding. The best setting for the 280X will be 1080p and "Ultra" settings. The GTX 770 can run at 1080p at "High" settings, or 2560x1600 at "High". 280X can also run 2560x1600 at "High".
For video cards below the 280X and 770 1080p is going to be the sweet spot. If the card has 2GB of VRAM, "High" settings will be playable down to a certain level of GPU, and we think it will be pretty far down the value tree. If you have a 3GB card you might find "Ultra" playable at 1080p.
Overall, this game is not a huge burden on video cards, nor does it require the latest and greatest and most expensive to have a good gameplay experience. In our experience an AMD Radeon R9 280X is probably your best value, that extra RAM will allow "Ultra" at 1080p and allow you to play at higher resolutions at "High" settings.
The Bottom Line
We hate to be harsh, we had hopes that Wolfenstein: The New Order would be better. We had hopes that the issues discovered in RAGE would be fixed. We had hopes this would be a forward looking, PC oriented game. In all cases, we were let down.
This game is not a forward looking PC game. It lacks basic settings and features PC games need. It has too many restrictions and too many negative graphical issues that harm gameplay. This game has the same issues RAGE had, it is as if nothing was learned, or no one cared. The gameplay is somewhat fun if you are looking for a fast paced first-person shooter, with a hollow storyline and immersion breaking graphics.
We have been itching and scratching to update our gaming suite, waiting for a game here in 2014 that is worthy to add. We are still waiting. We are now five months into the year, and there has yet to be a game that seems next generation to us on the PC gaming platform. Wolfenstein: The New Order will not be evaluated further from us, nor is it worth to add to our gameplay suite. That said, I'll play through the rest of it on my own gaming time just to complete the experience and nostalgia of this series, and that's about all there is to say about this game. All of us here say save your money as the new Wolf is only suitable as a bargain bin purchase.

There are tons of categories I could put this up for in the Steam Awards, but I chose the naming one and called it "We Are a Family - Not Just a Community" Award. I chose this name because I feel that's what this game did for all of the community. When I think of Steam, I almost always think of Portal 2. The gameplay and storyline were great, but I think of it because of the staple of community inputs this brought to all of us. For years now, people have been making mods, maps, and addons in this great game and it's brought people together to play, experiment, test, and just have fun. While there are others like Garry's Mod and Team Fortress 2 that impliment user creations, none really compare to what Portal 2 means to the community.

Currently running this on the HD 4600 on an i5 4690k. With no overclock, I get an average of about 40-45 and drops to about 30 in large battles on 100% res scale and very low settings. I'm quite impressed, considering how terrible the HD 4600 was supposed to be.
Anyway, the game. If it's played properly, it's a strategy game where you command real people instead of NPC's. If you're on the ground it's basically sci-fi battlefield, but with more people and (arguably) better gameplay. It has all the shooter elements you'd expect; class customisation, vehicles, squads, commanders etc but what's nice is that it also incorporates MMO elements like guilds (or 'outfits' in this game') and the huge playercounts. Instead of 32vs32 in Battlefield, in one area alone this game can have 200+ people in one area, all fighting. The feeling when you're with 100 people charging at an enemy base as if it's space D-day is just incredible. Or perhaps you're the lone infiltrator who brings down the defenses of a base and brings the vanguard inside.
If you want to play this game tactically, you absolutely can. Set up an outfit and command your troops. If you don't, you don't have to, and that's a great thing.
Without question, I absolutely recommend this game. If you like shooters, you'll love this. If you like MMO's, you'll love this. If you like sci-fi, you'll love this. A great game all-around, except for a slight imbalance on the weapons, which makes sense canonically but is still annoying. A Terran soldier vs Vanu in close range will never work out for the TR.
One thing to note is that if you install this through steam, files will fail to validate a lot causing DC's while in-game. I'm not sure why this is, but using the version from
(don't worry, it's a safe link) doesn't have this problem, and I DC a lot less. I wouldn't recommend installing it from Steam, just in case you encounter the same problem. For me, I constantly got 38 files failing to validate after about 3 hours in-game (doesn't have to be in one sitting).

Probably one of the best, if not the best shooter so far in 2014. Not only does this game make you feel like a badass, it does it in many different ways.
I played the game on Uber difficulty and earned the Super Hero achievement.
The AI in the game is a bit weak and some enemies are very dumb. Stealth is very easy in the game and is quite rewarding. (Perhaps a bit too easy) The guns in the game are great and the upgrades are also quite helpful. The gameplay is rather linear although there are some in-game choices that you do have to make. There are also tons of secrets and easter eggs to find. The game is quite long but not as long as triple A games could be. (About 8-12 hours) (Took me 8 to 9 on Uber without finding all of the secrets/collectibles)
The only thing I disliked is that the developers chose to use ID Engine 5, which is horrible in terms of optimization for the game. I play on an overclocked i7, 32 gigs of ram, with dual Nvidia 680 GTX graphics cards and had to tweak Nvidia settings so that parts of the game didn't stutter in terms of FPS. (I played on Ultra settings).
With that being said, I also noticed stuttering and brief 1 second skips/pauses during cutscenes and events which kind of annoyed me.
Overall, I do recommend this game since it's a great action-shooter packed with tons of references, easter-eggs, and secrets. However, the game did not seem as polished as it could be and may have been rushed in terms of development on the technical side.
TLDR: Play it, it's great. Just make sure you can run it and hopefully they'll patch it to improve optimization.

You know how they say it's about the journey, not the destination?
The New Order gets neither of those right.
Let's start with what the game *does* get right. The technical execution is nearly flawless, props to them for that — it's gorgeous visually, the sound design is great, etc. Some of the situations you're placed into are really damn cool (I won't spoil, though). The hybrid of regenerating & classic medkit health is nice. The stealth system was fairly enjoyable. The game alternates between massive battles and exploration levels with not a lot of fighting: the pacing is good. The storyline and cutscenes are very awesome and they're definitely what will keep you going for more. This is as far as it goes, though.
Around half of the enemies you will be facing are complete bullet sponges. Given the amount of ammo you have to work with, you will run out of bullets extremely quickly. You have several huge robots remaining in front of you, and you don't have anything more to shoot them with. You're then forced to work around the area in a really awkward manner, usually by backtracking to the latest mounted gun turret, and then you run back and forth between the place where the enemies are and the turret reloader (because those things too don't have enough ammo!!).
, it's hard, you will have to do this several times per level after the first few chapters, it's a major pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ It amounts to being nonsensical difficulty spikes.
The game implements a weird CoD-like cover shooting mechanic which isn't clearly explained to you, and handles poorly (you have to hold ALT+WASD).
The secrets hidden throughout the levels don't unlock anything interesting at all (just New Game+ variations such as unlimited ammo mode, hardcore mode, super hardcore mode, super super hardcore ironman one-life only mode).
There's a handful of sex scenes shoehorned in, kinda out of nowhere. It's 2014 and it'd be nice if AAA video games didn't feel the need to porno it up in an attempt to keep teenagers glued to their screens. It's cringeworthy at best.
And last but not least, the ending is horrible, it provides absolutely no closure to the end of the game and is enormously inconsistent with everything that happened so far. SPOILERS FOLLOW: you survive many crashes (including a space shuttle returning to Earth and crashing at 300km/h on a suspended bridge), you get poisoned, stabbed multiple times, you fall from huge heights, etc. and at the end of the game, a grenade blows up a meter away from you (after you spend a good 4 seconds staring at it instead of running away), and the protagonist is all "oh no guess i'm dead now I will never have a family with the woman I had a sex scene during the first 2 hours of the game".
Fade to black, credits roll, you don't get to see what happens to all the people you just rescued. It's absolutely TERRIBLE. It's not "Mass Effect 3" terrible but it's certainly up there with it.
Overall the game is decent-ish as a shooter and not really good as a game once you get past the first few levels.
I won't deny I had some fun but it could have been so much better. As a result I cannot recommend Wolfenstein: The New Order, at its current price point of 50€. Get it when it's cheap on sale.

I simply cannot recomment the game to a new player.
This game looks amazing, and it once was... now i feel as if it is a shell of its old self.
The devs made a new system of crates, which you earn after battles, or can buy. This system gives rewards off of pure luck, with better crates giving a "higher" chance of reward. In practice, rewards are slim and random, which means in order to get an item you want, you either have to pray that you get your item, or "forge" it.
you earn robits from "recycling" items, which you use to "forge" new items. (you can also get robits from the roboshop, if you are lucky enough to get your bot noticed).
The biggest problem is that "recycling" gives very little robits, which means actually "forging" an item is very difficult, and generally as time consuming as waiting for it.
Basically what this means is that the grind is horribly slow, and especially for a new player, in order to get any items you may want, you either need to constantly play for a long time, or give in and spend quite a bit of money.
Now i understand that the devs are in debt, and need cash, but their system is essentially made to milk money out of players who dont like to grind for years. I am not affected so much, but new players definately are.
So, for me at least, this system is a nuisance, but i can still play and properly build most of the things i want. See, i played this game ALOT before (and i am playing it now too...), and as such, I have most of my old items from long ago, guns, wings, and alot of blocks. And, I can build to my hearts content and shoot pew pews at enemies, without having to worry and pray that maybe one day a protonium crate could actually give me a legendary... (looking at you mega hover, you dont count).
To sum it up: a new player will be forced into a grind far worse than the game ever gave, and as such they will either be bored with it, pay money, or somehow survive the horror (like 10%). The game is DEFINATELY NOT HORRIBLE or RUINED, no, it really isnt that bad, and still, at least visually resembles the game we loved back in 2014. But it certainly is different, and many veterans like me remember when it was arguably alot better (and kinder to new players) , the "golden age" so to speak.
TL/DR: I would stay away new players, at least until they fix recycling, or (we all pray) make a robit based economy... Older plyers checking in, play if you want, but make sure you have the parts you need before, dont expect anything good from the crates unless you pray to a four-leaf clover.

If you can ignore the technological hangups that sadly seem to be a "feature" of the ID Tech 5 engine, you'll find a pretty damn good shooter.  It isn't anything revolutionary or mind blowing but it doesn't feel like it is trying to be, all its trying to do is taking you on another patently bizarre and violent journey that the series is known for and this is certainly a memorable one.  The action is tense, fast paced and does a good job mixing the fast twitch based gameplay of the ID Software classics with more modern enhancements and aesthetics.  In fact I'd say that it's rather refreshing to have this mix here, because shooters lately have been so stale and formulaic so its good to see a game that lets you actually explore the environment and have dynamic battles that aren't quite as scripted.  Plus sniping down a big baddy and then converting my sniper-rifle into a laser to cut down the stragglers is just plain fun.  The only real disappointments gameplay wise do come in the fact that while there are fun additions to the arsenal like the aforementioned sniper/laser combo, you don't get anything as wild and exotic as the tesla gun, Particle Cannon or Leichenfaust 44 - there is a laser that you gradually upgrade and while it is fun to use, it still ain't the same.
Storywise the game is... alright.  Normally I wouldn't bring up story in reference to a Wolfenstein game since they can be summed up as such:  The Nazis have hired their silliest generals to do weird-sciency stuff and even weirder-occult stuff, GO KILL THEM! but this game has a much stronger focus on the story, and has plenty of cinematics.  It is well written, but there are too many things unanswered and at times the story actually disappoints by setting up some absolutely absurd idea and then not fully capitalizing on it; for example, the Moon level.  Now when you hear that in the context of Wolfenstein, you expect to be jumping around in low gravity cutting down Nazis on the goddamned moon, sadly most of it takes place indoors and the only part on the moon is five minutes long and only has 3 robotic drone enemies.  You do get your Sniper-Rifle-Laser conversion kit, but there are so many missed opportunities for having a level set on the damned moon!  Not to mention I was hoping to see more of the Nazi controlled world, but you get some countryside in Poland, London, and Berlin and that's your lot.  Its setting could have been taken much further in general.  But it makes up for it if not solely for the games villains.  General Deathshead from the past 2 games returns, retaining his promotion from side-character in Return to Castle Wolfenstein to primary antagonist of Wolfenstein '09 and he's a lot more interesting here than he was before, in fact he's downright terrifying in this game.  His grin alone is worth a thousand chills.  Then there's Frau Engel, she's intimidating from the getgo but when she becomes truly memorable is when her character is "upgraded" (by way of a downgrade, ironically.) and produced a scene that will linger in my bloody nightmares.  There's still just enough of that patent Wolfenstein absurdity to them to make them fun though, like Deathshead's nod to Hitler's mech from the first game to Frau Engel having a boytoy named "Bubi."  Not sure about the ending of the game though, the writers seem to be banking on the idea that you are really invested in B.J. Blazkowicz as a character despite the fact he's still really just a trigger-happy tool that minces anything that dares goosestep.
All in all, its just a fun ride and provides something refreshingly fast paced and proves that a game CAN be scripted while having more freedom and dynamic elements to gameplay and combat.  It's over the top and that's how it SHOULD be.  I do recommend playing the game on its harder difficulties though, while it does increase in difficulty later on the game and provides a fair challenge it felt a little easy for me when I started at a medium difficulty.

ARRRGHHHH!
That is my primary reaction while playing Dirty Bomb.
Dirty Bomb can be an extremely fun game. It has a lot going for it. The objective based modes are unique and a good load of fun, the maps are huge multi-part affairs with various points of engagement and every character in the roster has a unique feel and personality. This game is also extremely fast paced and employs a simple parkour and momentum based movement system; In Dirty Bomb motility is key, almost as much as your aiming skills. This makes it a refeshing change of pace from most other online FPS out there with the added benefit of this being completely free-to-play.
However, this game is plagued by some crippling problems:
1. LACK OF POLISH - As you would expect from most free-to-play games, Dirty Bomb suffers from a lack of polish. The graphics are average, there are performance issues, especially in the menus and I have had trouble joining games on occasion.
2. POOR NETCODE - It is extremely common to get shot around corners you think you have crossed or get shot through solid objects/walls (Dirty Bomb does not have wall or cover penetration akin to Battlefield, so this should not be happening).
3. BAD BALANCING - The game has poor balancing and a huge portion of games just end up being one sided slaughter fests.
3. POOR UPDATES AND LACK OF NEW MAPS - I will acceed that Dirty Bomb's maps are huge multi-layered affairs and must take time and effort to create, however the devs have barely released any new maps in a long while now. Meanwhile, they have continued to crank out new purchaseable characters like clockwork. Also, Dirty Bomb remains in beta for a year now, with a fully functioning in-game store. These occurences have led me to lose trust in the devs.
4. HACKERS - Oh god. This is what completely kills this game for me. Dirty bomb is rife with hackers of various degrees. aimbotters and wallhackers are commonplace, and any game with these hackers become exercises in frustration. The game's anti-cheat system is a joke and according to forums, no action is taken against these cheaters even if you report them.
As you can see, I have put quite a few hours into this game, however I cannot say I enjoyed them all. This game suffers from some serious problems that the devs do not seem to be interested in solving, and with a plethora of hero/character and objective based shooters coming out this year, i'm going to jump ship without a second thought as and when they release.
P.S. - I have spent some money on this game (15 dollars), but with 3 free characters to begin with along with the weekly rotation, free-to-play players should not suffer any obvious disadvantages. In the game's defense, I felt that it's microtransaction model is mostly fair.
TL;DR - The game has some unique ideas and can be fun on occasion, however it is let down by lack of polish, poor netcode, balancing issues, bugs and is rife with hackers. Look elsewhere and spare yourself the frustration.

That is my primary reaction while playing Dirty Bomb.
Dirty Bomb can be an extremely fun game. It has a lot going for it. The objective based modes are unique and a good load of fun, the maps are huge multi-part affairs with various points of engagement and every character in the roster has a unique feel and personality. This game is also extremely fast paced and employs a simple parkour and momentum based movement system; In Dirty Bomb motility is key, almost as much as your aiming skills. This makes it a refeshing change of pace from most other online FPS out there with the added benefit of this being completely free-to-play.
However, this game is plagued by some crippling problems:
1. LACK OF POLISH - As you would expect from most free-to-play games, Dirty Bomb suffers from a lack of polish. The graphics are average, there are performance issues, especially in the menus and I have had trouble joining games on occasion.
2. POOR NETCODE - It is extremely common to get shot around corners you think you have crossed or get shot through solid objects/walls (Dirty Bomb does not have wall or cover penetration akin to Battlefield, so this should not be happening).
3. BAD BALANCING - The game has poor balancing and a huge portion of games just end up being one sided slaughter fests.
3. POOR UPDATES AND LACK OF NEW MAPS - I will acceed that Dirty Bomb's maps are huge multi-layered affairs and must take time and effort to create, however the devs have barely released any new maps in a long while now. Meanwhile, they have continued to crank out new purchaseable characters like clockwork. Also, Dirty Bomb remains in beta for a year now, with a fully functioning in-game store. These occurences have led me to lose trust in the devs.
4. HACKERS - Oh god. This is what completely kills this game for me. Dirty bomb is rife with hackers of various degrees. aimbotters and wallhackers are commonplace, and any game with these hackers become exercises in frustration. The game's anti-cheat system is a joke and according to forums, no action is taken against these cheaters even if you report them.
As you can see, I have put quite a few hours into this game, however I cannot say I enjoyed them all. This game suffers from some serious problems that the devs do not seem to be interested in solving, and with a plethora of hero/character and objective based shooters coming out this year, i'm going to jump ship without a second thought as and when they release.
P.S. - I have spent some money on this game (15 dollars), but with 3 free characters to begin with along with the weekly rotation, free-to-play players should not suffer any obvious disadvantages. In the game's defense, I felt that it's microtransaction model is mostly fair.
TL;DR - The game has some unique ideas and can be fun on occasion, however it is let down by lack of polish, poor netcode, balancing issues, bugs and is rife with hackers. Look elsewhere and spare yourself the frustration.

Amazing effects, great graphics, gun play is a blast.. the attention to detail is evident in every facet of the game.  Down to the blood splatters and the about 30 different ways to explode someone's head.  The story is so compelling too.

1. Robocraft was such a nice game back then! I remember... we had the Tier-Classes which were really important for a fair match! (Today you get thrown into a match, flooded by "pro's" which one -or two shot you with the ion distorter or any legendary weapon, which practically isn't affordable if you don't want to spend 100 bucks for these ♥♥♥♥♥♥ protonium crates.)
2. Adding those "crates" was the worst idea ever. We all know that games with these "crates concepts" died shortly after release. Should i tell you why? Because there will be a lack of fun! Back then I wanted a strong weapon. What I did was farming RP because I had the motivation to get this weapon! After like 10 - 20 matches I had enough to buy this weapon. It felt rewarding because you knew that you worked for it. Today you get a gold/diamond crate (..meh..), with maybe 1 or 2 rares which in my opinion belong into a dustbin. Beside this "rare" catch you get f*cking blocks and without premium chances are pretty good that you won't get the good♥♥♥♥♥♥for years!
3. What happened to the Tech-Tree? It was abandoned. The Tech-Tree gave you freedom to unlock whatever you thought was useful for your bot. Whenever you saw something interesting you worked for it and also had fun! By removing the Tech-Tree and RP Robocraft lost its foundation.
4. The "repair-feature" during a match made "Nano-Bots" worthless.
5.  The weapons were nerfed way too much. Remember the rail gun? It was strong as f*ck, but it had to reload several seconds to unleash a strong shot. Also the chance to miss was pretty high and on close quarters you had to run away, because you couldn't do nothing but miss! - In my opinion this was balanced! Also the drivers seat was removed. Why? You had the urge to protect you driver, because you knew if he wasn't secured to 1 Block you would've been insta-killed. In my opinion this feature added tactics, because you had to figure out where the weak point of the enemy robot was.
6. Now to a new feature: Recycling! Prices are way tooooo low. You just get 25% worth of that item and we all know you just get crap outta those crates. So to buy an other item which won't appear in a crate you got to farm.... how long? 1, 2, 3 hours like in the past? Heeell no! It takes forever just for an item!
7. Now to the Forge: Prices are too high! How the f*ck are you able to forge a moderate item when the recycling just yields 25% worth of that item?
8.  Back then you had to buy cosmetics, garage space, and other non-game-breaking equipment with real money. The garage space was limited, pretty fair tho?
9. I like the idea of the Factory, but there are several problems. People don't got Robits because the crates just yield crap and the prices are too high. So how do they buy robots? They don't. And this is the reason why the Factory is senselessly!
10. The company of course needs money, because they also have families to feed. But this (in the past) glorious game was ruined  because of greed! It wasn't a smart move to change the game concept from "FreeAndFunToPlay" to a "PayToHaveFunOrFarmYourselfDead" concept. The company will see that if they  hadn't been so greedy they would have earned more money....
Rest in Peace Robocraft. We (The veterans and myself) will forever remember you!

You want to play a game. Not just any game though; you want to play a game that will take you to a massive world with lots of people playing. A game that promises to give you an exciting adventure and make you feel happy with it.
But you heard of Planetside 2.
Its alright, however. Its a free game and by some miracle you have a computer that can atleast run this at at the lowest resolution at the lowest graphics setting at around 30fps. Technically its all good in the interstellar hood. You get the game downloaded and feel excited about the journey ahead. Maybe you will be a sneaky sniper that takes out important targets. Maybe an engineer or medic to help people and gain allies in jolly cooperation. Maybe you will be a grissled baddass of norse legend, running into combat with nothing but a LMG and pride for your made-up nation.
You decide to go the faction that is basically Space-America, because the other two are about as morally north as the moral compass of the Westboro Baptist Church. You go through training, and boy is it arduous. A whole tutorial on what a gun is and how to walk around. You also learn how to use teleporters, which are all around for an unknown reason that supports no claim to sound logistical usage.
Its time. Its finally time to get out there and not only be somebody, but kill somebody in the name of Space-'Murica. You drop into the battle, heart on your sleeve and smile on your face. Its game time. The pod crashes in the most intense fighting on the whole continent and you are at the center of it. You take a whole 5 seconds to survey the scene: a squad of your infantry is decimated by an explosion as a tank drives past you, seven shades of dropship are bringing in friendly and enemy troops, tracers are going everywhere...
Death...4....3....2...................2? SPAWN
Thats alright. You're still positive. Its just that you are new. Its fine. Your claim to fame will come. You decide to take it easy and become an Infiltrator. Hanging back, spotting high value targets, maybe taking a few out here and there. Sounds pretty sneaky. And awesome....mostly awesome.
However this doesn't last long because there are dozens of other snipers out there, all are better then you. You try every class in the game and slowly treck through every territory on the map hoping for a fight you can win. What you didn't realize is that Space-America is the worst faction in the game. They have less people and apparently don't know what vehicles are because you haven't seen a friendly one in ages. Wait...is that dropship ours? Oh thank god! Thank sweet merciful christ! Take me with you, I want to have fun!
He swoops down as if to pick you up. And then runs you over at terminal velocity. Death....4.....3.....2.......4....SPAWN
You are in dismay now. You wanted a fun experience and to get into large fights that seemed to be so equal and coordinated. Massive tank assaults, valiant infantry raids. None of that seems to be there for you. You just run from base to base as each one is taken by another faction. The enemy vehicles and infantry seem inexhaustible and the armor of both is impenetrable. There is no hope of your success; of your feeling good. You are just a cog in a dying war machine.
You go to the top of one of your last friendly bases and watch your allies march on to the front. You never did learn how to get into a squad with people. If only the tutorial had explained how to do that. Oh well, you leap off of the base and hurtle to the ground below, striking it with what you imagine would be a soft squish.
Death.....prepare to respawn.

Tried to get into the game but couldn't. The deal breaker for me was the way hits are handled. A few examples are as follows.
1.) Two people with shotguns shoot at each other at the same time but only one person dies and the other person takes no damage.
2.) You run behind a wall but die. The post-death shows you getting killed before you made it at the wall.
3.) You shoot a person multiple times yet he takes no damage while damaging you.
These three things turned me off from the game completely. I looked up the issue and it seems that it's because of the way lag works. I always found it odd that sometimes I would be instantly gunned down by people turning corners but it's because their ping is 3-5 times mine and it allows for them to hit me before my hits register.
Fun premise but getting killed by high ping players is a big no-no. Didn't have this issue in TF2.

Wolfenstein The New Order is without a doubt in my mind an amazing game.
Machine Games knew the risk of developing this and I feel they pulled it off.
The gameplay is an incredibly fluid and accessible experience. The variety of not only missions and situations but also your own equipment and tactics is staggering. Just like in classic old school shooters you're allowed freedom in how you tackle situations. The gameplay never feels rigidly scripted and the player is free to break stealth into a deadly assault at their own choice.
For many people this will range from silently evading and assassinating targets one by one to running in guns blazing with your dual assault rifles in a relentless assault. The game promotes and encourages the player to experiment with a variety of both weaponry and multiple paths throughout the mission area. Despite being a game with linear progression, it never truly feels that way and offers a high amount of re-playability.
One notable example is a night time assault early in the game. While it encourages stealth, it is completely possible to run in loud. In-fact it is even possible to combine the two, silently killing the commanders and then zip-lining to the nearby roof. To open fire with your dual assault rifles on the Nazis below you. The possibilities presented are endless and just as open from one mission to the next, with minimum control by the game for certain story related events.
However, I feel the true defining factor in TNO is the gripping weave of both intense gameplay and touching narrative. Despite being in an alternative universe with retro-scifi robotic Nazi soldiers, Machine Games was able to produce a world that contrasts clearly with ours and holds no punches back with its brutal reality.
The idea of a world controlled by the Nazis is very real and incredibly chilling. No expense is spared to show how such a world would function. The world is "perfect", under control of the regime and their fascist ideals. Every single facet of the Nazi doctrine is clear, the world is purged of the inferior; science is amoral and followed fanatically with a bent to weapons research to ensure maximum control and dominance. The world is rigid, inspected, "safe" and without due process. Everything monitored, controlled, and censored by the state.
But the story is more than just the bigger picture. The struggle of the resistance and of humanity is a huge focus as well. Characters are incredibly well written and display believable emotion that is aided by amazing acting, both the facial/motion capture actors and voice actors.
Its heavy on the symbolism and commentary. Going as far as to point out the hypocritical violence and slaughter the main character thrives in, but even further to show the hypocritical treatment of minorities during the 1940s. Machine Games also had no problem showing the extent of human psychology and the way people attempt to justify their actions. The main antagonist justifies not only his creations but also of the Nazi idealism “It matters not what you destroy, but what of you Create”.
TNO is not only a fun game, but also an intelligent one. Its a game that bucks the idea that video games are not art, that video games cannot be meaningful and that old school shooters are nothing more than mindless violence. It is as poetic, symbolic, and intelligent as it is violent, energetic, and fun.

The original Age of Empires II is was my favourite PC game, without question.
The HD edition fixes all manner of issues that plagued the original on modern systems, replaces the long-discontinued microsoft gaming zone with the steam lobby, and adds workshop support. I can't speak to the latter, having not tried to add any mods yet, but working multiplayer and fixing the graphics glitches are more than enough to breath new life into the game for me.
The HD addition also increases the highest population cap setting in random map games to 500, and the Forgotten DLC adds (among other things) a larger map size.
In summary, this is a good reimplementation of classic game. And if you get it on sale, it won't cost you a fortune.

Ok, coming from me, the original FPS fan, this is AMAZING. I'm only a few hours in, but this game is everything I wanted and more. This is worth the money - I feel like some ID really put some serious thought and effort into making an enjoyable game.
Pros: Some truly uncomfortable horror scenes, compelling story, well-developed characters, highly destructible dynamic environments, satisfying gore, action straight out of a 80's Ahnold movie, and special effects worth writing home about. You will not get bored playing this game - it's clear that a lot of thought went into it. It even has a "lite" stealth system and accompanying choices of how to strategically approach each situation. It also doesn't hold your hand through every individual scenario ala Call Of Duty (and this is coming from a COD fan.) While it is linear, there is a greater degree of choice involved here in how to attack it. The AI is very, very good. They're not shooting gallery pop-ups hiding behind a single piece of cover. They move to flank, stalk, investigate, retreat etc. Hide in a room to catch your breath for too long, and one of them will run up, throw a grenade inside, and retreat for cover again to flush you out.
Cons: It ate♥♥♥♥♥♥and crashed to desktop until I installed the latest AMD/Catalyst update. I have a high-end gaming-specific computer, and it still stutters frequently on the sound - particularly during in-game cut scenes. While not nearly as linear as COD, it is far from being as open-approach as Dishonored (which it seems to be getting frequent comparisons to for some odd reason.) No multiplayer of any kind - this would have been a badass co-op game.
In summary, if you're on the fence at all: BUY IT. As long as your system can support it, it's worth every penny to the devoted shooter fan.

PlanetSide 2 is one of a kind. There are currently no other games like it on the market, except PlanetSide 1 which requires a subscription. The game is Combined Arms. Infantry, Vehicles, and Aircraft, with a tag line "Size. Does. Matter." If you want giant battles that feel like D-Day with Sci Fi technology, this is the game for you. The game, like every other game since Pong, has it's issues. Balance is a big thing that is constantly being discussed. The Devs up until this point have played an endless game of Buff and Nerf with actual improvements few and far between. The game has three different factions you can play as, which changes the formula from the same boring 2 Faction system most people are used to. The game is also in it's current state, NOT new player friendly at all. This has been acknowledged by the developers and are taking steps to change that. Until then, if you are new and wish to learn this game then find an Outfit, a real Outfit. Lots of Outfits aren't the most strategiclly minded you could say.
The Community, on the surface of it can appear to be very toxic for a new player who does not know. Frankly in a lot of ways it is, and it is mostly due to the developers lack of progress. It has made the fans rather bitter over time. However often times, lots of the trash talking you see in the Chat is all in good fun. Of course this also depends on your chosen server. Some are worse than others. On my Server of Emerald, after a long, hard fought Event, the teams will congragulate each other on a hard fought match (most of the time). Try not to take comments too personally, easier said than done to be sure. There are tons of videos on Youtube that go over the basics of the game, made by the players for new people since the game currently lacks a real introduction for people. I highly recommend watching them before you even start the game up.
PlanetSide also contains a very rich and deep back story, if you are interested in that sort of thing. From my observations 95% of the player base eaither does not care or does not know about it. Insisting the Red faction are Commi Russians (They aren't). The game seems like it portrays the Blue faction (The New Conglomerate) as the "good guys", and most of it's players are always screaming about Freedom. This is not the case at all, as the NC is mearly Mercs who are fighting for Corporations who desire no Government oversight so they can be as shady as they want. The Red faction (The Terran Republic) is the legitimate Government that came from Earth, they have become a military dictatorship since being stranded on the planet of Auraxisis. They seek to restore Peace to the planet at any cost, and reestablish contact with Earth. The final faction is the Vanu Soverignty. These are basically techno cultists who worship an alien called Vanu, and believe humanity's future is to merge with this strange alien technology.
SOE no longer exists, and the new owners have been replacing the old SOE Dev teams and have started cranking out optimization patches in the last month. There are lots of things still in the pipline, and have been for years, so the fans aren't that excited yet. The game is NOT Pay2Win, whoever tells you that is frankly wrong. Paying money simply removes hours of grind, and nothing more. With Planetside 2, there is proof that F2P doesn't always mean P2W, and that a gaming community is capable of creating their own playspaces and narratives better than any scripted event series.

This game is a massive treat, especially with dual weilding all but two of the weapons in the game, being able to unleash hell upon swarms of nazi soldiers as a one man army. Along with having the ability to either play stealthy, tactical or balls to the walls guns blazing inferno. The only downside is that you cannot shoot while sprinting but you're able to shoot while jumping, even though the jumping feels more like you're skipping along the ground. There's also a hint system that could disable or enable if you wish that'll help you out if you get stuck in certain sections including a seperate hint for loot as well for when you get close enough to them. There's also unlockable perks that in all honesty, don't really change the gameplay up.
For my 3 year old computer, the game looks pretty good on average settings and runs fairly decently except for within a few places, mainly during the first few missions of the game but besides that, the game runs perfectly fine most of the time. In terms of graphics options, majority of the options have been fitted under the same option rather than them being seperate, you are also given the option between fullscreen and window mode and the screen resolution options are filtered to the ones that would best fit your monitor.
The story is a pretty accurate on how far the Nazi's would've advanced in technology if they achieved world domination, their sole focus on these kind of things would've meant faster acceleration. However, it kinda goes a little crazy when you get half way through the story. Without spoiling it I can easily say that the ending is pretty bad and totally not what I was expecting either, which is a massive disappointment, there's also next to no replayability to this game besides chosing who dies during the intro chapter which changes one character within the hideout and provides different cutscenes & dialog in relation to this character. Oh and there's no dialog difference between the two characters that you had to pick during the intro chapter either, they say the exact same thing in both play throughs most of the time, with only very few differences between the dialog for me. So besides replaying for dialog and cutscenes and upgrading health and armor along with perk unlocking, there's nothing else worth while to make you revisit the game a third time.
Now, there was a leak before the launch of the game that revealed that melee units had extremely poor AI, which is basically true, but you only have to deal with melee units twice within the whole game, both times are prison breaks as well. The only melee unit that was actually fine was the dogs, which of course, just run up to you and attempt to bite you in a QTE.
Besides that, most of the time the AI feels like dumbed down aimbots, that just walk around and shoot at you if they see you, even if its on the otherside of a giant room, losing them however is possible, since they don't know where you are majority of the time if you choose to break line of sight often. However with two boss battles that I encountered, both times fighting giant mecha units, they constantly knew where I was, constantly shot at me even when behind cover and where basically just walking bullet sponges with turrets attachted that would rip you apart if you stayed out in the open. From what I've also noticed, is that the difficulty only changes how much damage you need to deal in order to kill enemies and how much damage they deal to you, which in honesty, doesn't change the difficulty, it just ruins gameplay, slows you down and turns the gameplay into a chore.
There's also special units that you'll encounter throughout the game, ranging from four varients, one that'll call backup if he spots you or he's alerted of your position. Bullet sponges that come with either a rocket launcher, shotgun or machine gun and robots that are also bullet sponges and will rip you to shreds if you get to close, oh and they'll also instant kill you if you attempt a melee kill. You're also unable to kill rocket launchers and shotgunners with melee as well as they just block your attack or their armor is to thick for your knife. Oh and giant attack dogs that'll only be killed by machine guns or explosives.
And as stated before the difficulty only changes the damage you recieve and how much damage the enemies can take, from what I can see the AI behavour between normal and easy isn't different, besides that basic soldiers won't lob nades at you constantly if you hide behind cover. But they'll still act like walking aimbots.
Most of the time you're always heading down a set path, in some sections you are granted a little more freedom when approaching areas that involve you plowing down tons of enemies or if you're in some rooms that happen to be crawling with nazi soldiers. As for detail, the game is enriched with it, every environment is unique and different to each other and really capatures the atmosphere.
Gameplay is pretty fun, being capable of totally destroying nazies to shreds with any weapon(s) that you obtain and being able to play differently in each section if you wish.
Graphics is pretty good, looks pretty decent on my computer and runs just fine at most times.
Story is ok, but it kinda becomes a massive disappointment with its ending and there isn't much a difference between the sacrifice choice during the intro chapter.
Difficulty is not challenging, becomes repetitive and turns the game into a chore due to the massive excess of bullet sponged enemies that can instant snap to you along with bosses that know where you are, constantly, non-stop.
Level design is really appealing, each environment is different, doesn't feel repetitive, as for the flow of movement most of the time it feels linear, you're constantly moving in one direction and most alternate paths loop.
This game is great if you just want to have fun while killing Nazi's.
This game will run decently on most computers that are around 3 years old now, older than that however you might encounter some difficulties running this game.
This game is ok when it comes to its story, but as said, the ending is a disappointment.
This game will not challenge you, as the difficulty only changes the damage and some minor AI behaviors like nade lobbing and being able to see you through walls.
This game is extremely appealing to the eyes with each environment enriched with detail, so much to look at, so much to read and listen to, it's like candy.
