Okay, so after playing a bit over five freaking hundred hours of Dirty Bomb I think that I got a pretty solid opinion about this game.
Overall Dirty Bomb is a fun shooter with real fun mechanics and pretty interesting mercs, albeit loadouts could use some more variety, personally I think they probably could find a way of testing some new weapons for certain mercs, because unfortunately, for me, after all this play time, the game got stale.
Don't get me wrong, it's a really fun game, used to play it 8 to 12 hours straight on some days, but because of that I learned everything about every merc, whom are quite easy to learn and read after a while of playing with/against them.
Anyway, back to the "stale" issue. The game has five overall "classes", Medic, Support, Assault, Engineer and Recon. Now, back to the loadouts I was talking about earlier. Loadouts come from cases (they have RNG chance to drop after any match or you can buy them from their in-game store for 1000 credits, trust me, it's not that much), maxing out at bronze (actually it's Cobalt but anything above Bronze is purely cosmetic) with 3 perks that can "help" your merc, imo 90% of them are useless apart from the Chopper perk (which is the only perk that actually adds damage, to your melee, except for that, no other damage perks for any other weapons), moving on, loadouts come with 3 different weapons, Primary (Rifle, SMG, Sniper, whatever you get the idea), Secondary (Pistol or weaker SMG for some classes) and melee obviously.
Now this is the part that made the game for me stale:
Overall loadouts come with a lot of different perks, but roughly the same 3 or 4 primary, secondary or melee weapons. For example:
A Recon merc will always have a sniper (unless we're counting Phantom, the spooky invisible ghost, that has SMGs as primaries), a Medic will always have either a shotgun or that one rifle, okay everything seems fine and dandy right? Well what if I told you that Engineers use exactly the same weapons as the medics, almost all Support classes use some Assault rifle, see AK47 and M4 from CS, or a burst rifle that fires 3 shots per click (not interchangeable with full auto-fire). Some Support mercs don't even have an assault rifle at all and just burst rifles (which makes you keep a distance and really focus on your aim on a game that's based around movement.
Anyway, I presume that you can now tell how the game got stale for me after so much playtime, using the same weapons on multiple mercs, having the same damage, it's easy to get bored of playing the "same" thing, the only difference sometimes only being the special skills on the merc, for example some repair objectives or plant C4's faster, some give out ammo, some heal, etc. But that's it.
I think, to conclude, the game is good, apart from some bugs here and there, totally worth a try or 7, I mean, I was addicted to it at some point, so like any review, take what I'm saying with a grain of salt, mainly because I have friends that are still playing the game a lot. I am still playing the game now and then for an hour or two, but overall there's just not enough variety for me, anymore.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a game set in 1960. Not the swinging sixties, the nazi sixties. Doesn't really have the same ring to it. You play as B.J. Blazkowicz, who is part of the resistance against the Nazi overlords.
I won't say much more about the story apart from I rather liked it.
The guns are loud and dangerous. They also produce a lot of blood out of nazi foes, also sometimes taking limbs off and popping open their chests. (I love you shotgun)
Enemy AI isn't 100%. I sometimes found enemies shooting at walls and a bit dim with stealth sections. Although tougher enemies warrant some caution when attacking them as they deal large amounts of damage in one or two hits. (on medium difficulty)
Graphically isn't 100% either. It's not "rendered" on DirectX 11 or 10, this is done by OpenGL. (OpenGL and DirectX are called APIs) Textures look flat if you get too close. Darker areas seem to have some kind of grainy-ness to them. Cutscenes are either done on a different API or just for some reason look way better than the actual game. The eyes of characters in cutscenes are really high quality as is the texture work on character's faces.
Levels are nicely designed and quite nice to look at despite some textures not being so great. Levels are large and rife with places to explore.
Voice acting is rather good. B.J Blazkowicz is well voiced by the same guy who voiced by Kane from the Kane & Lynch games and Jackie from The Darkness II. Every other significant character is nicely done too.
I believe some players may be put off by the fact of no multiplayer (personally not me) because no replayability. I've completed the game in around 9 hours. But, that is just one "timeline" that I have completed. There are also enigma codes to find. Which you then decrypt for different gamemodes or game types.
Overall, I rather liked this game. I recommend this game to anyone who loves shooting the hell out of Nazis.
Quick edit: There is one bug which irritated me was a fps glitch where I would get 2fps randomly, at the start of levels, after cutscenes. Only closing the game then relaunching would fix. Could be a driver problem, not sure.
Also, the system requirements are rubbish. I played this on:
i5 3570K at 3.40Ghz (Yeah. Not an i7.)
8Gb RAM
nVidia Geforce GTX 770 2Gb VRAM.
Windows 7 64bit Home Premium.
Ran at 60fps constantly. (Apart from the above bug/driver issue)

The learning curve isn't steep and if you have experience in this genre you'll be fluent in no time. All game modes are objective based, making it rewarding for gamers that like to frag, contribute to a main goal or support other players. Dirty bomb rewards you with ingame currency when you do daily missions, receive a win of the day and play all game modes. In no time you will be able to unlock your favourite content. Everything is immediately available through micro transactions but in no way is it pay to win. DB reminds me of all the things I like in older fast paced FPS shooters but was missing in the modern ones.

As a longtime player of the first PlanetSide, and having been with PlanetSide 2 since the technical test several years ago, I figured I'd share my opinion with prospective Auraxis troopers now that SOE has become Daybreak Games.  Before I go on, I want to say that I HIGHLY recommend the game, but I am going to open up with the 'bad' before going on to the good.
Despite the game having been out for some time, the meta of the objectives (taking territory) is still very weak; this is not the global strategic warfare that was so evident in the first game.  Outside of Alerts (a feature which emphasizes a certain continent for a couple of hours), territory is essentially meaningless.  What this means it that the game as a whole is for the most part a glorified, large-scale death match, and while this is not necessarily a bad thing in and of itself, fans of the first PlanetSide's intercontinental strategy will be dissapointed.  Hopefully, this will be something that becomes more prevalent in time.
One of the biggest questions I see when people ask about the game is how "pay-to-win" is it.  The answer; not very, especially if you compare it to other F2P FPS games out there.  Weapons and weapon attachments can all be purchased with real money or in-game currency (certification points, or 'certs').  While a new weapon can cost anywhere between 250 to 1000 certification points (a hefty sum for a new player, but not nearly as expensive as some would think), the thing about the many weapons available is that essentially, they're all sidegrades or situational; the weapons the game starts you with are some of the more reliable and well-rounded guns you have access to, and there are plenty of players who primarily use just what the game gives them to start with.
Another commonly voiced concern is the level (Battle Rank) disparity; when you make your level one character, you will be facing level 100 characters right off the bat.  How much of a difference does this make in a firefight?  Assuming equal skill on both players' parts, very little.  A higher level essentially means access to a wider variety of class tools and alternate abilities (a resist shield instead of a mesh shield, for example), but very little in the way of escalating strength.  Yes, a level 100 will probably have access to a health kit he can pop behind cover, or have shields that recharge a little quicker, but those things matter little when staring at the barrel of a level 1's weapon.
Having said that, one of the biggest deterrents for new players is just how different, even overwhelming, the game can be.  In a huge open world with hundreds of infantry players battling it out,  planes and bombers overhead, and tanks and armored vehicles shelling the landscape, all in numbers unparalled in any other game you've played before; you will die, and you will die a lot.  Regardless of what other FPS games you've played, there will be a learning curve when you first begin, and you may feel like you are useless or just 'bad' for some time.  Watching others place via stream, or even looking up a guide, can go a long way in how to orient yourself.
The game has had a history of optimization woes, but the remaining issues are minimal for those with a decent gaming PC; again, there are plenty of guides on the forums and elsewheres for tweaking your performance, particularly if you have an older computer.
So why do I recommend PlanetSide 2?  Because there's nothing else out there that matches it in terms of the expansiveness of the battlefields and sheer number of players and options those players have to fight on them.  Players have the option to fufill whatever role they wish, from medic to air transport pilot, and everything in betwen.  Tactically, it might be severly dumbed down from PlanetSide 1, but it's still miles beyond any other game out there.  It's a rich, flavorful world that is constantly being added and expanded upon, each of the three factions unique and appealing in their own style.

Like a lot of people, I approached the new Wolfenstein with quite a bit of trepidation. After all, the original Wolfenstein 3D, and Return To Castle Wolfenstein are both standouts of their respective generations, while the last Wolfenstein game (2009) was a mixed bag, and came at a strange time in the evolution of the FPS. The involvement of Starbreeze staff certainly piqued my interest, while the presence of IDTech5, which powered the inconsistent and troubled RAGE made me wonder if this would be another mediocrity which traded on nostalgia.
While not reaching the classic status of Wolf3D or RTCW, this is a fine iteration of the game, delivering more than enough Nazi-shooting for the seasoned FPS player. IDTech5 problems do render the framerates inconsistent at times, but the graphics are largely powerful and impressive, with a number of superb set pieces. The ballistics that RAGE was known for are not present in WTNO - and some of the firearm sounds are underwhelming, most notably the shotgun which lacks the satisfyingly bassy 'BOOM' of the Doom or Quake shotguns. The game delivers on the gore front, and it one of the most gruesome shooters since Soldier Of Fortune/Double Helix - body parts are sheared away as blood splatters on the walls and floors.
Is a storyline in a Wolfenstein title a kind of heresy against the legacy of the series? Perhaps. This is not a pure shooter, as Wolf3D was, but it is certainly not a prescriptive, linear corridor shooter in the tradition of Call Of Duty. It's a kind of hybrid of the two, closer in feel to the Shadow Warrior remake, with cutscenes providing context for the action, but certainly never substituting gameplay. Like a lot of people, I approached the new Wolfenstein with quite a bit of trepidation. After all, the original Wolfenstein 3D, and Return To Castle Wolfenstein are both standouts of their respective generations, while the last Wolfenstein game (2009) was a mixed bag, and came at a strange time in the evolution of the FPS. The involvement of Starbreeze staff certainly piqued my interest, while the presence of IDTech5, which powered the inconsistent and troubled RAGE made me wonder if this would be another mediocrity which traded on nostalgia.
While not reaching the classic status of Wolf3D or RTCW, this is a fine iteration of the game, delivering more than enough Nazi-shooting for the seasoned FPS player. IDTech5 problems do render the framerates inconsistent at times, but the graphics are largely powerful and impressive, with a number of superb set pieces. The ballistics that RAGE was known for are not present in WTNO - and some of the firearm sounds are underwhelming, most notably the shotgun which lacks the satisfyingly bassy 'BOOM' of the Doom or Quake shotguns. The game delivers on the gore front, and it one of the most gruesome shooters since Soldier Of Fortune/Double Helix - body parts are sheared away as blood splatters on the walls and floors.
Is a storyline in a Wolfenstein title a kind of heresy against the legacy of the series? Perhaps. This is not a pure shooter, as Wolf3D was, but it is certainly not a prescriptive, linear corridor shooter in the tradition of Call Of Duty. It's a kind of hybrid of the two, closer in feel to the Shadow Warrior remake, with cutscenes providing context for the action, but certainly never substituting gameplay. This is a game that you play, not watch - you will be required to fight your way through the Nazi hordes more often than sitting in anticipation as you watch another shoddily written cutscene.
While it doesn't add to the Wolfenstein legacy - it is too focused on finding a space in the cluttered FPS marketplace to function as a pure extension of the Wolf3D template - WTNO is certainly a fine example of the modern FPS; taut, sharp, and muscular - all meat and no fat. The lack of multiplayer is irrelevant; any multiplayer would have been redundant and peripheral, adding nothing to what this game is attempting to do. Instead, we have an exercise in FPS traditionalism, cut with a modern aesthetic, and a willingness to embrace the action movie tropes of the past, dispensing with the irony of Serious Sam, or the rebellion of Rise Of The Triad, and instead choosing to authentically honour the legacy of one of the finest FPS series' in gaming history.

Dont let my hours detur you, i have over 200 hours clock into the game from the website. Though i reccomend it to get a larger playerbase on it, the game is in turmoil right now. In Emerald(the US server) the vanu still reign supreme, the TR and NC perfer to fight each other rather than the VS(unless one of those two have ~40 territory control). You play in good/fun fights then watch as your faction either gets steamrolled into oblivion, or proceeds to do that and kill the fight. I have a BR60(ish) TR and its hard to find a fight where i am not getting murdered or just playing it on easy mode. On top of all that, PS2 just went through a management change, so its likely we wont see much on top of that. The main issue is, though, is that the gameplay is COD domination and nothing more. yea you have 3 factions, vehicles, and much much larger maps, but the core gameplay has remained the same for 2 years now. Go to this place, Cap this(these) points, hold these points for 3-20 minuites(depending on contestion), kill the enemy still around, move on, rinse and repeat for X amount of territories, then be on the recieving end of that cycle.                                                                                                                  After all i said, i still love thsi game. It will give hours of fun and enjoyment of team work and cooperation. You will feel the thrill of being the last squad holding the final point for the last 20 seconds, to the despair of being wiped out. You have 3 whole factions to choose from, all of which have different playstyles, a huge community who will help newer players at a moments notice, and when you arent getting steamrolled, have some of the biggest battles that any modern FPS could only dream of creating.                                                  So for right now, play it for a while. If you dont liek it, wait a couple of months and see what happens. I personaly give it a 9/10 for overall game quality, even though PS2 is in a rough spot at the moment.

Dont let my hours detur you, i have over 200 hours clock into the game from the website. Though i reccomend it to get a larger playerbase on it, the game is in turmoil right now. In Emerald(the US server) the vanu still reign supreme, the TR and NC perfer to fight each other rather than the VS(unless one of those two have ~40 territory control). You play in good/fun fights then watch as your faction either gets steamrolled into oblivion, or proceeds to do that and kill the fight. I have a BR60(ish) TR and its hard to find a fight where i am not getting murdered or just playing it on easy mode. On top of all that, PS2 just went through a management change, so its likely we wont see much on top of that. The main issue is, though, is that the gameplay is COD domination and nothing more. yea you have 3 factions, vehicles, and much much larger maps, but the core gameplay has remained the same for 2 years now. Go to this place, Cap this(these) points, hold these points for 3-20 minuites(depending on contestion), kill the enemy still around, move on, rinse and repeat for X amount of territories, then be on the recieving end of that cycle.                                                                                                                  After all i said, i still love thsi game. It will give hours of fun and enjoyment of team work and cooperation. You will feel the thrill of being the last squad holding the final point for the last 20 seconds, to the despair of being wiped out. You have 3 whole factions to choose from, all of which have different playstyles, a huge community who will help newer players at a moments notice, and when you arent getting steamrolled, have some of the biggest battles that any modern FPS could only dream of creating.                                                  So for right now, play it for a while. If you dont liek it, wait a couple of months and see what happens. I personaly give it a 9/10 for overall game quality, even though PS2 is in a rough spot at the moment.

This used to be such an incredibly fun game to play and fill time with for hours on end. It was a free game with simple mechanics; build a bot to crush your opponents, you die once and you're sent back to main menu to join another game, you win and you feel like the effort you went into building your craft was well worth the blood, sweat and tears. This was a game that didn't beg you to spend a cent of your money on it (although I did, often, and never minded doing so ... it was worth supporting). Now what really matters is your wallet size. What really matters is what you find in loot-crates. That's very disappointing to me, and many others that started around when I did and before me. Skill and creativity are completely thrown out of the window, and into the vaccuum of space.
A couple of years ago I saw this game on Early Access with a $0 price-tag. It costed nothing and that really meant it. It was way too good to be true. I jumped in with high expectations and they met all of them (aside from being occasionally railed by one-gun bots in the sky you could barely see). Enter sleepless nights of building and battling, jumping game-to-game, win-after-win or death-after-death; It didn't matter. If you were skilled enough you could build the battlebot you've always wanted. If a player had a differently colored hull on their bot from everyone else you knew that this person was skilled and was pushing through the ranks. These were the players you either knew to stay away from on red team, or to stick close to on blue.
There was a time when I would recommend this game to anyone. Now, it's a broken shell of its former self. I would never play this anymore. Match-making is broken, "Epic Loot" is BROKEN, gaining credits for parts through skill is a laughable method to gain them, the tech tree was great until they broke it, lower-teired weaponry actually does better in most cases than higher-tiered weaponry that you probably paid for, playing with friends in your platoon was so fun until they broke that, too.
This game needs a roll-back. It was still playable up until the respawn mechanic in my opinion. If they took that effort to stop p***ing off their old player-base then this game is definitely worth coming back to. For now, don't even bother looking at this blatant scam P2W title.

Ladies and gentlemen welcome to an old school shooter. I've really run tired of all these FPS military tactical shooter nonsense that has been released for a really long time, so this game was a breath of fresh air to say the least and it is AWESOME!
I'm not gonna go into much detail about the game since i do not want to spoil any of the fun for ya but i will mention some of the game mechanics.
This has it all (for me at least) to be called an old school shooter. You can carry a whole arsenal of weapons so bye bye two or three weapon carrying limit, you can actually dual wield most of the weapons in the game which is really fun. The game also has a perk system which requires you to do certain skill shots or the like to unlock them some are very basic and generic while a few of them requires a little bit of effort to complete.
Although the game is a run and gun there is a cover system you can use, it is a little bit weird though since it requires you to hold down a key to be able to lean out with the A or D keyes, I did however find out that if you stand a little bit out to the edge of a door opening or some other cover you will automatically lean out when aiming. It works fairly well although I haven't used it that much. You can however take a lot of punishment, this will of course differentiate as to what difficulty setting you choose to use.
There is also stealth in the game however basic it does work well and i can attest to it being a really good idea to use.
Graphics wise it is not the best I've seen, in certain areas you'll notice that some textures or modelling is very basic while other places are really well done in my honest opinion it is'nt bad at all and to be fair most of the game is really gorgeous.
Throughout the game there will be different kind of collectibles to obtain some of them will unlock additional game play modes, I can however not confirm what kind it is since I haven't been able to do this but i will say that the game has a fair amount of hours game play it took me around 16 hours to complete my first playthrough.
This game has a pretty good story the voice acting is very well done, it has a lot of humor and I really enjoyed it very much
so if you're into these kind of shooters with lots of gore good story and lots and lots of shooting this will be your kind of game on a scale from 0-10 I'd give it a 9.

I used to play this game often. I would come home and jump on for an hour or two just to have lots of fun and stff with my friends... However having fun allowed me to get to level 110 over my time playing and as I can see myself as a vet I can say this game went from good to bad.
Firstly, Yes this game has its good points like the ability to show creativity and to have fun with your friends. But the bad points are just so much that its really taken the fun out of it.
"- Over 200 cubes and components to collect and combine to make a million different Robot designs " Which are instantly thrown against the noobs as they start off with weak little robots with smgs. I bet you can tell how it would feel to be this small little robot and having 7 snipers 100 rockets and a few planes coming at you. Not good.
"- Watch as your enemy's robot breaks apart cube by cube as you destroy them with powerful weaponry" As you obvs know exactly how to play from the get go and have all these weapons at the start... He lied.
"- Invite friends and chat in-game" as long as you only have 2 friends... If you have 3 then expect to pay for the game. Any more then that and you are out of luck.
"- Save your robots in the garage to the cloud and share them with other players via the in-game Robot Factory." Assuming anyone will actually buy your robot. You will have to pay to get it on the store and unless you are well known or have a fantastic design then no one will buy your robot and you will have just lost dust (in game currency).
"- Free-to-win, everything required to get to the very top of the tree in Robocraft can be gained for free" Assuming you grind for hours and hours and hours and die far too often. The best way to get to the top would be to be a medic and hide behind 6 guys with big guns. But you cant get the medic gun unless you actually grind.
The loot crate system... First of all this whole concept can suck a bag of d***s. The devs used the games popularity to make the game a pay to win. The best way to get new stuff is to get it in a crate unless you are max level and can grind out the dust to pay for these items. But then again the best thing you will get out of the crates will be 20 cubes. These cubes are worthless and you cant even get anything new if you wanted to sell those cubes. The epic loot will only be found on your 1000th crate you open and that not even the best items you can get.
And finally. Once you get all of these cubes and items and whatnot, You can build with these items or you could sell these items for 10% of what it would cost to buy these items again. The game has turned call of duty on us and revolve around getting these loot crates.
Overall. This game was good.
But now...
Not so much.

Ladies and gentlemen welcome to an old school shooter. I've really run tired of all these FPS military tactical shooter nonsense that has been released for a really long time, so this game was a breath of fresh air to say the least and it is AWESOME!
I'm not gonna go into much detail about the game since i do not want to spoil any of the fun for ya but i will mention some of the game mechanics.
This has it all (for me at least) to be called an old school shooter. You can carry a whole arsenal of weapons so bye bye two or three weapon carrying limit, you can actually dual wield most of the weapons in the game which is really fun. The game also has a perk system which requires you to do certain skill shots or the like to unlock them some are very basic and generic while a few of them requires a little bit of effort to complete.
Although the game is a run and gun there is a cover system you can use, it is a little bit weird though since it requires you to hold down a key to be able to lean out with the A or D keyes, I did however find out that if you stand a little bit out to the edge of a door opening or some other cover you will automatically lean out when aiming. It works fairly well although I haven't used it that much. You can however take a lot of punishment, this will of course differentiate as to what difficulty setting you choose to use.
There is also stealth in the game however basic it does work well and i can attest to it being a really good idea to use.
Graphics wise it is not the best I've seen, in certain areas you'll notice that some textures or modelling is very basic while other places are really well done in my honest opinion it is'nt bad at all and to be fair most of the game is really gorgeous.
Throughout the game there will be different kind of collectibles to obtain some of them will unlock additional game play modes, I can however not confirm what kind it is since I haven't been able to do this but i will say that the game has a fair amount of hours game play it took me around 16 hours to complete my first playthrough.
This game has a pretty good story the voice acting is very well done, it has a lot of humor and I really enjoyed it very much
so if you're into these kind of shooters with lots of gore good story and lots and lots of shooting this will be your kind of game on a scale from 0-10 I'd give it a 9.

EXPLAINING THE GAME:
It's like Starcraft when it comes to gamemechanics.
You have some units that are better against other, and weaker against some. You have other units that are decent towards other units, and have no real weakness. If we're talking in terms of Starcraft, you have the units such as the Terran valkyrie, or in Starcraft II, the Protos Pheanix, both great against air, but very exposed towards ground. Then you have the well known marines, that are decent towards anything, but again, no strenght or weakness, In Age of Empires II you have the swordsmen, no pluss or minus, and the cav, good against swords, weak against spear. So as I mentioned, the mechanics are pretty much the same as Starcraft.
But the concept is a bit different. You start in the dark age, and can chose to get up to the imperial age, giving you a lot of benefits in terms of military and economical strenght. In difference to Starcraft, economy plays a bigger role in Age of Empire II than it does in Starcraft. Age of Empires is more like the full RTS version of Rome: Total war, economy is just as important as anything else.
THE VERDICT:
So Age of Empires have it's simularities, which I think is great. But everything isn't fun if it is the same story again, and the developers have made sure to take that into considiration. Age of Empires features simple economy management, which plays a big role in the game. It's not hard to handle, but if you focuse to little on one resource, it sure will give a knockback when you really need those resources. To put it all in a easier way, you will like it like any other game, but it all comes down to the player, and if he likes to have a mix between settlers and starcraft.

I've been playing this game for years. Among MMOs this is definitely one of my favorites of all time.
There's a lot to learn and I think the new game experience might be overwhelming for many new players who were expecting a traditional FPS. That said,
. There may not be a lot to do currently (it's always base capture) but because of how complicated it is to capture most bases, and how much teamwork and coordination is required to attack or defend during organized pushes, it's always fun for me.
As a testament to how it's not a traditional FPS, the most useful people are usually not the ones with the best kill:death ratio, but the ones who follow orders and almost always the ones who do support things well.
For example: full-time medics don't usually get kills, but they are essential in massive pushes in reviving MAX suits and engineers who repair them. At the end of a major push that medic might get 0 kills and several deaths as he risked his life several times to save others, but without that medic and others like him, the push most likely would've failed.
Another example, drivers and pilots can't get kills except by running enemies over, which isn't very common. But transporting troops at the right time with the right coordination will often turn the tide.
Short answer: not in any way.
It's pretty easy to earn in-game currency to unlock weapons and perks with. You can't unlock perks with real money but you can buy weapons and skins of course with real money. Buying weapons might sound like a pay-to-win thing but it really isn't, and here's why.
The weapons available in game aren't necessarily better or worse than each other overall. Instead you unlock weapons that have certain strengths and weaknesses.
For example, the standard weapon for a Lightning Tank is called a C75 Viper. It fires 6 semi-automatic shots in fairly rapid succession with good range and accuracy, a decent blast radius for infantry, and decent damage against armor, and the projectile is fast enough so that you can damage low-flying aircraft with it as well. You can replace that weapon with a "Skyguard", which is a multi-barrel anti-air weapon. It's a very rapid-firing gun with lots of ammo and gets a flak burst that's highly effective against aircraft, but its lack of accuracy and armor piercing make it less useful against infantry and armor.
The standard weapons for each class or vehicle are usually all-around and very well balanced, and they are useful even at high levels.
And again, like I said, the upgrades that actually matter (weapon attachments, abilities) can't be bought with real money and need to be unlocked using in-game currency, which you earn by doing things that help (kills, healing/repairing, transporting troops, etc.).
It's a fun game that's best played with a team (you can find squads/platoons in-game). Best played with a mic so you can coordinate with others. You don't need TeamSpeak or other third-party voice chat clients as the game has its own effective voice chat system (including proximity chat, selective muting, individual volume sliders for that one guy whose mic is way too loud, etc.), but some Outfits like to use third party software too.
Once you get the hang of all of the little intricacies and what it takes to capture a base, it's very fun and I always get a sense of accomplishment whenever I was part of a massive victory.

This game is a lot of fun to pick up and play with friends, it's not difficult to learn the basics, and since I first sampled this game in its early stages, it has improved greatly. The entire experience is nice. This game is not without its flaws: The controls for anything but the walkers are clunky, the UI is cluttered in some spots, completely barren in others, the sound has to be set to 10% or below to avoid blowing out your eardrums, and unless RNGesus smiles upon you, or you buy premium, it takes an eternity and a day to get the guns you want or the pieces to make a coherent vehicle. The premium is a bit pricey, and of dubious worth, but not having it isn't any real disadvantage in game. All in all, the game does feel nice most of the time, until someone has the proto-seeker gun which deals massive damage in a short amount of time without missing. Beyond that, all the weapons are balanced, the matchmaking system is based on how complex your robot is, so if you feel like goofing off with/against newbies, you can just keep a simple robot on standby. The price tag of $0.00 makes it a definitely worthwhile game to give a shot.

Wolfenstein the new order had a shakey launch which put worries in the minds of me and everyone else. However despite this rough transition the game is very good. It's a reimagination of the classic Shoot-Bang we all know and love, with a few sci-fi twists, beyond of course just the major one. The paradigm that is Full Nazi Invasion was realized in a stunning display of graphic violence, a dark steampunk age in technology, and the cruelty that would be well expected of a nazi invasion.
However our hero is an over the top, certified bad♥♥♥♥♥ I was a little concerned when I found out you could eat dog food to restore health, but poor hygeiene aside he is more than capable of standing up to the nazi menace.
Without further adue
Good:
-Hardcore action FPS that feels as good as it looks.
-Enemies combat roll, take cover, curse at you in German, and though can be a bit derpy at times they get the job done.
-Interesting weapons and you can duel wield just about anything.
-Despite the occaisonal stab trading, melee combat is very compelling
-Story is great to follow, lots of cutscenes, will lilely provide many hours of campaign.
Bad:
-Low Res Textures hurt the PC visuals, and FPS capped at 60. The FPS doesn't bother me, but I am sure people with 120 refresh monitors might be disappointed.
-Perk system is forgetable and could have been done a lot better.
-Stapled objects. Bottles, cans, boxes, etc. They are all stapled to the world, as hard solid objects that cannot be moved. It breaks the fun and immersion level that even games as old as Half Life 2 have had.
-Stealth is not always an option, it often forces you to stealth, or forces you not too.
-The ending cuts off before covering a proper closing
8/10, rocky launch, Low res textures, and the lack of any groundbreaking features hinder the games score.
The lack of multiplayer is NOT A SCORED FLAW, but will also hinder the games sales no doubt.

Ah Yes, wolfenstein, a great series as im sure you will all agree. This one, is absolutely amazing.
First ill start with the negatives, even though there arn't many.
The game is a little short . . . I was expecting more levels for a game with a size of 50GB
Which brings me onto the next problem, file size. For many people it takes forever to download regular games, let alone a whopping 50GB, it also doesn't help that they started preload way to late, I mean come on guys...
And thats it, yep, really, that is all the negative things I can think of.
This is hands down one of the best games I have ever played, and believe me, I 've played a lot, I mean just look at the amount of games on my steam account ... Wallet warrior FTW!
Anyway, the game runs great, I don't know what people are complaining about, perhaps their systems are slightly configured incorrectly or their specs are slightly too low, I don't know, but mine runs fine.
Ok . . fine I admit my PC might be a little overkill, you know, GTX 690, i7 12 core and 24GB of DDR3 RAM but still!
The gameplay is fenomenal, it is really varied and it really makes you feel like you have the choice of stealth or guns blazing. Wonderful.
The story behind it, and especially the way it is told is also incredible, there are a huge amount of collectibles, clues and cutscenes which help you uncover what is going on and find many secrets, it keeps the game very interesting.
The graphics are amazing, another example of how PC is far superior to consoles!
Weapon variety in the game is . . OK. There are quite a few, but once you are halfway through you won't find many new ones. They don't even have proper names, but who cares? Assualt Rifle 1960 sounds badass enough to me!
To sum things up, people expected a lot from this game, and yes there may be technical troubles and graphical glitches, but come on guys, the game was just released, give Bethesda a break ...
This game is definetely a 10/10 for me, and I recommend that everyone gives it a shot, whether you are an old Wolfenstein veteran or you are new to the series, there is something for everyone here.
Now what are you waiting for? Get out there and kick some♥♥♥♥♥with your dual Assualt Rifle 1960's!

This is the best Free-to-Play First Person Shooter on the market. Okay so with competition like TF2 maybe it isnt, but this much I can say: It has the best F2P system I have ever seen from a shooter. Basically you have loadout cards for all the characters that have rarities: Lead, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Colbalt. These loadout cards vary in weapons, perks, and skins, however Bronze cards are the best the cards get gameplay-wise, the three tiers above that are purely cosmetic differences. To get these cards you can buy a case for 1000 in-game-credits that has one card in it, and if you complete three challenges and two win of the day bonuses (one per game mode) you can get 5000 credits a day. These cards also trade up (3 cards of any chacter = 1 of the next rarity for a character of your choice, beyond bronze its more than 3 cards and more expensive credits-wise but again those cards are purely cosmetic). The other thing you can get with credits is characters themselves. Remember how I said you can easily get 5000 a day? The most expensive characters are 50,000 credits, thats only ten days to get a new character not including if you play more beyond completing challenges. The gameplay is great but I mainly wanted to focus on the fact that I loved the F2P system in this game, and even went and bought some cards for myself in support of splash damage <3

Robocraft has much to recommend it.  It’s a great game, with a combination of building, single-player, and multiplayer elements and a fair reward system.  A wide array of parts support an even wider variety of play styles.  Robocraft isn’t pay-to-win; premium membership, while available, does not provide any insurmountable obstacle to frugal gamers, as most battles are determined by skill and experience, and the lobby creates match-ups by win/loss history and robot specs.  Even though it’s in alpha, it’s more functional and enjoyable than many established, big-budget games.  (Well, in my opinion.)
The game has a few flaws, two of which bother me particularly.  First, the game has a slightly lower tolerance for slow connections than some other games; on networks which normally give me few to no problems, I often disconnect from games and thus do not receive reward crates, which can be frustrating if I know I was more than pulling my weight in battle.  Second, the camera angle occasionally locks up, meaning I can only look and fire in one direction; this doesn’t necessarily make gameplay impossible (unless the camera is stuck at a really awkward angle), but it’s a major disadvantage.
Actually, the fact that I only have two complaints, neither of which is particularly pressing or substantial, bespeaks Robocraft’s quality.

Fast paced team action FPS. Every friend I have introduced to this game didn't like it at the start. A few games in, they settled down, started learning the mechanics and are now enjoying it. This game is an absolute blast to play. Definitely not pay to win as some might falsely state. Loadout cards are extremely easy to acquire and anything above Bronze tier is purely cosmetic.
All mercs are easily acquirable.  You have mercs on free rotation which change every 2 weeks. This allows you to try before you buy. Most of the in game items are accessible using in game money with very little only being accessible with real money.
There are 4 Class types to choose from. Healer, Assault, Objective Specialist and Recon. Each merc having a different skill to the next. Aura for example has a stationary healing station with Defibrilators for reviving and Sparks has a small medpack that heals only a little bit of hp, but has a revive gun that can revive from afar.
I have spent money on this game despite not having to because this is one of the few F2P games I have really enjoyed and would hate to see it go away like Nosgoth did. If you are into your fast paced team based shooters, definitely give this one a few hours of your time. Just don't go in thinking you are a pro and learn it. This game takes a few hours to learn the mechanics and a long time to master.

Updated review to reflect some recent game updates.
There was a good number of nice updates recently, such as removing the robot CPU limit, making it so that you can actually get currency by playing the game, some cool new items, revamped maps and gamemodes, all cool. Unfortunately some of the most gamebreaking issues remain unresolved, which simply doesn't allow me to recommend this game.
In short, the game is (still) terribly unbalanced, and as the updates pile up, nothing really changes. Weapons and parts get rebalanced, sure, but it has no real impact on the matches and how they play. Most of the times the match result is already decided by the time it starts - which results in players quitting prematurely, further damaging the gameplay.
On top of that now, you are also in the danger of getting randomly kicked by the game's anticheat telling you it's "Corrupted". I don't recall ever cheating in this game, nor is my internet connection weak. So yeah.
And best part about that it that the game actually penalises you for this the same as if you had left the match deliberately. That's very not cool. Disconnections caused by errors should not be penalised, only those who do really quit from their own decision.
It has (or had?) the potential to be something great. It is kinda enjoyable to play, but only if you don't take it seriously, and have some very strong patience. The developers seem to be actually still trying to fix it. So maybe one day this will reach a state where the game isn't pure lottery and doesn't die on you halfway through a match even though you're sitting right next to a powerful wifi.

In 1998, I was in sixth grade, and my father brought home a new computer. With Windows 98, the newest version of Microsoft Office, and even Encarta, it was a bright and glorious future. Day after day, I came home, exploring every possible thing I could do with it. We wouldn't have internet access until the next year, so every possible thing was, in fact,  somewhat limited. One day, searching through the folders of the Windows install CD (because what else do you do without internet?), I discovered a folder full of games. To be specific, trial versions of games. One of them was Age of Empires.
I was an immediate fan, playing the demo endlessly for (what I remember as) months while I tried to scrape together enough money to buy the full game. All my friends at the time were tranfixed by Starcraft, but I managed to talk a few of them into buying AoE as well, and we went through the confusing process of playing over direct dialup modem connection. I always kept the foldout tech tree near the computer, for easy reference. One day, my cousin saw it during a visit, and I found out that he too was a fan.. He was the one who, during his next visit, told me about Age of Empires 2.
The first game had simply clicked with me. The art style was simple and pleasent, and still doesn't look too bad these days. But by comparison Age of Kings was absolutely beautiful. There was detail - so much detail for the time, and so many little things that made the familiar game mechanics so much smoother. The first time I saw the rain of arrows coming down from a castle I think I laughed in the gleeful sort of way the only a preteen can. Age of Kings quickly became my favorite game of all time.
What I always loved most about either game were the custom campaigns. The superstars of scenario design made things with the campaign editor that can truly be called art. If you have no idea what I'm talking about, take a look at some of the downloads at
I recommend Ingo Van Thiel and Mark Stoker to name a few, but check out any of the top rated, it will be worth it. Since I was never actually very good at competitive online play, I spent most of my time on these elaborate single-player experiences,
Eventually I stopped waking up early to play before school. I played some other games, some by Ensemble Studios, many not. I discovered girls, and later alcohol, both of which occupied much of my time. I have never been far from this game, though.
So now we get to the HD not-quite-so-remake. Being not-quite-so because only a few things are actually change, making it more of a rerelease than a remake. Since Ensemble Studios, the group of masters who made the Age series, were inexplicably dissolved by Microsoft in 2008, its very possible to view this as just milking some intellectual property for every last dollar, with no profit to the developers. And honestly, most of the new things introduced here have been available for some time for the original game. HD means it supports high-resolution, which is also offered by the
, and the Forgotten Expansion is a polished version of the
What is really new then? There's the rendered, water. It does look pretty, though I feel like it might clash a bit with the overall art style. For me it caused lag, so I turned it off. There are other graphical changes as well. Interface icons are different - I'm not sure why they took the time to make them, as there seems to be no advantage or improvement. I'm neutral on this one. A lot of noise has been made online about new farms, but for me, the farms are exactly the same as ever. Perhaps they patched it? If they did, I wonder why they would have bothered to change the farms, but leave the cliffs. Yes, the cliffs in AoE2HD are absolutely horrible, weird gray smudged things that completely contrast with the landscape around them. Luckily, its easy to fix via steam workshop, but the real question I have is why? Why in the world would they go through the effort of adding something that just doesn't look right? Why not just leave it alone, less work for them!
This seems like a lot of evidence stacked against AoE2HD, so it may surprise you to find out that I think its still worth the buy. What it really comes down to is convenience. Getting the original game running on Windows 7 or 8 (or Linux, like I use) requires some steps, but AoE2HD downloads and runs without a problem (not native on Linux, granted, but that comes with the territory). There all those fun steam features to go along as well - achievements (so superficial, and yet so motivating), cards and badges, and easy multiplayer. The Steam Workshop seems like a perfect match, yet I haven't been all too impressed with the content there, compared with AoK Heaven. AoKH has had a few more years to build its collection though, so maybe I just need to give steam some time.
So in all, even though AoE2HD doesn't bring all the much new to the table, changing up my favorite game of all time would probably not sit well either. Therefore I do recommend that this be bought, but maybe buy it when its on sale.

Fun shooter, audio is weird, graphics are alright.  Runs on Rage's engine though soft modded the IDTech5.  Using the keyboard and mouse is a bit weird, but same even with the control pad.  The controls basically take a bit to get used to even if you are used to games like Rage, Doom 3 BFG, L4d, and many others with similar bindings.  Third difficulty is pretty balanced, but challenging at the same time.  The voice acting could be better, I do love the robots that remind me of Zoids, the enemies work like Halo's combat system where there's like one guy who's a challenge while surrounded by others, there's some stealth aspects to the game though those can change to quick combat scenes, and all around the game is pretty fun.  It seems a bit buggy, but not that much though can be fixed over time.  If you're looking for a somewhat different story implemented FPS that's aslo fun that will keep you wide awake with its bipolar mechanics...this is the game for you.  There are some cons to the game though.  1.  There's no multiplayer.  2.  The bugs oh the bugs!  Audio is so unbalanced and so unadjustable...might be because I'm using an ASUS Xonar DG...dunno.  There's also some white screen crashes for some people, and also there's a lot of texture tearing+in and outs that has been addressed yet not fixed.  3.  There's some unclear gameplay mechanics like exactly how to do things isn't as clear as it should be.  For example...when you're lock picking they don't tell you to hold the button they tell you to press it...that's it...when doing other parts like certain jumps...they don't exactly tell you to hold or when to press...they just say it in more of a generalization like "oh hey do this to do this."  You do it and ya fail the first time...because they always wanna leave a piece of the tutorial out.  <.< I'd give this a 7/10 because of the 3 beefs I have with this.  It does have replay value, and it pisses you off at the same time to the point that you want to come back to the game to prove to it that you can do it, but you're likely to rage quit a lot.  I will also say that at some point the AI's placement is both obnoxious and autistic...and at points they're just oped.  So some unbalanced AI could be considered a con I guess.  On another plus side...there's turrets that are detachable...oh look halo again!  Oh, and giant turrets that will blow up a giant robot...and other fun random stuff that makes no sense...they do try a bit to add old school wolfenstein elements into it like the robot dogs have food...and dog food as well as random food is implemented as health.  So I'd say the game is bipolar...trying to hard to identify as other games...yet old school wolfenstein at the same time...not exactly a 10/10 game granted, but if you like random FPS that are overly bipolar...then I'd suggest playing this.  Before I forget there are some more issues like...downsighting the aim is kinda pointless because the guns hardly stay aligned for the shot...they just randomly shoot straight and up...takes a bit to get used too.

I've been a long time Wolfenstein fan. I played Wolfenstein 3D for the first time when I was younger, and it was on one of those ridiculous shareware demo discs alongside the beloved Doom! Ever since, I've kept a close eye on the franchise and enjoyed every iteration, including the recent 2009 game that has sadly vanished without a trace for potential buyers. However, this new entry makes up for that with flying colors!
Wolfenstein: The New Order is, without a doubt, one of the most fun shooters of all time and possibly one of the best shooters ever made. Love, passion, and polish have been put into this game, and I have a lot to talk about. But let me try to make this as brief as possible, so you can get the best review possible!
The gameplay, which is exceptionally fun, allows for a great deal of freedom. Stealth, tactics, or assault. Gameplay can flow between any of these three at any moment. Although the level designs consist of corridors or big open atriums, they still allow for a lot of freedom in how you want to approach a situation. Within these levels, you can find any number of hidden goodies to find, such as collectible gold or special codes that unlock additional game modes. You also will find plenty of useful items hidden in fun locations. Although there is some level of linearity, the game still has alternate paths you can take, even if not all the time.
As you gun down waves of Nazis using some of the best gunplay I've ever heard or witnessed, the gun toting hero will unlock "perks" which provide passive bonuses in 4 perk trees. Although it isn't as robust or plentiful as, let's say, the perks in Fallout games, it is still a rather welcome modern addition and doesn't detract from the game.
The game also gives ample reason to replay it, and not just for the collectibles, as their are two alternate "timelines" which bump up the game to 20 hours of playtime! A major two way choice at the beginning of the game will actually CHANGE a few things about the game, including the characters you meet and what major area traversal skill you have. For example, lockpicking or hotwiring.
Now, the final aspects of the game are the story, setting, writing, graphics, sound, and characters. All of it is actually really surprising. The world is full of creative vision, texture, and flavor (the graphics are pretty nice, but rely heavily on effects). White concrete buildings with red Nazi banners proudly flapping in the wind, a group of prisoners being bullied by Nazi scum, and other things help to add to the world. The characters and story is shockingly good too. But before you criticize it, keep in mind that this in context with what kind of crazy game Wolfenstein is. The game has the best story it could possibly have in its current form! The voiceovers are brilliant, the cutscenes are seamless and cinematic. The characters feel very human and world weary, showing the horrors of Nazi rule!
Wolfenstein: The New Order is a qaulity shooter. It has some snags, of course, keeping it from its momentum towards success. Graphics problems, people having trouble running the game, mouse sensitivity issues in the menus/journal, and a few minor bugs. The game, also, can be repetitive or too linear as the last half or so of the game loses a bit of momentum, but that is a matter of subjective perspective.
I can safely say, with all of that said, that this is one of the best shooters at least for the year 2014. It's excessively fun, balls to the wall, and very playable. It has soul that so many shooters are lacking lately, and it will fill in that gap in your soul as well if you are a fan of shooters! Get this game, you will not regret it, shooter fans OR Wolfenstein fans!

Like a coffee gone cold, it's been easy to forget the golden age of the World War II FPS. Albeit edible, any thirsty developer approaches hesitant to the long-gone steam clouds of its hour of freshness. Back before the famed Call of Duty franchise strapped players into the combat boots of the WWII genre, the influential, genre-defining Wolfenstein 3D plotted willing adventurers into the labyrinths of a Nazi prison, with chances of survival as slim as the knife you begin with. Fictictious war hero B.J. Blazkowicz has since become a legendary icon in the realm of interactive media. It's 2014, and MachineGames has not feebly waltzed, but boldly marched back into the dated franchise, armed with a morbid, yet brilliant new concept with Wolfenstein: The New Order.
The war is over, the Nazis have won, and the future of humanity is bleak, all in exchange for Aryan supremacy. People are dying left and right under the non-chalant smiles of Nazi officers. Rudely awoken after a fourteen-year hiatus in an insane asylum, it's an understatement to say that William Blazcowicz has returned with all the bang for your buck, and then some. It's a setup that drains the hope of the world from even the optimistically devout. Depending on your gameplay preference, you may be hesitant to drop the $60 without multiplayer, but fret not. Even as a single-player exclusive experience, The New Order shines at its pacing and the satisfaction that bleeds from the gratuitous violence on the screen and cakes onto the player.
I didn't initially anticipate myself using the game's new, excessively versatile dual-wielding system, but in no time, I grew used to how surprisingly satisfying it clicked with my input. It drifts away from extreme realism and has you off of the training wheels and behind two assault rifles within minutes of play. It's like Skyrim, with, well...never mind.
Also new to Wolfenstein is a perk system, which, like its namesake, paves the way for new abilities, or "perks" throughout the riveting campaign. While the small touches in combat are welcome, stealth leaves a lot to be desired. It's satisfying, but I believe a lot more can be done with the mechanic, especially since every stealth-related perk is a trivial achievement that involves actions you may have performed already, thus unlocked or imminently such.
Wolfenstein: The New Order will approximately clock you around 10-15 hours, or just under that if you rush. No matter how fast you complete this critter, it will definitely leave you hungry like the Wolf for more.

Fun shooter, audio is weird, graphics are alright.  Runs on Rage's engine though soft modded the IDTech5.  Using the keyboard and mouse is a bit weird, but same even with the control pad.  The controls basically take a bit to get used to even if you are used to games like Rage, Doom 3 BFG, L4d, and many others with similar bindings.  Third difficulty is pretty balanced, but challenging at the same time.  The voice acting could be better, I do love the robots that remind me of Zoids, the enemies work like Halo's combat system where there's like one guy who's a challenge while surrounded by others, there's some stealth aspects to the game though those can change to quick combat scenes, and all around the game is pretty fun.  It seems a bit buggy, but not that much though can be fixed over time.  If you're looking for a somewhat different story implemented FPS that's aslo fun that will keep you wide awake with its bipolar mechanics...this is the game for you.  There are some cons to the game though.  1.  There's no multiplayer.  2.  The bugs oh the bugs!  Audio is so unbalanced and so unadjustable...might be because I'm using an ASUS Xonar DG...dunno.  There's also some white screen crashes for some people, and also there's a lot of texture tearing+in and outs that has been addressed yet not fixed.  3.  There's some unclear gameplay mechanics like exactly how to do things isn't as clear as it should be.  For example...when you're lock picking they don't tell you to hold the button they tell you to press it...that's it...when doing other parts like certain jumps...they don't exactly tell you to hold or when to press...they just say it in more of a generalization like "oh hey do this to do this."  You do it and ya fail the first time...because they always wanna leave a piece of the tutorial out.  <.< I'd give this a 7/10 because of the 3 beefs I have with this.  It does have replay value, and it pisses you off at the same time to the point that you want to come back to the game to prove to it that you can do it, but you're likely to rage quit a lot.  I will also say that at some point the AI's placement is both obnoxious and autistic...and at points they're just oped.  So some unbalanced AI could be considered a con I guess.  On another plus side...there's turrets that are detachable...oh look halo again!  Oh, and giant turrets that will blow up a giant robot...and other fun random stuff that makes no sense...they do try a bit to add old school wolfenstein elements into it like the robot dogs have food...and dog food as well as random food is implemented as health.  So I'd say the game is bipolar...trying to hard to identify as other games...yet old school wolfenstein at the same time...not exactly a 10/10 game granted, but if you like random FPS that are overly bipolar...then I'd suggest playing this.  Before I forget there are some more issues like...downsighting the aim is kinda pointless because the guns hardly stay aligned for the shot...they just randomly shoot straight and up...takes a bit to get used too.

I've been a long time Wolfenstein fan. I played Wolfenstein 3D for the first time when I was younger, and it was on one of those ridiculous shareware demo discs alongside the beloved Doom! Ever since, I've kept a close eye on the franchise and enjoyed every iteration, including the recent 2009 game that has sadly vanished without a trace for potential buyers. However, this new entry makes up for that with flying colors!
Wolfenstein: The New Order is, without a doubt, one of the most fun shooters of all time and possibly one of the best shooters ever made. Love, passion, and polish have been put into this game, and I have a lot to talk about. But let me try to make this as brief as possible, so you can get the best review possible!
The gameplay, which is exceptionally fun, allows for a great deal of freedom. Stealth, tactics, or assault. Gameplay can flow between any of these three at any moment. Although the level designs consist of corridors or big open atriums, they still allow for a lot of freedom in how you want to approach a situation. Within these levels, you can find any number of hidden goodies to find, such as collectible gold or special codes that unlock additional game modes. You also will find plenty of useful items hidden in fun locations. Although there is some level of linearity, the game still has alternate paths you can take, even if not all the time.
As you gun down waves of Nazis using some of the best gunplay I've ever heard or witnessed, the gun toting hero will unlock "perks" which provide passive bonuses in 4 perk trees. Although it isn't as robust or plentiful as, let's say, the perks in Fallout games, it is still a rather welcome modern addition and doesn't detract from the game.
The game also gives ample reason to replay it, and not just for the collectibles, as their are two alternate "timelines" which bump up the game to 20 hours of playtime! A major two way choice at the beginning of the game will actually CHANGE a few things about the game, including the characters you meet and what major area traversal skill you have. For example, lockpicking or hotwiring.
Now, the final aspects of the game are the story, setting, writing, graphics, sound, and characters. All of it is actually really surprising. The world is full of creative vision, texture, and flavor (the graphics are pretty nice, but rely heavily on effects). White concrete buildings with red Nazi banners proudly flapping in the wind, a group of prisoners being bullied by Nazi scum, and other things help to add to the world. The characters and story is shockingly good too. But before you criticize it, keep in mind that this in context with what kind of crazy game Wolfenstein is. The game has the best story it could possibly have in its current form! The voiceovers are brilliant, the cutscenes are seamless and cinematic. The characters feel very human and world weary, showing the horrors of Nazi rule!
Wolfenstein: The New Order is a qaulity shooter. It has some snags, of course, keeping it from its momentum towards success. Graphics problems, people having trouble running the game, mouse sensitivity issues in the menus/journal, and a few minor bugs. The game, also, can be repetitive or too linear as the last half or so of the game loses a bit of momentum, but that is a matter of subjective perspective.
I can safely say, with all of that said, that this is one of the best shooters at least for the year 2014. It's excessively fun, balls to the wall, and very playable. It has soul that so many shooters are lacking lately, and it will fill in that gap in your soul as well if you are a fan of shooters! Get this game, you will not regret it, shooter fans OR Wolfenstein fans!

Like a coffee gone cold, it's been easy to forget the golden age of the World War II FPS. Albeit edible, any thirsty developer approaches hesitant to the long-gone steam clouds of its hour of freshness. Back before the famed Call of Duty franchise strapped players into the combat boots of the WWII genre, the influential, genre-defining Wolfenstein 3D plotted willing adventurers into the labyrinths of a Nazi prison, with chances of survival as slim as the knife you begin with. Fictictious war hero B.J. Blazkowicz has since become a legendary icon in the realm of interactive media. It's 2014, and MachineGames has not feebly waltzed, but boldly marched back into the dated franchise, armed with a morbid, yet brilliant new concept with Wolfenstein: The New Order.
The war is over, the Nazis have won, and the future of humanity is bleak, all in exchange for Aryan supremacy. People are dying left and right under the non-chalant smiles of Nazi officers. Rudely awoken after a fourteen-year hiatus in an insane asylum, it's an understatement to say that William Blazcowicz has returned with all the bang for your buck, and then some. It's a setup that drains the hope of the world from even the optimistically devout. Depending on your gameplay preference, you may be hesitant to drop the $60 without multiplayer, but fret not. Even as a single-player exclusive experience, The New Order shines at its pacing and the satisfaction that bleeds from the gratuitous violence on the screen and cakes onto the player.
I didn't initially anticipate myself using the game's new, excessively versatile dual-wielding system, but in no time, I grew used to how surprisingly satisfying it clicked with my input. It drifts away from extreme realism and has you off of the training wheels and behind two assault rifles within minutes of play. It's like Skyrim, with, well...never mind.
Also new to Wolfenstein is a perk system, which, like its namesake, paves the way for new abilities, or "perks" throughout the riveting campaign. While the small touches in combat are welcome, stealth leaves a lot to be desired. It's satisfying, but I believe a lot more can be done with the mechanic, especially since every stealth-related perk is a trivial achievement that involves actions you may have performed already, thus unlocked or imminently such.
Wolfenstein: The New Order will approximately clock you around 10-15 hours, or just under that if you rush. No matter how fast you complete this critter, it will definitely leave you hungry like the Wolf for more.

Note: The game developers are no longer Sony Online Entertainment, and are now a new entity owned by Columbus Nova under the name Daybreak Games Company (DGC).
On the surface, it is fairly obvious that Planetside 2 (PS2) is a very unique game by being a MMOFPS. Its core FPS mechanics heavily resemble a Battlefield (BF) game with some differences. There are 3, relatively well balanced factions with different weapons. PS2 is set on 4 massive 64km^2 warzones where the lines in the sand are frequently redrawn, and rarely owned for a long time. The maps are persistent, with the only exception being when they are "locked" by one faction conquering the map during an alert (2 hour special event triggered by territory capture).
In my personal opinion, Planetside 2 is one of the most unique games on the market and it provides an experience replicated nowhere else, at least until Warhammer 40K: Eternal Crusade is released. I would highly recommend it for those who are seasoned shooter veterans and BF players who wouldn't mind a bigger playground to be in. If you read nothing other than this, I would highly recommend the game.
Like many games, PS2 has some upsides and some downsides.
Pros:
-The experiences you will have in this game are like none other in any game on the market. This makes gameplay relatively fresh compared to many other games, with many differences from other conventional shooters.
-The core gunplay will be familiar (for the most part) if you have ever layed hands on any of the BF series of games.
-There are many various playstyles to choose from, meaning you will likely never run out of things to try unless you pigeon hole yourself to a specific role.
-This game does F2P right, with most money being spent towards cosmetics or unlocking sidegrades faster. Even with the addition of implants, PS2 is still very fair to free players. The grind is noticable, but often your stock weapons may be the ones you use the most.
-If you have ever wanted more community in a game, PS2 is full of Outfits (clans/guilds) of varying types, specializations, and skill levels. Organized gameplay is the most rewarding (both xp-wise and gameplay-wise), making squading up and joining an outfit the best way to play the game.
-Speaking of community, the game's community isn't extremely toxic like many other FPS communities. Newb questions are often answered on the official forums or on the Planetside subreddit. Even more complex questions or technical issues are answered, so don't be afraid to ask.
-Whatever Anti-Cheat DGC uses, it is incredibly effective. Almost all of their games have little to no issue with hackers, usually driving the hacking scene for these games to extinction.
EDIT: As of the release of H1Z1, people have noticed an increase in hackers on the European servers. There have also been some changes in the Anti-Cheat, so take the above "pro" with a grain of salt.
-The developers (and ex-developers) are relatively active on social media such as twitter and reddit. They'll often post stuff about WIP or changes they may be experimenting with on the test server or their own private servers.
Now, the game does not come without its downsides, and they can be fairly hefty.
Cons:
-The game is very buggy and it is not uncommon for patches to break parts of the game (hence the joke name for the company, dey break games), or exploits to appear. This is due to the complexity of an FPS and an MMO, which are polar opposites as far as game stability goes. Patches and hotfixes appear fairly quickly though, and DGC has gotten much better about build management and bug fixing. Some bugs are more persistent than others, including crazy legs.
EDIT: rip crazy legs, flail on in bug heaven
-Balance is relatively good, and DGC has been getting better, but weapons are often overnerfed and then slowly rebuffed back to usable levels. Some weapons, like HE rounds for tanks, often get nerfed repeatedly or changed. The game is the most balanced it has been since its release.
-The game is a monster of a CPU hog. Like many MMOs, PS2 requires heavy amounts of CPU power and doesn't use the GPU as much as it should. The game also leaks memory like bad plumbing, which is a problem with all Forgelight games. Its hard to get your performance optimal, but it is still possible to get 60+ FPS on 1080p if your CPU is good and you optimize your settings (just keep in mind lower isn't always better, its hard to explain).
-This game will lag, especially in the massive fights it is famous for. If you have a Comcast monopoly in your area, you probably won't be able to experience the game as you might want to. However, clientside hit detection does make up for this, but it will lead to some pretty BS deaths against laggier opponents.
-The game has probably the steepest learning curve I have seen in any FPS. Expect to die, a lot. Eventually you will improve and you will enjoy the game more and more. new player experience has improved though, and the community has a multitude of videos for new players.
-With the recent aqusition by Columbus Nova, it is hard to see where the game is going. Some say the game is setting, while others say the game will liven up and improve. It is hard to tell, so the uncertainty of the game is a definite downside at the moment.
Overall, I feel the pros outweigh the cons. The game is still being supported, it is likely that it will still have servers up for coming years. However the game's population is slowly going down, and I feel that getting very invested in the game will lead to heartbreak. I would still recommend at least trying the game, as it is free to play.

Robocraft started out as an incredibley enjoyable game, with unique building, fun gamemodes, and constant updates. The game was not only fun, and had great potential, but the developers were out to make a game, not a profit. They listened to their community, and strived to improve the game. After the "New Meta" update, a lot of people were angry, but a minority supported this direction.
This resulted in many neutral updates, and one of the most hated updates of all - Team Orders. The update removed what made Robocraft fun and enjoyable, and turned Robocraft into another Dota 2, except instead of heroes, you had bricks with guns attatched. Despite Freejam noticing, their attempt to fix the problem with "Unleashed" was not the Trump Card everybody wanted. They removed tiers, replacing it with "Mk", and added a whole lot of gimmicks. Soon, they completely removed tiers.
After that, they continued to remove what made Robocraft unique. First tiers, then ranking, then level in general. Although I do like the paint system, tier flattening led to a lot of unbalanced items. They also unnessarily added new weapons - additions NOBODY wanted. And now they're still adding MORE weapons, while people are suffering from ghosting. Robocrafter YouTuber Lathrix had SEVEN games IN A ROW where somebody was ghosting (which is when a lagged out player damages and destroys other players even though they are destroyed). When the devs should've been fixing the game, they were adding to the game.
Now, the average match is very simple - build a tesla plasma bot. Wait for your team to severely damage an enemy, and then go in for the kill. If you deal 80% damage to an enemy, killing the enemy will reward you with more points, which brings me to say the truth: In any Robocraft gamemode (The developers SPECIFICALLY stated that kill stealling was an option in the FFA gamemode "The Pit"), you are forced to fight against YOUR OWN TEAM. People become utterly selfish, not healing, and stealing a kill you worked hard to get.
Just go to the reviews section of the Robocraft Steam Community, then scroll down, and savour the red square boxes with thumbs down symbols. It's so clear in the reviews. 3,691 recent reviews have been submitted, and 55% of those reviews (~2,030 reviews) are negative. Freejam is also silencing moderators who oppose the company, and actively responded on Twitter to the community "deal with it". Yet, they are still adding more weapons, that will a) add a potential risk for unbalanced weapons and b ) makes you want to spend real world money even more.
Freejam has gone from a small indie developer team that made an award winning small free to play game that people put thousands of hours into, to a money hungry profit machine.
• Make crates mono-tiered (or squashed), or just outright remove them. They're completely based on RNG and they just steal money from you. Premium doesn't change a lot of it.
• Revamp the points system so that if you say deal 50% CPU damage, you earn 50 points while if you kill an enemy, you earn 10 points. This will counter kill stealing.
• Fix ghosting. It can make a Protonium Crate earning hover bot that made someone put ten hours of their life to make the bot get to a Bronze Crate because a ghoster killed them.
•Get rid of the Premium Paint system. It defeats the purpose of being "creative".

Update 5/21: My system specs are as follows: Intel i5 2500K @ 3.3GHZ, 32 GB sys ram, 1TB HDD, Windows 8.1, Nvdida Drivers 335.23 ( I know they aren't the latest drivers, but I don't upgrade my drivers until I have trouble playing a game because  I've found sometimes new drivers can cause problems with games that were working fine).
This is a solid title. No doubts about it. The rumors about the AI being poor don't hold up to what I've experienced so far. Enemies will take cover, duck out to take shots, roll to make themselves harder targets, and commanders will even continuously call in reinforcements until they are killed. I started at "Hard" difficulty and it feels like the right setting for veteran gamers. One potential issue that can make the game easier is that there is a bit of overabundance in terms of medkits and armor for my taste. Every time you clear an area, you'll find that there are significant numbers of health, ammo, and armor picks-up scattered all around. Of course, you can be as judicious as you like in terms of how many you take, but they could have scaled back on the amount of pick-up a bit.
The visuals are generally very solid, with the occasional glitch here and there, and the framerate is smooth and steady. The only complaint I have in this regard is that there is still random screen tearing, even with V-Sync enabled, but it's rare, and hasn't really significantly impacted my experience. I have a GTX 660 with 32 gigs of system RAM.
I am still early on, but man does this game have atmosphere and some of the best voice acting I have experienced yet. And the cutscenes are quite well done.
The guns are fun so far, but I haven't yet really got anything exotic.  We'll see how that turns out with additional game time, though.
At any rate, the short of it is get this game if you enjoy FPSs. I am having some really good fun with this one, and I'm about to get back to it now! I'll update this review as needed.
Cheers!
Update: Made it into the castle proper, and the♥♥♥♥♥♥really hits the fan in terms of the cruelty and burtuality of the nazis. The game has a real sense of drama and solid pacing. They have created some of the creepiest, most warped characters I've seen in a while...Well done, Machine Games!
