Update 5/20: I am about 12-13 hours in now, and my initial impressions still hold. This game is a generally solid FPS experience. There's nothing revolutionary here, but it does what it does well. I forgot to mention that you can earn perks as you progress through the game, and the perks are aligned with different playstyles. For example, there is a perk line for stealth that allows you to increase some of the stealth actions at your disposal (i.e. throwing knives) or to improve upon them (i.e. reduce the amount of noise you make when you sprint). Also, all projectile weapons have alternate fire modes , but you have to unlock them through gameplay. I still recommend veteran gamers starting on at least "Hard".
Update 6/3/14: This update is about the weapons, now that I have had a chance to really sink my teeth in the game. There is some variety to be had here in terms of weapons, but you won't see the more exotic weapons (i.e. laser rifles) until much later on in the game. This could be an issue for those of us who are "gun bunnies", and want access sooner rather than later, but I wouldn't let that put you off from what is really a great game. You do get some incremental upgrades to the primary stable of weapons you have access to early on, which include (but are not limited to) the usual suspects like an assault rifle, shotgun, and pistols (which can be actively silenced at will). One such incremental improvement is the addition of a grenade launcher to the standard assault rifle. So, it's not a new weapon, but it definitely adds some additional punch to your damage output, not the mention the fun factor when you want to turn up the heat.
I should also note here that you can dual-wield most of your weapons, and, though I take the stealth route for the most part, I have had some solid fun with full-on assualts while dual-wielding shotguns and assualt rifles.

Last year during Quakecon as part of my first experience with the press pass I got the privilege of playing an hour demo of Wolfenstein New Order and Elder Scrolls Online. Needless to say at the time I was more excited about getting a chance to look at Elder Scrolls than Wolfenstein but after I played both I was on board for The New Order. All I got to play was an hour, so the question was, would this game live up to Return to Castle Wolfenstein and Wolfenstein 3d while implementing some modern gaming mechanics likes a well written story, characters and setting? The answer to that is an emphatic Yes.
Wolfenstein The New Order is an old school shooter with newer shooter elements in it. The levels are set up with lots of big halls and corridors in a way to allow for lots of gun fights with enemies big and small. What New Order does a bit differently from its predecessors is that it added the element of stealth. There are lots of secret hallways and vents where you can sneak around enemies in order to stab them in the back. In fact I would say unless I felt pumped up to go guns blazing around (there are some levels that made me feel like that) I, for the most part, was sneaking around the entire time. Another one of the more modern elements of New Order would be that of their perk system. To get bonuses and abilities towards your weapon skills and other character stats, you can earn perks that you acquire through getting kills in a certain way (stealth throwing knives, shooting enemies out of cover, killing them with grenades or the LKV, etc.).
The big strong feature of this game is how Machine Games has created a great pacing throughout the game. You aren’t bombarded with enemies constantly and even at times being able to stealth and sneak around enemies is a great plus to that pacing. You are moving from event to event while building upon the story with each step. It doesn’t have the mindless spawning enemies that games like call of duty and the newer battlefields have. You fight only the units that are already there.

Now that isn’t to say there isn’t a downside to the mechanics of New Order, one of those being that the AI is pretty bad. At times you can sneak up right next to enemies and stab them without noticing. I’ve had times where be stabbing a Nazi near another Nazi would cause the other to react from his sound and then I’ve had other instances where they wouldn’t react at all. In fact at times it can be so bad that the game will help the AI out. If I’ve killed one of the enemies’ comrades in a stealth manner and have moved away, if that enemy finds his body he will immediately know where I am regardless of where I’m hiding. Another trait of the AI is if they know you are around the corner they won’t make any attempt to come after you. They will end up staying in their same patrol route and not move. I could see this as a problem as they will make no effort to flank you and try to make the game challenging.
Another problem with this game (and this might just be me), I was running on a pretty good machine, 2600k/780 ti/8 gigs of ram, and I had problems with this game at times. The framerate was fine at ultra and all but at random occurrences during either loading screens or cutscenes, or even sometimes gameplay itself but to a lesser extent, I would get a temporary freeze of the game. It wouldn’t freeze the computer but the game itself would just hang for about 10-20 seconds and then be back to normal. At times it kind of made it difficult to really get into the game as cutscenes would stop and you could lose your focus of what was going on. Now this didn’t happen all that often but it happened enough for me to notice it.
The game starts in 1946 and you are BJ Blazkowicz, the same character in all the previous Wolfenstein games, and you are heading towards General Deathshead’s, also a reoccurring character, compound in order to kill the General. As it is, the Nazis are winning the war due to some ancient technology that the Nazis are using that is making them far more advanced than the allies. In the end the assassination attempt fails and Blaszkowicz is hit in the head by some shrapnel while trying to escape and is put in a coma. During his coma he is put in a polish hospital where he meets Anya (love interest) and he stays there motionless for 14 years unaware of what is happening on the outside world. As it turns out the allies surrender in 1948 when Germany drops an atomic bomb on the US thus making the Nazis the winner of WWII. When Blazkowicz wakes up he finds himself in an unfamiliar 1960 with complete Nazi control. He must find the resistance and attempt to complete what he started by killing Deathshead if they ever want to be free of Nazi rule.

Wolfenstein New Order runs off of the id Tech 5 engine that the game Rage before it ran off of. As you would guess, this game is absolutely beautiful but not at the cost of being able to run it. The minimum specs that are on most pages is an i7 3770k and a 600 series nvidia or higher card but I’d be willing to bet that you could get away with a system a little weaker.  But it isn’t just how the game looks, the aesthetics and the setting are amazing too. Machine Games took a sort of retro sci-fi feel with the world and it looks amazing. From a very militaristic feel of Berlin and London to a very high-tech feel of a German U-boat and the Moon. This game is very gorgeous and well made setting wise.

Machine games also did a fine job with the sound of the game. They didn’t have the voice actors use nothing but English like a lot of games tend to do. But instead they made sure to make it feel as real as possible as having many languages including German and Polish being spoken throughout the game. The music is top notch as well. Along with the symphonic soundtrack that occupancies you on various missions but they included 3 other tracks that illustrate how pop music would be if the Germans had won the war including a Nazi Beatles track called Ja Ja, Mund Mund.

Overall this game is a fantastic addition to the Wolfenstein franchise which frankly is a surprise as not much information was given about this game other than a few long trailers describing the Nazi rule of the world in the 1960’s. The pacing, story, characters, graphics, sound and gameplay are all fantastic but that doesn’t come without a few bugs and dumb AI. If you can look past those small problems you’ll really enjoy this old school shooter with new shooter features.

I'd only recommend for a VERY patient casual play.  You will spend large amounts of time waiting, and waiting, and waiting for certain things such as:
1.  Bug fixes.  There are bugs/glitches/exploits that have been around for months if not years that still have not been addressed.  Read some of the top negative reviews for a detailed look at some of the bugs (some are major).
2.  Content and deeper gameplay.  New content is released so sporadically that, if you decide to play, you shouldn't hold your breath for it. The gameplay itself is a team deathmatch grindfest for the most part.  It's up to you and friends to create your own in-game goals in order to keep yourselves entertained.
3.  Customer service.  This was the nail in the coffin for why I finally stopped playing.  There are currently so many customers in their support queue that they've disabled their online support chat and phone support number.  This was stated by their own twitter account.  At the time of writing this review (2/25/2015) there are several people tweeting to DaybreakHelp that have been waiting for WEEKS to even have their issues be heard.  Some, like me, were having major issues such as not even being able to access their game(s).  Instead of resolving any actual issues, people are simply receiving canned responses and having their support tickets closed.
It's worth checking out if you want something to play every now and then.  The f2p model is actually one of the best out there.  But given the fact that there's no real reason to stick around and keep playing the game, I can't recommend it.
P.S. Another major problem is H1Z1.  I know, you're asking what H1Z1 has to do with Planetside 2.  Well it's simple really... that is where Daybreak is focusing most of their attention now.  With the "restructuring" of the company, they are already spread thin on manpower, and now most of the staff is focused on their newest project.  Going back to point 3... people are waiting weeks to even access their games/accounts, yet the VP of customer service is dedicated to chasing H1Z1 hackers.  He only cares about H1Z1 hackers though... he doesn't seem to care if people hack in any other games.

Yes, it is invigorating to see such a massive world layed out where battles can be happening between hundreds of people across different fronts. At the same time, hundreds of people battling in clusters of anywhere from 10 to 100 on a side means that as an individual soldier, your presence matters far less that in other shooters. Killing one to several enemies almost inevitably reveals your position to other enemies who will rapidly end your life, driving a tank across the field results in all enemy tanks and anti tank gunners to quickly end your life.
There is no room in this game for solo or lone wolf style play beyond perhaps sniping in a support role. As a team game however, the game does work quite well.
Ultimately, the downfall of the game is that every point of conflict ultimately boils down to a very simple formula of attacking and defending capture points. The dynamic aspect is centered around where mobile spawns are placed and how many people happen to be on the attacking or defending side.
Now I admit, I do not have many hours invested in the game on steam but at this point, I dont feel much more time is needed to understand that this is essentially battlefield without the destructible environments and a larger player pool. Try it if you are curious but the repetive nature of combat combined with the slow pace of the game reminded me far too much of Halo.

I am re-writing my review and actually changing from Not Recommended to Recommended. Having written a bad review for one of the best RTS games ever was haunting me.  I wrote the "Not Recommended" review because I was unable to play with all AI slots filled on the new ludaKris(new larger map) and the new highest population range of 500.  After twenty minutes into the game it became extremely laggy and I lost control of the mouse except to scroll around (couldn't click units buildings or even menu options.)  My machine is not top of the line and it is 5 years old but it plays other games WoW, Skyrim, Diablo 3, Starcraft 2, Planetside 2 to name a few, perfectly.  Having said that, I had to Ctrl-Alt-Del out of AoE2 HD when it lagged out. After a bit more exploration of the features, I found that I can play the largest map with regular cap limit and few opponents no problem.  Or the smaller maps with a higher cap limit, just not both.  Since the clues seemed to look like it could be a memory issue on my end I have re-written my review. Still I warn other potential buyers that the game is somehow mind-bogglingy demanding when you play on the large map with the high pop limit and all opponents.  Also, I was slightly disappointed that the graphics weren't enhanced more with the "HD re-mastered" version.  However, the gameplay is still the same as what made AoE2 a great game back in the day and ultimately I recommend it for new playeres and those who want to throwback old times.
Here's a few bullet point take-aways I expeerienced:
-*Tougher/quicker AI.  Playing on standard all other AI opponents advanced to fuedal in 5-8 minutes.(yeah that's quick)
* Although Easist was still silly easy, the AI never actually attacked, and only defended when I   attacked their city, and even then it was silly.
-There is a larger map setting than Huge   ludaKRIS which is the map I experienced lag with
-Several new map types to play with
-You can set a higher pop than 200 from the original AoE2, 300, 400, and 500 are new choices
-I was expecting a little better graphics, but really the only major differences was prettier water and slightly better fires.
-New civilizations, some with a new set of building skins

Age of Empires II HD is a real-time strategy from Microsoft Studios. It is a remake of Age of Empire II: The Age of King and Age of Empire II: The Conquerors expansion pack reimagined in HD and now entirely as one single game. Everybody know what Age of Empire is unless you're really new to PC gaming, the game is a legend, was the best classic real-time strategy of that time.
All gameplay and features in this game is left untouched and are very exactly the same as the old Age of Empire II except for the new 500 population limit for skirmish play, let's you train even more units and having a larger battles and larger tactics than before.
The graphics has been improved slightly where you can see the new water and fire textures and effects are better than before. The new widescreen support for the game are also included. The rest still retain the same graphics as before.
Well, the exact same gameplay and features could be the good or bad thing, because most people don't like buying things similar with what they already have, own or taste, but if you're looking for the old Age of Empires II in a new and better way then it is for you. All the story campaign, civilization is all there and the new Steam workshop integration is the best thing so you now can download many user created content ranging from maps, scenarios, AI scripts and many more to customize your game or create your own stuff and share it with everyone in the Steam community. I say this is a good remake, I recommend this. And by the way, I've been playing this game for over 6 years :)

PS2 is a fun, enjoyable 3-way FPS with a fast pace in the action department.   5 different infantry classes and the option of multiple ground vehicles and air vehicles which also have multiple load outs gives you a large variety of options on how you can play the game.   This is not really a game you run around solo in, it does involve teamwork.  This does NOT mean you have to know folks, but simply join a squad (super easy to do each time you log in) and follow your squadmates around.  You also have the option to join an 'outfit' (Think "guild" if your a WoW player) and play with the same folks each time you log in.
You have the option to play the game for free, or you can purchase a subscription.   The subscription gives you a small edge on earning Certifications (Think 'gold' if your a WoW player) points faster, but you can earn certs and unlock all the goodies simply by playing the game.
Overall, I feel its a fun and entertaining game to play!

I am re-writing my review and actually changing from Not Recommended to Recommended. Having written a bad review for one of the best RTS games ever was haunting me.  I wrote the "Not Recommended" review because I was unable to play with all AI slots filled on the new ludaKris(new larger map) and the new highest population range of 500.  After twenty minutes into the game it became extremely laggy and I lost control of the mouse except to scroll around (couldn't click units buildings or even menu options.)  My machine is not top of the line and it is 5 years old but it plays other games WoW, Skyrim, Diablo 3, Starcraft 2, Planetside 2 to name a few, perfectly.  Having said that, I had to Ctrl-Alt-Del out of AoE2 HD when it lagged out. After a bit more exploration of the features, I found that I can play the largest map with regular cap limit and few opponents no problem.  Or the smaller maps with a higher cap limit, just not both.  Since the clues seemed to look like it could be a memory issue on my end I have re-written my review. Still I warn other potential buyers that the game is somehow mind-bogglingy demanding when you play on the large map with the high pop limit and all opponents.  Also, I was slightly disappointed that the graphics weren't enhanced more with the "HD re-mastered" version.  However, the gameplay is still the same as what made AoE2 a great game back in the day and ultimately I recommend it for new playeres and those who want to throwback old times.
Here's a few bullet point take-aways I expeerienced:
-*Tougher/quicker AI.  Playing on standard all other AI opponents advanced to fuedal in 5-8 minutes.(yeah that's quick)
* Although Easist was still silly easy, the AI never actually attacked, and only defended when I   attacked their city, and even then it was silly.
-There is a larger map setting than Huge   ludaKRIS which is the map I experienced lag with
-Several new map types to play with
-You can set a higher pop than 200 from the original AoE2, 300, 400, and 500 are new choices
-I was expecting a little better graphics, but really the only major differences was prettier water and slightly better fires.
-New civilizations, some with a new set of building skins

For anyone that enjoys FPS, wants something more that Battle Field and CoD can't give, and loves teamwork, Planetside 2 is just what you are looking for. A true MMOFPS that delivers. Choose from three factions (sides) to play as. Six different classes to play as and upgrade. Hundreds of different weapons that allow you to find what fits your play style, different vehicles and weapons for the vehicles to choose from and use, 12 man squads to 48 man platoons to run with, and constant battles 24/7 on 4 different continents. Free to play, though it does have micro-transactions. You can play and earn enough certification points to buy weapons, or you can use station cash to buy the weapons, which will allow account wide unlocks, allowing you to have the weapon for any character if it is all empires or for just the one empire it is designed for. SO though there is a pay option, it is not a true pay to win system. Cosmetics that, while are not necessary, are available for purchase with station cash, and do not provide any boost to your character (outside of effective camouflage use). A balance system that allows a level 1 to kill a level 100 as easily as a 100 can a level 1. As a player and planetside 1 veteran, there is no other FPS out there that can come close to how great of a game this is, nor can boast how much more it can offer.

Before you read this this review, I want to say that everything I have written in this game review is FROM MEMORY and very few things are from other reviewers. I have not looked up anything which you will find probably if you have played the game more recently and longer than I have.
Robocraft used to be an amazing game. It was balanced, people had amazing bot designs, and if you couldn't build for your life, you could go on the community market to find that one robot and modify it to your liking, all while being in the same caliber of matchmaking, and the CPU.
The game has changed multiple times before I started playing, and one of those mechanics I know off the top of my head was the progression system. It used to be where you gained the capability based on what you were building in the tree. Then, they introduced the level system. You instead gained the capability based on your level, without a skill tree. I started playing a bit after that was introduced. Admittedly, I bought into the game to get level 100, what at the time was the max level, for a bot after I had reached the 40s, because while I may or may not have probably had enough of the earned currency, I wasn't the level for it. I wanted to get a bot that I thought was really good, and seeing as how bots could disappear on the market, I wanted to get it while I could. My intention wasn't to get level 100, but it just turned out that way.
The balance changed over time when they added new weapons like lock-on missiles, anti-air, and the like. They added the capability to use multiple weapons on one bot. It changed Robocraft into more of a MOBA type of game, you can only use weapon/ability one at once and then switch freely. Because of this, it introduced a mana-like system that regenerates somewhat quickly, but in some builds, it can of course be drastic, but this adds to the trial and error of bots of course.
A while after the weapon mechanic update, they did the crates update. This is pretty much the basis of what ruined the game. Crates that you earn have different tiers, but there was only one crate (which I think is the highest tier) that you could purchase and depending on the bundle you bought with real money guaranteed legendaries. This update also destroyed progression, the old currencies, and how items are earned. Your level is now an indicator that shows how long you played and/or what you bought into beforehand. Because I stopped playing the game for a long time, I haven't leveled up in a long time, too. It's possible maybe there's something I don’t know of; for example, level ups may give free crates. There were two currencies; one that you earned and one that you bought. They were merged with the update. The effect was that you only get them from items you recycle. You now obtained items from crates and forging.
And a while after the crates update, they did the gamemode update in which they scrapped the original team deathmatch that really was a elimination, but it made up the player base and could fit the most players: 20 people, a 10v10. Instead of making it a separate gamemode (like calling it elimination), they replaced it with what is actually a team deathmatch but also held less players, and a not as good map. It was a 5v5 with a 20 kill counter. That is very low. This makes some bots completely and utterly useless, and because of this, you had to make new bots. And remember, because the currency is scarce, you either worked with what you had, or probably recycled your way up if you didn't buy your way into the game. Battle arena got a good update at least that removed capture towers that could easily be captured, instead replacing it with a proximity capture. But this mode was always a 5v5, and 5v5s in Robocraft usually have an AFK or ragequitter/someone who DC’d that makes the match completely unplayable.
tl;dr
The game was essentially better and worked completely differently, and one update pretty much started the downward spiral.

Ingredients:
DOUGH
3 to 3 1/2 cups Pillsbury BEST™ All Purpose Flour
1 package Pillsbury™ Funfetti® Radiant Red Cupcake & Cake Mix
1 tablespoon unsweetened cocoa powder
1 (1/4 oz.) packet quick-rising yeast
1/2 teaspoon salt
1 cup hot water (120° to 130°F)
3 tablespoons butter, softened
1 egg
CINNAMON FILLING
1 cup firmly packed brown sugar
1/3 cup Pillsbury BEST™ All Purpose Flour
1/2 cup butter, softened
1 1/2 tablespoons ground cinnamon
Crisco® Original No-Stick Cooking Spray
1 container Pillsbury™ Creamy Supreme® Cinnamon Bun Flavored Frosting
OR Pillsbury™ Creamy Supreme® Cream Cheese Flavored Frosting
1/2 cup chopped toasted pecans
Preparation Directions
For Dough: COMBINE 2 1/2 cups flour, cake mix, cocoa powder, yeast and salt in large bowl. Stir in hot water, butter and egg until dough pulls away from sides of bowl. Knead on lightly floured surface 5 minutes or until smooth and elastic, adding additional flour as needed. Cover with large bowl; let rest 10 minutes.
For Cinnamon Filling: COMBINE brown sugar, flour, butter and cinnamon in a small bowl with fork until crumbly. Roll dough to 16 x 10-inch rectangle on lightly floured surface. Crumble cinnamon mixture over dough; spread evenly. Starting with 16-inch side, roll up tightly, pressing edges to seal. Coat 13 x 9-inch baking pan with no-stick cooking spray. Cut dough into 12 slices. Arrange in prepared pan, creating 3 rows, each with 4 rolls. Cover loosely with plastic wrap. Let rise in warm place 45 minutes or until doubled in size.
HEAT oven to 375°F. Uncover pan. Bake 25 minutes or until golden brown. Cool in pan on wire rack 15 minutes. Place frosting in heavy-duty plastic bag. Cut very small corner off bag. Separate rolls and place on serving plates. Drizzle with desired amount of frosting. Sprinkle with pecans. Enjoy!

This game is a freak of nature in the world of videogames. It's completely free to play, WITHOUT much of a pay-2-win structure, and is still a complete blast to play? Damn.
This is an MMOFPS, a massively-multiplayer online first-person shooter. Emphasis on the "massively". Considering it's a first-person shooter, a 2000-player capacity per server is pretty impressive, especially since servers are almost always at least 75% full. Anyways, this amount of players results in HUGE battles, ALL over the place, ALL the time. We're talking futuristic fighter jets, all sorts of tanks, base-mounted anti-air cannons, dune buggies with Gatling guns mounted on top, you name it. Not to mention the variety of infantry classes marching along.
Let me back up. You can choose from one of three factions; the Vanu Sovereignty (VS), the Terran Republic (TR), or the New Conglomerate (NC). Each look completely different, but are all balanced quite similarly. From there, you get into battle. Or war, I should say. Take a look at the 64-square-kilometer maps of one of the four continents available, Indar (arid, desert-ish), Amerish (woodsy), Esamir (snow), and Hossin (swamp). Each one likely has many battles raging, so just pick one with a nearby spawn point, and get into the action! A selection of 6 infantry classes - Infiltrator, Light Assault, Combat Medic, Engineer, Heavy Assault, and MAX (a battlesuit-type deal) - each with PLENTY of weapons and attachments, will keep anyone entertained non-stop.
Now, this pay-2-win model. Not too existent, in my opinion. By using real cash to purchase things, you only speed up your progress of acquiring new weapons and attachments. There is nothing that is only available for cash that will give your character an advantage in the battlefield. Only cosmetic upgrades (i.e. camos, character and vehicle appearance, etc.) can be exclusively purchased with real money. Of course, this means that it is a grind earning enough certification points, or certs (in-game currency), to upgrade your vehicles, weapons, and character until you are content. For example; a decent player can earn roughly 30-60 certs an hour. A new assault rifle, or any gun for that matter, costs anywhere between 250 and 1000 certs, depending on quality of course. Attachments, anywhere from 30 to 250. Character boosts and upgrades, similar price range. You get the point.
Now, don't let my last point discourage you. PlanetSide 2 is one hell of a game, and I know I found it fairly easy to look beyond the grind time and just enjoy it. The enjoying part is a piece of cake. If you love teamwork, strategy, first-person shooters, vehicle combat, customization, large-scale warfare, any of the above, just do yourself a favor and install this. I don't even have to say "buy this", because it's ♥♥♥♥in' free. Jesus, what more do you need?

There's a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥ing, a lot of negativity, and a lot of people screaming about broken promises.  But, at the end of the day, people still come back to playing this game because there simply isn't another experience like it on the market. Try the game out, join a squad, keep to cover, and don't try to lone wolf it when you're new, and you should have a blast.

I don't have as much time invested in this game as many others, but I enjoyed it regardless. What Robocraft initially set out to do was easily the greatest free-to-play build and fight style game I had seen. For reasons that are far too complex to articulate, I had stopped playing.
Fast-forward three or four monthes later, I checked my email as usual. That's when I saw that there was a huge update to Robocraft. Naturally, I wanted to check it out.
The first glaring difference was the log-in screen, which I didn't mind (It needed a makeover anyway). About 30 seconds later, I was greeted with the unholy sight that is the new UI for the Main Menu. My initial reaction was something like "The f*ck is this?" and proceeded to d*ck around for 10 minutes until I figured out what the hell I was doing and opened the garage.
I was not amused.
Although, to give the developers credit, they didn't f*ck me over by deleting my craft (I called it Nyte Stryker, God help me...). Another 10 minutes was wasted looking for the tech tree (veteran Robocraftians will know what I'm talking about) only to find out they REMOVED IT and just had the inventory.
I've been around the proverbial block a few times to know a pay-to-win when I see one, and GOD DAMN WAS THIS IS OF THEM.
I'll tell you how I can to that conclusion; the aforementioned inventory? It had every single block, weapon, armor, etc. in the game in it with a price tag (in-game currency, which can be bought with real currency if you are stupid enough) and the amount of that specific item you had.
Granted, there were a few, and I mean a FEW good changes to the overall experience. BUT, the pay-to-win♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off because you could grind for hours for the in-game cash or a specific type of item (much like several mmorpg's that come to mind), and have all that work squandered by a brat with a loaded parent.
You tell me how that's fun anymore.

-Dont buy weapons to start, you get a free one when you make a new character upgrade your vehicles/abilities
-Dont get lost, early players will constantly get lost as they do not know the lay of the land, follow experienced players
-No ramboing, you are not invincible and the second you step out over cover you have a high chance of dying

I used to play Wolfenstein: Enemy Territory, an objective-based WWII shooter that scratched a certain itch no other game seemed to satisfy.
This game has some ET influences showing through, probably due to the fact that it's the same developer. I like that, I want a successor to ET. I also like that it takes a longer time to rank up, makes it more meaningful. It takes more than two or three shots to kill people most of the time, I like that too. An arcade-y shooter, fine.
It's got other influences showing through in the form of certain design trends that are there only because they're popular in other games.
Unboxing things, cards, rarities, items. The parkour thing. The incredibly fast-paced and movement-oriented nature of the game that nearly all new FPS games seem to be endorsing or adopting in some manner.
I don't like that. I could really go for shooters that are in fact a little slower-paced, as currently they could not become any faster. It doesn't make the game any better or any more balanced. Just popular things put in there because, well, you know, why not? Additonally, the faster-paced it is, the faster the hitmarkers and the +XP numbers appear on the player's screen which keeps them happy and playing the game.
It also doesn't adopt a design trend rightfully popular in other games, including even in their over-a-decade-old ET -- an unlock and progression system. ET had 4 classes and you could rank up skills in each of them, with some skills reflecting overall that benefited you in-game. It also had a rank/level-up system that had some perks too. It was surprisingly engaging, interesting and complex for it's time.
I can buy other mercs with large amounts of credits and hope for cool drops which serve only aesthetic purposes past bronze. Why would I though? I already have the merc I enjoy playing the most and I don't care how I look in-game. The amount of in-game currency it takes to buy new mercs is so ridiculous it seems they'd prefer you just paid actual money, as they do offer that option. So now I'm just earning XP, and it's a good XP system, rewards you for most things, for nothing.
It's decent enough mechanically and I have fun playing it, usually absolutely destroy people in 8v8 games because the guns seem to be nearly 100% accurate and have no recoil.
I really can't keep playing it though. It has this other feature which I'm going to call having basically no maps or content. There are 3 game modes, I think. I've played 2. There's a defuse mission which comes straight from CS:GO or Search and Destroy in CoD, whatever, a lot of games have this mode. Exactly the same rules.
There are a grand total of 2 maps for this mode. How long, I ask, can you play 2 maps over and over again?
The other mode is objective, vehicle escorts, repair, defense, etc. Varied, very much like ET. 6 maps for this. I can go back, download Wolfenstein ET, which is over 10 years old, and there are dozens of different maps which are all diverse in design and in the objectives one needs to complete.
A decade ago when I played CoD4 it launched with 16 maps, I thought this was a good ground floor, a good basic minimum for map variety. It was satisfactory, adequate, enough. There was a map pack which pushed it to twenty anyways, was free.
How does this compare? It's got 6 maps. Honestly I can't keep playing this, I'd like to, but there has to be, you know, content. Replayability. Variety. Again, I can go back to ET and play on a map recreating Minas Tirith from LotR, the allies scaling the 7 levels against the Nazi defense. Or, I can play Dirty Bomb and repair the EV on the same tiny, limited maps.
Haven't played the third mode but I don't think it has any unique maps.
Are there player-hosted servers with custom maps? I genuinely don't know.
Be glad to play this game again when the devs add like a minimum of 15 more maps to this game, hugely improve their variety in design and objectives and give some meaningful progression/unlock goals to work towards besides cards.
Until then, this game is incredibly bland.

Planetside 2 is, in my opinion, the greatest first person shooter of all time. People claim that it's pay to win but I must heavily disagree, as a player who has over a thousand kills with practically every weapon in the game I find the default weapons to be the best by far. The weapons can be bought with certs (in game money received by gaining experience) and many of the weapons fall within the 100 to 500 cert price point. Which takes an average newbie probably 2 hours of play time or less if they're specifically grinding experience by playing medic.
PROS: Amazing first time experience no other first person shooter on the planet can offer larger scale battles than planetside.
Graphics are amazing
Gun play is solid headshots are very rewarding, TR guns maybe a little OP in close quarters but on the whole guns are very well balanced. I never once thought to myself "Oh if only I had this weapon I would be amazing at this game" because all weapons are best utilized in different situations.
MAPS ARE HUGE, literally the continents are at least 15 times the size of even the very largest of Battlefield maps and there is a good diversity in environments.  Hossin the swamp continent with massive beautiful trees, Indar a barren desert with alien rock formations, Esamir a land of ice and massive crystals, and Amerish filled with mountains and forests.
Character customization is endless every week more camo, armor and helmets are added to the game. Many of them designed by players!
Loadouts are crazy customizable, you can choose from a huge variety of gadgets and weapons. And save your loadouts for future use.
Each faction again with it's strengths and weaknesses, the NC is the best at mid and long range combat with hard hitting weapons and the fastest muzzle velocity, TR is better for close quarters combat with a fast fire rate and large magazine size. VS is the middle ground faction with no bullet drop, fast reload and low recoil and high accuracy.
There are 7 different classes of infantry to play around as, each with their own unique abilities. Light assault: can fly for a short period of time, to help maneuver around walls and climb even the highest of mountains on Amerish. Infiltrator: has a predator like cloaking ability and sensor darts and can be equipped with sniper rifles and SMGs as well as having the ability to hack enemy terminals and turrets making it perfect for the assassination of high priority targets. Heavy Assault: Equipped with LMGs, rocket launchers and a activatable shield for tanking damage the heavy in the best class for killing... just about anything whether it be vehicles infantry or mech suits, AND DID I MENTION THERE ARE MECH SUITS!? The MAX class is the big♥♥♥♥♥walking tank that can run into buildings to wreak havoc on infantry and equipped with AA guns to decimate the enemy skies, they're not that OP when you start to know what you're doing in the game they are very vulnerable to explosives and most of the time a rocket to the back is enought to take them out. The engineer and medic are your basic support classes with the ability to drop ammo and revive respectively.
There's SOOO much to do, I've been playing this game for over 2 years now and I still find new ways of challenging myself or goofing off.
Incredible amount of unique types of vehicles, each faction with their own strengths. ATVs can cloak, ESFs (Empire specific fighters) (basically jets) can go in and out of hover mode making dogfighting an incredibly unique and fun experience as they are incredibly maneuverable.
HUGE fights it's typical to have fights where there are over two hundred people fighting at one part of the map.
Achievement system gives veteran players like myself something to strive for with rewards that are incredibly difficult to possess and show off your prowess on the battlefield.
Squad and platoon play are amazing in this game. An organized platoon of infantry could easily push back a force of two hundred given the right tactics.
Squad leaders can call down an orbital drop beacon for their entire squad to spawn at, which can change the tide of battle.
Bullet physics, unless you're vanu, making it a very identifiable game for battlefield players.
Game is frequently updated with new content
each free account is given 3 character slots (one for each faction)
Cons:
Connectivity issues with the servers from time to time (recently speaking) they'll probably resolve this in the future.
Game could be better optimized I find myself with less than 30 FPS in the larger battles numbering 200+ participants and I have a considerably beefy computer. Easily avoidable however by keeping to fights that don't exceed 100 players and turning the graphics down to medium.
Spawn camping is a problem, as there is no control for how many people on each side can be fighting there are times when fight's that are heavily overpopulated by enemies end up in a spawn camping mess.
Vehicle spamming and zerging is an issue. Outfits will organize a massive pull of main battle tanks that number in the hundreds sometimes and it is literally impossible to halt their momentum through your territory.
Capture mechanics are dull and repetitive, hold the point for 5 to 20 minutes depending on how big the base is, and keep the enemy hoards from recapturing the point.
Vehicles bombing the spawn points of bases, making it impossible to step foot outside the spawn without being blown to smithereens.
Huge learning curve as many things such as flying are completely unique to planetside 2
Bad tutorial
It's hard for new players to learn what's going on and how to do things basic to the game.
After the tutorial they orbital drop you into the biggest fight going on and you'll probably get killed instantly
Overall I very very Highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the FPS genre as it is a unique experince that no other game can offer.

There's a defuse mission which comes straight from CS:GO or Search and Destroy in CoD, whatever, a lot of games have this mode. Exactly the same rules.
There are a grand total of 2 maps for this mode. How long, I ask, can you play 2 maps over and over again?
The other mode is objective, vehicle escorts, repair, defense, etc. Varied, very much like ET. 6 maps for this. I can go back, download Wolfenstein ET, which is over 10 years old, and there are dozens of different maps which are all diverse in design and in the objectives one needs to complete.
A decade ago when I played CoD4 it launched with 16 maps, I thought this was a good ground floor, a good basic minimum for map variety. It was satisfactory, adequate, enough. There was a map pack which pushed it to twenty anyways, was free.
How does this compare? It's got 6 maps. Honestly I can't keep playing this, I'd like to, but there has to be, you know, content. Replayability. Variety. Again, I can go back to ET and play on a map recreating Minas Tirith from LotR, the allies scaling the 7 levels against the Nazi defense. Or, I can play Dirty Bomb and repair the EV on the same tiny, limited maps.
Haven't played the third mode but I don't think it has any unique maps.
Are there player-hosted servers with custom maps? I genuinely don't know.
Be glad to play this game again when the devs add like a minimum of 15 more maps to this game, hugely improve their variety in design and objectives and give some meaningful progression/unlock goals to work towards besides cards.
Until then, this game is incredibly bland.

As a child I had many games I enjoyed.  Most games I enjoyed were real time strategy (RTS) and turn based strategy.  I came across Age of Empires by accident (the original) and it was for 9 bucks... so I begged my dad to let me get the game,  After a while he gave and and I fell in love, and I was rather good at it.  Being able to jump on one computer and fight against my brother on another was an amazing achievement (in my mind).  Years down the road my family was on facation and I saw Age of Empires: Age of Kings on the shelf.  I absolutely had to have it.  So spending 30 dollars on a game (which was the most I ever spent at that time) I purchased the game.  As soon as I got home I spend the next few hours watching as the install happend (took way longer at that time than it does now).  And to my amazement this game was better.  It was at this point I was dedicated to the game.  Now enough of a back story how is my rating going to go?
When I rate a game I generally rate it on select criteria.  These are as follows
Advertisement - How did the game stick out to me making me want to buy it
Simpliciy - As a game it should be simple and easy to play as well as challenging in it's own way
Gameplay - How does the game play in general
Re-playability - if I'm giving my hard earned money to a game I want to be able to play that game over and over
Campain - (if available) as original as games were created themselver there has always been a "story" and the story of built into a campaign is an intergal part of enjoying the tale the game has to tell.
Graphic - Not a core detail I care for however asthetics definitly help for bonus points
I have not come up with an official numbering system to my rating as I'm figuring out so we are going to go over each and I will give my choice on the following levels
Must Have         - This game is truly amazing and you must have it in your gaming arsnal
Good to Play      - Played it and loved it would recommend it but you be fine if you don't get
Ok Game           - The game's ok I guess... I'm not really recommending it, but if your board enough go ahead
Avoid                - The game is really not that good avoid it if you can
Avoid and burn - This game is so terrible that if I could I would burn every copy so please help me if possible.
So lets break down Age of Empires II HD
Advertisement
So as I have already stated I loved the game from the begining, what sold me on the game was a sale.  As far as in this day and era most re-released games with upgraded graphics are for those who loved the game before others took it's place.  So the idea of a classic with better graphics definitly stands out.  Beging at a higher resolution and picture quality definitly helps, but in retrospect for new gamers definitly doesn't stick out, because at the core the graphics are not that of a "modern RTS"
Simplicity
Controls are fairly simple (if your use to RTS) and the tech tree that is specific to each culture is definitly an aspect that adds dynamic to the game.  It does have quite a bit of strategy, and if you start getting to the higher setting of difficulty it can get tedious to play after long hours just trying to find the one villeger or ship that's hiding in the corner doing nothing.
Gameplay
The game play is exactly how I remember it.  Smooth, yet rough.  The characters have basic animations that doesn't give the smooth look like some of the modern gamesl ike SCII however the sprites move in a fashion that makes up for this.  And the sequences of battles enterties and makes the gameplay interesting.  The computer AI is rather dumb, and sometimes can be quite annoying, and the only difference between difficulties is how quickly the computer attacks or collects resourses.  However all the AI battles in the same fasshion, so no changes in dynamics or tactics making the VS AI rather dull.  However the multiplayer against other human stll has it's fun.  This game is very susseptable to "Rush" attacks and if your not too careful you will lose a lot, so timing and planning is very important.  Games can take a long time, but they are still fun in general.  The tech tree system is different for each culture you choose giving some bonuses and disatvantages to some culture, and the vairety is awsome.
Re-Playability
The game definitly has some re-playability for the multiplayer, however the campaign doesn't make me want to do it over and over..  After beating the AI several times it does get rather dull once you figured out the best strategy of attack.  However multiplayer is always interesting against others.
Campaign
As mentioned the campaign(s) are not to replayable, and for me they can be tedious at times, however the captivating way they blend the gameplay with history definitly is a fun, and if your love history enough you may become interested in reading about the famous battles you fight in the game.  However each capaing is a play through once and your done, but the choices and variety of campains definitly allow plenty of time to enjoy.
Graphics
As this is an upgrade the textures visuals and styles are upgraded beyond that of the original making it "eye candy" for those who have played the original for years.  However if you compare this to some modern RTS and even some from back around the same period you may think the graphics are subpar, however this game definitly has it's own style of graphics and they flow well for the gameplay.
Overall I would definitly recommend this game as a Good to Play.  For those who played it in the past and love the AOE franchises definitly a must have however for those who just found this game and want a good RTS to play try this game out for size.  You will like it and it can be fun.
I hope this review can help you if your on the fence about this game.

Short version: If you like build games, where you can actually drive the things you make, then give this game a try. It also has a leveling system where you get exp. for battling, and in doing so (battling) you get crates with free stuff in them. The game is free; if you don't like it, uninstall it. You've lost nothing.
Long version: As MANY other reviewers have said, yes, this game has recently added a new items system where you get blocks from crates, as well as pretty much nullifying their in-game currency mechanics. (The only way to get more "money" is to either level up [max lvl is 150], or sell stuff. You can also buy crates with IRL currency.) As for the multi-player aspect, it is MUCH more rewarding to go into single player, and kill AI bots. Any weapon worth anything is really expensive, both in currency, and CPU. (The game's way of limiting how big your bot can be, your cap increases when you level up.) There's also a Premium feature that lets you level up twice as fast, gives you two extra platoon slots, and when you
in multi-player, gives you +100% earnings at the end of the battle as well as an extra +5% added to that for each player who also has Premium. So while this game is A LOT easier when you use money, you can still get almost anything in the game if you just level-grind. (Also, sometimes the developers give out codes for free Premium, so if you get this game, I would follow it as well for updates and such.)

I played Age of Empires when it first came out so very long ago, and I spent hours playing and loving that game. Heck, I enjoyed it so much that I ended up minoring in History in college just because the game inspired me to learn more about these cultures and people. When I saw Age of Empires II HD on Steam, I happily bought the game, expecting to relive a little of the magic of my youth. After playing some skirmish matches and on the campaign, I cannot recommend Age of Empires II HD for, really, any price.
My problems with this game do not have to do with the older graphics system or gameplay. On the contrary, the original visuals and gameplay were (and still are) quite charming and challenging respectively. My biggest problems stem from the hyped visual overhaul and new gameplay options. The original visuals were well done, yet I cannot distinguish any real difference between the original game's visuals and the "HD" visuals. The only difference, I assume, is that the "HD" means widescreen support as opposed to a real overhaul of the graphics. Since I don't play the game on widescreen, there's really no visual difference between the original and the HD.
As for the gameplay itself, I seem to encounter massive slow down in mid-to-late game skirmishes despite a pretty decent ROG laptop (Intel Core i5 2.5 GhZ, Nvidia GeForce GTX 660M, 8 GB RAM). The developers warn that population should only be set at 75, but if the option runs up to 500 and offers "LudaKRIS" size maps, why would I stick to one of the lowest population and map settings when my rig can run Total War: Rome II on med-high settings without stuttering? When I try to play at the higher or medium settings for Age of Empires II HD, the game becomes virtually unplayable. Even at population sizes of 100, I experience significant slow down when playing with 7 AI. The fact is, if a modern gaming rig can't handle this rehash of a much older game with barelu updated graphics, then why even own it in the first place? Really disappointing showing, and I should've spent more time checking out the reviews on metacritic and the like before buying this game.

For those who don't know,
was released in 1999. After that the
expansion was released, which almost everyone who has the original Age of Empires II also got. The game is one of the most popular RTS games in existence. It's most fun when played in multiplayer, my friends at college and I love playing multiplayers games all crowded together in one dorm room. Trouble is, we can't play over the summer because the online support for it was dropped years ago (it is an old game). A lot of us were disappointed by this fact, and Microsoft must've found out, because they modified the game to work with Steam's multiplayer system and re-released.
-Slightly updated graphics; almost everything looks exactly the same or identical to the old version, except for the water, which looks a lot better in the new version; the old game looked good (2D graphics), so no change is good here (but the new water is nice)
-New resolutions are supported, along with dual monitors (the old game only supported 1280x1024, 1024x768, and 800x600)
-There is a new AI, thanks to a recent game update (recent as of 6/29/14)
-The max population cap was move from 200 to 500, you can still limit it to all the old settings if you want
-All multiplayer works through Steam now
-The game requires a much better computer to play than the old one; this is actually very obnoxious, the graphics really are not much improved (except the water, of course), but it takes a lot more graphics muscle (yes, not just CPU) to play it smoothly
-Multiplayer is rather laggy, almost every game I've played has had a very unpleasant amount of lag; for this reason, if you are not a big fan of the game, you should not get it unless you want to play the campaigns and single player battles (which are still fun); I still play multiplayer almost exclusively, but I really like this game, so that's why
-LAN multiplayer isn't an option now; I would hope that it still uses only the LAN when all players are on the local network, but I don't know; however, while I say this is a bad thing, it hasn't actually caused a problem for me
Apart from what I mentioned above, the game is pretty much exactly like the old game. You can play it with no change in gameplay if you like, by setting the pop cap to 200 or less, and you can even choose to play agains the old AI. The game plays like the 1.0c update of the original
. Oh, and if you haven't figured it out already,
includes all the features of
expansion.

Dayum SON! You want explosions?! CHECK. You want vehicles?! CHECK.  You want invisibility and forcefields?! CHECK. You want a leveling system and customisable stuff?! DOUBLECHECK.
There's an awful lot to be said about Planetside but little that is of true importance. The game is "MASSIVE"; you could probably think of any "yo-mamma" joke and apply it to this game and it would almost be true.
So one minute you're New Conglomerate (NC) "REBEL SCUM" (as if this were Star Wars) on this hole of a planet Indar, sweating up the storm in the desert and BOOM, bullets are flying, jetpacks are roaring and things just got HECTIC. To the left you see the a squad leader placing a spawn beacon and then get TAKEN OUT by an aerial swoop from the right. Tanks are firing, grenades are popping off and all hell is breaking loose!
The next, you're freezing your man-bits off in the frozen wasteland of Esamir (or at least you would be if you had any since you're part of the Vanu Sovereignty (VS); an alien race bent on using purple and green for everything including lazers). You stare down the barrel of the new rifle you just decided to unlock with the credits you earnt IN-GAME looking for somebody who is having too good of a day. BANG a tank mine blows mere metres from you and you panic, BUT WHAT DO YOU DO?! You tap that button and walk into the girls locker room because ain't NOBODY seeing you right now.
Then you wake up.. Things are a little different here. It's like a scene from Predator with a lot of green.. water, shrubs, trees. One might call it your own slice of paradise... at least it would be.. if you weren't one of the many Terran Republic (TR) flaunting your red flag in the face of those you seek to oppress. You are the Law, you are the fist of the Emperor (or something of the sort), you are the boot to the face of the rebels that resist your reign. The gunships have arrived, cannon fire rains down like a hailstorm from heaven as you pave a road through to the next section of the map as you begin to capture it for the glory of your faction!
NOW most would with this narrative, immediately expect some kind of 20/10 overall. BUT (yes this was coming), the game does have areas for improvement and certain small aspects that dilute its fun from time to time.  Guess its time for the +/-
+ Unbelievable scale of game, hundreds of players per battle at times.
+ Tons of weapons at your disposal from shotguns to SMG's to Rocket Launchers.
+ Customisation providing a truly individualised experience when it comes to both your character and vehicles.
+ Great graphics quality (especially given the magnitude of the game).
+ Small features which prove a great help E.g. In-game AREA Microphone.
+ Multiple classes granting unique play styles and so there is always one to suit.
.. I could go on
- Can be difficult at times to find what some people would consider a "large-scale" battle when playing at off-peak times.
- Various weapons/perks can be earned through in-game credit but MANY require payment using REAL $.
- Some abilities e.g. Invisibility can be a nuisance to deal with but CAN be with the right equipment.
As the song goes: "If you haven't gotten it by now, you just ain't gettin it.."

Nothing to make it special, everything to make it horrible.
A dozen ways to flank any point (There are no bottlenecks or decently defendable areas in this game, and usually it's possible to flank from above as well which makes a 360° horizon check insufficient) means that it's very difficult to find out who's shooting you before you're dead, even with the half-hearted help of impact direction indicators.
If you do find out, you're still dead; because by the time you've found out, you'd be lucky to have one second of health left if not playing with very high health. In fact, you'd be lucky to survive one second in total, with the abundance and ease of instakills and obscene DPS.
Of course, because of the gear distribution system in this game, it sometimes works very differently for the person you're shooting at, especially if they're a heavy.
Flanking a heavy and then shotgunning them a few times at close range with starter equipment does hardly anything; and of course, when they finally find out which one of the dozen flank routes you're using, not at all helped by the unrealistically difficult to make out graphics and the fact that they have to be sure you're an enemy before they start firing, they will kill you pretty much instantly.
I don't think a passing mention of the graphics of this game is sufficient to explain how much of a problem it is.
When you look at someone in highly-saturated clothing from across the room, do they all of a sudden look almost grey? This game seems to think so, given the fog gradient.
And someone at about 50 metres is either a smudge or a silhouette. You can still kill them at that distance though if you have the right gear, and they can't do much about it unless they have the right gear also; because somebody forgot that one-way lethality is one of the most hated game mechanics there is.
Given that another graphical issue is that the ambient light of this game ranges from dim(sun shining right overhead) to a little bit darker than that(middle of the night), it's almost as if the developers of this game are trying to generate as much friendly fire as possible.
You can avoid being triggerhappy so as to not mow down every teammate who comes your way, since the lighting and inconsistency of uniforms means that the only reliable indicator of team is a tiny blue triangle for your teammates; but the cost of that is that in the very rare event that a face-to-face fight occurs, you don't end up firing straight away.
Thankfully, since obscurity of teams is a problem that plagues everyone, the person you're fighting will also start with the same awkward "friend or foe?" delay.
So that's one thing that went right with this game, as in something that could have gone wrong but didn't.
Even with that generous definition of "things going right" with the game, I still can't think of anything more to add to the list.

An excellent game where the actions of a single soldier get swept up into a larger global conflict. PS2 plays like nothing I've seen before and I keep coming back to it time and again to get my fix.
I'd suggest getting into an Outfit (ie. Clan) sooner rather than later to take full advantage of this game. At the very least, drop into random squads until you find an Outfit that aligns with your vision of the game. Experiment with the different classes, armoured vehicles, and aircrafts and familiarize yourself with their controls, advantages and disadvantages.
Lastly, after almost 250 hours of game time logged according to Steam, I can safely say this game is not Pay to Win. The default loadout of each class, vehicle, and aircraft feel powerful. Bought weapons add variety to the mix and definitely have certain advantages in a given situation - but for every advantage they also have a serious disadvantage. If you lost a battle it's not because the enemy had bought weapons, it is because of either the skills of players involved or the overwhelming advantage that throwing a large amount of bodies at a target can achieve.

Robocraft began as a humble little building battlebot game and was very fun for any audience.  I really enjoyed the combat, the map design and the tools I was given for building bots.  However the more recent take on this game has become far less humble.  Now you must surrender your wallet to the game in order to even begin to have the slightest chance to compete with other players.  If you are just starting out in Robocraft I sincerely wish you luck, as you will be confronted by the removal of the tiers system, allowing ridiculously overpowered bots the opprotunity to beat you into the ground over and over again.  The lock on legendary rocket launcher cannot be beaten by anything, simply because people just strap a helicopter blade to the top of it and fly to the flight cap and rain rockets from above that never miss.  Well I guess you could try to build a flier to compete with that rocket launcher, but wait there's more overpowered ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.  The AA gun that everyone on the ground seems to have makes flying a nightmare.  You barely even have to aim the big circle and one shot tears off all of your wings and engines, leaving you on the ground the whole match, desperately trying to crawl up to a decent flight level.  Also there are melee tesla coils that one shot you now so have fun with those as well.  This game used to have a system that prevented you from using more than one type of weapon on a bot and that was a good feature considering the fact that railgun ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥tters now have access to lasers for close range encounters.  So they kill you from across the map and when you finally get close, you're torn apart.
Honestly this game would be amazing if they would revert back to when loot crates were not a thing and you earned the block buying currency from playing games.  At least then I could buy armor blocks.  Now there is no tech tree and no armor tier.  All forms of progression have been removed in favor of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t lootcrate system,
If you did not play Robocraft while it was good don't even bother beginning an account, unless you are willing to fork over hundreds of dollars trying to get that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t rocket launcher or AA gun.  You may still enjoy the game if you played it while it was good if you managed to keep all your old items, that way you may have a reliable source of materials to at least let you attempt to compete with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.  But that might not work if you were one of the unlucky ones that had all your old items deleted, like two of my friends who sunk lots of time into the good version of this game only for their progress to be deleted.

Honestly, as a person who transitioned from TF2 to Dirty Bomb, I can say that the game is extremely harsh to play. BUT, it's extremely rewarding in my opinion.
The game's movement system is a bit clunky here and there, but it's at the same time much faster than your typical FPS. Being able to wall jump, leap through windows, reach areas you usually can't with enough practice feels so much rewarding when you get the jump on an opponent.
Dying feels cheap in Dirty Bomb, but it's also a constant reminder to improve your aim in the game. It really is an FPS that will not hold your hand, and with ammo being extremely scarce, every shot -does- count in this game.
I wish that Mercs did not cost as much to buy, but the way I see it is, if you want something for free, it's fair they have the option for us folk to afford that merc anyway. So it's a fair system.
My only real gripe is that with a hand full of hackers, and an already fairly obnoxious community, the game is going to need a fair amount of touch ups in that aspect. But then again it's a free online game, you're going to run into toxic players.
I'd only really recommend this game to people who play FPS' and want a break from the ordinary, or to hardcore gamers who are willing to sit there and study mechanics of the game. Because honestly, the game is really a quarter of how fun it really is when you don't know how to move.

Really fun game.  Feels a bit like CS:GO mixed with TF2, which are my two personal favorite games.  It's a bit ragey from the start because you don't know what all classes do, but if you keep playing past that initial annoyance you will see that it is indeed fun.  If you read some other reviews on steam or online you might see "Pay to win" often.  It's definitely not pay to win.  You earn in-game currency as you play, which allows you to buy certain classes.  It does take a while to get enough to buy classes with the in-game currency, but Dirty Bomb allows you to purchase in-game currency with Steam money.  So I would say that it is not "Pay to Win" it is more "Pay to Enjoy", but with enough work you can unlock all the characters, but I found that I have 6 favorites that I choose between, so you might not even have to buy all of them.  There's even something called a free rotation that allows you to choose between three different mercenary which switches every two weeks.  Overall very fun game which will take a while to "get old" because of all the various weapons, loadouts, and classes.

Over 1000 hours played:
Planetside 2 is a massive scale FPS that is also effectively an RTS for the players who are leading operations.  It focuses on combined arms tactics and A LOT of team work with the ultimate goal of territory control for your faction.  Balance is always being tweaked, but the primary balance feature is that the world is split into 3 factions, not just 2, so if any one of the 3 gets too strong, that faction gets ganged up on.  Also lots of built in VOIP, but some people run with their own 3rd party VOIP anyways.
If you like a game that focuses on community and teamwork, with many different roles that have to be filled and each of them being important, then this game is for you.
Also, if you like RTS, but get frustrated with how stupid the units are sometimes and wish that you could be commanding actual people, then this game is also for you.  It will take a while for players to trust you enough to lead them though.

I downloaded Dirty Bomb expecting another soulless free-to-play FPS game that I could put a couple hours into whenever I felt like mindlessly shooting things.
In that regard, I was dissapointed. My expectations were exceeded a thousand-fold.
This game is exactly what games under the free-to-play model should strive for; a solid experience for all players that the dedicated will gladly hand over cash for. Its pricing model reminds me of MOBA giant League of Legends- you have a few characters unlocked from the get-go, and get to sample a few extras every week, and you can unlock your favorites slowly with free currency, or unlock them instantly for cash.
But Dirty Bomb's respect for its players and their wallets are of course not the only reason for my reccomendation. The game is unique, balanced and, most importantly, fun!
Players start each match by selecting three of the "mercs" that they have unlocked. Each merc has strengths and weaknesses that will determine the player's role on the field. Skyhammer, the first character the player meets in the tutorial, is a basic fighter/assault character with a fairly high HP and a rifle with decent mid-range capabilities. He can supply his teammates with ammo packs and call in airstrikes. This latter ability is Skyhammer's "unique" power. Every character has a distinct ability as well as one shared by other, similar characters.
My personal favorite, Sparks, is a quick healer character armed with an SMG and a unique ability that allows her to revive teammates from range. She is easily dispatched, but if you work with a team full of assaults that know their roles, she can be extremely effective on the field despite her squishiness.
Once your squad is selected, you are dropped into a game and tasked with either completing a list of objectives or delaying the enemy team from doing so. Depending on the map, your team will either be rushing to move a cart or plant and defend a bomb or carry batteries or drugs...the game is very dynamic in this regard.
Adding to this dynamic nature is map-specific side-objectives that can turn the tide for one team or another. Running along the side of a map to the objective as Sparks, I noticed a platform indicating possible interaction. I pressed the action button and built a bridge to another section of the map that was previously only accesible by the enemy team. My team then rushed up the new bridge and dispatched the sniper that had been giving everyone trouble the whole game.
This game is currently in beta but it is already a fantastic experience, and if you're on the fence about downloading, I'd say it is 100% worth a try.

This is a great revision of an old classic. The AI Is highly improved and much more challenging, and the new content is great for people like myself who are heavy into scenario design. There were lots of things unlocked in map maker that existed on the original game (and expansion) official scenarios, like sea walls and gates for wooden walls, that are unlocked. But there are also tons of new things to use, including fire towers (think the fire ships turned into towers), a new fortified wall type, new "non-buildable" buildings to flesh out large towns with, and many of the wonders can be built as regular buildings without wonder-status, perfect for epic siege battles against towns.
As for the campaigns, I've only played some of the new official scenarios, but they're much more difficult and more "modern" in design. Instead of just having basically a standard game with technology tree limitations and some scripted goals, they are much more military-mission like in design, with a more linear play though. They remind me of Real Time Tactics games instead of traditional RTS style missions.
The new civilizations they added in the expansion are also great. They add the Italians, which are my new favorite civ, as well as a couple of civ from Easter Europe, a new Native American civ (Incas), and India as playable Civilizations. This is a great thing for international players who may have felt left out by the western European and East Asian focus of the original game.
As a whole, for the price point it is at, it’s a great way to relieve a classic game that has been brought up to date to offer new and exciting challenges.

This is a great revision of an old classic. The AI Is highly improved and much more challenging, and the new content is great for people like myself who are heavy into scenario design. There were lots of things unlocked in map maker that existed on the original game (and expansion) official scenarios, like sea walls and gates for wooden walls, that are unlocked. But there are also tons of new things to use, including fire towers (think the fire ships turned into towers), a new fortified wall type, new "non-buildable" buildings to flesh out large towns with, and many of the wonders can be built as regular buildings without wonder-status, perfect for epic siege battles against towns.
As for the campaigns, I've only played some of the new official scenarios, but they're much more difficult and more "modern" in design. Instead of just having basically a standard game with technology tree limitations and some scripted goals, they are much more military-mission like in design, with a more linear play though. They remind me of Real Time Tactics games instead of traditional RTS style missions.
The new civilizations they added in the expansion are also great. They add the Italians, which are my new favorite civ, as well as a couple of civ from Easter Europe, a new Native American civ (Incas), and India as playable Civilizations. This is a great thing for international players who may have felt left out by the western European and East Asian focus of the original game.
As a whole, for the price point it is at, it’s a great way to relieve a classic game that has been brought up to date to offer new and exciting challenges.

pros:

cons:

- client performance has been on a decline since performance update 01. it's been pretty terrible as of late, after code merge with ps4 version.
- server performance has been terrible/unplayable the past year. especially for EU players (having better connectivity, hit detection to NA servers, instead of home server on EU). the devs know about it, but just can't get their♥♥♥♥♥♥together, either because they stopped caring about the PC version, or they just don't have the experience to solve this.
- content/experience is player driven and since the community is lazy/stupid & there are no rules/restrictions to ensure quality, the fights are mostly unbalanced/one-sided/boring. a majority of the community either farms base captures (96+ vs. 2 guys in a spawn room, yey) or farms kills (mostly in vehicles/maxes or heavy assault) while not playing for any objective.
- new player experience is still one of the worst in gaming history. tutorial is very slim and doesn't really cover some important stuff. you drop to the biggest fights on the continent ang get slaughtered over and over again. all your support tools are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ly slow, and your can't get attachments for your weapons for a very long time. after all that, you end up in a platoon ran by a bad/lazy leader who teaches you the wonders of zerging like a stupid sheep, and than end up in a bad outfit that does it on a daily basis with an array of bad/lazy leaders. you also use a shotgun or a max suit everytime you can, cause why not.. and get used to completely playing the game on easy mode. and that's a the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ community expands and kills any competitiveness or fun you could have in this game.
- dev team size has been cut hard or shifted to ps4/xbox1, and as a result new content is rarely released, or released in a broken "phase 1" state, and left like that for a LONG period. (we still didn't get any phase 2 to any of the phase 1s that currently ruin the game [like the resource system phase 1]).
- weapon/class balance is terrible and the devs are generally out of touch/base their tweaks on spreadsheets, micro sales or forum/reddit outcries.
- bugs, bugs, bugs, some still existing ever since beta. every patch creates more bugs.
- game's netcode is clientside based, making the game pretty iffy for competitive play, where you die behind walls or can exploit packet loss to your advantage (therum style). the devs support the community with a competitive server you can scrim on (jaeger) doe.
- base design is bad and boring for the most part. recycled assets everywhere makes for a very repeatitive feel to the game.

Planetside 2 is a fun game. You control a circle, dot, square or triangle shaped cursor and the goal is to find other players with different colored clothing, position the cursor over them and press and hold or click the left mouse button (If you're playing as a medic you must press and hold the RIGHT mouse button while positioning the cursor over players wearing clothing that is the same color as yours).
There are 3 factions, one wears red and has cursors that make sort of a high speed rattling sound when depressed. One wears blue and makes more of a slower and lower pitched rattling sound with their cursors and there is a faction who wears the old prop clothes from a mid 90s sci-fi television series. Babylon 5 maybe? Not sure. There are hundreds of other players who are trying to position their cursors over you and if they do it before you do, they usually win. The game can be very difficult because you get stressed out sometimes and there is often a self-appointed person in charge who will be busy giving you directions via their mic while you are busy trying to simply avoid the plethora of enemy cursors positioning themselves over you. If you are playing as an engineer, you can set up turrets, and there is a mini game where other people on your team must try to kill you with a knife while you are using your turret.
You can join an outfit, but if you want to be told exactly what to do by a stranger, you only need to leave the volume on or read the yellow text on the chat window that ocassionally shows up to be ignored by everyone. You can unlock weapons in the game by earning points and these weapons will make it so you don't have to hold the left mouse button down quite as long when you are positioning your cursor over an enemy.
The game also provides angst-ridden teenagers a safe place to expirement with things they would never say to anyone in person and it simultaneously provides the more mature gamer a safe place to stab them for it with a tiny chainsaw. Everyone wins!
Seriously though. It's a fun game if you stick with it!
