I never, NEVER post any sort of review for anything, but this game in particular caught my eye. I've been playing it for the past couple days with my brother and have to say, it's nothing short of amazing! Playing for the first time, my brother and I spawned immediately in to the action. We found ourselves pinned down with a small group of friendlies in the snowy area of the map trying to defend (what was left of) our base. Outgunned and outnumbered, my brother and I activated our stealth field generators and made a run for it to higher ground, in this situation, the higher ground was an ice glacier. Playing as the sniper class, we managed to peck off a few of the enemy foot soldiers before friendly reinforcements arrived! Quite a few tanks and gunships came in from seemingly nowhere, with guns blazing, lighting the enemy force up like the fourth of July! The victory was ours! After doing a little tea bagging on the dead enemy soldiers, we made our way to a vehicle spawner and hopped in a 3 man dune buggy. While I drove to the next objective, my brother was in the gunner's seat firing at any enemies that would cross our path.
While that was far from the beginning of the adventure me and my brother had that day, it is needless to say that this game is action packed!
The pros and cons that follow below are strictly from personal assessment and point of view, I hope they will help!
PROS
- Very large map
- Action is non stop
- Great graphics
- Good fighting mechanics
- Vehicle designs are cool
CONS
- Game mechanics make your vehicle (whatever it may be) more likely to flip
- You have to grind a lot to get a good amount of certs (free in-game money) to buy a decent weapon
- You can easily pay your way with real money to gain a slight advantage over your opponent, but at the same time everything is balanced. (I know those two sentences conflict but once/if you play the game you'll understand.)
Overall this game is fantastic for a f2p. I hope my review has helped!

When I started playing Robocraft last year, I recommended it to everyone. As an early beta it was rough around the edges, but the issues it had were mostly bugs and balance issues. These are things that should have been possible to fix given time.
Since then, the developers have released update after update, adding new features and making major changes. Under normal circumstances, I would be happy about that, because it shows that the devs really are actively working on the game. However, with each major update features are removed or completely reworked. I can recall three times where entire core components were removed from the game. Bugs are not often addressed, and balance issues seem to be ignored in favor of overhauling the core of the game. I would argue that the balance has gotten worse, not better.
Currently, Robocraft is flat-out broken. The combat system was recently reworked such that the effectiveness of every weapon class changed. Granted, there were balance issues in the previous system, but the replacement has magnified some old issues and introduced even more new ones. Rather than simply modifying the stats of each weapon, the developers opted to change the way they function at the base level.
Even if these balance issues are addressed, I am not confident that the developers will keep the current system in the future. I am well aware that Robocraft is still in Early Access, but the game does not seem to be moving toward a final release. It looks like the developers have no idea what direction they should be going in.

This was actually a pretty great game when I downloaded it a few years back, about the megabot update. I really enjoyed building and improving my designs, even if the grind became rather noticeable at tier 6 or so.
The game went downhill from there. The tech web was removed for a linear tree that forced you to progress through modules you didn't want until you could get to that new gun or movement part you were looking for. "Oh hey there's another type of shield I never asked for, now only 7 more useless modules until I get a new SMG."
The next problem was the respawning health. It felt like it got rid of a lot of the strategy in building a redundent machine that could take a beating and keep on swinging, not to mention the fact that medic bots were made next to useless immediatly. Also, paint became locked away from non paying users. As someone who didn't mind the orange and blue and didn't make art bots, I didn't care hugely but it was still a bit of a jerk move by the devs.
And then... Epic loot. I log into my account to find my savings decimated, my ability to create a new bot gone, and the few loot boxes I opened before quiting were incredibly unsatisfying compared to saving up cash after a few games and buying your desired part. Oh, and can't forget how weapons like the SMG have been made incredibly unsatisfying and how weapons like the missile launcher are insanely overpowered.
I wanted to get to tier 10 when I started. I wanted to make a sweet, red and black tank to roll over my foes. I wanted to keep playing the game that let me have moments like when I got 10 kills in a game because of tactics, a medic, and good bot design.
RIP Robocraft. You were good to me.
P.S. Mech legs were dumb when they let a huge bot hop around on one leg when my tank gets taken out of the fight if all the tracks on one side are destroyed, or when losing a few wheels or hovers immobilises you.

I'm recommending it, based on objective, unemotional input.  However, personally, let me be probably the first to not recommend this game.  No, its not a bad game, really, its not.  When it works, it works.  There are just some things that I personally don't like about the game.
But first, let me say what I do like about it:
-Gigantic Play space.  So much land!  I can't express how much land there is.  So much so you'll probably spend HOURS just running from Outpost to Outpost before you even SEE an enemy!  Eh... thats not so exciting, though.  Unless you're the sneaky stealth type that has no problem wasting hours on walking because getting in a vechicle gets destroyed before you can approach an occupied outpost.
-IF you're computer can handle the graphic load of max settings, the game looks fantastic. [I have 8 gigs of RAM and suffer a lot of graphic lag yet, even though the page SAYS max is 6GB.]  If not, you're better off playing Battlefield 3 or... I dunno, Tactical Intervention.
What I don't like:
-The game feels sluggish.  Considering you're likely to spend a lot of time on foot, sprint doesn't last nearly long enough.
-Maybe its just a setting under controls that I didn't see, but when I move the mouse, I expect the crosshair to move with it.  Instead, there's a wide deadzone that makes it feel like the extra second or two between mouse movement and crosshair movement seem THAT much longer and has been the cause of my death in close quarters WAY too much.
-I don't like that after all of this time, its still not available for Mac.  This would fix probably every performance issue I have.
-And lastly, people don't seem very interested in working together in this game.  This is not a fault of the developers, it is the fault of the gamers.  Far too much landspace to fight over, and most skirmishes end up being 1 sided, or all out war.  It can be fun, but most of the time, for me, ends up just wasting loads of time on travel.
It's an OK game but its really way too big to just do what you want.  Going solo isn't an option but I find myself on my own a lot anyway.

Dirty Bomb is quite an anomaly in the F2P arena. It has solid mechanics and base gameplay. Everything is accessible to everyone. You do have to have to buy new characters to use and loadouts (which vary up the weapon selection and minor perks), but the time it takes seems fair. There are plenty of missions that rotate every three hours and daily bonuses that allow you to rack up 1000s of credits every day in addition to receiving credits for just playing. A new merc will take you about 1-2 weeks to unlock if you time your missions right.  If you don't want to use in-game credits for this, there is the option to spend real world money. This does seem a bit high for what you get though and I recommend getting the bundle when it goes on sale. You're not at a loss for choice though at the start. You get Aura (a medic) and Skyhammer (a fire support class / jack of all trades type) permanently for free in addition to three rotating mercs that are freely available and change up every few weeks.
The feel of the game is quite smooth. There are plenty of trickjumps and shortcuts to find on the various maps. Just about every weapon is hitscan. This means that damage is dealt directly to whatever it is you click on. You can generally take several shots before dying and with a medic nearby to revive you, you're never too long removed from the action. It's similar in several ways to Enemy Territory, another free game released a decade ago by the same team, that was hugely popular as well as TF2. There are similar classes that you can choose from. Medics revive and heal. Assault dishes out damage as well as taking it. Fire support provides your team with ammo and helps destroy objectives and whole teams from afar. Engineers repair much faster as well as planting/defusing bombs. And Recon helps your team with map awareness and picking off enemies from a distance. Lots of basic functionality is shared across the classes and there's plenty of combinations to choose from if you're looking for something that'll fit your playstyle.
Finally, the community itself is fairly laid-back and welcoming. Especially compared with other FPSes I've played. And I've been playing since the 90s. This is likely a result of how small it is. There's something like 3-4k players on typically. Just enough to have a decent selection of servers across multiple maps and game modes. In addition to there being pick-up games you can find being formed across the many community voice servers if you're looking for more of a challenge.
There is some hitching with certain combinations of hardware and software. It's recommended that you get a CPU that is very powerful on one core at least. The latest quad-core from Intel overclocked a decent amount should allow consistent 144 fps and up. A mid-range GPU should suffice. I can personally run this at 1440p @ 144hz on a 4930k @ 4.3ghz and a 7970 ghz Edition @ 1165 Core / 1575 Memory. I generally get up to 200fps with this setup and the GPU runs at about 40-60% usage.
This is probably among the better deals in not only F2P games, but more expensive ones as well. TF2 players will love it for the similarly fast paced action and the different classes provided. CS:GO players will enjoy the small teams and similar weaponry that they are already used to. Not to mention the greatly reduced recoil. While alternatives exist in the rapidly expanding genre of class-based shooters, Dirty Bomb has that perfect fit of fast action and teamplay that I find lacking elsewhere.

One of my past childhood favorites, worth the money spent, especially when it's put upon sale.
Historical accuracy? For the most part, yes. Even the way they died is often accurate. It's mainly reenacting the famous battles during the middle ages, with you acting as the commander. There are some instances that aren't as accurate. The new expansion adds five more nations to the fold, effectively making it so there is twenty-three nations in total. Whereas the best part is that despite having the same generic units, and having only one or two unique units to each and their own.
The outcome of the battle can truly be decided with what technology and talents each and every civilization holds, and how much you use it to your advantage.. Where each civilization has four or five, maybe even six bonuses, one of those bonuses going to the team it's on, and itself. They have one unique technology exclusive to it's own nation, and one or two unique units depending on the civilization itself. Not only that these special units are powerful in their own field, but they're exclusive to your nation and anyone else being of the same nation. Therefore making it so the only way to get those units when not being of that nation is to convert them.
Each civilization has it's own playstyle, defensive or offensive, no matter what, you need to use those traits to an entire advantage. On top of that, said civilizations have their own technology trees, which has some historical inaccuracy, sadly. Though these trees balance the game a little as well. Though when in control of a civilization, you need to know not only it's strengths, but it's flaws, and how to combat them.
The HD version changes actually, very little of the same, safe for graphics that were revised, the gameplay and controls were not touched one bit, therefore allowing any Age of Empires veteran to join in the fun.
The new expansion is worth it, by adding more civilizations, technologies, and units to play around with. So with that, this game is good for those who love a historically accurate real-time-strategy type game. Where each and every civilization has those aforementioned strengths and difficulties.
So, what are you waiting for? Hit that green button.
